title: outram-foam-mesh: snappyHexMesh must preserve cyclic (coupled) patch conformity — blocks cyclic BC meshes
description: snappyHexMesh cannot currently produce a mesh usable with cyclic BCs. Evidence (verified 2026-08-13): snappy_hex_mesh/snapping.rs collects ONLY PatchKind::Wall patch points to project, and its module header states the parallel/COUPLED-PATCH and displacement-diffusion machinery is deliberately omitted; grep finds zero 'cyclic' mentions anywhere under outram-foam-mesh/src/snappy_hex_mesh/. blockMesh DOES parse cyclic/cyclicAMI into PatchKind::Cyclic (block_mesh.rs:1664), so a cyclic background mesh can be built — but castellation+snapping do not preserve face-for-face conformity across a coupled patch PAIR, so the N/S and E/W patches stop matching and the cyclic BC is invalid. Needed: (a) treat coupled patch pairs as constrained during castellation (refine both sides identically), (b) constrain snapping displacement on cyclic patch points to the patch plane / apply the transform to the partner, (c) a conformity assertion (same face count + matching face centres under the cyclic transform) as the V&V gate. Raised by external GitHub issue #3 (subchannel with spacer grid + fuel rods, needs cyclic N/S and E/W). Distinct from op-ulo.5, which is the SOLVER-side cyclic support in outram-foam-basic-lib.

notes.content: Done in commit 47476d1308. Two gaps fixed: (1) castellation now emits Cyclic patch pairs via CastellationControls::with_cyclic_axis, with halves sorted into corresponding order so local face i <-> face i holds by construction; (2) snapping no longer freezes cyclic-plane points — displacement is projected into the plane then partner-averaged across the seam. New snappy_hex_mesh::cyclic module provides check_conformity, the geometric V&V gate FvMeshBuilder lacks. Measured: seam motion 2.474460e-2 m with conformity preserved to 1e-9 m, vs exactly 0 m frozen baseline; 76-face pair, max non-ortho 25.44 deg, 0 inverted cells. Translational only — rotational/AMI rejected. NOTE: still does NOT close GitHub issue #3 — that needs STEP->STL import (absent) and a two-phase solver (outram-foam-multiphase is scaffold), and the reporter's geometry.zip could not be fetched.

chem-eng: revisit the 9-decimal-place input-change guard now that it buys no performance
description:
Follow-up from op-fm5 (2026-08-11).

Every transfer-function block gates on

    (current_input * 1e9).round() - (previous_timestep_input * 1e9).round() != 0.0

and only records an increment when that fires. The guard was originally a PERFORMANCE guard: under the old design each input change pushed a response onto a growing vector, so suppressing tiny changes suppressed vector growth. After the O(1) rewrite an increment costs a couple of flops and no memory, so the guard buys nothing.

It was deliberately KEPT in 0.2.0 so the recurrence ignores exactly the same sub-nano changes the old code did, i.e. so the rewrite was a pure cost change. But it has a real downside worth revisiting on its own merits: because previous_timestep_input is only updated when the guard fires, an input that ramps by less than 1e-9 per step is ignored INDEFINITELY rather than accumulating -- the block sees a frozen input until the running difference happens to cross the threshold. For a slow drift that is a genuine (if small) modelling error, and it is the sort of thing a real-time twin running for a long time can hit.

PROPOSED: either drop the guard entirely (increments of zero are free and harmless), or keep it but make it compare against the last ACCEPTED input in a way that lets sub-threshold changes accumulate. Whichever is chosen, re-run the analytic-superposition verification tests in */stable_transfer_functions/recurrence_tests.rs, and note that changing this WILL change numerical output very slightly, unlike the 0.2.0 rewrite.

Low priority -- correctness nit, not a defect anyone has hit.

title: materials: MATPRO Zircaloy dnu/dT may have the WRONG SIGN -- literature unread, egress blocked
description:
SUSPECTED DEFECT, UNCONFIRMED. Filed as a TODO at the maintainer's request 2026-08-05. Do not act on it as if confirmed, and do not 'fix' the sign on the strength of this bead alone.

THE OBSERVATION: PoissonRatioModel::MatproZircaloy computes nu = E/(2G) - 1 from MATPRO's independently-fitted Young's and shear modulus lines. The resulting nu INCREASES with temperature -- measured 0.386353680 at 600 K, 0.5674999999999999 at 1500 K, crossing the incompressible limit 0.5 at 1354.84 K (this crossing is what op-6sl.7 gates on, now refused rather than clamped in LinearElastic::from_models).

WHY THAT LOOKS WRONG: the abstract of Northwood (1975) on Zircaloy elastic constants states that measured Poisson's ratio DECREASES with temperature. If that is right, the port reproduces a correlation whose temperature derivative has the opposite sign to the measurement it is meant to represent -- and the 0.5 crossover would be an artefact of the sign error rather than a real (if unguarded) upstream defect.

WHY IT IS UNCONFIRMED: only the ABSTRACT was read. The paper itself is unread because outbound egress in this container blocks every literature host (see the egress bead). An abstract is not sufficient evidence to overturn a transcription -- it does not say over what temperature range, for what alloy/texture/cold-work state, or whether the quoted trend is of measured nu or of a derived quantity.

WHAT WOULD SETTLE IT, in order:
1. Read Northwood 1975 in full and record the actual nu(T) table with its range and material condition.
2. Re-derive nu = E/(2G) - 1 from the MATPRO E and G fits as transcribed here and check the port reproduces MATPRO's own arithmetic -- i.e. separate 'did we transcribe correctly?' from 'is MATPRO right?'. These are different questions and only the first is this port's responsibility.
3. Only if the transcription is faithful AND the literature contradicts MATPRO: document it as an upstream defect with the measurement cited, exactly as the rkdcha.F90 and nmvpir.F90 discrepancies are handled. Reproduce, pin with a test, never silently correct.

DEPENDS ON THE EGRESS BLOCKER. This cannot be resolved in this container.

Related: op-6sl.7 (crossover gating, now decided -- refuse), docs/validation/poisson_ratio_zircaloy.md (the validation case, whose benchmark data is blocked on the same egress problem).

fracture: FV vs FEM accuracy at the crack-tip singularity is an open research question
description:
MAINTAINER RAISED 2026-08-05: 'FV doesn't do as well around sharp corners whereas FEM might. this is indeed an open question.'

This is the residue of op-a7p.6 after the FE-blocked claim was corrected. That correction established what is NOT the problem: the G-theta domain integral G = int_V [sigma:grad(u).grad(theta) - W div(theta)] dV is discretisation-agnostic, OpenFOAM ships solidDisplacement as an FV solid solver, and offbeat's mechanics module is already a port of it. So no finite-element framework is required to host G-theta.

WHAT REMAINS GENUINELY OPEN, and is the subject of this bead: whether cell-centred FV can resolve the crack-tip field accurately enough for G-theta to be trustworthy.

The tension:
- The crack-tip field is singular: u ~ sqrt(r), sigma ~ 1/sqrt(r).
- FE has purpose-built machinery for it -- quarter-point elements (Barsoum), which place the mid-side node at L/4 so the isoparametric map reproduces the sqrt(r) displacement exactly, and enriched/XFEM bases that add the Williams series to the approximation space.
- FV cell-centred gradient reconstruction (least-squares or Green-Gauss) is first or second order on smooth fields and has no equivalent trick. Its accuracy degrades precisely where the singularity is.
- G-theta is only usable because of its DOMAIN INDEPENDENCE -- the ring integral should give the same G for any ring enclosing the front. That property depends on an accurate grad(u) THROUGHOUT the ring. If FV grad(u) is polluted near the front, domain independence breaks and the computed G depends on which ring you picked, which is exactly the failure mode that makes a result untrustworthy without announcing itself.

POSSIBLE ROUTES, none yet evaluated:
1. Graded mesh -- refine aggressively toward the front and rely on the outer ring being smooth. Cheapest, but the refinement needed is unquantified and may be impractical in 3-D.
2. Place the ring far from the front where the field is smooth, exploiting domain independence deliberately rather than incidentally. Trades singularity error for a larger domain and more W integration.
3. Enrichment of the FV reconstruction with the Williams series -- an FV analogue of XFEM. Research-flavoured.
4. Extract K from the far field by fitting the Westergaard solution (westergaard_unit_field is already ported and verified) and skip the domain integral entirely for simple geometries. Limited, but needs nothing new.

FIRST STEP is a literature review, not code: published FV J-integral work exists and should be read before committing to a route. BLOCKED IN THIS CONTAINER -- egress blocks every literature host (see the egress bead). This is a genuine reason this bead cannot start here, not an excuse.

DO NOT start porting gbilin.F90/gbil3d.F90 against an unevaluated route. They are the right first targets once quadrature exists (gbil3d is JEVEUX-free, gbilin needs only the material lookup, both pure per-Gauss-point algebra) but their only meaningful test is that the ring integral reproduces a known G -- which is precisely the property this bead is about.

  thermo/black_oil.rs        api_gravity, oil_specific_gravity_from_api, liquid_molecular_weight, liquid_normal_boiling_point, solution_gor, oil_density, viscosities
  petroleum/generate_compounds.rs  BulkCharacterizationOptions + generate_compounds -> Vec<PseudoComponent>
  petroleum/pseudo_component.rs    PseudoComponent (wraps a thermo Component), Riazi/Lee-Kesler correlation sets
  petroleum/assay.rs         BulkAssay / CurveAssay
  columns/                   full rigorous MESH solver, side draws (Stage::with_side_draws), ColumnType::RefluxedAbsorber, PengRobinson package
  columns/dynamic.rs         DynamicColumn (RK4), already V&V'd under op-6rhz

KEY DESIGN DECISION, put to the maintainer and answered: black oil is a TWO-pseudo-component PVT model (stock-tank oil + solution gas) with no composition, so it cannot itself yield naphtha/kero/diesel cuts. Chosen approach: BLACK OIL CHARACTERISES, ASSAY CUTS. The black-oil bulk spec (API gravity, gas SG, GOR) supplies exactly the three fields BulkAssay wants — specific_gravity_60f, molar_mass, average_boiling_point — and generate_compounds cuts that into the pseudo-component slate the column runs on. That is how a refinery specifies a crude when no full assay exists, and it uses both modules for what they are actually for.

Rejected alternatives, recorded so they are not re-proposed: a literal 2-component black-oil column (produces only a gas/liquid split, not a crude unit), and a TBP-curve-primary model (more realistic but reduces black oil to a density correlation).

Scope: library module in dwsim-libs AND a GUI sim, per the maintainer's answer.

No human V&V is claimed for anything this epic produces.

What it could not have known is that two defects sat between the pieces, both only reachable with a wide-boiling feed, and both invisible to the benzene/toluene case the dynamic model was validated on:

  1. op-190j.5 — the steady bubble-point solve. CubicEos returned Some(NaN) where it meant None (a compressibility root at or below the covolume), and the bracket-expansion heuristic chased the supercritical asymptote where K collapses to 1. All three cubic packages now solve the reference crude column, monotonic, agreeing with each other and with Ideal.

crude: black-oil -> BulkAssay -> pseudo-component slate
description:
petroleum/crude_distillation.rs, part 1. A BlackOilCrude spec (API gravity, gas specific gravity, GOR, BS&W) that produces a pseudo-component slate.

The composition is exact rather than approximate: black_oil::oil_specific_gravity_from_api, ::liquid_molecular_weight and ::liquid_normal_boiling_point produce precisely the three Option fields BulkAssay carries (specific_gravity_60f, molar_mass, average_boiling_point), which BulkCharacterizationOptions then hands to generate_compounds.

Acceptance: a named reference crude (pick a real published API/SG, cite it) yields a monotonic pseudo-component slate — boiling points ascending, mole fractions summing to 1, every Tc/Pc/omega finite and physical. Assert against the black-oil correlations' own published ranges, and state where the crude sits relative to them.

notes.content:
Done. BlackOilCrude -> BulkAssay -> pseudo-component slate works and is tested (5 tests).

The composition turned out to be exact rather than approximate: black_oil::oil_specific_gravity_from_api, ::liquid_molecular_weight and ::liquid_normal_boiling_point produce precisely the three Option fields BulkAssay carries. Viscosity fields are deliberately left None so generate_compounds falls back to Abbott's correlation rather than being handed a fabricated measurement.

Measured for the 38 degAPI light-sweet reference crude: SG 0.8348, MW 206.5 g/mol, mean NBP 538.8 K. An 8-cut slate spans normal boiling points 390.1 K to 825.2 K with mole fractions summing to 1 within 1e-9 and all Tc/Pc/omega finite and monotonic.

Tests assert: API<->SG round-trip is inverse to <1e-12; all three bulk properties land in crude-like ranges; a heavier crude (22 degAPI) characterises as heavier on all three; the slate normalises; CrudeCut bands tile the temperature axis with no gaps.

ONE THING THE SLATE REVEALED that matters downstream: the heaviest cut has an acentric factor of 1.16, far past the omega < 0.49 limit of standard Peng-Robinson's kappa correlation. That is a property of a real crude's heavy end, not a bug here, but it means PR cannot be used on this slate — see op-190j.2.

description: teddy0@snrsi-arch-desktop
title: teddy0@snrsi-arch-desktop
crude: CDU column configuration with side draws
description:
BLOCKED on the wide-boiling solver gap — see the sibling bug bead.

Configuration code is WRITTEN and compiles: CrudeColumnConfig (stages, feed stage, pressure, reflux, bottoms, liquid side draws), CrudeColumnError with five specific validation rejections, CutResult/CrudeColumnResult, and solve_crude_column wiring the slate through RigorousColumn with Stage::with_side_draws. Config validation and material balance are tested and pass.

What does NOT work is the solve itself. The end-to-end test is committed #[ignore]d with the full diagnosis in its doc comment rather than deleted or quietly loosened, so the failure is visible to the next reader.

Decision made and recorded in CrudeColumnConfig's docs: this is a REBOILED column, not the refluxed-absorber-with-stripping-steam a real CDU is. ColumnType::RefluxedAbsorber exists in the enum but RigorousColumn::distillation() is the only constructor and fixes the type. The consequence — no stripping steam, no pump-arounds, no furnace, so the energy balance is not a refinery's — is stated in the docs rather than hidden.

Resume when the solver gap is addressed.

notes.content:
WORKS. The crude column converges to a physical, monotonic profile with a realistic cut slate.

38 degAPI crude, 10 pseudo-components, 650 K residue cut point, 12 stages, 3 side draws, RR 3.0, ideal K-values, Wang-Henke: converged in 38 iterations to 6.7e-7.

  stage  0 (overhead) 0.3376 mol/s  423.6 K (150 C)  naphtha
  stage  4            0.0900 mol/s  494.9 K (222 C)  kerosene
  stage  6            0.0750 mol/s  511.7 K (239 C)  kerosene
  stage  8            0.0600 mol/s  530.8 K (258 C)  diesel
  stage 11 (bottoms)  0.4373 mol/s  588.5 K (315 C)  residue

Those land in the conventional CDU bands (overhead 120-150 C, kero 200-250 C, diesel 250-300 C, flash zone 340-370 C) — a sanity agreement, not a validation.

TWO REAL ERRORS were found and fixed, and both had produced a 'converged' answer with a small residual:

1. FEEDING THE COLUMN ITS OWN UNDISTILLABLE HEAVY END. A crude's pseudo-components run past 800 K NBP and cannot vaporise at 1.2 bar. Asking the fractionator to separate them is asking it to separate something with no vapour phase. Fixed by routing everything above a residue cut point around the column straight to the bottoms — which is exactly what a refinery does, and why atmospheric residue goes to a vacuum tower. Measured: cut points 560/650/700 K all converge monotonically in 26-32 iterations; no cut point gives non-monotonic in 79-90.

2. SIDE DRAWS LARGER THAN THE INTERNAL LIQUID. With draws as absolute rates, the bypass shrank the column feed until draws (0.15 mol/s) exceeded internal reflux (0.10 mol/s), draining the column above the feed. Draws are now FRACTIONS of the column feed so they scale with it, and the doc states the reflux_ratio/(1+reflux_ratio) ceiling.

So op-190j.5 needs rewriting: the wide-boiling difficulty was real but it was NOT primarily a solver defect. Two of the three symptoms were my modelling errors. What survives as a genuine gap is the PR78 absence and Wang-Henke reporting success on a non-physical profile.

Also retained from before: this is a REBOILED column, not the refluxed-absorber-with-stripping-steam a real CDU is, and CrudeColumnConfig says so.

notes.content:

columns: bubble-point solver fails with ANY cubic package; and reports success on non-physical profiles
description: Description:

notes.content:
FIXED 2026-09-04. Both findings, at their source.

FINDING 1 — two compounding defects, neither in the EOS (the bead's own evidence that ln_phi is healthy at 400-600 K was right; the solver goes far higher than that):

  (a) CubicEos::select_root accepted a compressibility root at or below the covolume B. ln_phi then evaluates ln(Z - B) on a negative argument and returns Some(vec![NaN, ..]) rather than None, so k_values' existing 'no usable root -> Wilson' fallback never fired and NaN propagated. Measured: PR liquid ln_phi is NaN from ~1500 K up, well above the slate's highest Tc of 981 K. select_root now requires Z > B for both phases, restoring the meaning of the Option.

  (b) Above the critical region both phases return the SAME root, so every K collapses to 1 and the bubble residual decays asymptotically to 0 without crossing. solve_scalar's expansion moves whichever endpoint has the smaller |residual| — precisely the wrong move against an asymptote — so it chased it away from the real root and reported NoBracket with best |residual| = 1.1e-16. Added scan_for_bracket: on NoBracket or a trivial converged result, sweep the interval and take the LOWEST non-degenerate sign change, which is the physical bubble point. The scan skips degenerate stretches, which exist at BOTH ends of the range, not just the top.

Measured on the reference crude column (12 stages, 8 pseudo-components, 1.2 bar), all monotonic:
  Ideal             T 423.6 -> 588.5 K
  PengRobinson      T 424.9 -> 586.1 K
  PengRobinson1978  T 424.9 -> 586.9 K
  Srk               T 424.8 -> 586.4 K
The three cubics agreeing with each other and with Ideal is the cross-check that they are on the physical root.

FINDING 2 — columns::bubble_point::check_monotonic_temperature now rejects a converged profile whose temperature falls going down the column, with a message that says so. Stages carrying a specified heat duty are exempt: an intercooler legitimately reverses the gradient. 4 unit tests including the exact dip shape the bead describes.

Also added SaturationError::TrivialSolution so a K = 1 'solution' can never be returned as a saturation point. A single component is exempt — for pure i the residual IS K - 1, so K = 1 is what Tsat means, and testing for triviality there would reject every correct answer (caught by 4 pre-existing single-component flash tests).

CrudeColumnConfig gains a `package` field defaulting to PengRobinson1978; the Ideal pin and its explanatory comment are gone. 678 tests pass.
notes.author: teddy0@snrsi-arch-desktop

notes.content:
CORRECTION to my earlier notes on this bead, after pulling 44a2001339 (fixed by another machine).

My diagnosis was RIGHT IN ITS EVIDENCE AND WRONG IN ITS CONCLUSION. I reported that CubicEos::ln_phi returns finite liquid and vapour fugacity coefficients across 400-600 K for both PR and PR78, and concluded the EOS was healthy and the defect lay elsewhere in the bubble-point iteration.

The evidence was true. The conclusion was wrong because I checked the wrong range: THE BUBBLE-POINT SOLVER EXPLORES TO ROUGHLY 1950 K, not 600 K. The actual defect was in the cubic path after all — select_root accepted a compressibility root at or below the covolume B, so ln_phi evaluated ln(Z - B) on a negative argument and returned Some(vec![NaN, ...]) rather than None, which defeated k_values existing no-usable-root fallback.

The lesson worth keeping: I probed the range the COLUMN operates in, not the range the SOLVER searches. Those are different, and only the second one bounds where a numerical failure can occur.

Consequence for what I wrote elsewhere: my claim that PR78 was "necessary but not sufficient" is superseded. With the cubic path fixed, PR78 is now the DEFAULT package for the crude column and it solves — 34 iterations, error 8.875e-7, monotonic profile. The doc comments in crude_distillation.rs have been re-measured and corrected.

One finding survives and is worth keeping: on ideal K-values, no cut point gave a CONVERGED but non-monotonic profile; on PR78 the same case reports NotConverged after 100 iterations at error 5.9e-3. The cubic path fails honestly where the ideal path failed silently. The underlying complaint — that a solver can report success on a physically impossible profile — is unchanged and still deserves a monotonicity check.

dwsim: wire PR78 into PropertyPackageModel
description: ALREADY PORTED, only needed wiring. src/thermo/pr1978.rs was a complete standalone PR78 implementation (kappa, alpha, a_i, a_mix, z_factor, ln_phi, dadt, enthalpy/entropy departure) with PR78_OMEGA_THRESHOLD = 0.491 — it just was not reachable through PropertyPackageModel. The crate CLAUDE.md already listed PR78 among the ported advanced EOS; checking that before writing anything saved duplicating it.

notes.content:
Done. PR78 reachable as CubicEos::PengRobinson1978 and PropertyPackageModel::PengRobinson1978.

Wired as a CubicEos VARIANT rather than a parallel dispatch path, because PR78 differs from base PR in exactly one thing — the alpha-slope kappa(w). Same Omega_a (0.45724), same Omega_b (0.07780), same (u,w) = (2,-1). So four of the five match arms just gained  and only alpha_slope branches, delegating to pr1978::pr78_kappa so there is ONE definition of the correlation rather than two that can drift.

The enum-dispatch rule paid for itself: adding the variant produced a non-exhaustive-match error at columns/thermo_bridge.rs:508, a second dispatch site I would not otherwise have found.

3 tests: the variant is bitwise identical to pr78_kappa across w = -0.1..2.0; bitwise identical to base PR below the 0.491 threshold and genuinely different above it; shares base PR's prefactors. Measured at w = 1.16 (the heaviest cut a 38 degAPI crude generates): PR kappa 1.80046, PR78 kappa 1.90704, difference 1.066e-1.

HONEST OUTCOME ON THE MOTIVATING CASE: PR78 does NOT rescue the crude column, and I had expected it to. Measured on the same case, all with 'non-finite value in input or K-values':

  PengRobinson      BubblePointFailed at stage 0
  Srk               BubblePointFailed at stage 1
  PengRobinson1978  BubblePointFailed at stage 4   <- furthest, still fails
  Ideal             converges, 38 iterations, 6.7e-7

PR78 gets materially further, which is consistent with the kappa fix helping, but is not sufficient. Crucially the EOS is NOT the culprit: ln_phi was checked directly and returns finite liquid AND vapour fugacity coefficients for this slate at every temperature 400-600 K, for both PR and PR78. The failure is in the bubble-point solver's temperature iteration with a cubic package — a separate defect, now recorded in op-190j.5.

So the crude column stays on ideal K-values, with that decision and its measurements documented at the call site rather than left as an unexplained choice.

notes.content:
CORRECTION after pulling 44a2001339. My close note said PR78 'does NOT rescue the crude column' and was 'necessary but not sufficient'. That is superseded.

It was necessary. The other half was two defects in the cubic path (select_root accepting a root at or below the covolume; ln_phi then returning NaN rather than None). With those fixed, PropertyPackageModel::PengRobinson1978 is now the DEFAULT for the crude column and it solves: 34 iterations, final error 8.875e-7, monotonic profile, draw temperatures 424.95 / 494.89 / 511.25 / 529.94 / 586.85 K.

So the wiring done here is load-bearing after all — the crude column runs on it.

My supporting evidence was also mis-scoped, and that is the part worth remembering: I checked ln_phi over 400-600 K, the range the COLUMN operates in, and concluded the EOS was fine. The bubble-point solver searches to about 1950 K, and that is where it broke. Probe the solver's search range, not the model's operating range.

OPCPFluidArray energy equation: div(phi,h) is pure central differencing -- dispersive over/undershoot at an advected thermal front
description:
MEASURED 2026-08-12 in crates/outram-park-fork-coolprop, while fixing the inlet-enthalpy BC (op-2qsf). NOT fixed -- this is a discretisation-scheme question, deliberately left alone rather than half-fixed.

SYMPTOM. The energy equation's explicit convection term is fvc::div(&self.phi, &self.he), and fvc::div interpolates the convected scalar with fvc::interpolate, i.e. LINEAR (central) interpolation. The energy equation is advection-dominated (cell Peclet >> 1 for a gas), so an advancing thermal front carries dispersive over/undershoots.

MEASUREMENT (Nitrogen, 8 cells, 1 m, 1e-4 m2, 1 bar, 0.5 m/s, dt 2e-4 s, uniform seed with a step inlet BC):
  seed 300 K, inlet BC 500 K: at 3000 steps the inlet cell reads 556.52 kJ/kg against a 520.45 kJ/kg BC -- 117 % of the imposed step, i.e. a 36 kJ/kg overshoot; at 10000 steps interior cells reach 571 K, above both the 500 K inlet and the 300 K seed.
  seed 500 K, inlet BC 300 K: at 3000 steps the inlet cell reads 296.13 kJ/kg against a 311.20 kJ/kg BC; at 10000 steps a cell reaches 274.45 K, ~25 K below anything imposed.
Magnitude is ~10-15 % of the imposed step on this 8-cell mesh -- textbook central-difference dispersion, not an instability (the fields stay finite and bounded over 10000 steps, damped by the alpha_h laplacian).

WHAT A FIX WOULD BE. OpenFOAM's rhoPimpleFoam does not use plain linear for div(phi,h) -- upwind or a limited scheme (limitedLinear / vanLeer) is the norm. The fvc::muscl / fvc::reconstruct_pos_neg machinery for a limited face reconstruction already exists in openfoam_source and is used by the HybridAllMach KNP path, so the pieces are there.

WHY NOT DONE HERE. (a) it is a scheme change, not a BC fix; (b) fvc::div is shared vendored code used by every solver path and by the sibling tampines-steam-tables copy, so changing it moves numbers across both crates; (c) any change to it must be justified against the crate's existing V&V numbers rather than slipped in. Document, measure, then decide.

Recorded in the doc comment of lateral_coupling::tests::inlet_enthalpy_bc_heats_uniform_field_without_reapplying_each_step so a reader meets the caveat where they meet the test.

title: CIET educational simulator v3 — tampines library + digital-twin GUI, OPCPFluidArray-backed
description:
Maintainer direction 2026-08-13. Third generation of the CIET educational simulator.

ARCHITECTURE (as directed):
  - The SIMULATOR IS A LIBRARY and lives in crates/tampines.
  - The GUI BINARY lives in crates/outram-park-digital-twin-engine.
  - This split already matches the twin crate's own rule that it carries NO physics.

WHAT CHANGES vs v2:
  - Replace the TUAS array backend with OPCPFluidArray.
  - New widget art for heater, shell-and-tube heat exchanger, cooling fans, pump and piping, all on the new widget libraries.
  - Real-time capable, with an OPC-UA server that FITS THE EXISTING CLIENT unchanged.

WHAT ALREADY EXISTS - verified by grep 2026-08-13, so none of this is greenfield:

  1. CIET v2 IS SUBSTANTIAL AND SHIPPING. Two binaries in the twin crate:
       ciet_educational_simulator_v2  (src/bin/ciet_educational_simulator_v2/)
       ciet_v2_opcua_client           (src/bin/ciet_v2_opcua_client/)
     plus src/ciet_opcua/ at 2,965 lines - state.rs 707, node_map.rs 746, simulator.rs 588, pki_paths.rs 200, server.rs 184, discovery.rs 71, user_controls.rs, mod.rs. The reactor-agnostic half (transport, server thread, tokio runtime, PKI, mDNS, address space, read/write callbacks) is already factored out into src/opcua_core/ and explicitly documented as serving ANY OUTRAM PARK simulator. v3 supplies its own half of that contract; it does not rewrite opcua_core.

  2. THERMINOL IS ALREADY IN THE COOLPROP FORK (maintainer was right): crates/outram-park-fork-coolprop/src/incompressibles/ carries Therminol, with tests (incompressible_t66.rs, incompressible_freeze_psat.rs). No new fluid-property implementation should be written for the CIET coolant.

  3. OPCPFluidArray LIVES IN THE COOLPROP FORK, at src/openfoam_algorithms/rhoPimpleFoam/, and is already consumed by tampines-steam-tables. crates/tampines ALREADY depends on outram-park-fork-coolprop, so the dependency edge for this migration exists today.

  4. WIDGETS THAT ALREADY EXIST in the twin crate components/: heat_exchanger.rs, pump.rs, pipe.rs, pipe_component.rs, bend.rs, valve.rs, cooling_tower.rs. MISSING: a heater widget, and a cooling-FAN widget (cooling_tower is not the same thing).

  5. THE RE-VALIDATION TARGET EXISTS: tuas .../ciet_educational_simulator_loop_prototypes/regression_tests.rs plus the coupled-DRACS natural-circulation suite. v3 must pass the SAME tests.

NAME COLLISION - MUST BE RESOLVED BEFORE ANY CODE (see child bead): 'version_3' ALREADY MEANS SOMETHING ELSE. tuas .../ciet_educational_simulator_loop_prototypes/version_3/mod.rs (1,435 lines) is v2's PID control with branch mass flowrates on separate threads - a thread-parallelism variant, not this new generation. Two different things called v3 in one workspace will cause real confusion.

AI-drafted capture of maintainer direction; nothing here is validated.
acceptance_criteria: v3 runs as a tampines library driven by a digital-twin GUI binary; passes the same TUAS CIET regression tests; hits real time; and the EXISTING ciet_v2_opcua_client drives it without modification.

title: CIET v3 NAMING DECISION: resolve the 'version_3' collision before any code
description:
BLOCKS EVERYTHING ELSE IN THIS EPIC. 'v3' is already taken and means something different.

EXISTING: crates/tuas_boussinesq_solver/.../ciet_educational_simulator_loop_prototypes/version_3/mod.rs, 1,435 lines, dated 2026-08-12. Its own doc comment: 'Version 3 keeps version 2's CTAH and TCHX PID control but solves the branch mass flowrates on separate threads (thread::spawn) to run faster than the serial version 2.' It is a THREAD-PARALLELISM variant of the loop prototype - measured 4000 s simulated in ~875 s on three threads vs ~1900 s serial.

PROPOSED (this epic): a new simulator GENERATION - tampines library, OPCPFluidArray backend, new widget art, real-time, OPC-UA.

These are not the same thing and both cannot be 'v3'. Maintainer decision needed on one of:
  (a) rename the TUAS prototype (e.g. version_2_parallel / version_2_threaded), freeing v3;
  (b) name the new generation something else entirely;
  (c) keep both and accept the ambiguity, documenting it loudly in both places.

Recommendation, for the maintainer to accept or reject: (a) - the TUAS thing is a parallelisation of v2, and its own doc comment says so, so 'version_2_parallel' describes it more accurately than 'version_3' does.
acceptance_criteria: A single unambiguous name is chosen and both locations reflect it; no two modules in the workspace claim 'CIET v3'.

title: CIET v3 art: PIPING widget — update existing pipe/bend/pipe_component
description:
UPDATE, not new: components/ already has pipe.rs, pipe_component.rs and bend.rs. Rework onto the new widget libraries.

Relevant existing state: op-wqk.9.4 records that a schematic omitted PipeVisual because of its heavy fluid-array backend - and the htgr_sim_v1 schematic later did use it for every connector. widget_studio/pipes.rs already exercises pipes over multiple flow backends including OPCPFluidArray, which is exactly the backend this epic migrates CIET to, so that file is the closest existing reference.

CIET is a three-branch loop plus DRACS - the piping IS the topology the student reads, so connector clarity matters more here than in a single-loop plant.
acceptance_criteria: Piping widgets render the three-branch-plus-DRACS topology legibly on the new widget libraries, backed by OPCPFluidArray, exercised in widget_studio.

title: CIET v3: GUI binary in the digital-twin crate
description:
The GUI binary lives in crates/outram-park-digital-twin-engine, NOT in tampines. Physics stays in the tampines library; this binary only drives and draws it.

Follow the existing v2 layout exactly - Cargo.toml already declares:
    [[bin]] name = 'ciet_educational_simulator_v2', path = 'src/bin/ciet_educational_simulator_v2/main.rs'
    [[bin]] name = 'ciet_v2_opcua_client',        path = 'src/bin/ciet_v2_opcua_client/main.rs'
with the binary's own module tree under src/bin/<name>/. v3 adds a third binary in the same shape.

Reuse the app scaffold rather than rebuilding threading: op-wqk.5 records src/app_scaffold/ as a reusable eframe::App threading/locking scaffold, and gui_frame_metrics.rs / frame_cost.rs landed recently for measuring frame cost.

Known GUI hazards already recorded, worth reading before starting: op-fngw (the htgr_sim_v1 GUI stepped the plant at a rate no test drove, and crashed), op-v5zb (physics thread cannot reach real time - fixed sleep after compute rather than a deadline), op-szmi.16 (still felt laggy after a texture bake, and could not measure itself).
acceptance_criteria: A ciet_educational_simulator_v3 binary in the twin crate drives the tampines v3 library, built on app_scaffold, with the physics/GUI boundary intact.

title: CIET v3: OPC-UA server that the EXISTING ciet_v2_opcua_client drives unmodified
description:
Maintainer requirement: 'opcua server capabilities that should fit the existing opcua client'. Read literally - the bundled client must work against v3 WITHOUT being modified.

WHAT ALREADY EXISTS (2,965 lines, verified 2026-08-13) - this is a contract-compatibility job, not a from-scratch server:
  src/opcua_core/  - reactor-AGNOSTIC half: TCP transport, server thread + tokio runtime, PKI paths, mDNS discovery, address-space construction, read/write callbacks. Its own docs say it serves ANY OUTRAM PARK simulator. DO NOT rewrite this.
  src/ciet_opcua/  - CIET's half: state.rs (707), node_map.rs (746), simulator.rs (588), pki_paths.rs (200), server.rs (184), discovery.rs (71), user_controls.rs, mod.rs. Its header explicitly names it 'the shared interface between the two CIET v2 binaries'.
  src/bin/ciet_v2_opcua_client/ - the client that must keep working.

THE ACTUAL WORK is deciding how v3 relates to ciet_opcua's node map: either v3 populates the SAME node map (client works untouched, which is the stated requirement), or the node map gains v3 variables ADDITIVELY so existing node ids keep their meaning. A breaking node-id change fails the requirement.

async-opcua was chosen deliberately for RustCrypto over openssl-sys, so the module builds headless on Termux/aarch64-linux-android with no target gate. v3 must not break that.

If adding a SECOND simulator to the shared core, ciet_opcua/mod.rs points at opcua_core::simulator as the thing to read first.
acceptance_criteria: ciet_v2_opcua_client, UNMODIFIED, discovers and drives the v3 simulator; node ids that v2 defined retain their meaning; the module still builds headless for aarch64-linux-android.

title: CIET v3: real-time performance gate, measured not assumed
description:
v3 must be a REAL-TIME simulator. This bead is the measurement that proves it.

BASELINE TO BEAT, from the existing prototype's own doc comment: on an i7-10875H, 4000 s of simulated time took ~1900 s serial and ~875 s with three threads at a 0.04 s timestep - i.e. the parallel prototype already ran at better than 4x real time. v3 on OPCPFluidArray must not regress below real time.

MEASURE IT, do not assert it. The workspace has repeatedly been bitten here:
  op-v5zb - physics thread cannot reach real time; a fixed sleep after compute is not a deadline
  op-775s - htgr_sim_v1 per-tick physics compute cost was never measured
  op-szmi.16 - a simulator that 'still feels laggy' and cannot measure itself
  frame_cost.rs / gui_frame_metrics.rs landed 2026-08-12 for exactly this
Use a real deadline scheduler, not sleep-after-compute, and report the achieved ratio of simulated time to wall-clock.
acceptance_criteria: Achieved simulated-to-wall-clock ratio is measured and reported on named hardware at a stated timestep, with a deadline-based scheduler rather than a fixed post-compute sleep; v3 sustains >= 1x real time.

title: CIET v3: tampines library skeleton — module layout and the physics/GUI boundary
description:
Stand up the v3 simulator as a LIBRARY in crates/tampines. No GUI, no eframe, no egui in this crate.

The boundary is already enforced by convention elsewhere: crates/outram-park-digital-twin-engine documents that it carries NO physics, and src/ciet_opcua/mod.rs states it contains 'no physics and no GUI' so it compiles headless on Termux / aarch64-linux-android with no target gate. v3 must preserve that property - the tampines library must build headless for Android, and the GUI binary stays in the twin crate.

tampines already depends on outram-park-fork-coolprop (where OPCPFluidArray lives), tuas_boussinesq_solver, tampines-steam-tables, outram-foam-basic-lib, outram-foam-multiphase, chem-eng, dwsim-libs and boon-lay - so no new workspace dependency edge is needed to start.

Blocked on the naming decision.
acceptance_criteria: A tampines library module exposes the v3 loop with no GUI dependency; cargo check --target aarch64-linux-android --all-targets is clean for the tampines library.

title: CIET v3: replace the TUAS array backend with OPCPFluidArray
description:
The core migration of this epic.

OPCPFluidArray lives in crates/outram-park-fork-coolprop/src/openfoam_algorithms/rhoPimpleFoam/ and is already consumed by tampines-steam-tables, so there is a working precedent to copy rather than a new integration to invent. Read that consumer first.

Scope: the CIET three-branch-plus-DRACS loop's fluid arrays move from TUAS's one_d_fluid_array_with_lateral_coupling to OPCPFluidArray, keeping the lateral-coupling behaviour the CIET components depend on.

DO NOT silently drop TUAS from tampines' dependencies as part of this - other tampines code and examples still use it, and the CIET regression tests being ported ARE TUAS tests. Whether tampines eventually sheds the TUAS dependency is a separate decision.

Watch for the known TUAS defects already tracked, so they are not faithfully reproduced into v3: op-4542 (Wakao correlation has swapped exponents, 5.84x divergence at Re=1000), op-lmye (CIET heater v2 feeds hydraulic-diameter Reynolds into a particle-diameter Wakao correlation), op-j7d0 (SolidColumn cylindrical-shell end control volumes built from a solid rod).
acceptance_criteria: The CIET v3 loop runs entirely on OPCPFluidArray with no TUAS fluid arrays in its path; the known TUAS defects above are either avoided or explicitly inherited-and-documented, not silently carried.

title: CIET v3 ACCEPTANCE GATE: re-validate against the SAME TUAS CIET regression tests
description:
v3 is not done until it reproduces v2/TUAS behaviour on the SAME tests. This is the bead that decides whether the OPCPFluidArray migration was faithful.

TARGET SUITE - crates/tuas_boussinesq_solver/.../ciet_educational_simulator_loop_prototypes/regression_tests.rs:
  ciet_coupled_nat_circ_set_a1_for_three_branch
  zero_flow_for_three_branch_ver_1
  flow_diode_reverse_flow_for_three_branch_ver1
  flow_diode_fwd_flow_for_three_branch_ver1
plus the coupled-DRACS natural-circulation and parasitic-heat-loss suites under pre_built_components/ciet_steady_state_natural_circulation_test_components/.

TOLERANCES ARE NOT TO BE LOOSENED. The existing suite carries its own (e.g. pri-loop relative tolerance 0.061, DRACS 0.062). If v3 misses, that is a finding to report, not a tolerance to widen - the workspace rule is explicit that a long or inconvenient test is never a reason to relax a bound.

RUNTIME WARNING from the workspace CLAUDE.md: these CIET natural-circulation tests integrate a coupled loop at 0.1 s timestep for 2000-2500 s of simulated time. They are VERY long running, MUST be run in parallel (never --test-threads=1), and a default 120 s command timeout will kill them mid-run. A timeout is not a failure.
acceptance_criteria: v3 passes the named regression tests at the EXISTING tolerances, run in release mode and in parallel; any deviation is reported with measured numbers rather than absorbed by widening a bound.

title: CIET v3 fluid properties: use the coolprop fork's Therminol, do not reimplement
description:
Maintainer note 2026-08-13: 'coolprop has therminol vp-1'. CONFIRMED by grep - crates/outram-park-fork-coolprop/src/incompressibles/ carries Therminol, referenced from src/lib.rs and the README, with tests at tests/incompressible_t66.rs and tests/incompressible_freeze_psat.rs.

CIET's coolant is the biphenyl/diphenyl-oxide eutectic - Dowtherm A and Therminol VP-1 are the same chemistry under two trade names. TUAS today carries its own Dowtherm/Therminol property path across many files under array_control_vol_and_fluid_component_collections/.

TASK: route v3's coolant properties through the coolprop fork rather than TUAS's own implementation, and CHECK THE TWO AGREE before switching - a property discrepancy would show up as a regression-test failure attributed to the array migration, which would waste debugging time on the wrong layer.

Do not write a new Therminol correlation. If the coolprop fork's coverage is short somewhere (temperature range, a property TUAS has that it lacks), report that gap rather than papering over it.
acceptance_criteria: v3 obtains coolant properties from the coolprop fork; a documented comparison against TUAS's existing Dowtherm/Therminol path shows agreement (or the disagreement is quantified and reported) BEFORE the regression suite is run.

title: CIET v3 art: HEATER widget — does not exist yet, new build
description:
NEW WIDGET. Verified 2026-08-13: crates/outram-park-digital-twin-engine/src/components/ has NO heater.rs. Everything else on the maintainer's art list already has a starting point; this one does not.

CIET's heater is the electrically-heated test section that drives the loop. It needs to show at least: applied power, surface/fluid temperature distribution along its length, and on/off or power-setpoint state.

Build it on the NEW widget libraries, consistent with the recently-reworked components (see excursion.rs, pebble_bed_texture.rs and control_rod_drive.rs for the current house pattern, and the widget_studio example for how tabs exercise a widget in isolation).

Note the existing performance lesson before drawing anything heavy: op-szmi.12 recorded 19,874 circles per frame from shared pebble-bed artwork causing GUI lag in BOTH simulators, fixed by a texture bake. Do not re-introduce per-frame primitive floods.
acceptance_criteria: A heater widget exists, is exercised by its own widget_studio tab, and renders without measurably degrading frame time.

title: CIET v3 art: cooling FAN widget — does not exist yet, new build
description:
NEW WIDGET. Verified 2026-08-13: components/ has cooling_tower.rs but NO fan widget. A cooling tower is not a cooling fan - CIET's CTAH and TCHX are air-cooled heat exchangers with fans whose speed is the control input.

The fan widget must expose fan speed as a driven state, because that is what the PID control acts on in the v2 CIET loop (CTAH and TCHX PID control is what version_2/version_3 of the prototype implement).

Build on the new widget libraries; same frame-cost caution as the heater bead.
acceptance_criteria: A cooling-fan widget exists with fan speed as a visible driven state, exercised by its own widget_studio tab.

title: CIET v3 art: shell-and-tube HEAT EXCHANGER widget — update existing
description:
UPDATE, not new: components/heat_exchanger.rs already exists. Rework it onto the new widget libraries for CIET's shell-and-tube geometry (DHX and the CTAH/TCHX arrangement).

Check what the existing widget already does before rewriting it - the workspace search-before-building rule applies, and there is also steam_generator.rs and condenser.rs in the same directory which may already carry reusable shell-side drawing.

Should show shell-side and tube-side inlet/outlet temperatures distinctly, since counter-flow behaviour is the teaching point of an educational simulator.
acceptance_criteria: The heat-exchanger widget renders CIET's shell-and-tube arrangement with shell/tube sides distinguishable, on the new widget libraries, exercised in widget_studio.

title: CIET v3 art: PUMP widget — update existing
description:
UPDATE, not new: components/pump.rs already exists. Rework onto the new widget libraries.

CIET's pump drives the forced-circulation branch; the v2 prototype's steady-state test is anchored on Zou's published 0.18 kg/s through the CTAH and heater branches. Pump state (on/off, speed or head) should be visible because forced-vs-natural circulation is the core teaching contrast in this simulator.
acceptance_criteria: The pump widget is on the new widget libraries with drive state visible, exercised in widget_studio.

title: njoy THERMR DEFECT: coherent-elastic discards the extra-temperature S(E) tables — sigma_coh_el is only ever available at the base temperature
description:
VERIFIED 2026-08-11 by running the port against ENDF/B-VIII.0 tsl-crystalline-graphite.endf (MAT=30).

DEFECT: src/thermr/mf7.rs parse_elastic() reads the LTHR=1 coherent-elastic section correctly, but for each of the LT extra-temperature LIST records it keeps ONLY the temperature value and THROWS AWAY the S(E) table:

    for _ in 0..lt {
        let list = cur.read_list()?;
        extra_temperatures_k.push(list.head.c1);   // <-- S values discarded
    }

Consequently CoherentElastic (mf7.rs:33) stores a single s_of_e for the base temperature, and CoherentElastic::cross_section(&self, e_ev) (src/thermr/coherent.rs:29) takes NO temperature argument. There is no way to evaluate sigma_coh_el at any temperature other than the base one.

The struct doc is honest about this ('their S tables are not yet retained'), but src/thermr/mod.rs:17 lists coherent as '**done**', which overstates it.

WHY IT MATTERS (HTR-10 critical path): graphite is the HTR-10 moderator and coherent elastic is its DOMINANT thermal channel (measured via the port at 0.0253 eV: sigma_coh_el = 4.55 b vs sigma_inel = 0.49 b, so ~90% of thermal scattering). The graphite evaluation tabulates 10 temperatures: 296, 400, 500, 600, 700, 800, 1000, 1200, 1600, 2000 K. The IAEA HTR-10 B1-B4 benchmarks are at 20/120/250 C (293/393/523 K) and operation runs hotter. Using the 296 K Bragg structure factor at 523 K or 1000 K gets the Debye-Waller suppression wrong and therefore the thermal spectrum and k_eff wrong.

FIX: retain the per-temperature S(E) tables (the LIST records also carry an LI interpolation scheme between temperatures), and give CoherentElastic a temperature-aware cross_section(e_ev, temp_k) / bragg_reflections(e_ev, temp_k). Related but distinct from op-cjw.22 (which is about interpolating the INELASTIC S(alpha,beta) across temperature).

SIZE: small-to-medium. The record layout is already parsed; this is retaining data that is currently dropped, plus threading a temperature through two methods and their callers (src/acer/thermal.rs is the only in-tree consumer).

notes.content: FIXED 2026-08-11 (this session; unverified-by-human, not committed yet). parse_elastic now retains every LT extra-temperature S(E) LIST (shared Bragg-edge grid validated, LI codes captured): CoherentElastic is now {bragg_energies_ev, temperatures_k, s_tables, temp_interp}. coherent.rs evaluates cross_section(e_ev, temp_k)/bragg_reflections(e_ev, temp_k)/s_of_e_at(temp_k) with the shared policy: NJOY rdelas tolerance match (T/1000+5 K) -> LI-law interpolation between bracketing tabulated temps -> NjoyError::TemperatureOutOfRange (new variant) outside the range. acer thermal_from_mf7 writes ITCE/ITCX from s_of_e_at(temp_k). MEASURED (tests/thermal_graphite_coherent.rs, MAT 30, 0.0253 eV, b/atom): 296K 4.5514, 400K 4.3731, 500K 4.2049, 600K 4.0418, 700K 3.8849, 800K 3.7344, 1000K 3.4529, 1200K 3.1968, 1600K 2.7529, 2000K 2.3871 - strictly decreasing (Debye-Waller), 48% suppression 296->2000K. Interpolated 523.15K = 4.1672 in (4.0418,4.2049); 393.15K = 4.3849 in (4.3731,4.5514); 293.15K snaps to 296K within tolerance and reports it. NOTE also found+fixed: endf::interp::terp1 had ENDF laws 3 and 4 SWAPPED vs ENDF-102/upstream endf.f90 (needed because MT4 extras are LI=4 log-lin in T); reconr linearize midpoint arm + its test updated. 393 lib tests + 6/6 graphite V&V pass, release mode.

notes.content:
VERIFIED FIXED 2026-08-13. The defect described above is gone; the bead had simply not been closed.

EVIDENCE, from the current source rather than from docs:

title: root@vm
nuclear oil refinery — HTR-10 process heat into a refinery flowsheet
description:
Offline demonstration coupling a high-temperature gas-cooled reactor heat source to a petroleum refinery flowsheet, built from outram-park-fork-dwsim-libs unit operations plus an HTR-10 primary loop.

INTENDED USE: education, research, capability building and V&V only. Offline demonstration, no connection to any operational or plant system. See RESPONSIBLE_USE.md. Nothing here is for facility operation, licensing, or safety-critical decisions.

WHY THIS IS GROUNDED: nuclear process heat for refining is a real, openly published application area — HTR-10 was built in part as a process-heat demonstrator, and the INL/NGNP programme published HTGR-integrated refinery and hydrogen studies. Validation targets therefore exist in open literature at the BLOCK level, though no integrated nuclear-refinery plant exists to validate the whole flowsheet against. See the V&V child.

STARTING CAPABILITY (audited 2026-08-11):
HAVE — outram-park-fork-dwsim-libs carries a refinery-grade thermo layer with zero todo!(): Peng-Robinson/PR1978, PRSV2, Lee-Kesler-Ploecker, Chao-Seader-Grayson hydrocarbon K-values, black oil, sour water, inside-out flash (Boston-Britt), VLLE/LLE/SLE, Gibbs multiphase, and conversion/equilibrium/Gibbs/PFR/CSTR reactors. Also heater, cooler, heat_exchanger, compressor, expander, pump, valve, mixer, splitter, separator, pipe.
MISSING — no distillation column, no crude assay / pseudo-component characterisation, no flowsheet solver with recycle convergence, and no process-heat coupling unit op.

HEAT SOURCE CAVEAT — READ BEFORE CLAIMING ANYTHING: there is NO validated HTR-10 model in this workspace. docs/reactor-scoping/htr10.md (audit 2026-08-06) records that nothing HTR-10-specific is in the repository, the packed-bed Ergun pressure drop is a todo!(), pebble-bed effective radial conductivity has zero code, the solid database has no graphite, and the existing htgr_sim_v1 example is PRISMATIC, not a pebble bed. Do not describe the heat source as validated. This epic must either block on the HTR-10 core work or run against an explicitly labelled surrogate heat source.

title: refinery: DECISION — energy balance and temperature match, then pick the demonstration scope
description:
Gating scoping bead. Everything downstream depends on the answer, so do this before writing any flowsheet code.

THE PROBLEM: HTR-10 is 10 MWth. A modest crude distillation unit furnace is tens to a hundred MW. The reactor cannot run a whole refinery, so the honest deliverable is a bounded process-heat demonstration, not a plant.

WHAT TO ESTABLISH:
1. Heat demand curve of each candidate refinery duty (crude preheat, atmospheric furnace, reboilers, reformer) in MW and at what temperature.
2. Available helium outlet temperature and duty from the HTR-10 model, and what fraction of each duty it can actually supply.
3. Temperature match: HTR-10 helium outlet is high enough for crude heating by a wide margin, but steam reforming sits near the top of the range. State which duties are reachable and which are not.
4. Choose the demonstration scope explicitly. Options include a single reachable duty at true 10 MWth scale, a scaled multi-module plant, or a deliberately labelled scale-up. Whichever is chosen, the scale assumption must be stated in the simulator UI and docs, not buried.

ACCEPTANCE: a written energy and temperature balance with numbers, and one recorded decision on scope. No fabricated figures — derive from the model and cited open literature.

title: refinery: transient mode — port the DWSIM dynamics integrator and dynamic-mode execution
description:
The maintainer wants a TRANSIENT simulator; steady state is the baseline starting point, not the destination.

UPSTREAM EXISTS — correcting a common assumption: DWSIM is not steady-state-only. DWSIM.DynamicsManager (12 files, 972 lines) carries Integrator.vb, Schedule.vb, Event.vb, EventSet.vb, MonitoredVariable.vb and CauseAndEffectMatrix.vb, and DWSIM.FlowsheetSolver handles dynamic-mode execution. So this is a port with a reference, not a from-scratch design.

SCOPE: the integrator loop and its time stepping, the schedule and event model, monitored variables, and the dynamic-mode branch of the flowsheet execution order. The DynamicsManager itself is a thin orchestration layer — the actual transient behaviour comes from unit operations carrying holdup, which is a separate bead.

Steady-state solve remains the initial condition provider for every transient run.

title: refinery: dynamic unit-operation holdup and inventory — what actually makes it transient
description:
An integrator alone does not make a transient simulator. Transient behaviour comes from state that accumulates: mass, energy and momentum holdup inside vessels, drums, columns and pipes.

SCOPE: add inventory state to the unit operations that need it — separator and vessel liquid level, column stage holdup, pipe line-pack, heat-exchanger metal thermal mass — and integrate those states rather than solving them algebraically. Steady state must fall out as the zero-derivative limit, which is a directly testable property.

TEST THIS PROPERTY EXPLICITLY: a transient run started from the converged steady state and held at constant boundary conditions must stay at that state. Any drift is a conservation bug in the integrator or the holdup terms.

Depends on the flowsheet data model and the integrator.

title: refinery: pressure-flow network solve for dynamic mode
description:
In steady state, flows are specified. In dynamic mode, flows must be SOLVED from the pressure field, otherwise a valve closing changes nothing downstream and the simulator is not really transient.

SCOPE: a simultaneous pressure-flow network over the flowsheet graph, with the resistance of valves and pipes and the head of pumps and compressors, so that flow rate becomes a computed variable driven by pressure differences and inventory changes. This is what couples a valve stroke to a downstream response.

Relates to op-1z3o.5 (the steady-state sequential-modular solver) but is a different mathematical problem — simultaneous rather than sequential — so it deserves its own solve path.

Reference DWSIM dynamic mode for the formulation. Enum dispatch over element types, no trait objects.

title: refinery: real-time pacing and digital-twin engine integration
description:
Once the transient solver runs, decide whether the refinery is a batch transient study or a real-time interactive twin, and if the latter, wire it into crates/outram-park-digital-twin-engine alongside the reactor simulators.

The engine already provides widgets, animation, threading and an OPC-UA telemetry path. Note that op-xvye is an open P0 against the engine for pacing sign-collapse and u64 underflow in both simulation loops — fix or account for that before trusting real-time pacing.

Offline demonstration only. No connection to any live or operational system, per RESPONSIBLE_USE.md.

title: refinery: DECISION — real-time execution, which DWSIM dynamics does NOT give you
description:
MAINTAINER POINT, recorded 2026-08-11: porting the DWSIM dynamics gets a TRANSIENT simulator, not a REAL-TIME one. These are different problems and the port does not solve the second.

WHY: DWSIM Integrator.vb advances simulated time as fast or as slow as the solve happens to take. Each step calls flash and property evaluations of unbounded cost, and a stiff or poorly converging step can take arbitrarily long. Real-time requires bounded worst-case wall-clock per step, which nothing in the upstream provides.

WHAT MUST BE SETTLED:
1. Define the target. Soft real-time for an interactive twin (drop or interpolate on overrun) or hard bounded step. These have very different costs.
2. Measure first. Instrument the ported transient loop for per-step wall-clock, worst case not mean, before designing anything. op-fm5 is the precedent: a 28 us/step plateau was MEASURED in TUAS and drove a rewrite to O(1) recurrences.
3. The likely cost centres are flash calls in the inner loop and the recycle/pressure-flow convergence iteration count, both of which are unbounded by construction.
4. Candidate strategies, to be chosen on evidence not assumption: cache or tabulate property evaluations, fix the iteration budget and carry the residual forward, precompute reduced-order surrogates for slow blocks, or run the rigorous model off the real-time thread and pace a reduced model against it.
5. See docs/real-time-multifidelity-scoping.md, which already frames the multi-fidelity approach for this workspace.

ACCEPTANCE: a measured per-step cost distribution from the actual ported loop, a stated real-time target, and one recorded decision on strategy. Do not claim real-time capability without a measured worst-case number.

title: shortcut column follow-ups: one-composition K-value entry + promote mixture liquid density
description:
Follow-ups from the ShortcutColumn port (src/columns/shortcut.rs, ported 2026-08-11 from DWSIM ShortcutColumn.vb @ 1abf72d1b6b41d3e9a8cc770d3cc4e8fc76e5766, 9/9 tests green in release, Android check clean).

1. PropertyPackageModel has no one-composition K-value form. Upstream calls DW_CalcKvalue(z, T, P) (ShortcutColumn.vb:201); the port approximates it with ColumnThermo::k_values(z, z, T, P) — exact for Ideal, first-order for cubics. Add a K(z, T, P) entry to the package enum and switch the shortcut (and any future caller) to it.

2. Mixture liquid density (upstream AUX_LIQDENS Rackett route, PropertyPackage.vb:7674) is implemented inline in the shortcut sizing block via Kay's-rule pseudo-criticals into petroleum::aux_props::liquid_density_rackett. Promote a package-level liquid-density entry into crate::thermo so shortcut sizing, pump NPSH inputs, etc. share one implementation.

3. (Optional, NOT upstream) Kirkbride feed-stage correlation as an alternative to the ported Fenske-ratio method — only if a design comparison is wanted; the port is deliberately faithful to upstream, which uses the Fenske ratio (ShortcutColumn.vb:512-519).

title: refinery: scoping doc docs/reactor-scoping/nuclear-refinery.md
description:
Write the scoping document in the same shape as docs/reactor-scoping/htr10.md and msre.md: framing, plant configuration, capability audit split into HAVE / SCAFFOLD / MISSING, open validation data with access tier, recommended sequencing, and open questions for the maintainer.

Must record the open-literature basis for nuclear process heat in refining, with provenance per DATA_POLICY.md: source, author/organisation, title, licence/access terms, URL or DOI, date accessed. Candidate open sources include the INL/NGNP HTGR-integrated refinery and hydrogen-production studies and the published HTR-10 process-heat demonstration intent.

DO NOT assert report numbers, identifiers or measured values that have not been read from the actual documents. Mark anything unverified as unverified, exactly as htr10.md does.

title: refinery: crude assay and pseudo-component characterisation in dwsim-libs
description:
No refinery flowsheet can exist without this. A crude oil is not a component list, it is a boiling curve that must be cut into pseudo-components.

SCOPE: true-boiling-point curve input, cut into pseudo-components with normal boiling point, specific gravity and molecular weight; correlations for critical properties and acentric factor from Tb and SG; hooking the resulting pseudo-components into the existing property_package so they flow through flash and the K-value methods.

FITS WHAT EXISTS: crates/outram-park-fork-dwsim-libs/src/thermo/ already carries chao_seader_grayson.rs (hydrocarbon K-values) and black_oil.rs, both of which want pseudo-components as input. This bead supplies them.

Document every correlation with its source and stated range of validity per the human-interface rule. uom types on all public signatures.

title: refinery: rigorous distillation column (MESH equations, inside-out) in dwsim-libs
description:
The single largest missing unit operation. crates/outram-park-fork-dwsim-libs/src/ has heater, cooler, heat_exchanger, compressor, expander, pump, valve, mixer, splitter, separator, pipe and reactors — but no column.

SCOPE: multi-stage vapour-liquid column solving the MESH equations (material balance, equilibrium, summation, enthalpy balance), with condenser and reboiler, multiple feeds, side draws and pumparounds. Prefer the inside-out algorithm to reuse the existing flash_insideout.rs machinery rather than writing a new solver from scratch.

V&V per the workspace rule — methodology AND results: validate against a published test problem from the open distillation literature with the reference numbers, tolerances and the measured outcome recorded in the test doc comment.

Enum dispatch for column variants, no trait objects, no Box, no lifetime parameters.

title: refinery: flowsheet solver — sequential-modular execution with recycle convergence
description:
dwsim-libs has unit operations but no engine to connect them. A refinery is defined by its recycles (hydrogen recycle, pumparounds, stripper returns), so a flowsheet without recycle convergence is not a refinery.

SCOPE: material and energy stream types, a unit-operation enum covering the existing blocks, execution ordering with cycle detection, tear-stream selection, and an accelerated successive-substitution convergence loop (Wegstein or equivalent) with reportable residuals and iteration limits.

DESIGN RULES: unit operations dispatch through an enum, not Box<dyn>, so adding a block is a compile error at every match site. No lifetime parameters — share the property package with Arc.

ACCEPTANCE: a small flowsheet with a real recycle converges to a stated tolerance, with the residual history available for inspection rather than a silent converged/not-converged boolean.

title: refinery: nuclear process heater — the helium-to-process coupling unit operation
description:
THE actual nuclear part of this project. Replaces a fired furnace with a heat exchanger whose hot side is reactor helium.

SCOPE: a unit operation taking helium inlet temperature, pressure and mass flow on the hot side and a process stream on the cold side, returning duty and both outlet states, with a real pinch check so the model cannot silently transfer heat up a temperature gradient. Reuse the LMTD and NTU algebra already in dwsim-libs heat_exchanger; helium properties come from crates/outram-park-fork-coolprop (full Helmholtz EOS plus real transport correlations, already tested).

SAFETY-RELEVANT MODELLING NOTE for the docs: a real coupling would need an intermediate loop and tritium-permeation and pressure-boundary considerations between reactor and hydrocarbon process. This is an offline demonstration and models none of that. State that limitation explicitly rather than implying a deployable design.

Blocks on the scope decision (op-1z3o.1) and on a heat source existing at all.

title: refinery: steam-methane reformer as a Gibbs equilibrium block for hydrogen
description:
The classic HTGR process-heat application and the highest-temperature duty in the flowsheet, so it is the interesting stress case for the temperature match.

SCOPE: wire crates/outram-park-fork-dwsim-libs/src/reactors/gibbs_reactor.rs to a reforming feed, with the reformer duty supplied by the nuclear process heater rather than by burning fuel gas. Report approach to equilibrium, methane conversion and hydrogen yield as functions of temperature, pressure and steam-to-carbon ratio.

V&V per the workspace rule: validate the equilibrium composition against published equilibrium data or an independent equilibrium calculation, and record the actual numbers with tolerances in the test doc comment. Do not report a yield that was not produced by running the model.

Depends on the reformer being reachable at the available helium outlet temperature — see op-1z3o.1.

title: refinery: hydrotreater block consuming the reformer hydrogen
description:
Closes the loop between the hydrogen plant and the refinery, and gives the hydrogen recycle that makes the flowsheet solver earn its keep.

SCOPE: a conversion or equilibrium reactor block for hydrodesulphurisation duty using the existing conversion_reactor.rs / equilibrium_reactor.rs, fed by makeup hydrogen from the reformer plus a recycle stream, with a separator and recycle compressor closing the gas loop. Sour water and hydrogen sulphide handling can lean on the existing sour_water.rs property package.

Reaction stoichiometry and conversion data must come from open published sources with provenance recorded per DATA_POLICY.md. Kinetics may be lumped — say so in the doc comment rather than implying a mechanistic model.

title: refinery: V&V plan — what each block is validated against, and what cannot be validated
description:
Per VERIFICATION_AND_VALIDATION.md and the CLAUDE.md rule that V&V documentation must carry BOTH methodology and measured results.

THE HONEST POSITION: no integrated nuclear-refinery plant exists, so the whole flowsheet cannot be validated end to end. Validation is therefore per block, plus conservation checks on the assembly. Say this plainly in the docs instead of implying plant-level validation.

PER-BLOCK TARGETS: distillation column against a published test problem from the open separations literature; flash and property packages against the existing dwsim-libs test suite and published phase-equilibrium data; reformer against published equilibrium composition data; heat exchanger against LMTD/NTU analytical cases.
ASSEMBLY-LEVEL CHECKS: mass and energy closure across the converged flowsheet to a stated tolerance, and a pinch check proving no heat flows up a temperature gradient.
HEAT SOURCE: inherits the HTR-10 V&V status, which is currently nothing. Until the pebble-bed closures are validated, every result carries an explicitly labelled unvalidated heat source.

Record measured numbers with uncertainty and the date taken. Never report a result that was not produced by running the check.

title: tampines-steam-tables — IAPWS-IF97 + steam turbine + choked flow
description: In-house IAPWS-IF97 steam/water properties with uom units, steam-turbine + converging-diverging nozzle equations incl. choked (HEM) two-phase flow, FHR secondary-loop simulator. GPL-3.0.

notes.content: Provenance (2026-07-08): tampines-steam-tables is the user's own IAPWS-IF97 implementation -- inspired by rust-steam early on but that was abandoned. Not a fork; excluded from the trademark-compliance renames (op-ahi.7 closed: no rename).
notes.author: teddy0@snrsi-arch-desktop

title: Choked-flow (HEM) multiphase critical-flow solvers
description: Unified dispatcher + in-dome / subcooled / superheated-vapour solvers, validated vs Moody(1975), Zaloudek, Marviken. All stagnation buckets + the near-bubble-point x~0 artifact fixed. Only known discrepancy: isobar_pref_0_25 (p0=1.72 bar) #[ignore]d (IAPWS isentrope vs incompressible-Bernoulli at extreme pressure ratio).

title: Wire real IAPWS-IF97 (p,h) flash into TampinesSteamArray::correct_thermo()
description: Follow-up to op-21g.9 (which extended TampinesSteamArray with the OPCPFluidArray-like lateral-coupling/geometry/flow-bookkeeping interface but left correct_thermo()'s placeholder rho=psi*p EOS untouched, flagged as a separate task). User asked to do this next in the same session (2026-07-13).

title: Harden TampinesSteamArray::correct_thermo() against out-of-range (p,h) panics
description:
TampinesSteamArray::correct_thermo() (crates/tampines-steam-tables/src/openfoam_algorithms/rhoPimpleFoam/mod.rs, from op-21g.10) calls t_ph_eqm/v_ph_eqm/kappa_t_ph_eqm/mu_ph_eqm/lambda_ph_eqm/cp_ph_eqm directly per cell -- these PANIC (not Result) if (p,h) falls out of the valid IAPWS-IF97 range (e.g. below 273.15K), unlike OPCPFluidArray::correct_thermo() (outram-park-fork-coolprop), which does 'if let Ok(state) = flash::state_ph(...) { update } else { keep previous rho/T/psi for this cell }' -- a graceful degradation, not a panic, if a cell wanders out of range mid-simulation.

Fix direction (not yet decided/implemented): either (a) wrap the tampines-steam-tables (p,h) flash calls in a fallible variant if one exists or can be added, matching CoolProp's graceful-degradation pattern, or (b) some other guard against out-of-range panics during a running PIMPLE loop.

User explicitly deferred this (2026-07-13) -- wants to check the situation manually first before any fix is attempted. Do not implement without further discussion.

title: TampinesSteamArray::step() pressure oscillation with nonzero inlet velocity BC
description: Discovered 2026-07-14 while building set_inlet_velocity/set_inlet_enthalpy/set_outlet_pressure BC setters for TampinesSteamArray (lateral_coupling.rs), in service of wiring TampinesSteamArray into fhr_sim_v2's steam generator tube. First real exercise anywhere in the crate of step()'s pressure-velocity (PISO) coupling under a nonzero Dirichlet velocity BC -- every prior test uses default zero-gradient/passive BCs or drives he alone via set_temperature_vector. Reproduction: 10-cell, 1m pipe, 1e-4 m^2 area, dt=5e-5s (acoustically stable per dx/c_sound), pre-conditioned near 370K/1bar, then inlet velocity=0.5 m/s + inlet enthalpy=4.2e5 J/kg + outlet pressure=1e5 Pa fixed. Pressure develops a large non-physical oscillation within ~10 steps (ranging ~1e5 to ~9e5 Pa across cells against a fixed 1e5 Pa outlet BC and modest inflow -- nothing in the setup should drive a 9x pressure excursion) and panics out of the valid IAPWS-IF97 range by step ~27 (see ph_flash_eqm check_if_within_ph_validity_region). Kept as an #[ignore]d regression test: openfoam_algorithms::rhoPimpleFoam::lateral_coupling::tests::inlet_outlet_bcs_drive_flow_and_outlet_pressure_settles_near_imposed_value. Suspect the source_p boundary-flux special case for BoundaryCondition::FixedValue velocity (mod.rs step(), the 'match self.u.boundary[pi].bc' block) but not confirmed -- root-causing the PISO instability was out of scope for that session. Blocks: op-21g.6 (multiphase suite work that might build on this) is unaffected, but any consumer wanting to drive TampinesSteamArray as a prescribed-BC pipe (e.g. tampines fhr_sim_v2's steam generator tube) is blocked until this is fixed.

notes.content:
2026-07-14 follow-up: root-caused and fixed one real bug (phi_hbya boundary write-back missing for FixedValue velocity patches in mod.rs step() -- self.phi kept HbyA's always-zero-gradient boundary extrapolation instead of the corrected flux used in the pressure source, corrupting the next step's rhoEqn continuity). Also added the user-requested SIMPLE/PISO/PIMPLE infrastructure: get/set_n_outer_correctors, get/set_n_inner_correctors, get/set_pressure_under_relaxation, get/set_velocity_under_relaxation, and set_piso_algorithm/set_simple_algorithm/set_pimple_algorithm presets (mod.rs). With SIMPLE + heavy under-relaxation (alpha_p=0.02, alpha_u=0.3) and staying well clear of the saturation boundary, the pressure oscillation is much better behaved (bounded ~25% swing surviving 40+ iterations, vs a 9x blowup crashing by iteration 27 before the fix) but NOT fully resolved -- temperature still drifts upward and eventually exceeds the 1073.15K validity ceiling; the energy equation's stability under residual pressure noise was not root-caused. Separately (not the same run, found by moving inlet enthalpy near h_f at 1 bar): correct_thermo's (p,h) region classification and thermal_conductivity's internal (T,p) re-classification can disagree right at the saturation boundary, hitting pt_flash_eqm::cp_tp_eqm_single_phase's FwdEqnRegion::Region4 => todo!() panic -- this would block real steam-generator (boiling) use regardless of the pressure-oscillation outcome. All three findings documented in the (still #[ignore]d) regression test inlet_outlet_bcs_drive_flow_and_outlet_pressure_settles_near_imposed_value's doc comment. Net: real progress, but wiring TampinesSteamArray into a driven steam-generator-tube use case (e.g. fhr_sim_v2) remains blocked on findings 2 and 3.
2026-07-14: FINDING 3 (saturation-boundary todo!()) RESOLVED. lambda_ph_eqm's critical-enhancement term (thermal_conductivity::lambda_2_crit_enhancement_term_tp_two_phase_estimate) delegated cp/cv/kappa_t to single-phase (T,p) routines that todo!() in region 4 (T,p not independent on the saturation line). lambda_ph_eqm calls this for EVERY region (x=0 region1, x=1 region2/3, interior region4), so the fix branches: single-phase (x==0 or x==1) keeps the exact (t,p) single-phase values bit-for-bit (verified: the 53 single-phase steam-table lambda tests that a naive t_sat-everywhere version broke now all pass again); genuine two-phase (0<x<1) quality-weights the saturated region-1/region-2 values at t_sat, mirroring cp_ph_eqm's own region-4 handling. Two new verification tests (both pass): thermal_conductivity::tests::lambda_ph_two_phase_is_finite_and_bracketed (finite, positive, bracketed by sat vapour..liquid, monotonic in quality at 1 bar) and openfoam_algorithms::rhoPimpleFoam::tests::correct_thermo_survives_two_phase_boiling_cell (a TampinesSteamArray cell at 1 bar / h=1.5MJ/kg / x~0.48 survives correct_thermo, T~T_sat, all fields finite). Full suite 909 passed / 0 failed. This unblocks a boiling steam-generator-tube model. Remaining on this bead: the PISO/stiff-liquid pressure-oscillation robustness (findings 1-2) for driving TampinesSteamArray hard; the source-clobber root cause (separate) is already fixed + pushed in 540fd45.
2026-07-14: TampinesSteamArray WIRED into fhr_sim_v2's steam-generator tube (secondary_loop/mod.rs), replacing the lumped h_out=h_in+Q/mdot energy balance with the spatially-resolved (p,h) steam-table physics. Persistent array (build_steam_generator_tube), driven 25 acoustic-CFL substeps per TH step, outlet enthalpy read back to feed the turbine. New standalone validation test steam_generator_tube_boils_feedwater (feedwater 80degC -> boiling at 2 bar, x crosses 0 at step 5416, passes). New API set_uniform_velocity_field (pre-condition velocity to avoid water-hammer). Two integration bugs found + fixed (see tampines-steam-tables/docs/notes.md 'Correction log'): (1) default pressure floor was sat_pressure_4(273.15) EXACTLY -> clamped cells land on saturation line -> (p,h) validity guard's exact-equality Region-4 test todo!()-panics; fixed by nudging floor *1.001 into Region 1; (2) pre-init pressure (2 bar) mismatched operating outlet BC (1.2 bar) -> depressurisation rarefaction cooled a cell below 273.15K; fixed by matching pre-init to operating pressure. Live sim now runs 30s clean (0 panics), SG tube heats feedwater 90->97degC and warming. Maintainer guidance recorded: arrays use (p,h) flashing by default, not (T,p) single-phase. Remaining on this bead: the deeper stiff-liquid transient robustness (the array still panics if driven far outside its envelope, per the panic-on-out-of-range design) and enthalpy bounding as a future analogue to pressure bounding.
notes.author: teddy0@snrsi-arch-desktop
