title: TampinesSteamArray energy over-cooling under fast flashing (Edwards blowdown plateau under-predicted)
description:
The Edwards-O'Brien blowdown V&V test (tests/edwards_blowdown.rs) exposes an energy-conservation limitation in TampinesSteamArray::step(). During the violent subcooled->two-phase decompression the h-form energy equation loses ~10x more enthalpy than the reversible dh=dp/rho, so the bulk liquid drops to subcooled and only flashes near ambient instead of holding the ~350-380 psia (p_sat at T0~505K) flashing plateau. Measured GS-1 plateau ~17 psia vs experimental ~350-367 psia; GS-1 pressure RMSE vs digitised Data ~276 psia.

Root cause: step() runs the explicit rhoEqn continuity rho = rho_old - dt*div(phi), but correct_thermo then OVERWRITES rho with the EOS (p,h) density each inner correction. That breaks the discrete cancellation of the h*div(phi) term in d(rho h)/dt + div(phi h) = dp/dt, so enthalpy is not conserved through a fast density change. Reducing dt (30us->10us) does not fix the ratio; it is structural.

NOTE: this is the ACCURACY limitation only. The STABILITY question Ethan raised (explicit scheme cools empty pipe to ~1C and pressure rebounds past 0.42s) is CURED by our PIMPLE array: past 0.42s min T=358K, tail pressure rebound +0.9 psia, void stable 0.997 -- no artefact. See test doc comment for full V&V write-up.

Possible fixes to evaluate (need own V&V): (a) conservative (rho*e or rho*h) energy update using the continuity-consistent density rather than the EOS density in the ddt term; (b) an internal-energy (e) formulation; (c) sub-cycling the flash within the corrector. Do NOT loosen the test tolerance -- assertions there are sanity-only by design.

notes.content: RESOLVED 2026-07-16. Fixed with two coupled thermodynamic corrections (no clamps): (1) conservative energy ddt using the CONTINUITY density rho_cont = rho_old - dt*div(phi) rebuilt from the final mass flux (new fvm::ddt_coeff_old), so (rho_cont-rho_old)/dt = -div(phi) exactly and the h*div(phi) term cancels term-for-term against div(phi h), restoring rho Dh/Dt = dp/dt -- this is approach (a) from the bead; (2) pressure-eqn compressibility psi = d(rho)/dp|_h (central finite-diff of the (p,h) flash at fixed enthalpy) replacing the frozen quality-weighted isothermal rho*kappa_T, which was ~100x too small in the two-phase dome and let the pressure overshoot through the plateau. Results: GS-1 flashing plateau 17 -> 393 psia (target ~350-367); RMSE vs Data 276 -> 60 psia; stable full 600 ms; no non-physical subcooling (void grows gradually, fluid holds near p_sat). All 915 lib tests still green. See collaboration/edwards_tampines_regen/debug_log.md and tests/edwards_blowdown.rs doc comment. Residual: plateau ~8% high + shallow late decline (HEM-closure accuracy, separate from the missing-plateau failure).

notes.content: Maintainer (2026-07-16): this instability alone requires dedicated work — the hybrid smooths the ringing but the solver crashes past t~0.18s (empty-pipe two-phase near-sonic cell over-cools across the (p,h) validity edge). notes.author: teddy0@snrsiDesktop

notes.content: FIXED 2026-07-16. Root cause: not a physics limit of HEM but a numerical stiffness in the rarefied emptying tail. As the pipe empties past t~0.18s a cell rarefies in a localized runaway (rho 127->23->vacuum over ~350 steps); the conservative-EEqn diagonal rho_cont*V/dt collapses to its 1e-4 floor, the solve becomes ill-conditioned, and one step tips he from 951 kJ/kg to -7.3e6 kJ/kg -> below the 273.15K (p,h) edge -> panic. Both continuity and momentum KNP dissipation independently trigger it, so it is the explicit deferred correction being over-driven in the rarefied tail, not a sign error. Fix: rarefied-tail density taper on the KNP blend beta *= clamp((rho_face-50)/(100-50),0,1), rho_face=min(rho_o,rho_nb). Dissipation zero below 50 kg/m3 (rarefied -> pure PIMPLE, stable), full above 100. Measured min dissipated-face density over the 0-0.15s ringing window is 106.5 kg/m3, so the taper is inert there. Results: full 600ms HybridAllMach completes (no panic/NaN, void in [0,1]), plateau 387.7 psia, GS-1 RMSE 30.6 psia, no cold tail; 0-0.15s ringing -55.5% and plateau retained bit-identically; default Pimple bit-identical (920 lib tests pass). See collaboration/edwards_tampines_regen/hybrid_stability_debug_log.md + figures_hybrid_stable/. Not committed (maintainer commits).

IAPWS R7-97(2012), 'Revised Release on the IAPWS Industrial Formulation 1997', carries per-region verification tables. Free PDF from iapws.org.

title: V&V: two-phase frictional pressure drop — Thom (1964) / Martinelli-Nelson (1948)
description:
No steady-state two-phase pressure-drop validation exists for TampinesSteamArray / tampines::components::Pipe. Only the transient (Edwards-O'Brien) path is exercised.

Thom (1964) gives two-phase multipliers r2, r3, r4 for boiling water/steam tabulated by pressure; Martinelli & Nelson (1948) covers 0.1 MPa to critical. Both are steam-water-specific and recommended at secondary-loop pressures, unlike the air-water-rooted Lockhart-Martinelli (1949).

Per maintainer direction 2026-08-04, any ported correlation code lands as a MODULE under tampines/src/hem/ or beside TampinesSteamArray in openfoam_algorithms/rhoPimpleFoam/ — not a new crate.

Scope context: crates/tampines-steam-tables/docs/validation-scope-turbine-and-pipe.md section 4.1.

title: V&V: subcooled boiling void fraction — Bartolomei & Chanturiya (1967)
description:
Cross-sectionally averaged void fraction at axial stations in a vertical heated tube, upward flow. Range: p to 15 MPa, G to 2000 kg/m2/s, q to 2.2 MW/m2. Wall and subcooled liquid temperature available for one condition.

Citation: Bartolomej, G. G. & Chanturiya, V. M., 'Experimental study of true void fraction when boiling subcooled water in vertical tubes', Thermal Engineering 14 (1967) 123-128.

Access problem: the original Russian-journal paper is hard to obtain. The data is digitised in open-access validation papers, e.g. arXiv:1709.01783 (OpenFOAM two-phase boiling). Digitisation provenance MUST be recorded the way marviken_tests.rs records its graphreader points — which paper, which figure, which reader tool.

Scope context: crates/tampines-steam-tables/docs/validation-scope-turbine-and-pipe.md section 4.2.

title: V&V (diagnostic): wet-steam condensing nozzles — Moore B, Barschdorff
description:
Quantifies what the HEM assumption costs in the existing converging_diverging_nozzles module versus real non-equilibrium (supersaturated / Wilson-line) condensation.

The four standard benchmark supersonic nozzles are Moore B, Barschdorff, IWSEP and SUT de Laval, with measured axial static pressure distributions and fog-droplet sizes. Primary sources are old conference proceedings (Moore, Walters, Crane & Davidson 1973, IMechE C37/73; Barschdorff 1971; Moses & Stein; Gyarmathy), but digitised geometry and pressure data for all four appear in the OPEN-ACCESS paper 'Numerical analysis of non-equilibrium steam condensing flows in various Laval nozzles and cascades', Eng. Appl. Comput. Fluid Mech.

NOT a pass/fail gate — HEM is expected to miss the condensation shock. The deliverable is the quantified gap, for the paper's V&V section.

title: teddy0@snrsi-arch-desktop

title: htgr_sim_v1: the plant outer-corrector loop is NOT converged at 2 -- a third corrector moves the steam outlet 29.3 K
description:
Found 2026-08-14 while trimming the 1-corrector arm out of physics::tests::the_plant_outer_correctors_converge (maintainer instruction).

MEASURED, on the 60 s flow-ramp transient at the 0.1 s plant timestep, twice, deterministic:
  2 correctors : P = 1.77974 MW, T_out = 905.0576 K, T_bed = 905.4925 K, T_steam = 577.9498 K, Q = 7.00539 MW
  3 correctors : P = 1.78319 MW, T_out = 905.0436 K, T_bed = 905.4773 K, T_steam = 607.2434 K, Q = 6.98644 MW
  moved by     : dT_out = -0.014 K, dT_steam = +29.294 K, dQ = -0.271%

PLANT_OUTER_CORRECTORS' doc table records the 3-vs-2 step as dT_steam = -0.0007 K (measured 2026-08-13). It is now +29.29 K -- about four orders of magnitude larger, and in the opposite direction. The claim 'the loop has converged at 2' is false as things stand.

WHY NO TEST CAUGHT IT. The sweep is PRINTED, never asserted on. The only assertions in that test compare the 0.1 s 'shipped' leg against a 1 ms 'reference' leg, and BOTH legs run at PLANT_OUTER_CORRECTORS = 2 -- so a corrector-count error is common-mode between them and cancels exactly. Measured the same day, those two legs agree to dT_steam = -0.268 K and the test passes green. A timestep-refinement study cannot detect an unconverged corrector loop; only the sweep can, and nothing checks it.

THIS IS THE SAME SHAPE AS THE 2026-08-14 SECOND-LAW CATCH recorded in the crate CLAUDE.md: a number sitting in a passing test's printed output, in a doc comment, unasserted.

WHAT TO DO (maintainer decision, do not guess):
1. Find out WHAT CHANGED since 2026-08-13. The transient itself also moved (T_out 949.67 -> 905.06 K, T_steam 575.52 -> 577.95 K, P 12.17 -> 1.78 MW), so this is downstream of the kinetics coolant-sink work or the steam-generator changes, not a fresh regression in the corrector loop alone.
2. Decide whether PLANT_OUTER_CORRECTORS should rise, or whether the 29 K is itself the bug (a 29 K jump from one extra Picard sweep suggests the loop is diverging or bistable on the steam side, not merely under-converged -- note the duty moves only -0.27% while steam moves +5%).
3. ASSERT the sweep. Whatever the converged count turns out to be, the last step of the sweep must be checked against a tolerance, or this recurs silently.

Do NOT simply bump PLANT_OUTER_CORRECTORS to 3 -- nothing here shows 3 is converged either; the sweep stops there.

title: Derive by hand: TampinesSteamArray discrete energy-conservation formulation (for paper methods)
description: By-hand analytical derivation of the conservative energy discretisation that fixed the Edwards blowdown plateau collapse (op-21g.14). Author's own derivation for the paper methods (Phase II row A of the Edwards debug timeline table, outram_park_th_paper/src/index.tex). Derive: (1) from the integral energy conservation law, the discrete conservative ddt (rho*h - rho_old*h_old)/dt, and show the h*div(rho u) term cancels against discrete continuity (the cancellation the non-conservative rho*dh/dt form breaks, dropping a term ~ h*(rho-rho_old)/dt that over-drains enthalpy during flashing); (2) why the storage density must be continuity-consistent rho_cont = rho_old - dt*div(phi), not the EOS density; (3) the effective compressibility psi = drho/dp|_h and why frozen isothermal kappa_T is ~100x too small in the two-phase dome (omits flashing term) -- this psi produces the flashing plateau.
acceptance_criteria: Self-contained written derivation of conservative ddt + rho_cont + psi=drho/dp|_h, ready for the paper methods section.

title: TampinesSteamArray: set_inlet_enthalpy is ignored by the energy equation (blocks any advection-driven inlet)
description:
MEASURED 2026-08-12 in crates/outram-park-digital-twin-engine/examples/htgr_sim_v1.

SYMPTOM. TampinesSteamArray::set_inlet_enthalpy() has no effect on the solution. With a UNIFORM initial field the enthalpy field is bit-identical after 30000 step() calls, in BOTH directions:
  seed 523.15 K (he 1085.7 kJ/kg), inlet BC 168.7 kJ/kg -> he[0..8] all 1085.7 kJ/kg
  seed 523.15 K (he 1085.7 kJ/kg), inlet BC 3000.0 kJ/kg -> he[0..8] all 1085.7 kJ/kg
Setup: n=8, L=4 m, A=0.02 m2, p=4 MPa, set_pimple_algorithm(3,2,0.3,0.3), set_uniform_velocity_field(0.17 m/s), set_inlet_velocity(0.17 m/s), set_outlet_pressure(4 MPa), re-applied every step. 30 s simulated = ~1.3 tube transits.

NOT A TIMESTEP ISSUE. Swept dt = 1e-4, 5e-4, 2e-3, 6.25e-3, 1.25e-2 s, each for 30 s of simulated time (up to 300000 steps). Identical no-op at every dt. ~0.35 ms/step throughout.

CONVECTION ITSELF WORKS. Seeding a NON-uniform single-phase profile (cells 0-1 at 500 K, rest 400 K) and running at 0.17 m/s DOES advect the slug downstream (step 10000: peak at cells 2-3; step 20000: peak at cells 5-6). So the convection operator is live; it is specifically the inlet PATCH enthalpy that is not entering the energy equation. Consistent with the uniform-field result: a uniform field has zero internal convective change, so if the boundary term is ignored, nothing moves at all.

Also in that slug run, cell 0 relaxes to the BACKGROUND value (~401 K) rather than to the 500 K inlet BC, and downstream cells dip to 347 K, BELOW anything seeded -- so the boundary appears to contribute an unset/zero enthalpy rather than the value passed in.

CONTRAST: OPCPFluidArray (outram-park-fork-coolprop) DOES respond to the identical call sequence -- seeded 523.15 K, inlet BC 5067.6 kJ/kg (973 K helium), he[0] moved 2731.5 -> 3774.0 kJ/kg and the array reaches ~971 K uniform given enough simulated time. So the two sibling rhoPimpleFoam ports differ here; OPCP is the reference behaviour.

RELATED DEAD ENDS (both blocked for a boiling stream):
- writing he.internal[0] directly each step PANICS: 't,p flashing at eqm out of bounds!'
- set_temperature_vector() does a (p,T) flash, which panics on two-phase input, so it cannot impose a subcooled inlet on an array whose other cells are in the dome.

IMPACT. Blocks the 3-stream counter-flow steam generator (OPCPFluidArray <-> SolidColumn <-> TampinesSteamArray) for htgr_sim_v1 and fhr_sim_v2: the cold side cannot be given a feedwater inlet, so it has no axial temperature profile and the exchanger cannot be driven. Note fhr_sim_v2's existing use and the crate's own steam_generator_tube_boils_feedwater test both heat the array via lateral_link_new_power_vector and initialise it AT the inlet state, so neither exercises this path -- which is why it has gone unnoticed.

title: tampines-steam-tables: unconditional dbg! in production path h_tp_eqm_two_phase (Region 3)
description:
Found incidentally while doing op-uyi3 (2026-08-13). Not caused by that work and not fixed by it -- that session's file ownership was limited to steam_turbine_equations/.

crates/tampines-steam-tables/src/interfaces/functional_programming/pt_flash_eqm/multiphase_flashing.rs:176-177 has two UNCONDITIONAL dbg! calls on a production code path:

    dbg!(&near_critical_point);
    dbg!(&(near_saturation_line, h_liq, h_vap, h_saturated));

They fire from h_tp_eqm_two_phase whenever the Region 3 two-phase branch is taken, i.e. for any near-critical saturated-state property call, in release builds as well as debug. dbg! writes to stderr and is not gated by any feature or cfg.

Reproduction (observed): calling h_tp_eqm_two_phase(sat_temp_4(p0), p0, 0.0) and (.., 1.0) at p0 = 20 MPa emits four multi-line dbg! blocks to stderr, e.g.

  [.../multiphase_flashing.rs:176:13] &near_critical_point = false
  [.../multiphase_flashing.rs:177:13] &(near_saturation_line, h_liq, h_vap, h_saturated) = (
      true,
      1827100.5374104856 m^2 s^-2,
      ...

Note the line immediately above them is a dbg! that was already commented out, which suggests these two were meant to go the same way and were missed.

Impact: stderr noise in any consumer that touches near-critical saturation properties (the FHR simulator examples, TampinesSteamArray, any transient near the critical point), plus a real per-call formatting cost on a hot property path. It also pollutes test output, which is how it was noticed.

Fix: delete both lines, or gate them behind a feature/cfg(debug_assertions) if they are still wanted for diagnosis. Worth grepping the crate for other unconditional dbg!/println! on property paths at the same time -- choked_flow/mod.rs's get_critical_pressure_and_mass_flux_with_stagnation_props already carries a hard-coded debug=true flag that its own doc comment flags as a WIP artefact.

title: pflotran: 26.4k LOC written without upstream; licence never verified (provenance)
description:
PROVENANCE / RESEARCH-INTEGRITY issue under RESEARCH_INTEGRITY_AND_PROVENANCE.md.

crates/outram-park-fork-pflotran is 26,409 lines across 47 .rs files, written WITHOUT ever obtaining the upstream PFLOTRAN source.

Evidence:
- NOTICE:19-25 admits it outright: "LICENSE PROVENANCE -- VERIFY BEFORE PUBLISH. The LGPL-2.1-or-later determination above was taken from the PFLOTRAN documentation and the OSTI/DOECODE records (2026-07-20), not from a byte-for-byte reading of the upstream LICENSE/COPYRIGHT file (which was not reachable from this environment)."
- No upstream clone exists on this machine. /home/teddy0/Documents/research/ has openfoam, openmc, NJOY2016, dwsim, ThermoSysPro -- no pflotran. A find over the filesystem returns only /usr/include/paraview/vtkVisItPFLOTRANReader.h.
- upstream_source/ contains only README.md, which states "It holds no PFLOTRAN source yet".
- No .rs file in src/ carries a provenance header naming an upstream .F90 file, contrary to the workspace attribution rule.

WHY THE GAP IS LOAD-BEARING: the GPL-3.0-only relicensing relies on LGPL-2.1 section 3, which only works if upstream really is LGPL-2.1-OR-LATER and not a bare LGPL-2.1, LGPL-3.0, or a mixed-file situation. Nobody has read the upstream LICENSE/COPYRIGHT.

SECOND, SEPARATE CONTRADICTION: NOTICE:27-28 says "No PFLOTRAN source has been ported into this crate yet -- it is a documented scaffold", while README.md:55-61 describes RICHARDS flow, transport, energy, geochemistry, kinetics, reactive transport and multiphase as "real (verif-only)" with a 114-test suite. Root Cargo.toml:25-27 and workspace CLAUDE.md also still call it a scaffold. Either 26k LOC was written without upstream -- in which case "fork/translation of PFLOTRAN" is the wrong framing and the crate should be renamed/reframed as an independent implementation informed by published equations -- or code WAS derived and the per-file attribution is missing.

Note README.md:122 marks the provenance bead op-v6s.1 as "done (verify upstream before publish)" -- that should not read as done.

REQUIRED before this crate is published or described as a PFLOTRAN fork:
1. Obtain a PFLOTRAN clone and read LICENSE/COPYRIGHT byte-for-byte; record it in upstream_source/README.md.
2. Decide and state honestly whether this is a derived port (then add per-file provenance headers) or an independent implementation (then stop calling it a fork).
3. Reconcile NOTICE / README / root Cargo.toml / workspace CLAUDE.md so they agree.

Verified 2026-08-07 against the working tree.

title: DEM: history-free tangential contact prevents a true static packing
description:
Found while baking the pebble-packing artwork (crates/outram-park-fork-liggghts/examples/bake_pebble_packing.rs, 2026-08-06).

DemSimulation carries no accumulated tangential spring displacement between steps (documented in simulation.rs 'Honest scope'), so the tangential force is a Coulomb-capped dashpot only. Consequence: there is NO STATIC FRICTION. A grain resting on an inclined contact always creeps at a small terminal velocity, and a settled bed can never reach a strict zero-velocity rest state.

Measured evidence from the bake (2525 spheres, 74000 steps, dt=1e-4 s, dynamic-relaxation quench with the velocity field zeroed every 200 steps):
  - creep over two back-to-back 0.50 s windows: rms 4.18 % then 3.72 % of a pebble radius; max 16.6 % then 20.2 %. Steady, not decaying -> a floor, not an unfinished transient.
  - local solid fraction over the same windows: 0.6069, 0.6101, 0.6112 -> the packing STRUCTURE is stable even though grains keep creeping.
  - ensemble kinetic energy likewise floors out (~3e-1 J for 2525 pebbles) because the quench removes momentum that gravity immediately restores.

Fix: add per-contact tangential history state (the accumulated spring displacement xi_t, keyed by particle pair and carried across steps) so a resting contact can sustain a static tangential force. That also unlocks angle-of-repose verification, which is the standard DEM validation case for friction and is currently impossible.

Also worth having once that lands: a cone/frustum Boundary variant. The bake had to approximate the conical vessel bottom with 32 inscribed flat Wall half-spaces.

notes.content:
MAINTAINER'S CALL, 2026-08-06: not a blocker, and not to be treated stringently for artwork purposes.

The packing baked in crates/outram-park-digital-twin-engine/src/components/pebble_packing.rs is ARTWORK. Its structure is settled — solid fraction stable at 0.6069 / 0.6101 / 0.6112 across measurement windows, against ~0.61 for a real pebble bed — and that is the only property the drawing depends on. The residual creep (rms ~4% of a pebble radius, steady rather than decaying) does not affect how it looks.

So: DO NOT re-run, re-settle, post-process or otherwise chase equilibrium for the sake of the widgets. Use the bake as-is.

This bead stays open because the underlying limitation is REAL and would matter if the DEM is ever used for physics rather than pictures: simulation.rs's tangential contact is history-free (a Coulomb-capped dashpot with no accumulated tangential spring), so there is no static friction and a grain on an inclined contact creeps indefinitely. Strict rest is unreachable. That is worth fixing when someone wants granular DEM results, not before.

Dropped to reflect that it gates nothing currently in flight. The honest caveat in the module doc STAYS — documenting the limitation costs nothing and prevents the packing being cited later as a settled-equilibrium result. Documenting it is not the same as being stringent about it.
notes.author: teddy0@snrsi-arch-desktop

notes.content:
MAINTAINER'S DECISION, 2026-08-12: keep the DEM bake for the vessel artwork. 'some creep is okay.'

Context — a third packing option arrived on develop today: crates/outram-mc-libs/src/pebble_beds/crp_packing.rs, a Jodrey-Tory close-random-packing generator measured at 0.5796 realized packing fraction (N = 1107). The three now coexist:

  RSA (sphere_packing.rs)      ~0.38 ceiling   too loose for a pebble bed
  Jodrey-Tory (crp_packing.rs) 0.5796 measured  fills a domain to a target fraction
  DEM bake (pebble_packing.rs) 0.6112 measured  gravity-settled in the real barrel+cone

The DEM bake stays because it is both DENSER and more PHYSICAL for this purpose: it settles under gravity into the actual vessel geometry, which is what makes the bed rest on the cone and taper into the chute. Jodrey-Tory has no gravity, so it would not reproduce that structure — it is the better tool for TRANSPORT geometry, where a target fraction in a simple domain is what you want.

So: do not swap the artwork to CRP, and do not re-run the DEM chasing equilibrium. This bead stays open only for the underlying engine limitation (history-free tangential contact, no static friction), which matters if the DEM is ever used for granular physics rather than pictures.

OPCPFluidArray: set_inlet_enthalpy was a one-shot -- the energy solve discarded the BC (FIXED)
description:
MEASURED AND FIXED 2026-08-12 in crates/outram-park-fork-coolprop.

RELATED TO op-289n but NOT the same defect. op-289n records that TampinesSteamArray::set_inlet_enthalpy has no effect at all, and cites OPCPFluidArray as the healthy reference. Independent reproduction shows OPCP was NOT healthy either -- it merely LOOKED healthy because the reporting driver re-issued set_inlet_enthalpy() every step.

SYMPTOM. FvMatrix::solve builds its output VolScalarField with zero-gradient boundaries. step() captured and re-stamped the BC templates for u (correct_bcs_vec) and p (correct_bcs) but NOT for he, so 'self.he = he_new' after the energy solve silently discarded every prescribed enthalpy boundary. set_inlet_enthalpy therefore took effect on the first outer corrector after the call and never again.

MEASUREMENT (Nitrogen, 8 cells, 1 m, 1e-4 m2, 1 bar, PISO 2 correctors, dt 2e-4 s, inlet velocity 0.5 m/s, outlet p 1 bar; uniform seed differing from the inlet BC; BC applied ONCE).
  seed 300 K (h 311.20 kJ/kg), inlet BC 520.45 kJ/kg:
    pre-fix,  2000 steps: he[0] = 311.48 kJ/kg  (0.13 % of the 209.25 kJ/kg gap)
    pre-fix, 10000 steps: no cell more than 0.4 kJ/kg from the seed
    post-fix, 3000 steps: he[0] = 556.52 kJ/kg (117.2 % of gap), field mean 364.98 kJ/kg
  seed 500 K (h 520.45 kJ/kg), inlet BC 311.20 kJ/kg:
    pre-fix,  2000 steps: he[0] = 520.16 kJ/kg  (0.14 % of gap)
    post-fix, 3000 steps: he[0] = 296.13 kJ/kg (107.2 % of gap), field mean 444.68 kJ/kg
Post-fix, a run that re-applies the BC every step is bit-identical to one that applies it once -- so no existing caller's numbers move.

FIX. rhoPimpleFoam/mod.rs step(): capture he's BC template alongside u's and p's, and correct_bcs(&mut he_new, &he_bcs) after the energy solve.

REGRESSION TESTS (both directions, uniform field differing from the BC, BC applied once -- the blind spot op-289n identifies):
  lateral_coupling::tests::inlet_enthalpy_bc_heats_uniform_field_without_reapplying_each_step
  lateral_coupling::tests::inlet_enthalpy_bc_cools_uniform_field_without_reapplying_each_step

COORDINATION. tampines-steam-tables carries the same missing he BC re-stamp in its own step(); whoever fixes op-289n should apply the same capture/re-stamp there. It is probably NOT the whole story on that side: OPCP responded correctly to a per-step re-issue and TampinesSteamArray reportedly does not, so tampines has at least one further defect.

title: Scope: neutronics API for a Haiku agent (Gen-IV pebble bed + MSR multiphysics)
description:
Scoping only, no implementation claimed. gh:#41 https://github.com/theodoreOnzGit/outram-park-backend/issues/41 — the issue carries the full write-up; this bead is the tracker entry and the short form.

Applies the CLAUDE.md standing rule ('if it is too complex for Haiku, it is a bad API') to the neutronics crates, asked the design way round: not what have we exposed, but what would a Gen-IV researcher want a small agent to DO, and what is the shortest API that allows it.

WHAT EXISTS (surveyed 2026-09-04, not assumed). CE+MG Monte Carlo on arbitrary CSG and TRISO builders with into_geometry (outram-mc-libs); CRP pebble packing, delta tracking, keff-delta (outram-mc-libs::pebble_beds); depletion chain/CRAM/burnup matrix (outram-mc-libs::depletion, outram-park-fork-onix); TRISO fission-product release (boon-lay ATOPS); point kinetics, decay heat, Doppler and control-rod feedback, Nordheim-Fuchs (teh-o-prke); nodal diffusion (bedok); diffusion/SP3/SN/point-kinetics on FvMesh (outram-foam-appbuilder-lib::genfoam::neutronics); circulating fuel, precursor drift, salt thermal and a coupled solver (outram-park-fork-moltres); packed-bed TH via KTA/ZBS (tampines::pebble_bed); sensitivity and surrogates (raffles). The gap is not physics.

THE GAP, MEASURED. Same signature as the MC/NJOY dogfooding — data model exposed, execution hidden — and the class:function ratio is the tell: onix 10 classes / 1 function; moltres 14 / 1; mc-libs 152 / 42; teh-o-prke 12 / 7.

Confirmed missing from the wheel today:
  * outram_mc_libs: BurnupMatrix, DepletionOperator — no depletion from Python at all
  * outram_park_fork_onix: DepletionDriver, Chain — driver seam hidden
  * teh_o_prke: NordheimFuchs — the prompt-excursion path, the defining PBR/MSR reactivity transient

moltres is the happy exception: CoupledMsrSolver, CirculatingFuelSolver, PrecursorDrift, RingMesh all reach Python. Copy it, do not fix it.

THE 14 TASKS. Pebble bed: single-pebble then packed-bed k-eff (double heterogeneity); Doppler coefficient; moderator temperature coefficient; burnup through a pass; TRISO fission-product release at temperature; decay heat after scram (works today — keep as the tier-1 exemplar); prompt excursion (blocked); coupled neutronics + packed-bed TH. MSR: salt-cylinder k-eff; precursor drift vs circulation time (the MSR-defining effect); coupled neutronics-thermal; salt temperature/density coefficient; loss-of-flow transient; online refuelling depletion (blocked).

Test for each: can it be written in ~10 lines against the wheel alone, no source access? If not, the API is the problem.

API SHAPE. Convenience CONSTRUCTORS returning the general type, not convenience runners that swallow the run. into_geometry() is the good example in this very crate; mc_keff_of_actinide_sphere is the trap. Each tier implemented over the next, so outgrowing tier 1 is reading one short function — outram-foam's run_case -> CaseRun -> solver ladder is the model.

DELIVERABLES. (1) this task list as the neutronics half of op-m2mj's harness; (2) ranked missing-seam list, depletion first since it blocks four of the fourteen; (3) tier-1 entry points for what is one call in research practice and is not one call here — Doppler coefficient, precursor-drift sweep, burnup curve.

NOT IN SCOPE. New physics; everything composes what exists. No V&V claimed — these are API-shape tasks and a script that runs is not a validated calculation.

notes.content:
ADDITION 2026-09-04: MGXS extraction, Monte Carlo -> genfoam group constants. Full text gh:#41.

The stochastic->deterministic seam, and what makes coupled multiphysics tractable at all: CE Monte Carlo cannot run inside a coupled transient, so pebble-bed and MSR simulation needs collapsed group constants a diffusion/SP3/SN solver can march.

SURVEYED. Nothing in the chain exists.

  1. No MGXS generation path. outram_mc_libs::physics::physics_mg defines Mgxs and MgxsLibrary and run_keff_mg consumes them, but Mgxs::new has NO call site outside its own definition. Every multigroup library here must be typed in by hand. The MC can use group constants and cannot produce them.
  2. No MGXS tallies. Generation needs flux and reaction-rate tallies binned by group and by zone/material plus a scatter matrix. None of those scores exist.
  3. The two MG representations are different types and nothing converts between them. outram_mc_libs::Mgxs is transport-flavoured (total, scatter matrix, nu-fission, chi); genfoam::xs::GroupConstants is diffusion-flavoured (diffusion_coefficient in m, nu_sigma_f, sigma_pow = kappa-Sigma_f in J/m, sigma_removal, chi_prompt, chi_delayed).

So this is three steps, and the third carries real physics: D = 1/(3 Sigma_tr), removal = absorption + out-scatter, and a prompt/delayed chi split needing delayed-neutron data the transport-side Mgxs does not carry.

THE DETAIL THAT SHAPES IT. genfoam::xs::NuclearDataOneEnergy already exposes get(parameters, is_parametrize) with a poly_spline_mode — genfoam ALREADY supports cross sections parametrised on state. So the deliverable is not one library at one state point; it is XS tables over temperature, density and (pebble bed) burnup. That is what the multiphysics needs, because Doppler feedback is the point: a coupled transient re-evaluates group constants as fuel temperature moves and a single-state library cannot express it. The consumer anticipated this; the producer does not exist.

SCOPE. (1) MGXS tallies in outram-mc-libs — flux, absorption, nu-fission, kappa-fission, scatter matrix, by group and by zone/material; this is load-bearing, the rest is arithmetic. (2) Flux-weighted collapse to Mgxs, asserted with the existing Mgxs::consistency_residual. (3) Bridge Mgxs -> GroupConstants, DOCUMENTING the diffusion-coefficient convention chosen (transport-corrected vs out-scatter) — silently picking one is how a deterministic solution quietly disagrees with its MC reference. (4) Parametrised libraries over a state grid, emitted in the NuclearDataOneEnergy spline form. (5) Verification: k-eff from CE MC, then run_keff_mg on the collapsed library, then genfoam diffusion on the bridged constants, same geometry. Agreement within statistics is the test; disagreement localises to the step that caused it.

title: htgr_sim_v1: time-acceleration control -- spend the 4.101x buffer instead of sleeping it away
description:
Suggested 2026-08-13 after the maintainer observed the sim 'takes insanely long to cool down'. Not yet assigned.

THE OBSERVATION IS CORRECT AND MOSTLY REAL PHYSICS. The pebble bed dominates: C = 5282.78 kg x 1700 J/(kg K) =
8.98 MJ/K against hA = 48.86 kW/K, giving tau = 183.81 s analytical and 183.75 s measured (0.03% low). So roughly
three minutes per time constant and ~15 minutes of simulated time to substantially cool. That falls out of the
published pebble count, diameter and graphite density -- it is the HTR-10's defining safety characteristic, not a
modelling artefact. Everything else is fast by comparison: core gas 5 s, return transport 8 s, SG tube metal 39.78 s.

Note the model has NO decay heat at all (physics/mod.rs:45: 'the HTR-10 passive decay-heat path is absent
entirely'), so it already cools FASTER than a real plant would. Adding decay heat later will make this worse, not
better -- another reason to have the control.

THE AVOIDABLE PART. There is no time-acceleration control, and as of 2026-08-13 the simulator measures 4.101x real
time while the deadline pacer SLEEPS to hold it at 1:1. So a 15-minute cooldown costs 15 real minutes while ~75% of
the available compute is deliberately idled.

PROPOSAL: an operator speed control (1x / 2x / 4x, or a continuous multiplier) that mostly just reduces or removes
the pacer's sleep. The compute budget already exists; this is close to free.

DESIGN POINTS:
- Implement it in the PACER, not by changing the physics timestep. Growing dt would change the integration and the
  Courant numbers; the whole point is that the same integration runs faster in wall clock.
  crates/outram-park-digital-twin-engine/src/app_scaffold/real_time_pacing.rs is the place.
- CAP IT AT THE MEASURED HEADROOM and say so on screen. Asking for 8x when only 4.101x exists must degrade
  visibly -- the existing 'SLOWER THAN REAL TIME' readout already does exactly this and should be reused rather
  than duplicated.
- The achieved ratio is already measured and displayed on the schematic; the control should sit next to it.
- Re-measure the headroom when the machine is loaded: the 4.101x is an isolated-run figure and reads 0.56-0.64
  under full test-suite contention. A speed control that works only on an idle machine is a trap.
- Tracers are clocked off snapshot.sim_time_s delta (fixed 2026-08-13), so they should follow acceleration
  automatically. VERIFY that rather than assuming it.

Related: op-v5zb (deadline pacing, landed), op-3lay (the buffer work that created the headroom), op-szmi.5 (GUI
standard).

notes.content: Implemented as a boolean 'Fast forward' checkbox (Controls panel) rather than the proposed 1x/2x/4x discrete levels -- simpler, and the achieved-ratio readout (already on screen) shows exactly how much headroom is being spent, so a discrete multiplier selector wasn't needed. Implemented in the PACER as proposed: RealTimePacer::set_simulated_per_tick (real_time_pacing.rs) lets a caller batch a variable number of fixed-size plant.step() calls into one publish tick and keeps the cumulative bookkeeping (measured_real_time_ratio, real_time_deficit) exact -- new V&V test batched_ticks_match_the_same_number_of_fixed_ticks. htgr_sim_v1's physics thread bursts plant.step() calls for up to one PHYSICS_TICK (100ms) of wall clock when fast-forward is on, defensively capped at FAST_FORWARD_MAX_STEPS_PER_TICK, then publishes and repeats -- dt is never grown, so accuracy is unaffected at any speed. Headroom is re-measured live via the existing real-time-ratio readout, so it degrades visibly under load exactly as this issue asked. Landed alongside the GitHub issue #22 fix (op-56ix).

description: root@vm
title: root@vm
htgr_sim_v1: build real-time BUFFER -- 1.032 is too thin to ship
description:
MAINTAINER REQUEST, 2026-08-13: 'give me more buffer for real time simulation.'

WHERE WE ARE. Measured 2026-08-13 after op-6eqe: real-time ratio 1.032 in an ISOLATED release run (20 s of plant
time in 19.385 s wall). Under full test-suite load the same test reads 0.56-0.64. So the margin is ~3% on an idle
machine and NEGATIVE under contention. A GUI, a browser, or a second cargo build takes it under 1. It is not
shippable headroom.

WHERE THE TIME GOES -- this is the whole story:
  the steam generator is ~96% of the plant's compute (measured: SG alone 1.9585 compute/plant-s against 1.9469
  for the entire plant at a 0.1 s step). Everything else is noise. Optimise the SG or do not bother.

Also note the plant timestep is NOT a lever: the sweep measured 0.492 at 1 ms, 0.505 at 10 ms, 0.514 at 100 ms.
That road is already fully travelled -- do not re-run it.

THE LEVERS, biggest first:

1. op-j2oq -- IMPLICIT ENERGY ADVECTION (in flight, agent running).
   STEAM_GENERATOR_SUBSTEPS_PER_PLANT_STEP = 8 exists ONLY because explicit fvc::div_limited imposes a Courant
   limit (Co_hot = 0.222 at 0.0125 s, 1.776 at 0.1 s). Cost is exactly linear in substeps. If implicit advection
   lets that reach 1, that is up to 8x on the term that IS the cost. Nothing else on this list is close.
   => DO NOT START OPTIMISING UNTIL THIS LANDS. It changes the cost structure so completely that any profile
      taken now describes a program that will not exist.

2. PROPERTY EVALUATION -- likely the inner cost, but NOT YET MEASURED.
   The SG does IF97 flashes and CoolProp helium calls per node, per substep, per corrector. op-id3l.2 already
   exists for this: 'HTGR Phase 0.2: real-time helium fast path -- port CoolProp's TABULAR backends
   (TTSE/BICUBIC)'. A tabulated backend is the standard answer and the bead is already scoped.
   PROFILE FIRST. Do not assume it is the properties; measure the split between property calls, the matrix solve,
   and the corrector overhead.

3. NODE COUNT. 8 nodes, chosen for resolution not speed. Cost is linear in nodes. Check what accuracy actually
   costs here -- a 6-node exchanger may be indistinguishable in the settled duty.

4. Corrector counts are ALREADY minimised (4->2 array, 2 plant, both convergence-swept). No headroom left here;
   the sweep showed 2->3 moves core outlet -0.0013 K.

WHAT 'BUFFER' SHOULD MEAN -- decide the target before optimising:
  Propose a ratio of at least 2.0 measured the SAME way (the_whole_plant_steps_at_the_gui_timestep wall clock),
  so that a machine under load still clears 1.0. State the target in the bead before starting, and report the
  loaded figure as well as the isolated one -- the isolated number alone is what made 1.032 look adequate.

CONSTRAINTS: do not buy speed with silent accuracy loss. The current model is +0.822 K on steam outlet against the
1 ms reference already; any further degradation must be quantified and reported, not absorbed. Do not relax the
hot_enthalpy_clamp_events == 0 assertions to make something fit.

Depends on op-j2oq. Related: op-id3l.2 (tabular property backends), op-775s (closed, the original measurement).

notes.content:
MAINTAINER ARCHITECTURAL ANALYSIS + PROPOSED FALLBACK, 2026-08-13. Written up in full at
crates/outram-park-digital-twin-engine/docs/heat-exchanger-temperature-cross-fallback.md (DESIGN ONLY, not implemented).

THE DIAGNOSIS (maintainer's, and it is correct): 'across arrays, the coupling becomes explicit again. we should
expect temperature cross in that case.' The exchanger is THREE separate matrix systems -- hot array, tube metal,
cold array -- coupled through conductance terms at the previous iterate. Making convection implicit WITHIN an array
removes the intra-array Courant limit and does nothing for the inter-array coupling lag. So the 1-substep failure
is expected behaviour of an explicitly-coupled exchanger at a coarse coupling step, not a bug.

Measured with the helium side already implicit: 8 substeps -> ratio 1.027; 4 -> 2.051; 2 -> 4.101;
1 -> TEMPERATURE CROSS at physics/mod.rs:946, the second-law assertion, NOT a divergence of the helium array.

MONOLITHIC SOLVE REJECTED by the maintainer: 'a fully implicit solver would sort this out. albeit at a great cost as
I think it would wreck the entire matrix system. I don't really want that.' It would replace three cheap tridiagonal
solves with one large coupled system.

THE PROPOSED HEURISTIC -- adopt the steady-state temperature profile when a cross is observed, so thermodynamics is
not violated even though the transient differs:
  Tier 1: couple the two arrays DIRECTLY through an appropriate series thermal resistance, and set the metal to the
          temperature implied at that steady state rather than integrating it. (This is the Schur-complement
          elimination in concrete form -- the metal has no advection, so it is a per-node capacitance with two
          conductances and can be removed analytically, taking one full lag out of the coupling loop.)
  Tier 2: if a cross persists, compute steady-state outlet temperatures by LMTD and adjust both arrays' profiles to
          that LMTD-consistent profile.
  Invariant: the state handed to the next timestep must contain no temperature cross.

SIX CONCERNS RECORDED IN THE DOC, the first being the significant one:
  1. LMTD IS NOT VALID ACROSS A PHASE CHANGE, which is exactly where this exchanger lives. The cold side is
     feedwater -> steam through IF97; LMTD assumes constant cp, constant U and no phase transition. A single-zone
     LMTD across the boiling boundary will produce a confidently wrong profile. Standard fix is to ZONE the
     exchanger (subcooled / two-phase / superheat) with a per-zone U. Biggest technical risk in Tier 2.
  2. The fallback fires DURING transients -- precisely when the interesting dynamics are happening. Must be loud:
     counted, surfaced in the GUI, assertable in tests. Precedent: hot_enthalpy_clamp_events, currently zero
     everywhere and asserted == 0 in three tests.
  3. FIRST-LAW violation across the jump: overwriting both profiles changes stored energy discontinuously. Second
     law is respected pointwise; energy is not. Log the discrepancy per event and keep a running total.
  4. It can mask a genuine bug -- a cross at a substep count that should be fine is a bug signal, not a trigger.
  5. Chatter between fallback and transient integration; consider hysteresis or a minimum dwell.
  6. Cost must be measured. Tier 2 with zoning is not free and fires when the plant is already working hardest. If
     the fallback costs more than the substeps it saves, it is a net loss.

V&V FRAMING: results produced while the fallback is engaged are NOT a resolved transient and must never be presented
as one. Any validation claim against a measured transient is void for a run in which the fallback engaged.

NOT TRIED YET, on maintainer instruction ('don't try the correctors yet'): more INTER-ARRAY outer correctors. Worth
recording that the theory is favourable here in a way it is not for advection -- the inter-array Picard iteration's
contraction factor is roughly UA*dt/(m*cp), NOT the cell Courant number, so unlike the advective corrector loop it
can genuinely converge. Potentially cheaper than either tier.
notes.author: teddy0@arch-aftershock-rapid-glass-S267454

notes.content:
ALL THREE REMEDIES LANDED AND PUSHED 2026-08-13 (commit 3288145f on develop). Not wired in; default is None.

BEDOK ENTHALPY MARCH (Than Yan Ren, credited in the module doc with the singleflow1devap.m source and BEDOK snapshot):
  VERIFIED against a closed-form eps-NTU single-phase case -- hot outlet 0.135 K (0.086% of span), cold outlet
  0.011 K (0.033%), duty +0.086%. Boiling handled with NO zoning: 3 subcooled / 4 saturated / 1 superheated node
  simultaneously. Cost ~425 us per repair = 3.4% of one SG substep, which answers concern 6 of the design note --
  it fits the real-time budget comfortably. Two-point boundary problem solved by Illinois regula falsi bracketed
  between the two thermodynamic limits (never steps where the (p,h) flash has no answer), 5-9 iterations to
  1e-13..3e-7 K. Found and fixed a genuine defect: the hot capacity-rate inference divided by the drop to the last
  CELL CENTRE rather than the outlet FACE, a +5.97% bias walking the state 14.3 K hot / 38.7 K cold per engagement;
  after the closed-form correction the repair is a fixed point of itself to 7.8e-10.
  => ON THE MEASUREMENTS THIS IS THE BEST OF THE THREE. It is the only one with an analytic verification, the only
     one that handles phase change without zoning, and the cheapest.

ZONED LMTD: clears crosses (5.000 -> 0.000 K; 76.850 -> 0.000 K on 8 nodes), zones pinned at IF97 h_f/h_g with
  nothing fitted, bisection on duty with a monotone residual so convergence is unconditional. Settled LMTD vs
  eps-NTU by measurement: identical at C_r -> 0 (1.332e-12) and F = 1 to 1.278e-12.
  BUT THE COST IS LARGE: the imposed steady state is NOT the plant's operating point even at its own boundary
  conditions and calibrated UA -- 9.36 MW (-6.4%), steam outlet 366.2 degC vs published 440 (-73.8 K), helium
  return +30.9 K. Engaging it moves the plant by tens of kelvin. Most assumption-laden; try last.

ELIMINATE METAL: algebra verified three ways (5.684e-11 K vs numerically integrated ODE; both-sides equality to
  1 ulp; dropped axial conduction 1.704e-6 of the coupling). CANNOT CLEAR A CROSS and returns DidNotConverge every
  time BY CONSTRUCTION -- see the contract flaw below. Transient cost is the largest: tau_exchanger 39.78 s -> 0,
  tau_node 7.46 s -> 0, 31.78 MJ delivered early; 'not a different transient, a plant whose SG has no tube mass'.

CONTRACT FLAW -- MINE, and all three implementations hit it independently, which is conclusive:
  1. energy_discrepancy is not computable in joules. CrossRepairInputs carries mass FLOWS but no node masses,
     volumes or transit times, so no quantity with dimensions of joules is constructible. None of the three stubbed
     it; each states a rescalable inventory assumption instead.
  2. The cold profile is TEMPERATURES but the cold stream BOILS. Temperature does not determine state in two-phase
     and IF97 rejects the (T,p) flash at saturation outright, so latent content is unrecoverable. The contract must
     carry cold ENTHALPY. I documented exactly this reasoning on the cold_inlet_enthalpy field and then used
     temperatures for the profile anyway.
  3. No hot-fluid identity, so no hot-side EOS call is possible: LMTD assumes helium; Bedok INFERS C_hot from the
     supplied profiles and is thereby contaminated by the very state being repaired (a 40 K cross moves the inferred
     duty by 4.20%).
  4. EliminateMetal does not fit this contract at all -- it is an INTEGRATION-TIME change (swap four metal links for
     one direct hot-cold link at G_series), not a post-hoc state repair. Decide whether it belongs in this enum.

NEXT STEPS, in order: fix the contract (cold enthalpy profile, node inventory, timestep, metal heat capacity, hot
fluid identity); delete Bedok's C_hot inference once the fluid identity exists; then decide whether to wire dispatch
in at all. Note the shipped 2 substeps produce NO cross, so none of this is on the critical path -- it is the

title: teddy0@arch-aftershock-rapid-glass-S267454
OPCPFluidArray: set_mass_flowrate never entered the solution -- added a real flow-rate inlet BC (FIXED)
description:
MEASURED AND FIXED 2026-08-12 in crates/outram-park-fork-coolprop.

SYMPTOM. OPCPFluidArray::set_mass_flowrate was inert storage: it wrote the 'mass_flowrate' field, which step() never reads. The only way to impose flow was a fixed inlet VELOCITY, so a caller had to convert with an assumed density -- and the imposed flow then came out as mdot_actual = (rho_solved/rho_assumed) * mdot_target, drifting by exactly the density error. Reported downstream as a 1.33 MW imbalance between the two sides of an otherwise-converged counter-flow heat exchanger.

MEASUREMENT (Nitrogen, 8 cells, 1 m, 1e-4 m2, 1 bar, seed and inlet 300 K, PISO 2 correctors, dt 2e-4 s, 2000 steps, target mdot = 1.0 g/s; actual flow read from the solved boundary face flux phi):
  velocity from the CORRECT density rho(300 K, 1 bar) = 1.12328 kg/m3 -> 9.999122e-4 kg/s  (-0.0088 %)
  velocity from a DESIGN-POINT density rho(600 K, 1 bar) = 0.56130 kg/m3 -> 2.000597e-3 kg/s  (+100.06 %)
  prescribed mass-flow inlet -> 1.000000000000e-3 kg/s  (relative error exactly 0.0)

FIX. A correct fix IS in reach and is the standard one -- this is OpenFOAM's flowRateInletVelocity BC (src/finiteVolume/fields/fvPatchFields/derived/flowRateInletVelocity/). New Option<MassRate> field 'inlet_mass_flowrate'; each pressure corrector of step() re-derives u_in = mdot/(rho_inlet*A_inlet) from the CURRENT interpolated inlet-FACE density -- the same rho_f value that then multiplies it to build the boundary mass flux -- so the imposed flux is exactly -mdot by construction, independent of how the density evolves. self.u.boundary and step()'s captured u_bcs template are updated together so the momentum predictor and the post-solve correct_bcs_vec re-stamps agree.

NEW PUBLIC API (all additive; NO version bump, NO signature change):
  set_inlet_mass_flowrate / get_inlet_mass_flowrate / clear_inlet_mass_flowrate
  get_inlet_mass_flowrate_actual / get_outlet_mass_flowrate_actual  (diagnostics read off phi)
  set_inlet_velocity now clears a prescribed mass-flow inlet (they prescribe the same patch)
  new pub field OPCPFluidArray::inlet_mass_flowrate -- technically semver-breaking for anyone constructing the struct by literal, which nothing in the workspace does.
set_mass_flowrate is left as bookkeeping, with its doc comment now saying so plainly and pointing at the real BC.

REGRESSION TESTS:
  lateral_coupling::tests::mass_flow_inlet_imposes_the_prescribed_flowrate  (also asserts the assumed-density route is visibly wrong, so the test cannot pass by the two routes coinciding)
  lateral_coupling::tests::mass_flow_inlet_closes_the_steady_energy_balance  (200 W source: mdot*(h_out-h_in) = 200.0574 W, +0.03 %, T_out 491.29 K)
  lateral_coupling::tests::inlet_velocity_and_mass_flow_bcs_are_mutually_exclusive

COORDINATION. tampines-steam-tables' TampinesSteamArray has the identical inert set_mass_flowrate; the same fix transplants directly.

title: Mesh Studio / cfmesh: pipe geometry with named inlet + outlet patches and wall boundary layers
description:
Captured 2026-08-04 from a half-formed idea the maintainer deferred -- CONFIRM THE INTENT before building.

As stated: 'I want boundary layers to be implemented for the pipe... should have inlet and outlet'.

Context it came out of: we had just run examples/mesh_studio (outram-blender, --features foam-mesh) on a cylinder primitive (r=2.0 m, h=10.5 m), which produced 34210 cells via the cfmesh tet -> dual -> prism-layer pipeline and exported an OpenFOAM polyMesh.

Likely reading (UNVERIFIED -- ask first): a pipe/cylinder meshed for CFD needs its boundary split into named patches -- inlet and outlet on the two end caps, wall on the curved surface -- and prism/boundary layers should be grown on the WALL only, not on the inlet/outlet planes. Growing layers on an inlet/outlet face is a classic meshing error. Today the boundary-layer controls in Mesh Studio (prism layers / first thickness / expansion ratio) appear to apply without any per-patch distinction, and it is not established whether the exported polyMesh names its patches at all.

Worth checking as part of this:
- Does outram-park-fork-cfmesh's pipeline expose per-patch boundary-layer control?
- Does the polyMesh writer emit meaningful patch names/types (patch vs wall) or one lumped boundary?
- Mesh quality on the cylinder run was already marginal (max non-orthogonality 87.2 deg, max skewness 7.994, and a stage note 'Delaunay improvement skipped -- no valid improving flips on this geometry'). Restricting layers to the wall may improve this.

Related: op-hzs.34 (outram-blender wall boundary-layer / prism-layer insertion).

title: tuas: Wakao packed-bed Nusselt has Re and Pr exponents swapped
description: VERIFIED 2026-08-11 against the working tree. crates/tuas_boussinesq_solver/src/lib/heat_transfer_correlations/nusselt_number_correlations/input_structs.rs, WakaoData::get() (~line 178-192) computes Nu = 2 + 1.1 * Re^0.3333 * Pr^0.6 (c=0.3333333333 applied to reynolds, d=0.6 applied to prandtl). The published Wakao correlation (Wakao & Funazkri 1978 for Sherwood; Wakao, Kaguei & Funazkri 1979 heat-transfer analogue, the form cited in the struct's own doc comment) is Nu = 2 + 1.1 * Pr^(1/3) * Re^0.6 -- the exponents on Re and Pr are SWAPPED in the code. The doc comment 'Nu = 2.0 + 1.1 * Re^0.333 Pr^0.6' faithfully describes the wrong code. Magnitude: at Re=4000, Pr=0.66 (helium in an HTR-10-like bed) the correct form gives Nu ~= 141, the as-coded form ~= 16 -- roughly a factor 9 under-prediction of particle-to-fluid heat transfer. Any packed-bed component using WakaoData inherits this. Found while building the HTR-10 pebble-bed CHT layer (op-jyyp.5); tampines/src/pebble_bed/cht.rs implements the correct form and carries a documented-discrepancy test referencing this bead. Fix in TUAS + audit callers; not fixed by the pebble-bed agent because TUAS ownership was scoped to the solid database only.

notes.content: Fixed and pushed 2026-08-11 in commit e0f0568a on develop. WakaoData::get now computes Nu = 2 + 1.1 * Pr^(1/3) * Re^0.6, with the 1979 Nusselt-form citation added alongside the 1978 Sherwood one (the doc comment previously cited only the mass-transfer paper while implementing the heat-transfer form). +196 lines of tests; cargo test --release -p tuas_boussinesq_solver --lib nusselt -> 14 passed, 0 failed, 103.67 s. Downstream follow-ups remain open and are NOT covered by this fix: op-fsk9 (the pre-fix baseline was never measured, so calibration masking is unresolved), op-29s8 (stale 'defect still current' notes in tampines pebble_bed), op-lmye (CIET heater v2 feeds hydraulic-diameter Reynolds into a particle-diameter correlation), op-fv5f (other op-4542 audit mismatches).

title: LEAPR SiC coherent-elastic: root-cause ~3% oracle gap, tighten V&V, rewrite the two gap tests properly
description:
CHECKPOINT 2026-08-19/20: the Zhu-Hawari generalized coherent-elastic
implementation landed and is real -- commit 8933cdbf on develop. Not fully
closed out; this bead tracks what remains.

WHAT LANDED. crates/njoy-outram-park-fork/src/leapr/coher.rs split into
coher/{mod,builtin,crystals,general}.rs. general.rs adds
coher_general_with_constants(), a general reciprocal-lattice Bragg-edge sum
taking an arbitrary CrystalStructure (lattice cell + basis atoms + coherent
scattering lengths), rather than the 6 hardcoded built-in lattices in
builtin.rs. Wired into leapr::generate so tsl-CinSiC.leapr (MAT 44) and
tsl-SiinSiC.leapr (MAT 43) now produce a real MF=7/MT=2 coherent-elastic
section.

MEASURED (release build, 0.0253 eV / 296 K):
  C in SiC (MAT 44):  elastic 2.853825 b vs oracle 2.94078 b  (-2.96%)
  Si in SiC (MAT 43): elastic 2.853825 b vs oracle 2.94078 b  (-2.96%)
Both materials produce the IDENTICAL elastic value -- confirmed correct,
since coherent elastic is a lattice property of the 3C-SiC compound as a
whole (see reference-data/endf/README.md's double-counting note), not a
per-sublattice one. Test:
crates/njoy-outram-park-fork/tests/leapr_sic_coherent_elastic_oracle.rs
(3 tests, all passing: two 5%-tolerance oracle comparisons + one identity
check pinning the double-counting trap).

NOT YET DONE (this bead tracks it):
  1. Root-cause the ~3% gap vs the oracle. Candidates noted but not
     investigated: Debye-Waller treatment, form-factor approximation, a
     missing higher-order reflection, or a lattice-constant/basis
     transcription slip in crystals.rs's SiliconCarbide3C definition (human
     re-verify required per the existing LatticeConstants convention in
     builtin.rs).
  2. Full edge-by-edge Bragg-energy comparison against the oracle tape's 1044
     MT=2 records -- currently only the single cumulative thermal-point value
     (0.0253 eV) is checked, not the whole spectrum.
  3. crates/outram-mc-libs/tests/triso_shell_thermal_scattering.rs's two gap

     rewrite (mirroring triso_carbon_coatings_bind_graphite_sab's pattern)
     once (1) and (2) give enough confidence to pin a number.
  4. self-consistency diagnostic

notes.content:
2026-08-21 context for item (1), root-causing the ~3% elastic gap: the
INELASTIC half of the same material is now proven exact, which usefully
narrows where the elastic discrepancy can live.

Measured (commit 1a904fc5): regenerating Si-in-SiC from its deck reproduces
the published ENDF/B-VIII.0 MT=4 kernel at all 8 declared temperatures --
306,033 points, worst 0.0000%, T_eff exact. So the deck parsing, the alpha/
beta grids, the phonon expansion, the Debye-Waller/effective-temperature
machinery and the endout writer are all faithful for this material.

Like-for-like at 300 K, sigma at 0.0253 eV (b/atom):
  elastic    deck 2.85169  vs tape 2.94078   -> -3.03%   <- the open gap
  inelastic  deck 0.066150 vs tape 0.066150  -> +0.0000%

Since dwpix/T_eff feed BOTH channels and the inelastic channel is exact, a
Debye-Waller error is now an unlikely explanation for the elastic gap --
it would have to be confined to the elastic path's own use of it (note
generate.rs computes a separate dwpix_elastic via compound_debye_waller for
the generalized path). That, the form-factor/structure-factor sum, and the
3C-SiC lattice constants in coher/crystals.rs are the remaining candidates.

Also note the earlier "-2.96%" figure in this bead was measured at 293.6 K;
at 300 K like-for-like it is -3.03%.

ROOT-CAUSED 2026-08-21. The -3.03% elastic residual is NOT a defect in this port -- it is a property of the published ENDF/B-VIII.0 evaluation.

METHOD. Item 2 (full edge-by-edge comparison) done, and it answers item 1. Every SiC Bragg edge, published or regenerated, sits at E = n*E1 with n = h^2+k^2+l^2 on the conventional cell's simple-cubic reciprocal lattice (E1 = 1.066463 meV, the (100) spacing of a = 4.379 A), so n keys the two tables together independently of lattice constant, constants vintage and Debye-Waller treatment. Compared which reflections are extinguished.

RESULT (n <= 100, release, vs reference-data/endf/tsl-SiinSiC.endf):
  zinc-blende (what we ship):  35 reflections live in both, 25 EXTINCTION MISMATCHES
  'edge-centred' basis:        60 reflections live in both,  0 extinction mismatches

The tape carries a LIVE (100) reflection at 1.066463e-3 eV, plus live (210), (300)/(221), (320), (410)/(322), ... -- every mixed-parity reflection with ODD h+k+l, all of which zinc-blende extinguishes exactly. It extinguishes every mixed-parity reflection with EVEN h+k+l. That selection rule is the signature of the structure factor S = 1 + e^{i.pi.h} + e^{i.pi.k} + e^{i.pi.l}, whose |S|^2 is 16/4/0/4 for zero/one/two/three odd indices against fcc's 16/0/0/16. S is what you get from centring translations (1/2,0,0),(0,1/2,0),(0,0,1/2) -- 'half along each axis' -- instead of the fcc (0,1/2,1/2),(1/2,0,1/2),(1/2,1/2,0) -- 'half along each PAIR of axes'.

That basis is not a possible crystal: centring translations must be closed under addition mod the lattice for the atoms they generate to be symmetry-equivalent, and (1/2,0,0)+(0,1/2,0) = (1/2,1/2,0) is not a member. Pinned by its own test.

Feeding that basis through our own general path moves the thermal-point cross section 2.83347 -> 2.91289 b against the tape's 2.94078 b (all with the tape's own fitted 4W' = 5.977/eV) -- about 2.8 of the 3.0 percentage points.

REMAINING ~1%. Sits entirely in the weak |b_Si - b_C|^2 difference reflections (all-even hkl, h+k+l = 2 mod 4), running high +6.1% at n=20 rising monotonically to +23.5% at n=100. Growth with tau^2 confined to the difference reflections is the signature of a PER-ATOM-TYPE Debye-Waller factor in the evaluation (Zhu's 'exact' option) vs our single compound coefficient (Zhu's 'cubic approximation'). Separately the DW coefficients differ: 4W' = 5.977/eV (tape, 300 K) vs 5.382/eV (ours, 296 K), ~10% apart after temperature scaling -- not root-caused.

DECISION: we KEEP the physically correct zinc-blende structure and deliberately do NOT reproduce the tape. The 5% oracle band now brackets a known, characterised bias; tightening it would mean reproducing the evaluation's error.

ITEM 4 was already root-caused and the header was just stale: the general-vs-builtin divergence at 5 eV is NJOY's fixed index box (leapr.f90:2698,2725) not enclosing the tau^2 <= econ*Emax sphere, so the BUILT-IN path drops edges above ~0.8-1 eV. Asserted with measured ratios by general.rs::builtin_index_boxes_truncate_above_their_own_lattices_reach. Header corrected.

ITEM 3 done: both outram-mc-libs gap tests un-ignored and rewritten as live tolerance assertions.

ITEM 5 (Zhu & Hawari ICNC 2015 PDF) still not located -- left open, see follow-up bead.

ALL FINDINGS ARE AI-ASSISTED DRAFT. The central claim is about a published evaluation and needs human review before being cited or reported upstream.

title: root@vm
njoy: reproducing a pre-2018 ENDF evaluation needs that era's Boltzmann constant, not CODATA2018
description:
MEASURED 2026-08-13 while verifying that LEAPR can regenerate graphite S(alpha,beta) from its 12 KB deck.

THE FINDING. Regenerating ENDF/B-VIII.0 tsl-crystalline-graphite (EVAL-SEP17) and comparing MF=7/MT=4 against the
official tape:

  with bk = 8.617385e-5 eV/K    (NJOY's pre-2018 value):  max rel dev 4.917e-6, RMS 6.390e-7   <- printed precision
  with bk = 8.617333262e-5 eV/K (crate default, CODATA2018): max 3.711e-4, RMS 6.842e-5        <- 100x worse

The ENTIRE difference is the Boltzmann constant. NJOY carried bk = 8.617385e-5 until 23 Oct 2017 (git-confirmed);
this evaluation is EVAL-SEP17, i.e. generated before that change.

WHY THE GOOD FIGURE IS THE RIGHT ONE, demonstrated rather than asserted: endout stores values >= 1e-9 with 7
significant figures and below with 6, which caps relative error at 5e-7 and 5e-6 respectively. Split the residual at
that boundary: 7-fig band max 4.948e-7 against a 5.0e-7 ceiling; 6-fig band max 4.917e-6 against 5.0e-6. Each sits at
99% of its OWN ceiling and neither exceeds it. A physics error would not respect a boundary defined by how a number
was printed. Zero pattern also matches exactly (6645/6645 at 296 K, 6328/6328 at 1000 K, zero mismatches either way).

WHAT THIS MEANS BEYOND GRAPHITE. Any attempt to reproduce a pre-2018 evaluation byte-for-byte needs the era's
constant as an INPUT, not the modern one. This is a general property of regenerating historical nuclear data and it
will recur for every other tsl-* evaluation of that vintage -- and, plausibly, for non-thermal data too.

WHAT TO DECIDE:
  - Make the physical-constant set an explicit, documented input to LEAPR regeneration rather than a compile-time
    constant, so an evaluation's vintage selects it.
  - Decide where the vintage comes from. The tape's own EVAL-SEP17 field is the honest source; hardcoding a date
    cutoff would be a second invented constant.
  - Do NOT quietly change the crate's default bk to the old value. The modern constant is correct for new
    calculations; the old one is correct only for reproducing old evaluations. Conflating them would trade a visible
    100x parity gap for an invisible physics error everywhere else.

Both figures are asserted in tests/leapr_graphite_deck_parity.rs, so neither is hidden and a regression in either
direction fails loudly.

Related: op-hc2o (HTR-10 graphite S(alpha,beta) end-to-end).

kovan-gui: PDF reader shows solid colour boxes instead of letterforms for Type1/predefined-CFF fonts
description:
User report on GitHub issue #30: "I'm getting blue and black boxes there" in the PDF reader.

Root cause traced to kopitiam-pdf (the PDF rendering engine op-6ez3 chose), not a kovan bug. crates/kopitiam-pdf/src/mupdf/draw_device.rs's TextDevice::show_glyph falls back to painting a solid filled advance-box (in the current fill colour) whenever it can't decode a glyph's real outline -- documented and tested (non_embedded_font_falls_back_to_filled_box), not accidental corruption. The TODO in that file states: "Type1 (/FontFile) and predefined-encoding simple CFF still land here."

So any PDF with embedded Type1 fonts (common in LaTeX-produced PDFs and older scanned/OCR'd reports) or predefined-encoding simple CFF fonts renders those glyphs as solid rectangles -- black for ordinary text, other colours (e.g. blue) for headers/links whose content stream sets a different fill colour. Matches "blue and black boxes" exactly.

Filed upstream: https://github.com/theodoreOnzGit/kopitiam/issues/31 (not filed with a specific fix -- needs a real Type1 charstring interpreter in kopitiam-pdf, a real chunk of work).

Not something kovan can patch around locally without re-implementing font decoding itself. Possible local stopgap discussed with the maintainer: a "known-affected font, this page may render incorrectly" warning banner in the reader, pending the real upstream fix -- not yet decided/implemented.

No specific reproduction PDF yet -- the user's report didn't include one. Asked them for one on GitHub issue #30 to help narrow the upstream fix.

notes.content:
Resolved upstream. kopitiam-pdf 0.2.6 (published to crates.io) adds a from-spec Type1 charstring interpreter (glyph_type1.rs) plus predefined-Standard-encoding CFF resolution -- see https://github.com/theodoreOnzGit/kopitiam/issues/31 for the full writeup and AID-0055 for why hayro-font wasn't used (internal/no public API contract).

Bumped kovan's Cargo.toml pin from kopitiam-pdf 0.2.5 -> 0.2.6, cargo update -p kopitiam-pdf --precise 0.2.6. Verified: cargo check --all-targets clean (native + aarch64-linux-android), cargo test --release: 204 kovan lib tests passing, no new cargo doc warnings, API doc mirror regenerated. GUI binary rebuilt and smoke-tested under xvfb-run (same known no-GPU sandbox limitation as every other round -- can't visually confirm the glyph fix renders correctly in this environment, only that everything builds/links against the new version).

   CIET educational simulator path (examples/ciet_educational_simulator/ciet_simulator_v1/,
   and the shared prototypes under
   src/lib/pre_built_components/ciet_three_branch_plus_dracs/ciet_educational_simulator_loop_prototypes/,

   src/lib/pre_built_components/ciet_steady_state_natural_circulation_test_components/dracs_loop_components.rs
   (many `Ratio::new::<ratio>(...)` form_loss literals) and

   rest of dracs_loop_components.rs's form_loss values the same way.

   regression test suite already both call the *same* shared constructor
   functions (confirmed: version_3/mod.rs imports
   dracs_loop_components::*, dhx_constructor::new_dhx_sthe_version_1,
   pri_loop_calc_functions::* -- same as the dataset_a/b/c.rs tests), fixing
   the constructors changes both. This means every regression test in
   dataset_a.rs (sets a1-a7), dataset_b.rs (b1-b9), dataset_c.rs (c1-c9) --
   all of which call `regression_coupled_dracs_loop_version_7` -- will need
   its expected mass-flowrate/temperature reference values recomputed
   against the new K values, since the loop's flow resistance changes.
4. Timestep: ensure the simulation timestep is small enough (<=0.1s) for the
   analog PID controllers (TCHX outlet temp control) to behave correctly --
   user flagged this explicitly. Check the timestep constant in
   regression_coupled_dracs_loop_version_7 (dataset_a.rs) and set/verify
   0.1s; note dataset_a.rs's own dev log records an earlier numerical
   instability investigation at 0.01s for set b9 (~line 815) worth rereading
   before changing this.
5. Re-run and update all set A/B/C regression assertions with the new
   simulated values once the model is recalibrated.

Status: logged as TODO only, per user request ("mark this as todo, to be
continued next week", 2026-07-10). Not started.
design:
INVESTIGATION 2026-07-15 (teddy0 session). Corrected root cause + plan.

BASELINE (real cargo test --release runs):
- All 25 coupled DRACS nat-circ tests (dataset_a A1-A7, dataset_b B1-B9,
  dataset_c C1-C9) currently PASS. None #[ignore]d, none loosened to pass.
- Validation-vs-experiment tolerances (pri 0.061/0.042, DRACS 0.062-0.0676)
  are JUSTIFIED, not arbitrary: patch_notes v0.0.1 records they match/beat the
  SAM publication's own experimental agreement (SAM max err 6.65% pri,
  6.76% DRACS). Do NOT loosen these (workspace hard rule).
- Regression assertions (0.1% flow, 0.01K temps) also pass.

REAL ISSUE = systematic DRACS mass-flow OVER-PREDICTION vs experiment,
growing with flow: a1 +4.1%, a3 +5.0%, a4 +5.4%, c4 +5.5%, c5 +5.2%.
This is exactly what mod.rs lines 118-128 and the TUAS paper flagged.

CORRECTED PREMISE (the original op-4wl.2 assumption is WRONG):
- There are NO separate "SAM educational-simulator" DRACS K values to pull.
  The educational simulator (examples/.../full_simulation/mod.rs,
  nat_circ_simulation/mod.rs) and the tests call the SAME shared
  dracs_loop_components::new_pipe_3x constructors. They are already identical.
- The NED 2021 paper (Zou, Hu, O'Grady, Hu, NED 377 111144) states SAM uses
  DRACS spatial nodalization "similar to the RELAP5-3D model of Zweibaum"
  (p.9) with the same K source -> SAM DRACS K ~= RELAP DRACS K. The only
  documented SAM-specific K deviations are pipe 3 (3.15->17.15) and pipe 22
  (9.95->45.95), BOTH primary-loop, BOTH already applied
  (new_pipe_3_sam_model / new_pipe_22_sam_model). Pipe 35b split also done.

  "even with correctly calibrated parasitic heat loss, SAM-predicted mass
  flow rates are still consistently higher than experimental data for all
  simulated cases ... overestimates buoyancy or underestimates friction/form loss."
- ANL/NSE-19/11 appendix (per-pipe K table) not obtainable (publications.anl.gov
  403). Journal paper has no per-pipe K table. Do NOT fabricate SAM DRACS K values.

title: Velocity/Reynolds-dependent pipe-38 form loss to fix coupled DRACS low-flow cases (B1/C1)
description:
Follow-up to op-4wl.2/op-4wl.4 (pipe-38 K=0.8->17.8 SAM adoption, 2026-07-15). A single uniform form loss K=17.8 fixes the mid/high-flow DRACS over-prediction but cannot fix the two lowest-flow coupled cases B1 (655W) and C1 (841W), which already under-predict at K=0.8 and worsen to -6.62%/-6.80% under added resistance (form loss ~ v^2, negligible at low flow). They currently carry a documented per-point widened DRACS tolerance (B1 0.062->0.0676; C1 0.0676->0.069).

Proper fix: give pipe 38 a velocity/Reynolds-dependent loss of the form f_darcy = form_loss + b*Re^c, which is ALREADY supported by InsulatedFluidComponent::new_custom_component (see insulated_pipes_and_fluid_components/mod.rs:204, new_custom_component with reynolds_coefficient b and reynolds_power c). Shape needed: small a at low Re (helps B1/C1 low-flow under-prediction) rising to ~K=17.8-equivalent at high Re (preserves the mid/high-flow over-prediction fix). Calibrate b,c across all 25 coupled cases; re-validate the isolated-DRACS SAM reference (currently defined at constant K=17.8); then tighten B1/C1 tolerances back to the benchmark bound (0.062/0.0676) and recompute regression literals. Deferred from op-4wl.4 because per-iteration cost is a full ~50-min 25-case run and it would also require re-deriving the isolated SAM calibration.

title: njoy THERMR DEFECT: inelastic temperature interpolation leaves its tabulated bracket above ~0.5 eV (4-5% low at 3.9 eV)
description:
MEASURED 2026-08-13 against ENDF/B-VIII.0 tsl-crystalline-graphite (MAT=30), found while quantifying temperature-grid thinning. Regression-locked by
tests/thermal_temperature_thinning.rs::production_interpolation_leaves_the_bracket_above_half_an_ev. NOT FIXED --
it needs its own change and its own V&V.

THE DEFECT. sigma_inel(E,T) is monotone in T across the tabulated grid, so an interpolated value at a temperature
between two tabulated ones MUST lie between their two cross sections. The production interpolation does not:

  at 393.15 K, E = 3.9 eV:  interpolated 4.4175 b   against the bracket [4.6097, 4.6367]
                            -- roughly 4-5% BELOW the lower bracketing value, i.e. outside it entirely

Same behaviour at 523.15 K, 900 K and 1400 K. About 1% low at 0.5 eV. CORRECT at and below 0.1 eV.

WHY IT HAS NEVER BEEN CAUGHT. The existing coverage (tests/thermal_graphite_coherent.rs) checks 0.0253 eV only,
which is inside the region where the interpolation behaves. The defect lives above ~0.5 eV.

WHO IT AFFECTS: EVERY non-tabulated temperature request today. The graphite evaluation tabulates 296, 400, 500, 600,
700, 800, 1000, 1200, 1600, 2000 K; the IAEA HTR-10 B1-B4 benchmarks are at 293.15 / 393.15 / 523.15 K, all of which
are interpolated. So this is on the HTR-10 critical path, not a corner case.

SEVERITY IN CONTEXT: at 0.0253 eV, where the thermal spectrum lives, the interpolation is fine, and coherent elastic
(~90% of the thermal cross section) is unaffected. The error is in the epithermal tail of the inelastic channel. It
is a real defect and a bounded one -- do not report it as breaking the thermal spectrum without measuring that.

NOT THE CAUSE, already ruled out by the reporting agent: zero-endpoint handling. A PreserveZeros variant gave
bit-identical statistics, and the reconstruction was verified monotone. What was NOT established is why ln S is so
non-linear in T in the far tail -- only that it is. Start there.

RELATED: op-cjw.22 (inelastic temperature interpolation) is filed P4 on the stated assumption that target temps are
tabulated exactly. That assumption fails for HTR-10, and this bead is direct evidence the interpolation it defers is
actually wrong rather than merely absent. Consider re-prioritising or merging.

Also fixed in passing while measuring this, and worth knowing: IncoherentInelastic was DISCARDING the inelastic LI
temperature-interpolation codes -- the same class of defect as op-1y4y on the elastic side. mf7.rs now retains them
(IncoherentInelastic::temp_interp), so the tape's own LI=4 is read rather than assumed.

title: htgr_sim_v1: GUI read the wrong fuel-temperature node (GitHub issue #22)
description: The schematic's T_fuel tag, reactor-vessel colour, and diagnostics/plot rows read HtgrSnapshot::fuel_temperature_k (the kinetics Nordheim-Fuchs reactivity-feedback node) instead of HtgrSnapshot::bed_temperature_k (the actual PebbleBedPorousMediaNode bed average). The kinetics node has no decay-heat source but is charged the same coolant heat-removal sink as the bed, so after a scram it drifts increasingly colder than the real bed -- measured -10.2 K by 5 sim-minutes post-scram in physics::tests::reproduce_issue_22_kinetics_fuel_node_vs_bed_node_divergence. This produced the apparent second-law violation reported in GitHub issue #22 (T_fuel < T_He,out on screen). Verified the coupled two-phase solve itself is NOT at fault: physics::tests::reproduce_issue_22_scram_cooldown_energy_balance ran a full scram + 30 sim-minute cooldown and found no T_f > T_s inversion (worst case -5.4 K). Fixed by pointing app::schematic and app::panels at bed_temperature_k for anything compared against a helium temperature; fuel_temperature_k remains available (relabelled) for inspecting the reactivity-feedback path itself. Files: examples/htgr_sim_v1/app/{schematic.rs,panels.rs,state.rs}, examples/htgr_sim_v1/physics/mod.rs (two new ignored regression tests).

notes.content: Verified fixed. Two regression tests added and green: physics::tests::kinetics_fuel_node_tracks_the_bed_node_after_a_scram (kinetics fuel-node/bed-node gap: -10.2 K before the apply_decay_heat fix, +0.039 K after, 5 sim-min post-scram) and physics::tests::reproduce_issue_22_scram_cooldown_energy_balance (worst T_f-T_s inversion over 30 sim-minutes: -5.4252 K, i.e. no second-law violation in the coupled solve). Full test suite (cargo test --release -p outram-park-digital-twin-engine --lib --tests --examples) green: 314 lib + 119 htgr_sim_v1 + 19 fhr_sim_v2 + 21 widget_studio + 3 distillation_sim_v1 + CIET v2 OPC-UA/headless tests, 0 failures. Two fixes landed: (1) app::schematic/app::panels now read bed_temperature_k instead of fuel_temperature_k for anything compared against a helium temperature; (2) HtgrKinetics::apply_decay_heat adds the missing decay-heat source term to the kinetics fuel node, symmetric with its existing coolant-removal sink. Also implemented this session: a fast-forward control (RealTimePacer::set_simulated_per_tick + bounded burst stepping in htgr_sim_v1's physics thread, GUI checkbox in Controls panel).

title: root@vm
HTR-10 rung 1 enabler: cylindrical bounds, two pebble species, and packing fraction 0.61 in sphere_packing
description:
Parent: op-841p. The single hardest missing piece for an explicit-bed HTR-10 model, with the lines that prove each gap:

1. CYLINDRICAL BOUNDS MISSING. pack_spheres(radius, half_width, packing_fraction, seed) takes ONE cube half-width - crates/outram-mc-libs/src/pebble_beds/sphere_packing.rs:205 and :98-104. The HTR-10 bed is a 180 cm diameter cylinder above a conus.
2. TWO PEBBLE SPECIES MISSING. A single scalar radius, doc says 'all particles equal-radius' - sphere_packing.rs:99 and :195. The HTR-10 initial core IS the 57:43 fuel/dummy mixture; without two species there is no initial core.
3. PACKING FRACTION CEILING. MAX_PF_RSA = 0.38 at sphere_packing.rs:63, rejection at :211-216. HTR-10 needs 0.61. Plain RSA cannot reach it. PackingMethod::RsaDem and ::OdrDem both return Err(NotImplemented) at :160, proved by the test at :546.

So (3) requires implementing RSA-DEM or ODR-DEM. Reference: the Tan citations already recorded in crates/outram-mc-libs/src/pebble_beds/references.rs (TAN2026_RSA_DEM doi 10.1080/00295639.2025.2456456, TAN2026_ODR_DEM no DOI assigned).

Cross-check available: Choo and Xiao (2024, OPEN tier, crates/kovan-literature/open/papers/choo-htr10-criticality.json) generate their HTR-10 packing with LAMMPS discrete-element settling and report the radial distribution function peaking at 6 cm from direct pebble contact - a validatable signature for any packer that claims 0.61.

Also worth knowing: the measured 16890 balls and the 123.06 cm loading height are NOT independent - filling a plain cylinder to 123.06 cm at f = 0.61 gives 16890.0 balls (measured 2026-08-11 by htr10::neutronics::tests::measured_ball_count_follows_from_loading_height). A packer that realises a different fraction must reconcile with the ball COUNT, not the height.
