title: ciet_v2_headless_remote_control: intermittent failure under the full parallel suite -- likely an OPC-UA port/PKI race
description:
Observed 2026-08-14 on the Arch host (teddy0@snrsiDesktop).

SYMPTOM. 'cargo test --release -p outram-park-digital-twin-engine --lib --tests --examples' failed once with:
  test a_remote_client_can_drive_the_ciet_loop ... FAILED
  test result: FAILED. 0 passed; 1 failed  finished in 2.01s

The 2.01 s is the tell: the passing runs take 16.5-19.1 s, so it did not run the loop and fail an assertion -- it fell over almost immediately, consistent with a failure to bind or connect rather than a physics or control problem.

NOT REPRODUCIBLE ON DEMAND. Immediately afterwards:
  - alone ('--test ciet_v2_headless_remote_control'): PASSED, 17.08 s
  - full suite again, unchanged tree: PASSED, 18.58 s
Every other run in the same session passed (16.56 s, 19.08 s, 18.58 s). So it is intermittent and only seen under the full parallel suite. Maintainer's read, same day: 'it's likely a race condition' -- agreed.

WHY A RACE IS PLAUSIBLE. Two OPC-UA integration tests run as separate binaries and cargo runs them concurrently: ciet_v2_headless_remote_control and ciet_v2_opcua_roundtrip. crates/outram-park-digital-twin-engine/src/opcua_core/server.rs already isolates the certificate store PER PORT (instance_pki_dir(profile.pki_dir_name, format!('port-{}', config.port))) with the comment that this makes concurrent instances -- 'notably headless simulator tests' -- stop racing on one shared keypair. That mitigation assumes the two tests pick DIFFERENT ports. Worth checking:
  1. Do the two tests actually use different ports, or does one pick a fixed port that can collide with a previous run's server still shutting down? Note OpcuaServerHandle::shutdown() signals and returns immediately -- the thread and its listening socket close 'shortly afterwards', so a fast re-bind can land before the old socket is released (no SO_REUSEADDR is evident).
  2. Is there mDNS discovery contention (MdnsAdvertisement is withdrawn on DROP, not on shutdown())?
  3. Does the client retry, or connect once and give up?

WHAT NOT TO DO. Do not 'fix' it by serialising the suite or adding a sleep -- that hides the race and slows an already-slow suite. If the ports can collide, bind an ephemeral port per test and read it back from OpcuaEndpointInfo.

CAPTURE THE FAILURE OUTPUT NEXT TIME IT HAPPENS -- this report has the timing and the exit, but not the error text, because the run was grepped for 'test result' lines. Re-run with the full output retained.

title: container egress blocks every literature host -- validation work cannot source data
description:
MEASURED 2026-08-05 while sourcing benchmark data for op-6sl.7.

Every literature and report host tested refused at CONNECT with HTTP 403: osti.gov, nrc.gov, pnnl.gov, digital.library.unt.edu, inis.iaea.org, sciencedirect.com, link.aps.org, doi.org, arxiv.org. WebFetch is blocked session-wide (403 even on Wikipedia). Only code hosting (gitlab.com, github.com) and WebSearch were reachable.

CONSEQUENCE FOR THE PROJECT, not just for one bead: NO validation work that needs published experimental or benchmark data can be completed in this container. The workspace's whole V&V philosophy (VERIFICATION_AND_VALIDATION.md) rests on comparing against public literature and public benchmark data, and that comparison is currently unreachable. Verification against closed-form limits and upstream algebra still works fine; validation does not.

This already blocked op-6sl.7: the validation case is written and its admissibility criterion executes, but the two criteria needing measured nu are BLOCKED, and not one measured Zircaloy elastic constant could be obtained. The correct response was to deliver a gap list rather than invent numbers, but the maintainer's actual request — accurate benchmark data — is unmet.

OPTIONS FOR THE MAINTAINER:
- widen the environment's network policy for specific literature hosts (see https://code.claude.com/docs/en/claude-code-on-the-web for how the policy is configured);
- or fetch the papers outside the container and commit the extracted data with full provenance, which is what DATA_POLICY.md's provenance rule expects anyway;
- or accept that validation happens on the maintainer's own machine and that container sessions do verification only, and say so in VERIFICATION_AND_VALIDATION.md so nobody rediscovers this.

Note kovan-literature exists precisely for PDF-to-Markdown literature work, so the second option has tooling already.

---

title: kovan-cli: verify lsp-daemon's Windows fallback path on a real Windows machine
description:
op-fdph's keep-warm daemon (crates/kovan/src/commands/lsp_daemon.rs) is Unix-domain-socket-based and gated #[cfg(unix)]. On Windows, query()/serve()/stop() all resolve to the #[cfg(not(unix))] stub: query() returns None unconditionally (every caller then falls back to super::semq::connect's spawn-per-call RustAnalyzerSession path), serve() returns an error string (unreachable in practice since query() never spawns lsp-daemon-serve there), stop() just prints 'no lsp-daemon on this platform'.

This has only been reasoned about and compiled for (this dev machine is Linux; no Windows CI in this workspace per CLAUDE.md), never actually run on Windows. Needs verification on a real Windows machine (or at minimum a Windows CI runner if one gets added) that:
1. kovan-cli def/sig/refs actually work end-to-end via the spawn-per-call fallback (RustAnalyzerSession::connect_with_observed spawning rust-analyzer.exe, hover/references round-tripping correctly) -- nothing here is Windows-specific in that path's own code, but it has never been exercised on that OS.
2. kovan-cli lsp-daemon-stop's stub prints its message and exits 0 cleanly rather than erroring.
3. cargo build/test for the kovan crate (all three binaries) succeeds on a Windows target at all, given the new kopitiam-semantic/kopitiam-tokenizer dependencies (both already confirmed lightweight/pure-Rust by their own Cargo.toml deps, but not yet cross-checked against a live Windows toolchain).

Not blocking -- the design already treats 'no daemon on Windows' as an explicit, intentional fallback rather than a silent gap (see the module's own 'Platform scope' doc section) -- but the fallback path itself needs a real run to confirm, not just an argument that it should work.

title: kovan-literature: graph digitiser module (CLI + TUI + egui, graphreader-style)
description:
Extract data points from plot images in the literature archive. Requested by the maintainer 2026-08-11.

WHY THIS IS NEEDED AND NOT A TOY: several validation targets this project depends on exist ONLY as figures. docs/reactor-scoping/htr10.md records that the HTR-10 safety demonstration tests (loss of forced cooling without scram, rod withdrawal without scram) should be expected as digitised plots rather than tabulated data, and the same is true of the MSRE reactivity-insertion figures noted in vtb-findings.md. Without a digitiser those benchmarks cannot be used at all.

THREE INTERFACES, one engine:
- CLI - FULLY AUTOMATIC, no human in the loop. Detects axes, calibrates, traces curves, emits points. This is the agent-facing path and must be scriptable and deterministic.
- TUI (ratatui) - HYBRID: automatic pass first, then human verification and correction.
- egui - HYBRID: automatic pass first, then human verification and correction, with a graphical interface modelled on https://www.graphreader.com/ - load image, set two reference points per axis, choose linear or log per axis, auto-trace the curve, then drag/add/delete individual points, and export.

The automatic-first-then-verify shape is the point: the machine does the tedious part, the human confirms it, and the confirmation is recorded rather than assumed.

MANDATORY OUTPUT REQUIREMENT: every digitisation records its own provenance - source document and figure number, axis calibration reference points, linear/log per axis, reading uncertainty, whether the points were auto-traced or hand-placed or corrected, and by whom and when. Under DATA_POLICY.md digitisation is a processing step and must be documented as one. An exported dataset with no calibration record is not usable as validation evidence.

GOLDEN ORACLE: the sibling bead covers the maintainer supplying hand-digitised points from the Tobias decay-heat figures. Those are the acceptance test - the digitiser output must be compared against them with a stated tolerance, and log axes must be checked specifically because that is where naive pixel interpolation goes wrong.

PORTABILITY (HARD RULE): the CLI and the ratatui TUI must compile and run natively on Termux/Android like every other non-GUI crate - a terminal app is IN scope, not exempt. Only the egui/eframe interface is a genuine GUI exemption and must be target-gated so the library still builds headless for aarch64-linux-android. Image decoding must be pure Rust with no C toolchain.

DESIGN: enum dispatch over axis types and trace strategies, no trait objects, no Box, no lifetime parameters. Offline and deterministic, consistent with the rest of KOVAN - no cloud, no ML service.

title: kovan: a note-taking interface over catalogued documents
description:
MAINTAINER REQUEST 2026-08-11: "I think there should be a good interface for me to make notes via kovan." Filed for a later session, not started.

THE NEED. The archive now holds 16 documents and is growing fast — five HTR-10 papers arrived in a single morning. Reading them produces exactly the kind of knowledge that currently has nowhere to live: which figure holds the LOFC transient, which table the correlation came from, why one paper contradicts another, what a number actually means in context. Today that ends up in commit messages, bead comments, or nowhere at all.

WHAT IT SHOULD PROBABLY DO — for the maintainer to shape, these are candidates not requirements:
- Notes ATTACHED to a KovanDocument, not floating in a separate file, so a note cannot outlive or drift from the document it is about.
- Anchored where possible: page, section, figure or table number. A note saying "the 1046.6 C figure is at 120 percent overload, not nominal" is worth far more when it points at the page.
- Cross-document links, since the interesting knowledge is comparative. Real example from 2026-08-11: HTR-10 own fuel temperature LIMIT is 1230 C per Gao and Shi, while the 1600 C that pervades the modular-HTR literature including kugeler2017vhtr is the GENERIC coated-particle retention limit. Conflating them would misstate a safety margin, and that distinction currently survives only in a bead comment.
- Links out to beads and to source files, mirroring what CATALOGUE.md already does by hand.
- Notes are the maintainer own voice and should be distinguishable from extracted document text — never silently merged into the markdown body.

INTERFACE. The TUI is the natural home (kovan-tui, or the digitiser TUI pattern from op-5v5.8), since note-taking is a human activity and the CLI is the agent path. A CLI verb for appending a note non-interactively is still worth having so an agent can record a finding for the maintainer to review.

RESPECT THE EXISTING GRAIN:
- Notes on a PROPRIETARY document must stay gitignored with it. A note quoting a paywalled paper at length inherits its restrictions.
- huang2025waterIngress is a special case: its full text is deliberately not extracted because of a TDM/AI reservation (op-b7bx). Notes on it are the maintainer OWN words about it, which is fine and arguably the whole point — but the tooling must not use notes as a back door to reconstructing the text.
- Provenance discipline as everywhere else: who wrote the note and when.

RELATED: op-5v5.8 (graph digitiser, whose review workflow already records who verified what and when — the same pattern), and the KovanDocument model in kovan-common, which is the source of truth and would need a notes field or a sidecar.

title: tampines: TwoFluid1d solver core — six-eqn semi-implicit march, traced drag + interfacial heat transfer, interfacial-pressure regularisation

notes.content:
Groundwork for this bead was written 2026-08-11 and is sitting UNCOMMITTED in the working tree — crates/tampines/src/multiphase_1d/properties.rs, +556 lines. Not backed up anywhere else. Recording it here so it is not mistaken for un-started work.

WHAT LANDED IN THE TREE:
- IF97 range constants pulled out as named public items: T_MAX_REGION_1 623.15 K, T_MAX_REGION_2 1073.15 K, T_MIN_IF97 273.16 K.
- Metastability limits: MAX_METASTABLE_LIQUID_SUPERHEAT 30.0 K, MAX_METASTABLE_VAPOUR_SUBCOOLING 30.0 K. These are the thermal-non-equilibrium excursion caps the six-equation model needs and the drift-flux/HEM models do not.
- SaturatedTransport { at(p), is_stale_for(p), liquid_prandtl(..), vapour_prandtl(..), liquid_conductivity(), vapour_conductivity(), check_same_pressure(..) } with TRANSPORT_CACHE_TOLERANCE 1.0e-2 — a per-pressure transport-property cache with a staleness test, so the interfacial heat-transfer closures do not re-flash IF97 transport every cell every step.
- PhaseState { liquid_at(p,h,saturated), vapour_at(p,h,saturated), thermodynamic_temperature(), mass_density() } — the per-phase (not mixture) thermodynamic state the six-equation energy equations march.
- Helpers check_flash_inputs(..) and invert_monotone_fast(..).

STATE: compiles; `cargo test --release -p tampines --lib multiphase_1d` -> 6 passed, 0 failed, 3 ignored. None of those 6 exercises the new types — there is no TwoFluid1d solver to consume them yet, and two_fluid_tests.rs is still the 12-line placeholder registered so the module map stays stable.

CAUTION for whoever picks this up: TRANSPORT_CACHE_TOLERANCE = 1.0e-2 is a 1 % relative pressure window for reusing cached transport properties. That is an accuracy/speed trade nobody has measured the error of. Before the solver depends on it, quantify what a 1 % pressure staleness does to mu and k near the saturation line, where they vary fastest — or make the tolerance a documented, justified number rather than a chosen one.
notes.author: teddy0@arch-aftershock-rapid-glass-S267454

notes.content:
SOLVER CORE IMPLEMENTED 2026-08-12. crates/tampines/src/multiphase_1d/two_fluid.rs went from a 139-line scaffold whose step() returned NotYetImplemented to a working six-equation semi-implicit march (+2493 lines); two_fluid_tests.rs from a 12-line placeholder with zero tests to 18 verification tests (+1950 lines).

NOTE ON THIS BEAD'S TITLE: it says 'interfacial-pressure regularisation'. That is WRONG and was written before the source study. OpenFOAM's multiphaseEuler contains NO interfacial-pressure term at all -- no pInterface, no Stuhmiller, no Bestion, anywhere in the vendored tree (six-equation-regularisation.md section 1). What is implemented instead is VIRTUAL MASS folded inside the implicit 2x2 phase-coupling block, plus residualAlpha flooring, which is what upstream actually does for a fluid-fluid pair.

WHAT WAS BUILT:
- PhaseCouplingBlock / PhaseCouplingInputs: the 2x2 implicit drag + virtual-mass block per face, inverted in closed form. det = A_g A_l + A_g c_l + A_l c_g, a sum of non-negative terms, so it cannot lose its sign to cancellation and is strictly positive wherever residual-alpha flooring holds the diagonals up.
- Pressure equation derived from the VOLUME CONSTRAINT (sum of the phase continuity equations each divided by rho_k), so the flashing appears as a volumetric source Gamma (1/rho_g - 1/rho_l) and there is no kink to linearise across -- unlike drift flux, no secant is needed.
- Outer correctors are a proper Newton iteration on the volume residual R = alpha_g + alpha_l - 1, with the quasi-Jacobian -(V/dt) dR/dp assembled once per step. The first draft mixed a linearisation about p_old with a Newton correction and STALLED at R ~ 1e-4; fixed.
- Compressibilities taken along the ISENTROPIC path dh_k = dp/rho_k rather than at fixed enthalpy, because the energy equation applies the work term in the same step. Using the fixed-enthalpy derivative was measured to stall the correctors.
- Interfacial heat transfer solved IMPLICITLY in the phase enthalpies (closed form Q = dT/(1/K + dt/(m cp))), which is unconditionally stable and self-limiting.
- Conserved primary state is (m_g, m_l, m_g h_g, m_l h_l); alpha and rho are derived. Nothing is renormalised: the volume residual is reported and refused above 1e-4.

HONESTY: the regularisation is documented as TRACED TO UPSTREAM PRACTICE and explicitly NOT proven to restore hyperbolicity. No characteristic analysis was done, here or upstream, and two upstream tutorials run with no regularising term at all.

FOLLOW-UP BEADS FILED (7): the tampines-steam-tables Region-4 panic (P1); the low-void expansion-work refusal that BLOCKS a two-fluid Edwards case; the undiagnosed corrector non-convergence at small bubble diameter; the missing Dirichlet-pressure boundaries; the measured drift-flux/two-fluid compressibility disagreement; the virtual-mass port into outram-foam-multiphase; and performance.

ONE FILE OUTSIDE THE ASSIGNED SCOPE WAS TOUCHED: edwards_tests.rs::two_fluid_step_still_refuses_to_pretend asserted step() returns NotYetImplemented and could not compile against the new constructor signature. It was rewritten into two_fluid_constructs_on_the_edwards_geometry, which asserts only construction, and its doc comment records the change. That test's own docs had always described itself as the placeholder to replace when the solver landed.

kovan: DESIGN -- the 'kovan folder' project format (kovan.toml index, standard markdown sections, line-number pointers)
description:
Split from op-9c2e (GitHub issue #30, second comment, the largest single piece of the issue). Design pass, no code -- must land before op-9c2e.11/12/13.

THE SPEC AS GIVEN (verbatim structure from the issue): a folder the user points kovan at, containing:
  - kovan.toml           (index)
  - <user-named>.bib      (one main bibliography file, name chosen by the user)
  - pdf/                  (raw PDFs)
  - markdown/             (processed PDFs)
  - .git (if the folder happens to be a git repo)

markdown/ files hold, per the issue: summaries by author, summaries by AI, CSVs from digitised tables, CSVs from digitised plots, and the extracted full-text/prose (from kovan OCR or AI) -- 'in a standard markdown structure'.

kovan.toml points to: the bib entry for each document, where its PDF is stored, where its markdown is, where its summaries are, where its full text is, where its table CSVs are, where its digitised-graph CSVs are -- 'DOWN TO THE LINE NUMBERS'. kovan auto-generates and updates these line-number pointers whenever the markdown changes.

GUI can read/write the markdown content via the structured sections, but must NOT be able to change the standard structure itself.

MUST RECONCILE WITH THE EXISTING DESIGN RULE (docs/kovan.md, 'Canonical Representation'): 'Only the Rust struct is authoritative... Do not make: BibTeX, TOML, Markdown metadata authoritative.' kovan.toml as specified here is clearly meant to be a GENERATED INDEX, not a hand-authored source of truth -- this design bead must state that explicitly (kovan.toml is derived/cached from the KovanDocument structs + the markdown files' own standard section markers, regenerated on change, the same way CATALOGUE.md is already generated rather than hand-maintained for this workspace's internal literature archive -- see docs/kovan.md 'Storage Layout' and CLAUDE.md's 'CATALOGUE.md is maintained through kovan, not by hand' rule) so a future implementer does not accidentally make the TOML authoritative and violate the existing rule.

ALSO A NEW THING VS TODAY'S STORAGE LAYOUT: docs/kovan.md's existing 'Storage Layout' (open/proprietary/generated, fixed under crates/kovan-literature/) is THIS WORKSPACE's own internal literature archive. The issue is asking for a GENERALISED, user-pointable project format kovan can operate on for ANY folder, which is new scope layered on top of (not a replacement for) that internal archive convention -- the design pass should say explicitly how/whether the two relate (e.g. does this workspace's own crates/kovan-literature/ eventually become one instance of a 'kovan folder', or do they stay separate concepts).

DELIVERABLE: a written spec (kovan.toml schema, the standard markdown section set and its markers/headings, the line-number-pointer regeneration algorithm and when it fires, the read/write-content-not-structure GUI contract) for the maintainer to review before op-9c2e.11 (kovan.toml implementation), op-9c2e.12 (bibliography window) and op-9c2e.13 (structured markdown GUI editing) start.

notes.content: Design deliverable written: crates/kovan/docs/kovan-folder-format.md. Covers: kovan.toml TOML schema (array-of-tables, one per document, bib-key-joined, line-range sections); explicit reconciliation with docs/kovan.md's 'only the Rust struct is authoritative' rule (kovan.toml is a generated cache, never hand-authored, same pattern as CATALOGUE.md); the 5 standard markdown sections (ai_summary/author_summary/full_text/table_csvs/graph_csvs) marked by inert <!-- kovan:section NAME --> HTML comments (not headings, so heading text stays freely editable without breaking line tracking); the content-vs-structure GUI contract for op-wr08 (marker lines + fixed order are read-only, everything between markers is a free edit region, stale-range saves are rejected not silently overwritten); the line-number regeneration algorithm + trigger (fires synchronously after any markdown write, full-file rescan, atomic write); and explicit scoping vs this workspace's own existing kovan-literature/ internal archive -- they are declared two SEPARATE concepts, the internal archive is not planned to become 'one instance of a kovan folder.' Three open questions flagged for maintainer input before op-b1y5 starts: bib-key collision handling, multi-document-per-PDF, and whether digitised-CSV provenance (calibration/review status) rides along as a sibling JSON file when embedded into markdown or gets dropped to bare numbers. Not implemented -- this is the design pass only, per the bead's own scope.

htgr_sim_v1: global 0.1 s timestep with outer correctors -- the route to real time
description:
MAINTAINER DECISION, 2026-08-13: 'I need a global 0.1s timestep to be used. Have additional outer correctors to prevent the courant number problem.' Agent dispatched same day.

WHY -- pacing alone cannot reach real time. MEASURED, release mode, the_whole_plant_steps_at_the_gui_timestep, 20,000 steps of 1 ms:
  41.79 s quiescent / 49.00 s contended  =>  2.09-2.45 ms of COMPUTE per 1 ms of PLANT time
  old pacing (compute + 10 ms sleep per 10 ms tick): real-time ratio 0.29-0.32
  new deadline pacing (landed 2026-08-13):           0.41-0.48
Reducing SUBSTEPS_PER_TICK does NOT help -- it cuts plant time per tick in the same proportion as compute.
The physics is ~2.2x too expensive at dt = 1 ms. A longer timestep is the route; that is this bead.
The 20 percent duty figure in op-szmi.16 predates the nodalised SG (edbb2bd7) and is off by ~12x -- do not use it.

THE ASK:
1. ONE GLOBAL 0.1 s TIMESTEP. Today the step is pinned by at least THREE hand-maintained literals:
     app/mod.rs PHYSICS_DT_S
     physics/primary_loop.rs:421 STEAM_GENERATOR_SUBSTEP_S = 0.0125
     physics/primary_loop.rs:381 STEAM_GENERATOR_NODE_COUNT = 8 (interacts with it)
   Global means a single shared constant every consumer reads, not three literals that happen to agree.
2. OUTER CORRECTORS for stability. A 100x longer step will violate the Courant condition on advective paths;
   the maintainer wants PIMPLE-style iterate-to-convergence within a timestep rather than a smaller step.

SEARCH-BEFORE-BUILDING, already checked -- REUSE these:
  Courant: tuas .../fluid_mechanics_correlations/courant_number.rs;
           .../one_d_fluid_array_with_lateral_coupling/preprocessing.rs;

              outram-foam-appbuilder-lib/src/solvers/ and src/io/fv_solution/ (nOuterCorrectors vocabulary);
              MOST LIKELY DIRECT REUSE per root CLAUDE.md: TampinesSteamArray and OPCPFluidArray already wrap
              fvm:: operators WITH PIMPLE correctors, and the SG already uses those arrays -- check first.

CONSTRAINTS:
  - MEASURE the Courant number per advective path at 0.1 s, before and after correctors. Do not assume it.
  - Do not silently loosen a tolerance or convergence criterion to make 0.1 s look stable.
  - V&V numbers WILL move. Re-measure, update the number AND the date, and list every one changed.
    Do not quietly edit expected values, and do not delete or ignore a test that becomes inconvenient.
  - Report the new real-time ratio from the SAME test so it is comparable to 0.41-0.48.
  - Quantify the ACCURACY trade against the 1 ms model on at least one transient. Be honest if it degrades --
    a fast simulator that is wrong is worse than a slow one that is right.

RELATED: op-v5zb (deadline pacing, landed), op-775s (the measurement, now done), op-szmi.16 (GUI frame lag --
DIFFERENT symptom, do not merge), op-xvye (P0 pacing underflow, now known to be in FOUR sites).

notes.content:
DONE and PUSHED 2026-08-13 (commit 3acc9536 on develop).

Real-time ratio 0.492 -> 1.032, independently re-verified: 20 s of plant time in 19.385 s wall, isolated release run.

KEY FINDING -- the global 0.1 s timestep was NOT the win. Sweep: 1 ms 0.492, 10 ms 0.505, 100 ms 0.514. The steam
generator runs on its own clock and is ~96% of the cost, so raising the plant step bought 4%. The 2x came from the
exchanger's PIMPLE outer correctors being set to 4 when settled duty is identical at 1, 2, 3 and 4 (9.6854 MW each
against a 9.6851 MW half-substep reference). Cost is exactly linear in correctors; two of four were paid for nothing.

The timestep work still earned its keep: unifying a dozen scattered literals into PLANT_TIMESTEP_S is what EXPOSED
both the wasted correctors and a -84.5% point-kinetics error at 0.1 s (Lambda/beta = 0.154 s is comparable to the
step; fixed by sub-stepping kinetics at 1 ms). It also caught a live bug where a test window had silently doubled to
150 s and was running to 999.07 K against a 1000 K limit.

Courant measured, not assumed: Co_hot 0.222 at 0.0125 s, 1.776 at 0.1 s, hot side binding at 4.97x the cold.
Correctors provably do not lift the limit -- 0.05 s panics at 4, 8 and 16; 0.1 s at 8 and 32.

Clamp events zero everywhere, now asserted == 0 in three tests.

Accuracy: reactor power +0.0000% (STRUCTURAL -- both runs integrate kinetics at 1 ms, not a convergence result),
core outlet -0.0015 K, bed -0.054 K, SG duty -0.012%. WORSE: steam outlet +0.822 K, GUI 100 Hz -> 10 Hz.

Follow-on: op-3lay (build real buffer -- 1.032 is ~3% margin and goes negative under load).

kovan: DECISION -- PDF page rendering engine (foundational, blocks the reader/digitiser work)
description:
Split from op-9c2e (GitHub issue #30). Foundational -- almost everything else in the epic (integrated PDF reader, draw-box-then-digitise for plots and tables, BibTeX-from-open-PDF) needs a PDF PAGE rendered as a raster image, and kovan-literature has none today: pdf-extract and lopdf only give text/metadata/raw embedded images, never a rendered page.

WHAT NEEDS DECIDING: how kovan renders a PDF page to a bitmap for display + region cropping.

Candidates surveyed (none implemented, this is the survey to hand the maintainer):
- pdfium-render: wraps Google's pdfium via FFI to a prebuilt dynamic library (downloaded or vendored per-platform). Mature, accurate, but NOT pure Rust, NOT deterministic-build-from-source, and almost certainly NOT Android/Termux-buildable the way this crate's other deps are (workspace CLAUDE.md Android/Termux hard rule) -- a real tension with KOVAN's own 'Android First' / 'Local First' / 'Deterministic First' design principles (docs/kovan.md).
- mupdf-rs: wraps MuPDF (C library, AGPL or commercial dual-license) -- likely licensing friction with this crate's GPL-3.0-only(via workspace)/MIT posture, and again a C toolchain dependency.
- A pure-Rust PDF rasteriser (none mature/complete exists as of this survey -- pdf-extract/lopdf are text/object-model only, not renderers).
- Desktop-only escape hatch: gate PDF rendering behind a non-default feature the same way digitise-gui/gui already are, and let Android/Termux fall back to the existing text-only / image-file digitiser workflow. This keeps the core crate Android-clean at the cost of the PDF-reader feature itself being desktop-only.

DELIVERABLE: not code. A short written recommendation (crate choice, licence check per RESPONSIBLE_USE.md/DATA_POLICY.md, Android-story, feature-gating plan) for the maintainer to approve before op-9c2e.4 (integrated PDF reader) or op-9c2e.5 (plot digitise-from-region) can start.

title: root@vm
token accounting: query + historian drop merge-commit trailers (43% of recorded tokens invisible)
description:
Both `docs/historian/token_usage.py query` and `docs/historian/historian.py` build their commit list with `git log --no-merges`, so every trailer stamped on a MERGE commit is excluded from the reported token totals.

Measured on origin/develop at 2e085b2 (2026-08-06):

  trailered commits, all:        247   total 5,876,958,905
  trailered commits, non-merge:  172   total 3,363,701,768   <- what query reports
  trailered commits, merge only:  75   total 2,513,257,137   <- silently dropped

That is 42.8% of the recorded token spend.

Why this looks unintended rather than deliberate: CLAUDE.md's historian section says lines come from 'git log --numstat --no-merges' and describes the merge exclusion for LINES only. Excluding merges is correct for lines (a merge re-reports its side branch's lines). It is wrong for tokens, because each API-Usage-Since-Last-Commit trailer is a DISJOINT delta -- prepare-commit-msg stamps the delta since the previous commit and post-commit advances the baseline, so a merge commit's trailer is real work not counted anywhere else. In this workspace merge commits are where the expensive part lives: reading the diff, running per-crate release tests, Android --all-targets, provenance and sign-off checks.

Largest dropped trailers:
  205,934,989  26080c16  Merge branch 'claude/outram-foam-8ookor' into develop
  186,299,135  423a5db3  Merge branch 'claude/outram-blender-mggk7u' into develop
  175,539,906  0d949263  Merge branch 'claude/outram-foam-8ookor' into develop
  130,215,239  53b5bef9  Merge branch 'claude/outram-foam-8ookor' into develop

Sites: token_usage.py cmd_query line ~329; historian.py line ~85.

Suggested fix: drop --no-merges from the TOKEN commit list in both tools while keeping it for the numstat/lines path, and report merge-commit tokens as a separate line so the split stays visible. Needs the maintainer's confirmation that counting merge commits is the intended semantics before any code change -- this bead is the finding, not an authorisation to edit.

title: basic-lib: SurfaceScalarField::uniform sets boundary face values to 0 (nulls fvm::laplacian boundary coeff)
description: Found during genfoam thermoMechanics mesh-solve port (op-p6p.11). outram-foam-basic-lib SurfaceScalarField::uniform() builds boundary patches via PatchField::zero_gradient(p.size), whose values are 0. Since scalar fvm::laplacian computes the boundary-face diffusion coeff as gamma.boundary[pi].values[fi]*area/d, a uniform gamma silently yields ZERO diffusion coefficient on every boundary face -> Dirichlet contributions dropped -> solve returns all-zeros yet reports converged (normalised_residual of x=0 with b=0 is 0). Workaround used in mesh_solve.rs: build the SurfaceScalarField with PatchField::fixed_value(size, k) boundary patches. Fix: SurfaceScalarField::uniform should set boundary values to the uniform value (fixed_value), or laplacian should treat a zero-gradient gamma patch as owner-extrapolated. Not my subtree; reporting per workspace rules.

title: offbeat: wire rheology into the mechanics solve (inelastic strain feedback, state advance, timestep control)
description:
P0 mechanics (op-6sl.1) and P1 rheology (op-6sl.2) are both ported and tested,
but nothing wires them together yet. MechanicsSolver still assumes pure linear
elasticity; ConstitutiveLaw::correct is never called.

The rheology port documents exactly what the mechanics layer must do
(rheology/mod.rs, "what the mechanics layer must do"):

1. Pass mechanical strain = total strain MINUS eigenstrain. Passing total strain
   makes an unconstrained, freely expanding pellet look highly stressed -- and it
   will then creep, which is silently and badly wrong.
2. Own one RheologyState per cell.
3. Call correct() repeatedly inside the outer corrector loop from the SAME
   start-of-step state; call advance() ONCE, after convergence. Advancing inside
   the loop double-counts inelastic strain.
4. The corrected stress is softer than the elastic one, so the displacement field
   is no longer in equilibrium -- re-solve with RheologyState::inelastic_strain()
   fed back as an additional eigenstrain (upstream's correctAdditionalStrain).
5. Bound the timestep with CreepTimeStepControl: the creep integration is
   implicit in stress but explicit in state.

Acceptance: a stress-relaxation case where a clamped bar under sustained strain
relaxes toward the creep-equilibrium stress, verified against the closed-form
exponential decay; and a case where free thermal expansion with creep active
produces NO creep strain (the eigenstrain-subtraction check in item 1).

Blocked by nothing -- both halves exist.

title: offbeat mechanics: compact stress recovery for material interfaces (fvc::grad smears a discontinuous inelastic strain)
description:
Found while wiring rheology into the mechanics solve (op-6sl.11).

MechanicsSolver recovers the stress from fvc::grad_vec(D), which on a 1-D
structured mesh is the wide (2*dx) central-difference gradient. Where the
accumulated inelastic strain is DISCONTINUOUS across a material interface, that
recovery smears the jump over the two cells either side and reports a stress
there that violates 1-D equilibrium.

Measured 2026-08-05 (8-cell bar, cells 0-3 creeping with a linear Norton law,
cells 4-7 purely elastic, 200 steps of tau/20, both x-ends displacement-pinned):
  cell 3: sigma_xx = 18.2785 MPa
  cell 4: sigma_xx = 23.5674 MPa
  cells 5,6,7: sigma_xx = 20.75560 MPa, agreeing to 13 significant figures
i.e. a 25% spread concentrated entirely at the interface, with an exactly
uniform far field.

With a SMOOTHLY varying creep rate the spread converges away under refinement
(whole-bar 3.47e-3 -> 1.64e-3 -> 7.95e-4 at n = 16/32/64, first order because of
the one-sided end cells; interior-only 3.37e-4 -> 1.12e-4 -> 3.44e-5, close to
second order), so the equilibrium the solver ENFORCES is right. It is the stress
RECOVERY that is inaccurate at a discontinuity.

This is the trade-off OpenFOAM exposes as the solidDisplacement
'compactNormalStress' switch: the compact form uses snGrad (more convergent,
less accurate) and the non-compact form uses grad (less convergent, more
accurate). The port currently implements only the grad form for recovery.

Options: (a) port the compactNormalStress switch, including the
divSigmaExp = fvc::div(DEqn.flux()) branch that this port does not have;
(b) recover the stress from face snGrad instead; (c) document that a material
interface needs mesh refinement across it. Today the limitation is documented
and measured on
mechanics::solver::rheology_tests::spatially_varying_creep_keeps_the_axial_stress_uniform.

---

offbeat: mechanics must gate on MATPRO Zircaloy Poisson exceeding 0.5 above ~1355 K
description:
The ported MATPRO Zircaloy correlations fit Young's modulus and shear modulus as
independent lines, so nu = E/(2G) - 1 crosses the incompressible limit of 0.5 at
T = 1354.84 K and reaches 0.912 at 1800 K -- the top of upstream's own stated
validity range. At 600 K a retained cold-work fraction above 0.1197 does the same.

Consequence: lambda = E*nu/((1+nu)(1-2nu)) is singular at the crossover and
sign-flipped beyond it, and mechanics::LinearElastic::new rejects such constants
outright, so a hot-Zircaloy case will fail where upstream would silently produce
a garbage stiffness.

This is a faithful port of a real upstream defect, not a porting bug. Upstream
neither detects nor guards it.

PoissonRatioModel::is_admissible() was added for exactly this. The mechanics
layer needs to gate on it -- decide the policy: clamp below 0.5, fall back to a
constant Poisson's ratio, or refuse the case with a clear error. Maintainer call.

title: offbeat: deferred sub-models from the P3/P4 port (cracking, PyC anisotropy, PARFUME swelling, Lassmann burnup, relocation recovery)
description:
Deferrals recorded by the P3/P4 port agents, each documented in-file at the point
it applies. Collected here so they are not lost:

- Isotropic cracking (nCracks / sliceMapper / lhgr crack-softening) on the UO2,
  MOX and SCK-CEN Young's-modulus and UO2/MOX Poisson models. Needs damage-model
  state and a slice mapper, so not a pure function of MaterialState. All variants
  currently return the upstream nominal value.
- Transversely isotropic PyC: upstream itself returns the isotropic average
  (E_r + 2 E_t)/3 with a TODO. Real anisotropy needs a direction-dependent
  modulus in the mechanics layer.
- PARFUMEPyC thermal-expansion spherical-to-Cartesian tensor rotation: upstream
  does it in correct() using mesh_.C()[cellI]; it is a mesh operation and belongs
  in the mechanics assembly.
- swellingPARFUMEBuffer / swellingPARFUMEPyC: they integrate eps += rate*flux*dt,
  so they need fast flux and the timestep, plus a 2-D table interpolator in
  temperature x Bacon Anisotropy Factor and a 1-D one in coating density.
- burnupLassmann / burnupLassmannFBR (~75 KB): TUBRNP-style radial depletion
  solving a reduced Bateman chain for ~14 nuclides plus radial power
  reconstruction. That is neutronics and needs a flux solution.
- Axial-shape half of timeDependentAxialProfile: needs a mesh, pin direction and
  the profiles/ library.
- Relocation recovery (recoveryFraction/relaxRecovery), slice averaging, the
  max/min ratchets and the sensitivity scaling: history/mesh/contact logic.
- SCIANTIX physics: returns NotImplemented, never a silent zero. Separate
  MIT-licensed code with its own licence-provenance and V&V obligations.

Most of these are blocked on the same two things: the damage model and the
slice mapper. Worth sequencing them behind those rather than picking them off.

(273-1800 K), RelapZy (290-1800 K), MatproZy heat capacity (273-2099 K), IAEAZy

title: outram-mc: root-cause the transport_csg stuck-history (MAX_EVENTS guard is a band-aid)
description: Before the MAX_EVENTS=100k/history cap, a reflective-infinite-medium k-eff hung (~9 CPU-min, one looping history). Find the geometry/nudge corner case (suspect: history stuck near a reflective plane/corner or coincident-surface re-cross in run_keff_csg) and fix properly; the cap currently leaks such histories (small bias).

notes.content: Root-cause analysis (2026-07-24, from the op-6tz.34 work). The reflective-corner stuck-history is grazing-incidence ping-pong: a particle moving nearly parallel to a reflective wall, near a corner, alternately hits the two/three perpendicular walls at sub-nudge distances. Each fixed 1e-9 cm nudge advances it only ~1e-9 cm ALONG the wall, so traversing an O(1 cm) feature needs ~1e9 bounces >> MAX_EVENTS=100k -> the history is capped and leaked (the band-aid). This is distinct from op-6tz.34 (now fixed): that was a lattice-edge/wall coincident tie leaking histories OUT of the box; this is in-corner non-progress. A PROPER fix (per this bead: do NOT extend the band-aid) needs OpenMC-style token-based surface tracking (advance exactly to the surface, resolve the next cell by surface index + sense, and compose a corner reflection off all coincident reflective surfaces in one event) rather than a fixed position nudge. That is a larger rework best done against the OpenMC reference source (not available in this sandbox), so leaving open with this analysis. The residual ~2% surface-vs-delta gap in the op-6tz.34 regression test is plausibly this effect.
notes.author: root@vm

notes.content: Root-cause fixed: new Geometry::compose_corner_reflection in geometry.rs, called from cross_surface reflective arm. At a reflective corner/edge (other reflective walls within 1e-9 cm of the crossing point) it now reflects off ALL coincident walls in one event (reflections compose at a corner = retroreflection) instead of ping-ponging 1e-9 cm/event. Sign-agnostic crossing test so min-side corners handled; lone-wall case bit-identical. Marked honestly as a robustness fix for this crate's fixed-nudge tracker (no C++ ref on host). Regression tests in triso.rs. Measured: grazing history 100003 events + 20 corner leaks to 4 events + 0 leaks; small U235 reflective cube surface 2.22235+/-0.00334 vs delta 2.21925+/-0.00320 = 0.67 sigma. Suite green: 95 lib + 26 notebooks, 0 fail. CAVEAT: worktree based on main, 658 behind develop; develop-only nested-lattice ~2pct residual not measurable here. Verified fix ports cleanly to develop (cross_surface + triso imports identical). Not committed.
notes.author: root@vm

notes.content: Fixed in 69d8874 (integrated onto claude/outram-mc-setup-cb1bg9, which has op-6tz.34). Root cause: cross_surface reflective arm reflected a grazing near-corner particle off only the primary wall; the fixed 1e-9 cm nudge left it headed into the perpendicular wall(s), re-crossing at sub-nudge distances (~1e5-1e9 events → MAX_EVENTS leak, negative bias). Fix: Geometry::compose_corner_reflection composes the specular reflection of every reflective/white/periodic surface coincident with the crossing point (|evaluate(r)|<=1e-9) that the particle actually crosses (|u·n|>0, sign-agnostic for min/max-side axis-aligned walls). Retroreflection at a right-angle corner → particle leaves in one event. Lone-wall case is bit-identical to surf.reflect. MAX_EVENTS/NUDGE untouched. Tests: corner_reflection_composes_at_exact_corner (unit), corner_grazing_history_terminates_without_pingpong (worst 100003→4 events, 20→0 leaks), corner_reflective_cube_surface_tracking_unbiased (surface 2.22235±0.00334 vs delta 2.21925±0.00320, 0.67σ). 158 lib + 30 notebook tests pass; op-6tz.34 nested-lattice test still green. CAVEAT: robustness fix for this crate's fixed-nudge tracker (not an OpenMC routine port — only the physics is mirrored); non-orthogonal corners compose order-dependently (approximate), axis-aligned cube/lattice corners exact.

notes.content:
PARTIALLY CLOSED 2026-08-14, and the route changed. NOT closing -- one of the two targets is now blocked on a different, identified bead.

ROUTE CHANGE. This bead proposed un-gating the LIVE thermal tests by wiring them to EndfCache::fetch_tsl (network download). The embedded LEAPR decks added 2026-08-14 are a strictly better route for the same goal: no network, no cache, no IAEA availability question (that host is policy-blocked 403 from this environment, which is why this bead was marked 'NOT verifiable on this host'), and it works offline and in CI.

TARGET 1 -- GRAPHITE: DONE. tests/htr10_graphite_thermal_scattering_pebble_bed.rs and the new tests/triso_shell_thermal_scattering.rs both regenerate the graphite MF=7 law from the embedded tsl-crystalline-graphite deck via leapr::generate::generate_tape. No , no skip path, runs unconditionally. Verified: elastic 4.55555 b + inelastic 0.48162 b at 0.0253 eV, reproducing the 5.0378 b recorded under op-nhoa against the official ENDF/B-VIII.0 TAPE -- so the regenerate-from-deck path agrees with the tape path.

TARGET 2 -- outram-mc pincell.rs (tsl-HinH2O): STILL GATED, root cause identified and it is NOT this bead's to fix. The fallback is wired (locate_tsl_hinh2o now tries env var -> local path -> regenerate-from-embedded-deck), but regeneration FAILS for light water with NotPorted. Measured cause, from LeaprDeck::unsupported_features():
    'nss = 1 (secondary-scatterer mixed-moderator merge is not ported)'
tsl-HinH2O.leapr carries a SECONDARY SCATTERER -- the oxygen in the water molecule -- so producing its law needs the mixed-moderator merge, which this workspace's LEAPR port does not implement. That work is op-b2k (LEAPR copys/skold + run() driver + mixed-moderator merge). Graphite needs no secondary scatterer, which is why it regenerates and water does not.

The fallback is kept wired on purpose: it costs nothing when it fails, and the day op-b2k lands the pincell test un-gates ITSELF with no edit to this file. Adding op-b2k as a dependency to reflect that.

Also folded out a drift risk while in there: the S(alpha,beta) build temperature is now a single TSL_TEMPERATURE_K const shared by the regeneration call and ThermalScattering::from_endf_file, instead of two 293.6 literals.

notes.content:
DONE for the carbon/graphite half; the SiC half is blocked on a newly-found data gap (op-t33q). Delivered as tests/triso_shell_thermal_scattering.rs (5 tests) plus a rewritten scope note in geometry/triso_particle.rs.

THE BEAD'S PREMISE CHANGED. It was filed saying the wiring 'needs thermal-scattering data not present on this host' and depended on the download path (op-6tz.28). The data-availability half no longer holds: all 33 ENDF/B-VIII.0 LEAPR decks are embedded in njoy-outram-park-fork as of 2026-08-14, so every law regenerates offline with no download and no host-specific path. op-6tz.28 is NOT a blocker for this any more.

DESIGN FINDING -- this was never a triso_particle.rs change. That module assigns opaque material INDICES by design and its own doc says so. A thermal law binds to a Nuclide, not a material index, via Nuclide::with_thermal_scattering. So the wiring is caller-side composition; putting deck loading inside a CSG module would break the crate's data/transport boundary (outram-mc parses no ENDF). The deliverable is therefore the worked, checked composition, which is what a caller actually needs.

MEASURED 2026-08-14 (release, this environment), barn per principal atom at 0.0253 eV:
  C in graphite : elastic 4.55555 + inelastic 0.48162 = 5.03717; free-gas C0 4.9382 -> bound 5.0372 (+2.01%). Reproduces the 5.0378 b recorded under op-nhoa against the official ENDF/B-VIII.0 TAPE, so the regenerate-from-deck path agrees with the tape path.
  C in SiC      : elastic 0.00000 + inelastic 0.13291; free-gas 4.9382 -> bound 0.1329 (-97.31%). NOT USABLE.
  Si in SiC     : elastic 0.00000 + inelastic 0.06367; free-gas Si28 1.9914 -> bound 0.0637 (-96.80%). NOT USABLE.

Root cause of the SiC gap (confirmed from the decks, not inferred): card 4 iel = 1 for graphite but 0 for both SiC decks, so stock LEAPR emits no coherent-elastic section; and the SiC decks' own comments say their coherent elastic came from MODIFIED LEAPR source (Zhu and Hawari's generalized coherent-elastic formulation). Not a defect in our port -- a capability gap. Filed as op-t33q and wired as a blocker on op-6tz.35.

The two SiC tests assert elastic == 0.0 ON PURPOSE, so closing op-t33q makes them fail and forces the docs to be updated rather than leaving inelastic-only SiC data silently in use.

NOT CLOSING outright is the wrong call either way, so: closing this bead as done for what it actually scoped (wire the bound-atom law into the shell material composition, which is now done and verified for every layer where the data exists), with the SiC data gap carried by op-t33q. Human review still owed; no transport-level TRISO result here.

description: HexLattice::from_rings builds a 2-ring lattice whose central tile [n_rings-1,n_rings-1] receives outer-ring element index 3 instead of the single inner-ring element. Confirmed for BOTH orientations at n_rings=2: with outer ring [10,11,12,13,14,15] and inner [42], universe_at(centre)=13 (=outer[3]) not 42; the inner element lands off-centre (e.g. X orientation puts it at [2,0]). The geometry methods (center_offset/get_indices/get_local_position/distance) are CORRECT — the bug is purely in the ring->tile fill walk (fill_lattice_x src/lattice.cpp:546, fill_lattice_y :598) and/or the outer-first flatten order from_rings feeds them. The existing 4-ring y notebook test did not catch it because every ring's first element AND the inner ring all share the value 1, so a mis-slotted centre still reads 1. NEEDS the canonical OpenMC src/lattice.cpp fill_lattice_x/y to diff against (not available on this build host) before fixing, per the crate's mirror-canonical-source rule. Found while adding op-6tz.31 (X round-trip test); that test and the new from_rings_3d test both deliberately avoid asserting intra-level fill placement.

notes.content: Fixed in 590b0e0. Root cause: from_rings/from_rings_3d fed outer-ring-first input to the row-order fill_lattice_x/y walk (spatial rows, not hex rings) → central element mis-placed onto an outer tile; the whole placement was a non-round-tripping permutation. Fix: geometry-derived placement (fill_level via ring_slots/tile_ring/tile_xy) — per hex-radius k, sort that ring's skewed tiles by planar angle (+x start, CCW) and map ring elements onto them; proven bijection over all hexagon tiles, so universe_at(get_indices(tile_centre)) round-trips. New tests ring_fill_round_trip_{x,y} + from_rings_3d_single_level_matches_2d; 158 lib + 27 notebook tests pass. CAVEAT: within-ring +x-start CCW angular convention is best-effort per OpenMC's 'each ring starts along +x' doc; a line-by-line diff vs openmc/lattice.py is still owed. Round-trip correctness + valid bijection verified; NOT claimed OpenMC-bit-identical.

title: MSRE digital twin — offline demonstration (depletion + fission-product migration, real-time-capable)
description:
Offline demonstration digital twin of ORNL's Molten-Salt Reactor Experiment (MSRE, 1965-69) built on the OUTRAM PARK suite. Scope per RESPONSIBLE_USE.md: OFFLINE DEMONSTRATION / V&V / education only — no operational or live-plant coupling; MSRE is a public, decommissioned benchmark (ORNL-TM / ORNL-4xxx report series), so 'real time' means a real-time-capable simulation loop replaying/assimilating the historical record, not hardware monitoring. Data-policy clean (all MSRE data open literature).

Architecture: two-tier. OFFLINE high-fidelity (MC k-eig + depletion via outram-mc-libs+njoy; CFD via outram-foam; molten-salt Gibbs FP thermochemistry) generates reduced-order tables/models. REAL-TIME tier runs a circulating-fuel point-kinetics + 1-D loop TH (tuas/tampines, which already has FLiBe + HITEC salt correlations) + lumped Xe/FP-migration model in outram-park-digital-twin-engine (egui), with a state estimator (chem-eng real-time scaffolding) assimilating replayed MSRE data — which doubles as validation.

MSRE-specific hard physics: (1) circulating fuel => delayed-neutron precursors advect out of core (flow-dependent reactivity) - the defining effect; (2) Xe-135 gas stripping; (3) FP migration into three destinations (noble gases->off-gas, noble metals->plate on graphite/Hastelloy-N, salt-seekers->dissolved/precipitate) governed by salt redox (UF3/UF4).

Phasing: P0 zero-power circulating-fuel kinetics -> P1 add TH feedback -> P2 Xe+depletion -> P3 FP migration+chemistry -> P4 data assimilation. Each phase validates against a published MSRE dataset. All AI-assisted output is untrusted draft pending human V&V.

notes.content: Implemented cyclic (periodic) patch support (2026-08-04). Representation: cyclic pairing stored as BoundaryPatch::cyclic_partner (partner patch index, half0/half1 same-local-index correspondence) + FvMesh::cyclic_couplings (Vec<CyclicCoupling> of owner<->neighbour cell couplings), derived at build time; FvMesh::periodic_1d builds a 1-D periodic ring programmatically. Coupling assembled by APPENDING one LDU face per seam pair after the internal faces (FvMatrix/FvVectorMatrix::new pre-allocate the slots so all matrices on a mesh share structure and +/- line up); laplacian(_vec)/div(_vec) fill them with the internal-face formula (coeff=Gamma*|Sf|/d_seam, d_seam=|Cf_A-C_ownerA|+|Cf_B-C_ownerB|; upwind on seam flux). fvc interpolate/sn_grad use the paired cell across the seam. Non-cyclic behaviour byte-identical. V&V (verification, untrusted AI draft pending human review): cyclic diffusion == all-internal regular-n-gon ring mesh (operators identical A.x to <1e-12; solved fields agree <1e-9); periodic advection conserves (A.ones=0) and == ring; interpolate/sn_grad/vector-Laplacian seam checks. Both gates green: --lib 284 passed, --doc 25 passed (release). Honest scope: polyMesh parser does NOT yet read cyclic neighbourPatch ordering (must wire programmatically); DIC-PCG/GAMG not tuned for the appended seam faces (use Gauss-Seidel for cyclic, which is order-independent); first-pass orthogonal seam only.

title: HTR-10 pipeline: reproducibility manifest and headless scriptable entry point
description:
Parent: op-841p. Maintainer requirement 2026-08-11: the pipeline must be REPRODUCIBLE by someone else on another machine. This is a design constraint on the architecture, not a bolt-on - it changes what each stage writes to disk.

WHAT REPRODUCIBLE MUST MEAN HERE:
1. Every stage re-runnable from committed inputs WITHOUT re-running the stage above. Each hand-off is a real on-disk artefact with its own provenance, not an in-memory value. The MGXS library in particular must be a file a human can inspect and diff.
2. A MANIFEST PER RUN recording: workspace git commit; cross-section library and version (e.g. ENDF/B-VIII.0 and the exact tape); fidelity tier (from_core LOW vs from_endf HIGH); MC RNG seed, particles per generation, inactive and active generation counts; group structure; homogenisation choice; mesh and its generation parameters; and the code path taken at each rung. A result whose data version is unknown is not reproducible.
3. Deterministic given a seed. run_keff_delta_seq is already documented as the bit-reproducible reference (crates/outram-mc-libs/src/pebble_beds/keff_delta.rs:285-295) and the rayon backend is thread-count-invariant by seed jump-ahead (:382-393). Report sigma with every MC number.
4. Scriptable, not interactive - which is what makes rung-to-rung validation automatable in CI.
5. Intermediate artefacts ARE the validation evidence. A pcm comparison between rungs means nothing if the artefacts it came from are gone.

HEADLESS ENTRY POINT: a function taking a geometry description plus a run configuration, so outram-blender can drive it as a third solver bridge (op-hzs.53). Do NOT make it test-only.

WHERE IT GOES: crates/nee_soon is the designated coupling layer (op-fr2) and its xin_wang_sp3_workflow scaffold (src/xin_wang_sp3_workflow/, 828 lines, self-declared 'scaffold only' at mod.rs:26) is already the right SHAPE - a four-stage njoy -> mc -> genfoam chain. But today nee_soon exposes exactly one real method, NeeSoon::new_prompt_excursion_model (src/lib.rs:111-131), a pass-through to Nordheim-Fuchs. There is no headless pipeline entry point anywhere in the workspace yet.

CAVEAT TO CARRY: rung 1 reproducibility is compromised until op-rbo and op-jis close. Per crates/outram-mc-libs/CLAUDE.md (maintainer decision 2026-08-06) bit-for-bit parity with OpenMC is explicitly NOT required - statistical correctness and stream separation are. Frame the manifest requirement on that standard.

title: IF97 (p,h) and (p,s) flash panic above 1073.15 K -- too low for an HTGR, and Region 5 forward eqns already exist
description:
MAINTAINER REPORT, 2026-08-13: 'the 1073k cap for ph, ps flash is too low for a htgr, which can produce very high temperature steam.'

Correct, and the situation is better than the cap implies -- most of the work is already done.

WHAT THE CAP ACTUALLY IS. 1073.15 K (800 degC) is NOT the limit of IAPWS-IF97. It is the limit of Regions 1-4.
IF97 Region 5 covers 1073.15 K to 2273.15 K at 0 < p <= 50 MPa. What Region 5 does NOT have is BACKWARD equations:
the standard provides no closed-form (p,h) -> T or (p,s) -> T there. That is the entire reason for the cap.

CURRENT BEHAVIOUR -- IT PANICS, it does not error:
  crates/tampines-steam-tables/src/interfaces/functional_programming/ph_flash_eqm/mod.rs:51
      FwdEqnRegion::Region5 => panic!("temperature: {}", REGION_5_PH_UNSUPPORTED)
  same file :141 for specific volume; ps_flash_eqm/mod.rs has the same pattern.
A panic, not a Result -- so a caller cannot recover, and this is the mechanism by which a large htgr_sim_v1
excursion dies once the steel property range was widened (see op-szmi.17, which records the failure relocating to
the steam side).

WHAT ALREADY EXISTS, and makes this tractable:
  crates/tampines-steam-tables/src/region_5_steam_at_800_plus_degc/ implements the FORWARD equations --
  v_tp_5, u_tp_5, s_tp_5, cp_tp_5, cv_tp_5, w_tp_5, kappa_tp_5, alpha_v_tp_5, plus tau_5/pi_5.
  The (p,T) flash already routes Region 5 correctly and is verified at the envelope corners
  (see pt_flash_eqm/envelope_corner_tests.rs: 1073.15 K / 50 MPa -> Region5, h = 3.926050140e6, etc).

THE FIX. Invert the forward equation numerically. At fixed p, h_tp_5(T,p) is monotone increasing in T, so a
bracketed 1-D root find over [1073.15 K, 2273.15 K] is unconditionally convergent -- bisection or Brent, no Newton
needed and no risk of stepping outside the envelope. Same for (p,s) with s_tp_5. This is the standard treatment
where IF97 gives no backward equation, and it is what other IF97 implementations do.
  - State the tolerance and the iteration cap, and return an error rather than panicking if it is not met.
  - Above 2273.15 K or 50 MPa the state is genuinely outside IF97; REFUSE it explicitly, do not extrapolate.
  - Cost: an iterative flash is much dearer than a backward equation, and the SG calls the flash per node per
    substep. Region 5 should be the exceptional branch, not the common path -- measure it and say so.

WHY IT MATTERS FOR THIS PROJECT. 1073.15 K = 800 degC. HTR-10 phase 1 (700 degC helium) stays clear. HTR-10 PHASE 2
IS 900 degC, and a once-through SG with a small pinch can put steam near the cap; the GTHTR300 line
(op-id3l.12) is hotter still. Beyond design operation, any excursion crosses it -- and today that is a hard panic
that kills the physics thread rather than a diagnosable error.

RELATED, and should be coordinated rather than duplicated:
  op-t647 (P0) -- bounds-checked IF97 facade returning Result. THIS BEAD IS THE OTHER HALF: op-t647 makes the
    boundary return an error instead of panicking; this one MOVES the boundary from 1073.15 K to 2273.15 K. Both
    are wanted, and the error-vocabulary decision in op-ffg6.1 should cover them together.
  op-szmi.17 -- records that widening the steel range relocates the failure to the steam side. This is that side.

notes.content:
CORRECTION to the description, 2026-08-13: I wrote that ps_flash_eqm 'has the same pattern' as ph_flash_eqm. It does not, and the difference matters for how each is fixed. Verified:

  ph_flash_eqm/mod.rs -- 2 sites, explicit panic! with a named constant:
      :51   FwdEqnRegion::Region5 => panic!("temperature: {}", REGION_5_PH_UNSUPPORTED)
      :141  same for specific volume
    So (p,h) is a DELIBERATE, documented refusal.

  ps_flash_eqm/mod.rs -- 2 sites, bare todo!():
      :64   FwdEqnRegion::Region5 => todo!("region 5 ps flash not implemented")
      :154  FwdEqnRegion::Region5 => todo!("ps flash not implemented for region 5")
    So (p,s) is UNIMPLEMENTED rather than refused, and the file's own docs acknowledge it at :463
    ('todo! panics in t_ps_eqm/v_ps_eqm').
    That file also carries two further unconditional panics, :828 'p,s point is outside pressure range' and
    :833 'p,s point below 273.15K' -- both are validity refusals that should return an error, and belong with
    op-t647 rather than here.

Both still panic and both still cap the useful envelope at 1073.15 K, so the bead's substance stands. The fix is
also the same numerically -- a bracketed 1-D root find on the monotone forward equation, h_tp_5 for (p,h) and
s_tp_5 for (p,s), over [1073.15 K, 2273.15 K]. Note s_tp_5 is already present and already routed on the (p,s) side
(ps_flash_eqm:264+ dispatches Region 5 for u, h, cp, cv, w), so the forward half is in place there too.

SUGGESTED ORDER: convert the two todo!()s to the same explicit, named refusal the (p,h) side uses FIRST -- a small,
safe change that makes the boundary honest and removes two todo!() panics -- then implement the inversion for both
together.

title: htgr_sim_v1: measure the per-tick physics compute cost
description:
PREREQUISITE for op-v5zb. We know 1:1 with wall time is structurally unreachable (fixed sleep after compute); we do NOT know by how much. Measure before choosing a fix.

Cheapest read, no new code: time the existing test

  cargo test --release -p outram-park-digital-twin-engine --examples \
    the_whole_plant_steps_at_the_gui_timestep

It advances 20 000 steps at 1 ms = 20 s of simulated time through HtgrPlant::step, the same call the GUI physics thread makes. Wall seconds / 20 = the compute-only real-time ratio, excluding the 10 ms sleep. Then the achieved GUI ratio is 10/(10 + 10*per_step_ms).

Also worth splitting out, since it decides which fix is right: how much of the per-step cost is the steam generator. SteamGeneratorConfig::substep is 0.0125 s and the exchanger accumulates, so only ~0.8 array advances land per 10 ms tick -- the three coupled arrays may be a spike every 12-13 substeps rather than a uniform cost. chem-eng: IntegralController RampResponseRealTime loses precision on long real-time runs
description:
FOUND 2026-08-11 while doing op-fm5. NOT measured yet -- this is a code-reading finding, so it needs a measurement before it is acted on.

alpha_nightly/controllers/integral_controller/mod.rs, RampResponseRealTime::set_user_input_and_calc (:165-204). The integrator is kept as a line, y(t) = gradient_gain * t + offset, and each input change updates BOTH terms:

    gradient_change = a_i * k_c / tau_i
    offset_change   = -a_i * time_of_input * k_c / tau_i

That is already O(1) per step, so op-fm5 does not touch it. The concern is numerical, not algorithmic: offset accumulates a term proportional to the ABSOLUTE simulation time of every past input change, so for a long-running real-time simulation both 'gradient_gain * t' and 'offset' grow without bound while their SUM stays bounded. That is textbook catastrophic cancellation -- the significant digits available to the integrator output shrink as the run goes on. A real-time twin is exactly the use case where t gets large.

WHAT TO DO:
1. MEASURE FIRST. Drive an IntegralController for, say, 1e6 to 1e8 seconds of simulated time with a changing input, and compare against a Kahan-summed or periodically-rebased reference. Report the actual relative error growth. Do not act on the hunch alone.
2. If confirmed, the fix is to carry the accumulated integral directly (I += k_c/tau_i * u * dt, or the exact ZOH equivalent) rather than reconstructing it from a slope and an intercept, or to rebase the time origin periodically.

Relates to op-fm5 (transfer-function O(1) rewrite) and op-1z3o.14 (real-time execution).

title: cfmesh: fix tet-primal mesh quality — it is the real non-orthogonality source, not the dual
description:
Mesh non-orthogonality in the cfmesh pipeline traces to the TET PRIMAL, not to the dual operation or the solver. Fix the tet mesher.

EVIDENCE THAT THE DUAL IS EXACT (measured 2026-08-07, test re-run and passing):
crates/outram-foam-mesh/tests/poly_dual_mesh.rs:212 dual_quality_is_exactly_orthogonal_on_a_uniform_block asserts max_non_ortho_deg < 1e-12, mean < 1e-12, max_skewness < 1e-12 (:226-232). Re-ran `cargo test -p outram-foam-mesh --release --test poly_dual_mesh`: 3^3 block -> 64 dual cells, non-orthogonality max 0.000 deg / mean 0.000 deg, skewness 0.0000, verdict GOOD; 4^3 block identical. The metric itself is closed-form validated in crates/outram-foam-mesh/src/mesh_quality.rs:600 (Cartesian block = 0) and :651 (sheared block matches atan(k) at 45/60/86 deg to 1e-10).

IMPORTANT CORRECTION -- that test is NOT of cfmesh's dual. It exercises outram_foam_mesh::poly_dual_mesh, the CELL-CENTRE polyDualMesh (poly_dual_mesh.rs:25-41). cfmesh uses a DIFFERENT algorithm, the median/Donald vertex-centred dual (crates/outram-park-fork-cfmesh/src/dual.rs:48-70, which says so explicitly). cfmesh's four dual tests (dual.rs:441, :474, :499, :543) check only closure, volume conservation, boundary match and face count. So "the dual is exact" is MEASURED for outram-foam-mesh's dual and only INFERRED for cfmesh's.
=> First sub-task: add an orthogonality test for cfmesh's own median dual on a uniform block. Until that exists the diagnosis is one step short of proven.

WHAT IS KNOWN ABOUT THE TET PRIMAL:
- crates/outram-park-fork-cfmesh/src/tet.rs:93 pub fn tetrahedralize(mesh: &VolumeMesh) -- centroid subdivision (every cell -> cell.face.edge tets). description:
Maintainer request, 2026-08-13 07:4x. Assigned to the agent already holding the htgr_sim_v1 app files this session.

Requirement: the simulator must advance simulated time at wall-clock rate -- 1 s of plant time per 1 s of real time -- rather than free-running as fast as the physics steps, or drifting from wall clock.

Design constraints handed to the agent:
- Decouple physics dt from egui frame rate. Fixed-dt accumulator: accumulate wall-clock elapsed, step a whole number of fixed dt steps, keep the remainder. Do NOT scale physics dt to frame time -- a variable dt changes the integration and this plant has stiff couplings.
- Clamp the catch-up so a backgrounded/stalled app cannot attempt thousands of steps in one frame. When the clamp binds, simulated time falls behind real time VISIBLY rather than silently.
- Pacing is a scheduling concern; plant physics must not be changed to accommodate it.

META_LEMA_ANI: the two hypothesis branches' shear triples are exchanged
description:
In mfront/META_LEMA_ANI.mfront lines 151-158, the AXISYMMETRICAL and 3-D branches assign the Hill coefficient array differently, and the NORMAL components are self-consistent: AXIS uses axes (r,z,theta) with normals {MRR, MZZ, MTT}, 3-D uses (r,theta,z) with normals {MRR, MTT, MZZ}. Correct for each branch's own axis ordering.

The SHEAR triples, however, are exactly each other's: AXIS assigns {MRT, MRZ, MTZ} and 3-D assigns {MRZ, MRT, MTZ}. Swapping axes 2 and 3 between the branches should swap the first two shear slots too, so each branch appears to carry the other's shear ordering. That is the signature of a copy-paste transposition rather than a convention.

NOT SETTLED, and here is exactly why. Whether this is a defect depends on TFEL's hillTensor<N,real>(F,G,H,L,M,N) argument-to-shear-slot convention. Classical Hill pairs L with yz, M with zx, N with xy; if TFEL instead pairs L with xy the analysis changes from 'swapped' to 'cyclically rotated'. TFEL is a separate project and its headers are not present in this container (no Hill.hxx anywhere on the filesystem, no /usr/include/TFEL). Obtaining TFEL, or an authoritative statement of hillTensor's convention, is what closes this.

The metallurgy port reproduces the upstream ordering verbatim in HillAnisotropy::from_aster_3d, and names its struct fields by tensor slot so a caller can bypass the ambiguity. Do not 'fix' this without settling the convention first.

title: cfmesh: hardcoded /tmp in mesh_studio example + temp-dir cleanup leak (claim corrected)
description:
Recorded with the original claim CORRECTED -- the /tmp-exhaustion framing did not survive verification, but two smaller real defects did.

ORIGINAL CLAIM: cfmesh's polyMesh round-trip test resolves its temp dir from the system temp dir and fails on a small or full /tmp -- an Android/Termux hazard.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY TRUE (verified 2026-08-07):
- Location confirmed: crates/outram-park-fork-cfmesh/src/foam.rs:171, in test write_polymesh_disk_round_trip (:167-178):
      let dir = std::env::temp_dir().join(format!("cfmesh_polymesh_rt_{}", std::process::id()));
- BUT the data written is trivial. The mesh is cartesian_box(..., [2,2,2]) (:170) -- 8 cells, 12 internal + 24 boundary faces, 27 points (asserted :174-175). The written polyMesh is a few kilobytes. "Fails on a small /tmp" does not hold; only a completely full or unwritable temp dir would fail it.
- AND it is not hardcoded to /tmp. std::env::temp_dir() on Unix honours $TMPDIR, falling back to /tmp. Termux sets TMPDIR to its own prefix tmp, so on-device this resolves to Termux's writable temp. (Not verified on an actual device.)

TWO REAL DEFECTS THAT REMAIN:
1. A genuinely hardcoded /tmp exists ELSEWHERE: crates/outram-park-fork-cfmesh/examples/mesh_studio/main.rs:130
       export_dir: "/tmp/mesh_studio/polyMesh".into(),
   That one ignores $TMPDIR and would be wrong on Termux. (The example is Android-gated at :32-49, so it does not break the build -- but the path is still wrong for any non-/tmp TMPDIR, including some CI sandboxes.) Fix: use std::env::temp_dir().
2. Cleanup leak: foam.rs:177 `let _ = std::fs::remove_dir_all(&dir);` sits AFTER the assertions at :174-176, so a failing assertion leaks the directory. Fix: scope-guard the cleanup.

Note also that foam.rs has no target_os = "android" gate anywhere in src/ (only #[cfg(test)] at :103); the crate's only Android gates are Cargo.toml:36 (dev-deps) and examples/mesh_studio/main.rs:32/35/49. That is fine for this test as written, but worth knowing.

title: TurbineVisual: a state variant carrying BOTH a shaft speed and a steam state
description:
Found while wiring htgr_sim_v1's turbine to a real torque balance (op-eukg). TurbineVisualState has exactly two variants: SteamGenerator (spins, casing_temperature() returns None -> neutral grey) and SteamThermo (casing coloured by inlet steam temperature, rotor_angle() returns ZERO). A plant that knows BOTH -- which htgr_sim_v1 now does, it computes a shaft speed AND a live steam state -- has to give one up. htgr_sim_v1 chose rotation and lost the casing colour.

Suggested fix (maintainer's call, engine crate src/components/turbine.rs): either a third variant carrying (ThreePhaseElectricGeneratorTurbine, Turbine), or a builder-style .with_casing_temperature(T) override on TurbineVisual that the generator variant can use. The second is smaller and keeps the enum honest about what each PHYSICS source knows.

Also noted while there, lower priority: TurbineVisual defines the rotor phase as theta = omega(t) * t. That is the true accumulated angle only for constant omega; during a speed transient the drawn phase advances at omega + t*domega/dt, which over-states the rotation during a run-up. An app-owned accumulated-angle input (integrating omega) would be faithful; the current form is documented but not exact.

kovan: library did not build for Android -- kopitiam-pdf's default kpdf feature pulled rfd
description:
FOUND AND FIXED 2026-08-31 while running the mandated Android proxy check for op-9vo6.2.

SYMPTOM: cargo check -p kovan --lib --target aarch64-linux-android failed with 12 errors in rfd v0.17.2 ('error: could not compile rfd'). This is a violation of CLAUDE.md's Android/Termux HARD RULE, which puts kovan's library plus its kovan-cli and kovan-tui binaries explicitly IN scope (only the kovan GUI binary is exempt, behind the gui feature).

CAUSE: crates/kovan/Cargo.toml:107 declared

    kopitiam-pdf = "0.3.1"

unconditionally -- NOT inside the [target.'cfg(not(target_os = "android"))'.dependencies] block at line 180. kopitiam-pdf 0.3.1's feature table is default = ["kpdf"], kpdf = ["dep:eframe", "dep:egui", "dep:rfd"], so taking it with default features dragged eframe/egui/rfd into the LIBRARY's unconditional dependency graph. cargo tree -p kovan --target aarch64-linux-android -i rfd confirmed the single path: rfd v0.17.2 <- kopitiam-pdf v0.3.1 <- kovan.

FIX (one line):

    kopitiam-pdf = { version = "0.3.1", default-features = false }

kovan only uses kopitiam_pdf::mupdf::{PdfDocument, rasterize_page, page_to_stext, interpret::Processor}, which is core to the crate and NOT behind the kpdf feature -- kpdf only adds the standalone-shell dependencies.
