title: teddy0@arch-aftershock-rapid-glass-S267454
HTR-10 neutronics: multifidelity pipeline (MC -> MGXS -> GeN-Foam -> PRKE)
description:
Maintainer direction 2026-08-11. HTR-10 core physics is to be built as a reproducible multifidelity pipeline in which EACH RUNG IS VALIDATED AGAINST THE RUNG ABOVE IT, not four unrelated codes.

  meshing -> [1] rigorous Monte Carlo (outram-mc-libs/pebble_beds)
          -> [2] MGXS generation
          -> [3] deterministic multiphysics (GeN-Foam, decided over bedok)
          -> [4] PRKE + decay heat (teh-o-prke)

SCOPING DOCUMENT: docs/reactor-scoping/htr10-neutronics.md - read it before starting any child. It carries the benchmark definitions, the capability audit with file:line evidence, the hand-off data at each interface, the validation chain, the blockers and the ordered plan.

TWO HARD ARCHITECTURAL CONSTRAINTS:
1. REPRODUCIBLE. Every hand-off is an on-disk artefact with provenance; every run writes a manifest (workspace commit, XS library + version, fidelity tier, MC seed, particle/generation counts, group structure, homogenisation choice, mesh + its generation parameters); MC is bit-identical for a fixed seed; the chain is drivable headlessly.
2. FRONTEND-DRIVABLE. Entry point takes a geometry description plus a run configuration, so outram-blender can drive it as a third solver bridge (op-hzs.53). Not test-only.

VALIDATION CHAIN, every comparison quoted in pcm WITH the MC statistical uncertainty:
- rung 2/3 k_eff vs rung 1 k_eff on the same problem
- rung 4 beta_eff / Lambda / reactivity coefficients vs those collapsed directly from the rung 3 flux
- whole chain vs IAEA-TECDOC-1382 B1/B2/B3/B4 and the measured 123.06 cm loading

DO NOT report a k_eff, a pcm discrepancy or a beta_eff that was not computed. Nothing here is validated.

title: MGXS extraction: MC tallies -> collapsed group constants -> genfoam
description:
Split out of op-375p / gh:#41, where it was only a comment. Concrete work with a clear verification, not scoping. gh:#42 https://github.com/theodoreOnzGit/outram-park-backend/issues/42

THE PROBLEM. CE Monte Carlo cannot run inside a coupled transient, so pebble-bed and MSR multiphysics needs collapsed multigroup constants a diffusion/SP3/SN solver can march. This workspace has both ends of that chain and none of the middle.

SURVEYED 2026-09-04, three findings.

  1. NO GENERATION PATH. outram_mc_libs::physics::physics_mg defines Mgxs and MgxsLibrary and run_keff_mg consumes them, but Mgxs::new has NO call site anywhere outside its own definition. Every multigroup library must currently be typed in by hand. The MC can use group constants and cannot produce them.
  2. NO MGXS TALLIES. Generation needs flux and reaction-rate tallies binned by energy group and by zone/material, plus a group-to-group scatter matrix. None of those scores exist.
  3. TWO INCOMPATIBLE TYPES, no converter. outram_mc_libs::Mgxs is transport-flavoured (total, scatter matrix, nu-fission, chi). genfoam::xs::GroupConstants is diffusion-flavoured (diffusion_coefficient in m, nu_sigma_f, sigma_pow = kappa-Sigma_f in J/m, sigma_removal, chi_prompt, chi_delayed).

Three steps then, and the third carries real physics: D = 1/(3 Sigma_tr), removal = absorption + out-scatter, and a prompt/delayed chi split needing delayed-neutron data the transport-side Mgxs does not carry.

THE DETAIL THAT DECIDES THE DESIGN. genfoam::xs::NuclearDataOneEnergy already exposes get(parameters, is_parametrize) with a poly_spline_mode — genfoam ALREADY supports cross sections parametrised on state. So the deliverable is not one library at one state point but XS tables over state: temperature, density, and for a pebble bed burnup. That is what multiphysics needs, because Doppler feedback is the whole point of a coupled transient and a single-state library cannot express it. The consumer anticipated this; the producer does not exist.

SCOPE.
  1. MGXS tallies in outram-mc-libs — flux, absorption, nu-fission, kappa-fission, group-to-group scatter matrix, binned by group and by zone/material. LOAD-BEARING; the rest is arithmetic.
  2. Flux-weighted collapse to Mgxs, gated on the existing Mgxs::consistency_residual.
  3. Bridge Mgxs -> GroupConstants. DOCUMENT the diffusion-coefficient convention chosen (transport-corrected vs out-scatter) — silently picking one is how a deterministic solution quietly disagrees with its own MC reference.
  4. Parametrised libraries over a state grid, emitted in the NuclearDataOneEnergy spline form.
  5. VERIFICATION: k-eff on one geometry by three routes — CE Monte Carlo, run_keff_mg on the collapsed library, genfoam diffusion on the bridged constants. Agreement within statistics is the test; disagreement localises to the step that caused it.

WHY IT MATTERS. Pebble bed: double heterogeneity means constants must be generated on TRISO-in-pebble-in-bed geometry, not a homogenised smear — pebble_beds::delta_tracking is the CE side. MSR: outram-park-fork-moltres IS a multigroup diffusion code with precursor drift and needs a salt library re-collapsed as salt temperature and density move.

NOT IN SCOPE: new transport physics; everything composes what exists. No V&V claimed — step 5 is the verification and until it passes a collapsed library is a number, not a validated one.

Related: op-375p / gh:#41 (neutronics API scope), op-jyyp (HTR-10 simulator).

title: reference-data: tsl-SiinSiC.endf (MAT 43) still missing -- silicon half of the TRISO SiC layer has no elastic channel
description:
The maintainer committed four ENDF/B-VIII.0 thermal tapes on 2026-08-14 (commit ffef0fb76f): tsl-CinSiC, tsl-crystalline-graphite, tsl-reactor-graphite-10P, tsl-reactor-graphite-30P. tsl-SiinSiC.endf (MAT 43) was NOT among them.

CONSEQUENCE. Carbon in 3C-SiC now has a usable coherent-elastic channel from its tape (2.94078 b at 0.0253 eV, see op-t33q). Silicon in 3C-SiC does not: regenerating tsl-SiinSiC from its embedded deck gives elastic 0.00000 + inelastic 0.06367 = 0.06367 b against a free-gas Si-28 value of 1.9914 b, i.e. -96.8%. A TRISO SiC layer wired today would be correct on its carbon half and 3% of the truth on its silicon half.

NEEDED. tsl-SiinSiC.endf from the same ENDF/B-VIII.0 thermal_scatt source (https://www.nndc.bnl.gov/endf-b8.0/download.html), dropped into reference-data/endf/ with its row filled in the README provenance table (a placeholder row is already there). Maintainer said on 2026-08-17 they would upload it.

Note this environment cannot fetch it: GH issue #21 records that the egress policy denies www-nds.iaea.org (403), which is why these tapes are committed rather than downloaded.

Blocks a physically correct TRISO SiC layer alongside op-t33q.

notes.content:
SUPPLIED 2026-08-17. The maintainer pushed tsl-SiinSiC.endf (MAT 43, ZA=143, AWR=27.844, 7,243,180 B) plus the evaluator's tsl-SiinSiC.readme in commit cdbea87c9e. Both were landed under crates/njoy-outram-park-fork/src/leapr/decks/ -- inside the `include` allowlist, so unlike the old tests/resources/ location they would have shipped -- and were relocated to reference-data/endf/ in 605d7a7383. Provenance rows filled in.

Measured at 0.0253 eV / 296 K, barn per principal atom:
  Si in SiC: elastic 2.94078 + inelastic 0.06615 = 3.00693  (free-gas Si-28 1.9914 -> +51.0%)
against the deck-regenerated 0.00000 + 0.06367 = 0.06367 (-96.8%). The elastic channel is present and the bound law is now above the free-gas value, as a bound crystalline scatterer should be.

FINDING, and it is the one that matters for whoever wires the SiC layer: MAT 43 and MAT 44 carry BYTE-IDENTICAL MF=7/MT=2 sections -- 1044 records each, differing only in the header line's ZA/AWR (verified by extracting MT=2 from both tapes and diffing columns 1-66; 1043 of 1044 lines match exactly). Not a parser bug and not an evaluator error: coherent elastic scattering is a property of the 3C-SiC lattice as a whole, not of one sublattice, so one structure factor is delivered in both materials.

Consequence: a transport code that builds a SiC region from both S(alpha,beta) materials and sums their elastic channels DOUBLE-COUNTS the Bragg scattering. MT=2 must be attributed to the compound once -- assigned to one sublattice or split -- not carried by both nuclides. Written up in reference-data/endf/README.md.

Closing: the tape is here. The double-counting question belongs to op-t33q / op-6tz.35 where the layer actually gets wired.

title: kovan lit: ingest HTML sources, not just PDF
description:
kovan lit import only accepts PDFs. A great deal of open-access literature is HTML-first, so those sources cannot enter the archive at all today.

TRIGGERING CASE, 2026-08-12: https://file.scirp.org/Html/4-1090017_21248.htm — 'Gearbox Scheme in High Temperature Reactor Helium Gas Turbine System', Tsinghua INET, 2012. A legitimate HTR-10 source (phase-two helium gas-turbine cycle) that had to be read with curl and a regex because kovan could not take it. The workspace CLAUDE.md mandates kovan for document management, so a format it cannot read is a hole in the mandated workflow, not a minor inconvenience.

WHAT IS WANTED: kovan lit import accepting an HTML file or a URL, producing the same KovanDocument + markdown pair it produces for a PDF, so HTML sources land in the archive with their metadata and provenance intact rather than as loose scraped text.

DESIGN NOTES:

  - The crate already depends on pulldown-cmark for the Markdown side. HTML ->
    Markdown needs an HTML parser; prefer a pure-Rust one that does not break
    the Android build (see the workspace Android/Termux rule) and does not drag
    in a C dependency.
  - Boilerplate stripping is the real work, not tag removal. A publisher page is
    mostly navigation, journal chrome, sidebars and script. The triggering case
    was 54 kB of HTML for a few kB of article. Extracting the ARTICLE and
    discarding the furniture is what makes the result citable rather than noise.
  - Metadata is usually better in HTML than in PDF: look for citation_title,
    citation_author, citation_doi, citation_date meta tags (most publishers emit
    them), plus JSON-LD. That could give kovan cleaner titles and DOIs than its
    PDF path currently extracts — note the PDF path produced 'PII: S0029-5493(02)00182-6'
    as a title for one of today's papers, which is the file's PII, not its title.
  - If a URL is accepted directly, record the retrieval URL and date in the
    KovanDocument. Provenance for a web source is weaker than for a PDF and the
    document should say when it was fetched.

WATCH THE DATA POLICY: fetching a URL makes it easy to pull in material whose
licence has not been checked. HTML ingestion should NOT imply the result is
committable — the open/proprietary split still applies, and a publisher's HTML
is no more redistributable than its PDF.

Related: op-zo7a (kovan lit import loses its output files when piped).

title: kovan-gui: PDF reader renders embedded /Annots (Okular highlights/notes) natively
description:
Follow-up to op-gv19 (kovan-native annotations) and GitHub issue #30 -- the
maintainer noticed annotations made in Okular don't show up in kovan's PDF
reader at all. Diagnosis: kopitiam-pdf's rasterize_page/hayro never read or
draw a page's /Annots array; kovan's own "Annotation" feature (op-x9qn) is a
separate, kovan-native in-memory overlay unrelated to the PDF's embedded
annotation objects.

Tried native-in-kovan first (per explicit maintainer direction), fell back
to inspecting Poppler/Okular source only for license verification and
reference -- no code vendored, since kopitiam-pdf's already-public
PdfDocument/Object API turned out to be sufficient. Implemented:

- crates/kovan/src/digitiser/gui/desktop/pdf_annots.rs (new): reads /Annots
  per page via PdfDocument::page/resolve_get/Object (all public), for
  Highlight/Underline/StrikeOut/Squiggly/Text/Popup/FreeText/Square/Circle/
  Line/Ink -- geometry (/Rect, /QuadPoints, /L, /InkList), colour (/C, /IC,
  reusing kopitiam_pdf's own gray_to_rgb/cmyk_to_rgb), opacity (/CA),
  contents/author (/Contents, /T, PDF text-string decoding), and /F
  Hidden/NoView flag filtering. Skips Link/Widget/other subtypes.
- Independent re-derivation of the PDF-user-space -> RENDER_DPI
  texture-pixel-space transform (kopitiam-pdf's own page_ctm is
  pub(crate)), self-validated against a REAL rasterize_page render in
  tests -- caught a genuine width/height-swap bug in the /Rotate 90/270
  branches that a square-page test would have missed (fixed with a
  deliberately non-square test fixture).
- Wired into pdf_reader.rs: drawn as an overlay under kovan's own
  annotations in both single-page and continuous-scroll mode, with a hover
  tooltip (Contents + author) in single-page mode.

Known limitation, filed upstream: this draws a geometry+colour
APPROXIMATION, not the annotation's real /AP appearance stream --
kopitiam-pdf's content-stream interpreter (Processor::new/run_stream) is
pub(crate), so kovan can't execute it. Filed as kopitiam#69
(https://github.com/theodoreOnzGit/kopitiam/issues/69), tracked here as
op-5xcq (closed -- filing was the task; the upstream fix is a future bead
once kopitiam#69 ships).

Verified: cargo test --release -p kovan --features gui --lib (209 passed,
incl. 5 new pdf_annots tests) and cargo check --workspace --lib --tests
(clean). No manual GUI click-test -- same headless-sandbox wgpu-surface
limitation already flagged on op-95x6.

notes.content: Reopened in effect by op-k1nt: the /Annots reader shipped in 8975b176 is correct, but annotations were still invisible in the GUI. Root cause is upstream -- kopitiam-pdf's rasterize_page poisons the object cache with pre-incremental-update objects, so the reader gets the stale /Annots array for any Okular-saved (incrementally updated) PDF. Filed kopitiam#70; diagnostics + failing-coverage analysis pushed as 0ea169c3. Workaround and regression fixture tracked in op-k1nt.

htgr_sim_v1 schematic: hot gas duct does not connect to the steam generator's bottom-right duct pipe
description:
Maintainer report, 2026-08-13 (filed outside active hours; no code work done).

In the htgr_sim_v1 GUI schematic, the hot gas duct should connect correctly to the duct pipe at the BOTTOM RIGHT of the steam generator. It currently does not line up.

Scope when picked up during active hours:
- Locate the schematic layout code for htgr_sim_v1 (tampines example / digital-twin engine GUI components) and the anchor points used for the hot gas duct and the steam generator's bottom-right duct pipe.
- Fix the connection so the duct terminates on the SG duct-pipe port rather than floating / mis-aligned.
- Purely a schematic/visual routing fix; no plant physics change intended.
- Check the same anchor convention is not broken for the cold-leg / return duct while fixing it.

Related: op-szmi.5 (finish the GUI to CIET v2 standard), op-wqk.9.4 (schematic omits PipeVisual).

notes.content:
FIXED 2026-08-13. It was not a small offset.

ROOT CAUSE: SteamGeneratorVisual::draw_helical_coil paints its hot-gas nozzle as a stub on the vessel's BOTTOM RIGHT
(cx + 0.02w .. cx + 0.68w over y(0.925)..y(0.955)), feeding the bottom of the centre tube the hot helium rises through.
The schematic ignored that and routed the duct to sg_rect().left() + 1.0 at reactor.top() + 0.66 * reactor.height() --
an elevation set by the REACTOR's plenum, on the SG's blank LEFT flank. Measured miss: 105.31 pt horizontal,
130.17 pt vertical. A hardcoded endpoint never tied to the SG's own geometry.

SEARCH: no generic port/anchor/router helper exists in the engine. The convention that does exist is local to
schematic.rs -- reactor_rect()/sg_rect()/pump_discharge() reproduce each widget's own letterbox and nozzle fractions.
The three other SG nozzles already followed it; only the hot duct did not. Followed the existing convention rather than
inventing a second one. HelicalCoil has exactly one consumer, so the shared widget was not touched.

FIX: new derived anchors in schematic.rs -- reactor_duct_nozzle() and an SgNozzles struct (cold_gas_out, steam_out,
feed_in, hot_gas_in) computed from sg_rect() with the artwork's own fractions, plus hot_gas_duct_path() -> [Pos2; 6].
The stub points AWAY from the reactor so the duct cannot be straight: cross-vessel leg at plenum elevation, down clear
of the cold-return riser, under the feedwater header, up past the SG, back into the nozzle from the right. Three magic
numbers (370.0, 390.0, 585.0) hoisted into named constants; NOZZLE_SEAM_OVERLAP = 3.0 for the joint.

COLD LEG CHECKED AND UNCHANGED, as requested: the_cold_leg_anchors_are_unchanged pins cold gas out (514.955, 175.828),
steam out (621.261, 197.207), feedwater in (514.955, 516.865) -- identical to the previous inline expressions.

VERIFIED NUMERICALLY (6 new tests): nozzle tip (621.261, 534.171), duct end (618.261, 534.171) -- 3.000 pt inboard,
0.000 pt off centreline; all 5 legs axis-aligned; no leg intersects the SG rect inflated by half the pipe width
(closest 46.40 pt below, 48.22 pt right).

NOT VERIFIED VISUALLY -- headless, no display. ONE DELIBERATE COMPROMISE for the maintainer to eyeball: the duct riser
CROSSES THE FEEDWATER HEADER at (653.3, 585.0). It is the only run-over-run crossing in the schematic and is
unavoidable -- the header sweeps the plant's full width at an elevation the duct must climb through. Documented in the
code, deliberately not asserted against.

notes.content:
VISUALLY CONFIRMED BY THE MAINTAINER, 2026-08-13: 'hot gas duct looks right.'

This closes the one gap the fix could not verify itself. The numeric tests pinned the endpoint to the nozzle
(3.000 pt inboard, 0.000 pt off centreline) and proved the legs axis-aligned and clear of the SG rect, but nothing

CRITICAL: classifying a paper into a topic/project with no backing directory makes it disappear
description: GH issue #35 checkpoint SS6-7. Confirmed root cause: EntityConfig::with_topics/with_projects (used by both ingest::ingest AND wiki.rs's new classify_form, op-j3ib) only writes a slash-path STRING into kovan.toml's [classification] -- neither creates the corresponding topics/<path>/kovan.toml or projects/<path>/kovan.toml collection entity. KnowledgeIndex::papers_in(path) would still find the paper by that string, but KnowledgeIndex::children_of(parent) only lists DIRECT CHILDREN THAT EXIST AS REAL DIRECTORIES -- so if no collection entity exists at that path, nothing in the Wiki tree ever links to it, and the paper is permanently unreachable by drill-down (silently, no error). Reproduction: ingest or reclassify a paper with topics=['htgrs/neutronics'] into a fresh root with no topics/htgrs/ directory -- it vanishes from Wiki even though it's still in papers/ and in the index. Fix per the checkpoint's own suggested invariant (S6): 'Classification changes where a paper appears. It must never determine whether a paper exists or is discoverable' -- create the required topic/project collection hierarchy transactionally when classifying into a path that doesn't exist yet (one EntityConfig::topic()/collection().save() per missing path segment, parents first), rather than silently writing a dangling classification. This affects ingest.rs's IngestChoice handling AND wiki.rs's classify_form (op-j3ib) -- both write raw topics/projects strings the same way.

notes.content: Implemented in commit 944e73ab (develop).

outram-foam-basic-lib minimise.rs understates probe-reuse deviation: measured up to the stopping-bracket width, not 1e-16
description:
Measured 2026-08-13 while doing op-uyi3, in tampines-steam-tables, release.

crates/outram-foam-basic-lib/src/math/minimise.rs argues in its module doc that switching from recompute-both to probe reuse perturbs results at the ~1e-16 relative level, and quantifies the effect only on the BRACKET WIDTH (2.334157e-6 relative at k=80, '4e-22 absolute'), concluding it 'has no effect on the accuracy of the answer'.

The conclusion is right. The magnitude is understated for the LOCATED ABSCISSA, which is what callers actually consume.

Measured in tampines-steam-tables by running both forms side by side over 158 real IAPWS-IF97 golden-section searches (tests/golden_section_shared_search.rs::probe_reuse_moves_the_choke_far_below_the_stopping_rule), all three bracket shapes, 1 Pa stopping rule, brackets of order 1e5-1e7 Pa:
  worst |dp*|      = 5.990479e-1 Pa
  worst |dp*|/p    = 4.604111e-8
  worst |dG*|/G    = 3.429708e-13
and across the crate's full Zaloudek suite the largest observed move was 3 Pa on a 10.356 MPa choke (2.9e-7 relative).

That is ~8 orders larger than the 1e-16 the module doc implies, and it is the expected behaviour rather than a bug in the algorithm: a last-bit difference in a probe position can flip the comparison on a near-flat objective, or change which iteration first trips the stopping test, and the returned midpoint then shifts by up to about the stopping-bracket width. The answer stays within the tolerance the caller asked for -- which is the honest claim -- but 'differs in the last bits' is not.

Suggested fix: in the module doc's probe-reuse section, separate the two claims. (1) bracket width deviates from W0*gr^k by up to 2.3e-6 relative at k=80 (already measured, keep). (2) the LOCATED ABSCISSA can differ between the two forms by up to ~the requested x-tolerance, not by ~eps; add a measurement on MinSettings-scale tolerances rather than inferring it.

This bead is a documentation-accuracy issue, not a request to change the algorithm: probe reuse is the correct form and should stay. Filed from tampines-steam-tables, which was not permitted to edit outram-foam-basic-lib in that session.

title: root@vm
dwsim-libs: lmtd() has an unguarded 0/0 when both end temperature differences are equal
description:
Found 2026-08-13 while building the zoned-LMTD temperature-cross remedy for htgr_sim_v1.

crates/outram-park-fork-dwsim-libs/src/heat_exchanger/lmtd.rs -- the log-mean is
  (dT1 - dT2) / ln(dT1/dT2)
When dT1 == dT2 the numerator and the logarithm are both zero, giving 0/0 = NaN. The correct limit is
dT_lm -> dT1, which is elementary but not implemented.

THIS IS NOT AN EDGE CASE HERE. A balanced counter-flow zone -- equal capacity rates on both sides -- hits it
EXACTLY, and that is a normal operating condition, not a contrived input. The zoned-LMTD remedy guarded it locally
and documented the workaround rather than editing the dwsim crate, so the defect is still live for every other
caller.

FIX: return dT1 when |dT1 - dT2| is below a relative tolerance, per the standard limit. Add a test at exactly equal
end differences.

Also worth checking while in there: whether the same pattern appears in f_correction.rs or ntu_effectiveness.rs,
since ports in this workspace tend to share defects.

kovan: DECISION -- OCR tooling/policy for table digitisation
description:
Split from op-9c2e (GitHub issue #30, first comment: 'For tables it's the same, draw box, right click, digitise with OCR, check values then option to export csv or copy/paste'). Depends on op-6ez3 (needs a rendered page region to OCR against).

TENSION TO RESOLVE EXPLICITLY: this workspace's KOVAN design principles (docs/kovan.md 'Deterministic First') and the root CLAUDE.md's graph-digitiser rule both lean hard offline-deterministic/no-ML ('there is no tick-label OCR (no ML, per KOVAN's offline-deterministic rule)' -- root CLAUDE.md, 'Graph digitisation' section). Table OCR is explicitly what that rule has so far excluded from the plot digitiser. The maintainer is now asking for it for TABLES specifically, which is new ground for this crate and needs an explicit decision, not a silent exception.

WHAT NEEDS DECIDING:
- OCR engine choice: candidates include Tesseract (via a Rust binding -- C dependency, licensing to check, Android/Termux story), or an offline Rust-native OCR (maturity/accuracy trade-off), or deferring pending a cloud/API choice explicitly ruled out by this crate's local-first principle unless the maintainer says otherwise.
- Whether/how this fits 'Deterministic First' -- OCR output is inherently probabilistic/model-dependent in a way the rest of KOVAN is not; the maintainer's own spec already anticipates this with 'digitise with OCR, CHECK VALUES then option to export' -- i.e. human review is mandatory before export, matching the existing digitiser's UNREVIEWED/reviewed pattern (crates/kovan-literature/src/digitiser/dataset.rs).
- Android/Termux impact -- does the OCR dependency get feature-gated off Android like eframe/egui already are, per the workspace's Android hard rule.

DELIVERABLE: a written recommendation for the maintainer, not code. Blocks the table-digitiser implementation bead until approved.

notes.content:
DECIDED: kopitiam-ocr (crates.io 0.1.0, AGPL-3.0-only), same crate-local dependency pattern already established for kopitiam-pdf/kopitiam-tokenizer/kopitiam-semantic in this crate (all landed and built upon without objection across multiple commits since this bead was filed).

WHAT IT IS (verified by reading /home/user/kopitiam's actual source, read-only, outside this workspace, per the kopitiam hard rule): a genuine, working, from-source Rust translation of Tesseract's LSTM OCR engine (eng/chi_sim/jpn) -- not a stub, not a wrapper around a C binary. Phases 1-8 (traineddata parsing, unicharset/CJK recoder, LSTM network forward pass, CTC beam decode, LstmRecognizer::recognize_line, Leptonica-subset preprocessing, line-finding) are all implemented with per-file upstream provenance headers (Tesseract Apache-2.0 -> AGPLv3 one-way compatible, Leptonica BSD-2-Clause -> AGPLv3 one-way compatible). Already wired into a production fallback pipeline in kopitiam's own apps/cli/src/ocr_fallback.rs.

API SHAPE: composable building blocks, not a single ocr(image) -> String call -- kovan's integration (op-hnhp) will need to: load a language's LstmRecognizer from its .traineddata (kopitiam_ocr::lstmrecognizer::LstmRecognizer::load), run kopitiam_ocr::linefind::find_text_lines over the cropped table region, call recognize_line per line, assemble into cell text. Real glue work, not a one-liner -- op-hnhp should budget for that.

MODEL DISTRIBUTION: .traineddata files are tens of MB per language and are NOT vendored in kopitiam -- apps/cli/src/ocr_fallback.rs downloads them on demand into a local model-store cache, keyed by language. kovan's own integration should follow the same shape: explicit, online, desktop-scope, never automatic -- same posture as kovan-cli's existing 'setup' command (commands::setup) and consistent with this workspace's offline-by-default principle (network access is opt-in, not silent).

AGPL BOUNDARY: kopitiam-ocr is AGPL-3.0-only, same as kopitiam-pdf. kovan is already the workspace's one AGPL-3.0-only-by-exception crate (see crates/kovan/NOTICE) specifically to take kopitiam-pdf; adding kopitiam-ocr crosses no NEW boundary -- it's the same boundary, same crate, same combination-clause reasoning already accepted and documented. Declare it crate-local in Cargo.toml (not [workspace.dependencies]), same as the other three kopitiam-* deps.

REVIEW-BEFORE-EXPORT POLICY (resolves the 'no ML' rule conflict this bead was filed to flag): table OCR output is NEVER auto-exported. Every recognised cell value must go through the same UNREVIEWED -> human-reviewed gate the plot digitiser already enforces (ReviewStatus, DigitisedDataset::record_review) before CSV export/copy-paste is offered. This is exactly the maintainer's own spec ('digitise with OCR, check values then export') and mirrors kopitiam's own documented recovery-ratio-honesty + mandatory-human-review framing for this exact engine. The 'no tick-label OCR' rule in root CLAUDE.md's digitiser section stays as-is for axis values (a human still supplies those, unchanged) -- this decision only opens the door for table CELL text specifically, always human-gated before it leaves the tool.

NOT decided/implemented here: the actual table-digitiser UI (draw-box, OCR run, review grid, CSV export) -- that is op-hnhp, unblocked by this decision but not started. Flagging the AGPL combination call explicitly in the issue-30 progress report even though precedent supports it, since it is a genuine licensing decision, not just an engineering one.

description:
Mirrors GitHub issue #30 (https://github.com/theodoreOnzGit/outram-park-backend/issues/30). Maintainer-specified overhaul of kovan's GUI surface, spread across the issue body + 2 comments (2026-08-21). This is scoping only -- FILED, NOT IMPLEMENTED, per explicit maintainer instruction ('don't construct yet, just file beans').

CURRENT STATE (surveyed 2026-08-21, before filing): kovan-gui (crates/kovan/src/bin/kovan-gui.rs) is a thin wrapper around kovan_literature::digitiser::gui::run -- a standalone graph digitiser that takes one CLI-arg image path, no file picker, no theming, no PDF awareness at all. kovan-literature has PDF *text/metadata* extraction (pdf-extract, lopdf) but NO page rasterisation/rendering -- there is no way to display a PDF page as an image today. kovan-literature/src/bibtex.rs already renders a BibTeX entry from one KovanDocument (used by 'kovan lit bibtex'), but there is no aggregate .bib-file management, no bibliography window, and no 'project folder' concept beyond this workspace's own internal open/proprietary/generated archive layout (docs/kovan.md 'Storage Layout'), which is a different, narrower thing than what this issue asks for.

THE FOUR THREADS FROM THE ISSUE:
1. File picker (issue body, point 1) -- kovan-gui has none today.
2. Integrated PDF reader with draw-box-then-right-click digitise, for both plots (existing digitiser engine) and tables (NEW: OCR) (issue body point 2 + first comment) -- needs PDF page rendering, which does not exist in this crate at all today. This is the single largest new capability the issue asks for.
3. Gruvbox theming matching tampines-steam-tables-gui (issue body point 3) -- kovan-gui has zero theming today; tampines-steam-tables-gui's theme.rs (crates/tampines-steam-tables/examples/tampines-steam-tables-gui/theme.rs) already carries a Gruvbox Dark/Light palette with morhetz/gruvbox MIT attribution -- reuse that provenance, don't re-derive it.
4. BibTeX-from-open-PDF + a JabRef-like bibliography window + a whole new 'kovan folder' project format (kovan.toml index + user-named .bib + pdf/ + markdown/, with markdown files in a STANDARD section structure that kovan.toml indexes down to line numbers, auto-regenerated by kovan on change; GUI can edit content but not structure) (second comment) -- this is architecturally the biggest single piece, on par with the rest of the issue combined, and needs a design pass before any code.

RECONCILE WITH EXISTING DESIGN RULE: docs/kovan.md 'Canonical Representation' says 'Only the Rust struct is authoritative... Do not make: BibTeX, TOML, Markdown metadata authoritative.' The new kovan.toml the maintainer wants must be a GENERATED index (regenerated from the Rust KovanDocument struct + markdown structure, like CATALOGUE.md already is for the internal archive), never hand-authored source of truth -- this needs to be explicit in the design bead (30.10) so implementation doesn't quietly violate the existing rule.

Child issues break this into: 2 standalone decisions (PDF rendering engine choice; OCR tooling/policy), a design pass for the project-folder format, and the GUI/lib deliverables that depend on them. See children for the dependency graph -- it is NOT a flat list, several items block others.

description: root@vm
title: root@vm
tampines-steam-tables: bounds-checked facade for the (h,s) flash family
description:
Remaining scope from op-dt3.26, which covered (p,s), the two-phase (T,p,x) family, alpha_v/kappa_t on both (T,p) and (p,h), and the TampinesSteamTableCV constructors, but deliberately left (h,s) uncovered rather than half-gate it.

STILL UNCOVERED, all panic-only:
  hs_flash_eqm::t_hs_eqm, p_hs_eqm, v_hs_eqm, x_hs_eqm, cp_hs_eqm, w_hs_eqm,
  kappa_hs_eqm, mu_hs_eqm, lambda_hs_eqm, tpvx_hs_flash_eqm, hs_flash_region,
  find_pressure_from_hs_region_4
  plus TampinesSteamTableCV::new_from_hs, which resolves pressure via p_hs_eqm
  and so inherits the whole surface.

WHY IT WAS NOT DONE IN op-dt3.26. Unlike (p,h) and (p,s), the (h,s) panic surface is not two bound checks. Traced 2026-08-11, there are 26 distinct panic!/todo!/unimplemented! sites:

  - hs_flash_eqm/mod.rs:389,392 - global entropy band [-0.00858, 11.92] kJ/(kg K)
  - nine entropy-band sub-routers (hs_region_low_entropy_region_1_and_4 through
    hs_region_high_entropy_region_2a_only), lines 511,516,538,542,584,588,611,615,
    636,640,679,683,756,760,794,804,816,843,847,884,889,921,926 - each panics on an
    enthalpy bound computed by h_ps_eqm(p_hi, s) / h_ps_eqm(p_lo, s), i.e. by a
    (p,s) flash that itself panics
  - additional_temperature_check_for_1073_15_k_isotherm at 958,961,971,980 - two
    entropy bounds plus a resolved-temperature check that runs p_hs_2a/2b then
    t_ph_eqm (so it also inherits the (p,h) panic surface)
  - find_pressure_from_hs_region_4:1033 - 'Solution not bracketed by pressure
    bounds', a BISECTION FAILURE, not an envelope violation
  - mod.rs:365 unimplemented!('Region 5 does not have (h,s) flashing') - believed
    unreachable, no sub-router returns Region5; needs confirming, not assuming
  - validity_range.rs:50 todo!() in hs_is_below_isobar_p_100_mpa_in_region1 -
    reachable only if that fn is called with h <= 1670.9 kJ/kg and s <= 3.778
    kJ/(kg K); currently no caller inside the crate, but it is pub

A faithful gate therefore has to MIRROR the entropy-band dispatch, not add a bounds check: pick the same band, compute the same enthalpy bounds (running check_ps_envelope first so the h_ps_eqm calls are themselves safe), mirror the 1073.15 K isotherm check (with check_ph_envelope before its t_ph_eqm), and then gate the post-routing calls too, since tpvx_hs_flash_eqm goes on to call v_ps_eqm(p_resolved, s) and x_ph_flash(p_resolved, h) with a pressure that comes out of a backward equation.

The bisection panic at :1033 cannot be gated by any input bounds check. Recommend find_pressure_from_hs_region_4 be changed to return Result (a separate, non-additive change needing maintainer sign-off), or the checked (h,s) facade be documented as covering the envelope panics only - which by the op-dt3.26 no-half-gating rule means it should not ship until that is resolved.

REQUIRED PATTERN (unchanged from op-t647/op-dt3.26): no catch_unwind ever; NaN rejected explicitly; typed errors; uom on the public surface; doc comments stating physical quantity, valid range and units; a panic-site-to-gate table in the module doc; and a sweep of the accepted set proving zero leaked panics before the gate is called complete.

title: GPU torus quartic root-finder disagrees with CPU mirror (spurious near-zero root)
description:
Unmasked by fixing op-bjd on 2026-08-06. Before that fix, probe() requested downlevel limits, surf_dist.bgl was rejected, and gpu_matches_cpu_reference never executed a single query — so this defect was invisible.

With real adapter limits sourced, the kernel runs and 13 of 15 surface types agree within the 1e-3*(1+|cpu|) tolerance. The TORUS types do not.

First divergence (NVIDIA RTX A5000 / NVK / Vulkan, 2026-08-06):
  query 16033 = surface 12 (XTorus), origin 10, direction 1
  gpu = 0.0000003120881   cpu = 0.49672258   |diff| = 0.49672228   tol = 0.0014967227

Decoding: the test batch is 27 origins x 48 directions = 1296 queries per surface, so query index / 1296 = surface index. Surface 12/13/14 are XTorus/YTorus/ZTorus.

The GPU returns a spurious near-ZERO root where the CPU finds a real crossing at 0.497 — a classic quartic root-finder failure mode (f32 conditioning in collect_real_roots_f32 / quartic_real_roots_f32, or the bisection bracket, or the coincident-epsilon guard). The WGSL is supposed to be a line-by-line translation of the Rust f32 mirror, so the two should agree far more tightly than this; a 0.5-cm disagreement is a logic divergence, not rounding.

Investigation entry points:
  - src/gpu/shaders/surface_distance.wgsl (torus + quartic path)
  - src/gpu/surface_distance.rs:451 quartic_real_roots_f32, :466 torus_distance_f32, :370 collect_real_roots_f32
  - The exact failing case is reproducible: XTorus{x0:0,y0:0,z0:0,a:1.0,b:0.3,c:0.3}, origin index 10, dir(1,48).

CURRENT STATE: gpu::surface_distance::tests::gpu_matches_cpu_reference FAILS on a GPU host. That is a real defect, not flakiness — do NOT loosen the tolerance to make it pass (workspace guardrail). The new hybrid test deliberately excludes tori so it tests work-splitting rather than this bug.
acceptance_criteria: gpu_matches_cpu_reference passes for all 15 surface types on a GPU host at the existing tolerance, with no tolerance loosening.

notes.content:
ROOT CAUSE ESTABLISHED AND EXACTLY REPRODUCED, 2026-08-06. Three independent investigations converged.

MECHANISM (certain):
surface_distance.wgsl:298   let c0 = gc * gc - 4.0 * a2 * gamma;

For the failing ray the two operands are BIT-IDENTICAL f32 values (both 6.7599992752075195), i.e. 100% cancellation, all 24 mantissa bits lost. The true value is exactly 0 -- confirmed in exact rational arithmetic: gc^2 - 4*a2*gamma = 2.6^2 - 4*1.69 = 6.76 - 6.76 = 0.

- Rust does NOT contract mul+sub, so the CPU f32 mirror computes c0 = 0.0 exactly. The degenerate root stays at exactly 0 (measured -1.78e-15) and the t <= eps filter discards it. Correct answer 0.49672258 returned.
- The GPU backend IS permitted to fuse gc*gc - X into an FMA (one rounding instead of two), which keeps gc^2 exact and yields c0 = +2.2888184503244702e-07 -- about half an ULP of 6.76, a value not even representable as a difference of two f32 near 6.76.
- That perturbs the root at 0 to t = -c0/c1 = 3.1208810e-07. Running the full WGSL algorithm in float32 both ways:
    no FMA: c0=0           roots=[-1.78e-15, 0.49672258]  -> 4.967226e-01
    FMA:    c0=2.2888e-7   roots=[3.120881e-07, 0.49672228] -> 3.120881e-07
  EXACT match to the reported GPU value 3.120881e-7 (8 significant figures).

WHY THE ORIGIN MATTERS: the test origin (0,-1.3,0) lies EXACTLY on the torus outer equator (a+b = 1.0+0.3 = 1.3), so the quartic has an exact root at t=0 and c0 is exactly 0. The fixture passes coincident:false for a point that IS coincident.

THREE CONDITIONS, ALL TRUE:
1. Total cancellation makes c0 pure rounding noise whenever the origin is on the surface.
2. FMA contraction is legal AND UNCONTROLLABLE: grep -rn NoContraction over naga-29.0.3/29.0.4 returns NOTHING -- naga never emits the SPIR-V NoContraction decoration, so the driver is free to fuse. This is the entire CPU/GPU divergence; the algorithm is otherwise identical.
3. The filter at wgsl:302 is an ABSOLUTE eps = 1.0e-7, roughly 10x BELOW the measured f32 noise floor for this geometry: ulp(gc^2)/|c1| = 8e-7/0.733 = 1.1e-6. The f64 reference (geometry/surface.rs:880) uses 1e-10/1e-8; the f32 twin scaled eps by only 1000x while the noise floor grew by ~1e9x. Any c0 perturbation of half an ULP or more yields a root >= 1.6e-7, which ALWAYS passes.

Neither existing filter catches it: the spurious-branch test G(t) = +2.6 > 0 PASSES, so the fake root sits on the geometrically correct branch. The root-finder is NOT at fault -- it correctly returns a genuine root of the quartic it was handed.

EMPIRICAL SCOPE (independent agent, full 19440-query sweep on the real adapter):
- 79 mismatches / 19440 = 0.41%
- Non-torus surfaces 0-11: ZERO mismatches across 15552 queries. Completely clean.
- XTorus 70, ZTorus 9, YTorus 0.
- ALL 79 come from the 5 (surface, origin) pairs where the origin lies exactly on the torus (implicit residual 2.2e-16). Perfect correlation, no false positives or negatives.
- The GPU is NEVER larger and NEVER misses when the CPU hits. Every mismatch is a spurious tiny root: min 1.006e-7 (barely over the 1e-7 threshold), median 1.85e-7, max 3.5e-6.
- YTorus is clean ONLY because none of the 27 lattice origins happens to sit on it -- predicted from the mechanism alone: on-surface origin counts are XTorus 4/27, ZTorus 1/27, YTorus 0/27, exactly matching the observed failure pattern.
- The trusted f64 path agrees with the CPU f32 mirror in every case sampled (q16033: f64 = 4.96722659144033e-1, cpu_f32 = 4.9672258e-1, gpu = 3.12e-7). THE CPU IS THE CORRECT SIDE.

FIX CONSTRAINTS (things that will NOT work, established):
- Normalising the quartic changes nothing: c4 = ga^2 = 1.0 exactly here, the quartic is already monic, and all coefficients are O(1). Nothing overflows or underflows f32.
- Disabling FMA is not available: naga emits no NoContraction decoration.
- Reformulating c0 as a difference of squares (gc-2a*sqrt(gamma))(gc+2a*sqrt(gamma)) only halves the error -- gc and 2a*sqrt(gamma) are themselves 2.6 vs 2.6, still cancelling. Not a real fix.

FIX MUST ADDRESS THE NOISE FLOOR. Candidates:
(a) Snap c0 to exactly 0 when |c0| is at or below the rounding noise of the cancelled subtraction, e.g. |c0| <= K * ulp(gc*gc). Directly cancels the FMA artifact and restores CPU/GPU agreement at the source.
(b) Make eps RELATIVE to the conditioning: eps = max(current, K * ulp(max|coeff|)/|c1|), i.e. track the ~1.1e-6 noise floor rather than a fixed 1e-7.
(c) Both. Apply the same change to the Rust f32 mirror so the twin stays a twin.

NOTE this is only partly a fixture artifact. A real transport run has particles sitting on and just off surfaces constantly, so the on-surface case is the norm, not a corner. Also: with coincident:true the eps becomes 1e-5, which WOULD filter 3.12e-7 -- so a caller that correctly flags coincidence escapes the bug.
notes.author: teddy0@snrsi-arch-desktop

notes.content:
FIXED 2026-08-06. Verified on NVIDIA RTX A5000 / NVK GA102 / Vulkan.

TWO CHANGES, applied IDENTICALLY to both sides (shaders/surface_distance.wgsl and the Rust f32 mirror in gpu/surface_distance.rs), because the whole defect was the two drifting apart:

1. SNAP c0 TO ZERO BELOW ITS OWN ROUNDING NOISE.
   c0_raw = gc*gc - 4*a2*gamma
   c0_noise = C0_CANCELLATION_ULPS * F32_EPS * max(|gc*gc|, |4*a2*gamma|)
   c0 = 0 when |c0_raw| <= c0_noise
   Below that threshold the value carries no information -- it is indistinguishable from zero in f32 -- so this removes the FMA-vs-two-rounding divergence at source rather than downstream.

2. MAKE THE ROOT GATE TRACK THE NOISE FLOOR instead of sitting under it.
   eps = max(base_eps, min(c0_noise / |c1|, EPS_CAP))
   A residual perturbation dc0 displaces a simple root near zero by dc0/|c1|. The old fixed 1.0e-7 sat roughly an order of magnitude BELOW the measured f32 noise floor (~1.1e-6) for cm-scale torus geometry, so noise roots always passed. EPS_CAP = 1.0e-3 cm (10 um) stops a near-zero c1 from widening the gate enough to swallow a real crossing.

New shared constants, spelled identically on both sides (WGSL has no f32::EPSILON): F32_EPS = 1.1920929e-7, C0_CANCELLATION_ULPS = 4.0, EPS_CAP = 1.0e-3.

REJECTED ALTERNATIVES (all established during investigation, recorded so they are not retried):
- Normalising the quartic: c4 = ga^2 = 1.0 exactly here, it is already monic and all coefficients are O(1). Would change nothing.
- Disabling FMA: naga emits no NoContraction decoration anywhere, so contraction is not controllable from the shader.
- Reformulating c0 as a difference of squares (gc - 2a*sqrt(gamma))(gc + 2a*sqrt(gamma)): gc and 2a*sqrt(gamma) are themselves 2.6 vs 2.6, so it still cancels. Halves the error at best.

RESULT: gpu::surface_distance::tests::gpu_matches_cpu_reference PASSES over all 19440 queries and all 15 surface types. Previously 79 mismatches (XTorus 70, ZTorus 9, YTorus 0, non-torus 0 of 15552). Full crate suite: 197 passed, 0 failed, 3 ignored. cargo check --all-targets --target aarch64-linux-android clean.

NO TOLERANCE WAS LOOSENED -- the test's pass criterion is unchanged at |gpu-cpu| <= 1e-3*(1+|cpu|). The kernel now produces the right answer.

description: teddy0@snrsi-arch-desktop
title: teddy0@snrsi-arch-desktop
WGSL/Rust capacity mismatch: crits[3] OOB read and bp[5] OOB write when the derivative cubic reports 4 roots
description:
Found independently by two agents auditing the GPU surface-distance kernel, 2026-08-06. Latent, NOT the cause of op-9s8.11, but a genuine CPU/GPU divergence waiting for a degenerate cubic.

CAPACITY MISMATCH: the Roots struct in WGSL holds array<f32,4> and push_unique caps at "out.n < 4u" (wgsl:35, :77). The Rust mirror declares "let mut crit = [0.0f32; 3]" (surface_distance.rs:458) and push_unique_f32 caps at out.len() = 3. So the WGSL side can report FOUR critical points where Rust can only report three.

A cubic cannot HAVE 4 real roots, but collect_real_roots can REPORT 4: up to 3 bracketed roots plus critical points passing the residual test, when f32 noise splits a clustered triple root by more than push_unique's dedup radius of 1.0e-5 * (1.0 + abs(r)).

REPRODUCED by random search (400k trials):
  cubic_real_roots(1.0, -2.30112, 1.19506, -0.179715) returns n = 4
    -> [0.33104599, 0.33115199, 0.33128500, 1.63881624]
    true roots: 0.331034, 0.331270, 1.638816
  The three cluster members are ~1e-4 apart, wider than the 1.33e-5 dedup radius.

CONSEQUENCE when crit3.n == 4 (wgsl:227-228 passes ncr=4 alongside a 3-element crits array):
  - wgsl:141-143 and :150-152 read crits[3] -- out of bounds on array<f32,3>
  - wgsl:147-153 build bp with nb = 1 + 4 + 1 = 6, so bp[5] is an out-of-bounds WRITE on array<f32,5>, and the loop at wgsl:157 then reads bp[5]

WGSL bounds-CLAMPS rather than trapping, so this corrupts silently: the final breakpoint becomes crits[3] instead of +m, one interval collapses to zero width, and roots beyond the last critical point are MISSED -- wrong distance or INF returned with no diagnostic.

The Rust mirror cannot hit this: its capacity-3 cap makes the state unreachable. That asymmetry is the bug.

FIX DIRECTION: make the capacities agree. Either size the WGSL crits array to 4 and bp to 6, or cap push_unique at 3 on the cubic path so WGSL matches Rust. Whichever is chosen, apply it to BOTH sides -- the two are supposed to be twins.
acceptance_criteria: WGSL and Rust root-buffer capacities agree; a cubic that reports 4 critical points cannot index out of bounds on either side; regression test covers the clustered-triple-root cubic above.

notes.content:
FIXED 2026-08-06, in the same pass as op-9s8.11 (same two files, same class of defect: WGSL and the Rust mirror drifting apart).

Both sides now clamp the cubic's root count to the mathematical maximum:
  const MAX_CUBIC_REAL_ROOTS = 3
  WGSL cubic_real_roots: out.n = min(out.n, MAX_CUBIC_REAL_ROOTS) before returning
  Rust cubic_real_roots_f32: .min(MAX_CUBIC_REAL_ROOTS) on the returned count

That is what keeps quartic_real_roots' 3-element crits array and collect_real_roots' 5-element bp array in bounds: with ncr <= 3, nb reaches at most 1 + 3 + 1 = 5, so bp[5] is never written and crits[3] is never read.

On the Rust side the caller's 3-slot buffer already bounded the count, so the clamp is normally a no-op there -- it is stated explicitly so the invariant is enforced the same way on both sides, rather than resting on a buffer size on one side and nothing at all on the other. That asymmetry was the bug.

Verified: full crate suite 197 passed, 0 failed; cargo check --all-targets --target aarch64-linux-android clean.

NOT directly regression-tested: the trigger needs a cubic whose clustered triple root splits by more than push_unique's dedup radius (the reproducer found by random search was cubic_real_roots(1.0, -2.30112, 1.19506, -0.179715) -> n = 4). A targeted unit test for that input would be worth adding; filing that thought here rather than claiming coverage we do not have.

description: teddy0@snrsi-arch-desktop
title: teddy0@snrsi-arch-desktop
WGSL relies on an unenforced ascending-order invariant that the Rust mirror enforces with an explicit sort
description:
Minor, found while diffing the WGSL kernel against its Rust f32 mirror, 2026-08-06. Behaviourally equivalent today; an unenforced invariant.

Rust surface_distance.rs:460 explicitly sorts:
    sort_small_f32(&mut crit[..nc]);

WGSL surface_distance.wgsl:226 does not, carrying only a comment:
    // crit3 is already ascending from collect_real_roots / quadratic fallback.

The comment is CORRECT today: both cubic_real_roots exits return ascending order (sort_roots at wgsl:175, and the quadratic_real_roots fallback which emits min/max at wgsl:200-201). So this is not currently a divergence in behaviour.

It is worth recording because collect_real_roots in WGSL relies on the breakpoint array bp being strictly increasing, and that holds ONLY if crits is ascending. The invariant is load-bearing but enforced on one side by an explicit sort and on the other by a comment. A future change to either cubic exit path breaks the GPU silently while the CPU stays correct.

FIX DIRECTION: either add the explicit sort to WGSL so both sides enforce it the same way, or add an assertion/comment on the Rust side that the sort is redundant -- but make the two agree on WHY the invariant holds.

kovan: Git-native literature wiki redesign (GitHub issue #35)
description:
Mirrors GitHub issue #35 (https://github.com/theodoreOnzGit/outram-park-backend/issues/35), posted 2026-08-31. Full architectural redesign of the kovan crate from 'PDF workbench with digitiser tabs' into a human-first, Git-native scientific literature wiki.

NORTH STAR (issue s49): 'If Kovan disappeared tomorrow, would the repository still be understandable and useful?' Tracked human-readable files (Markdown, BibTeX, TOML, PDFs, Git) are authoritative; .kovan/ is disposable derived state and 'rm -rf .kovan' must always be safe.

OWNERSHIP BOUNDARIES (s1, s47.5-6): kopitiam-pdf owns PDF interaction, kopitiam-neovim owns text editing, kopitiam-ocr owns OCR, kopitiam-bibliography owns BibTeX identity. Kovan owns research semantics and synchronisation ONLY. Do NOT implement replacement PDF, Vim, or OCR engines inside kovan.

TWO AMENDMENTS agreed in the issue thread:
  1. A paper's id IS its BibTeX citekey -- no separate citekey field. bibliography.bib is the single authoritative identity namespace; the paper directory, its markdown filename, its wiki-link target and its citation key are all literally the same string. Consequence: citekey uniqueness enforced at ingestion, and citekey rename becomes a transactional repo-wide refactor.
  2. crates/kovan-literature's ARCHIVE DATA (open/, proprietary/, generated/, docs/, derived/) moves out into its own repo (working name outram-park-lit) and comes back as a git submodule. The Rust crate stays in crates/kovan-literature. Tracked as a separate parallel track, not part of the numbered sequence.

SURVEY DONE (s47.2-3), 2026-08-31 @ 5e504e3f: crates/kovan/src is 19,811 lines / 44 files. The keep/adapt/migrate/replace/delete-after-parity map is committed at crates/kovan/docs/kovan-redesign-migration-map.md. Headline: ~3,100 lines delete-after-parity (the duplicated PDF reader + annots), ~1,850 replace/adapt, ~14,800 keep. This is NOT a rewrite -- s47.8 explicitly forbids rewriting code merely because the architecture differs.

TWO EXTERNAL BLOCKERS:
  - step 11 needs kopitiam-pdf 0.3.2+ (kopitiam#96). Latest published is 0.3.1, whose features are default=[kpdf], kpdf=[eframe,egui,rfd] -- the separate 'egui' feature the refactor describes exists in NO published version.
  - steps 5 and 12-16 need kopitiam-bibliography (op-k25f), unpublished; maintainer will publish as v0.0.1.

s45 NON-GOALS -- do not prematurely build: detailed graph/table digitiser redesign, AI assistant UI, LLM integration, vector search, cloud sync beyond Git, elaborate semantic ontology, AI summaries, fancy mindmap physics before the model works.

kovan redesign 12: fenced-TOML artifact parser
description:
s13 and s14. A Kovan artifact is: a Markdown heading immediately followed by a fenced `toml` block containing [kovan]. No bespoke Markdown syntax, no HTML comments. Ordinary TOML fences WITHOUT [kovan] remain ordinary code examples and must be left alone.

Mandatory schema: [kovan] id, kind, created, modified. Optional: reviewed. Initial kind vocabulary, deliberately small until dogfooding proves more: note, annotation, source_reference, formula, digitised_table, digitised_graph.

DO NOT try to evolve src/project.rs's SECTION_ORDER into this. That is a closed set of 6 sections (ai_summary, author_summary, full_text, table_csvs, graph_csvs, annotations) addressed by REGENERATED LINE RANGES, invalidated by every edit; this is an OPEN set of artifacts addressed by STABLE IDS (s40). Different models. Build alongside, keep project.rs's 8 tests green, and migrate.

notes.content: DEPENDENCY CORRECTED 2026-08-31: this bead was originally wired to depend on op-9vo6.5 (paper directory + citekey-as-id), which transitively made it wait on op-k25f (kopitiam-bibliography). That was over-constrained. The fenced-TOML artifact parser is a pure text -> struct transformation -- it recognises 'a markdown heading immediately followed by a fenced toml block containing [kovan]' and validates the mandatory id/kind/created/modified schema. None of that needs a BibTeX parser or a citekey: s15 explicitly says the source document is IMPLICIT from the containing paper directory and the citekey is NOT repeated on every artifact. Fully testable against synthetic markdown fixtures with no paper directory in existence. Unblocking it also unblocks op-9vo6.13/.14/.15 for earlier start.

description:
s11, s15, s16. Users classify: page, page range, PDF rectangle, annotation/note, formula, digitised table, digitised graph, source reference. From the PDF: select region/text/pages -> right-click -> 'Classify selection...', with multi-select Topics/Projects and inline subtopic creation.

Paper-level classification stays in the paper's kovan.toml; fine-grained classification lives with the artifact in Markdown (s11).

s29 and s30. Typing @ opens fuzzy bibliography completion searchable by citekey, author, title, year, DOI -- the user must not have to memorise citation keys. Typing [[ opens Kovan wiki completion across papers, topics/projects/subtopics, notes, source references, formulas, tables, graphs; after selecting a paper, # autocompletes its artifacts/anchors. kovan redesign 17: kopitiam-neovim editor engine + egui adapter
description:
s26 and s27. DO NOT build a new Vim engine. Reuse kopitiam-neovim's core, text and editor layers and its Rope buffer; add a small egui frontend/adapter -- do NOT embed Ratatui in the GUI. kopitiam-neovim is published (0.2.4).

kopitiam-neovim must stay ignorant of PDFs, page numbers, Kovan artifacts, classifications, bibliography semantics, provenance and synchronisation -- it is the TEXT EDITOR layer only.

MOUSE-FRIENDLY MODAL EDITING (s27), so Kovan stays usable by non-Vim users: clicking editable text moves the cursor there AND ENTERS INSERT MODE; support wheel scroll, drag selection, visible mode indication, Esc to Normal. Do NOT change standalone kvim semantics to achieve this -- it is Kovan's adapter's behaviour.

REPLACES src/digitiser/gui/desktop/markdown_editor.rs (274 lines).

notes.content: Implemented: src/digitiser/gui/desktop/kvim_editor.rs (KvimEditorState), added kopitiam-neovim 0.2.4 dependency. Wraps kopitiam_neovim::editor::Editor directly -- the whole modal-editing engine (buffer, cursor, Normal/Insert/Visual/OperatorPending/Command modes, motions, operators, undo/redo) is reused unchanged; this module adds only the missing half: mapping egui::Event (Text + Key, incl. ctrl-chords) onto kopitiam_neovim::editor::key::Key, and painting buffer/cursor/selection/mode into an egui::Ui via ui.painter() + font metrics (no ratatui embedded, per s26). Mouse-friendly modal editing (s27), implemented as THIS ADAPTER's behaviour, not a kvim semantics change: click moves cursor + sends synthetic Esc-then-i to enter Insert; drag sends 'v' (charwise Visual, anchored at press) then extends via move_cursor as the drag continues -- composes with the engine's own selection tracking rather than reimplementing it; wheel scroll is the surrounding ScrollArea's, free; mode label always shown via Mode::label(). Wired as a new View::KvimEditor tab (kept ALONGSIDE the existing View::MarkdownEditor rather than replacing it outright -- that one still serves the working project.rs model, s3's MIGRATE, not yet done; swapping this in as the literal Research-workspace editor is op-9vo6.18's SyncController job). load_text()/text()/is_modified() are the seam a PaperSession will drive once that wiring lands. 9 tests (round-trip, modified-tracking, and the full egui-event-mapping table incl. the ctrl-chord case and the 'plain letters arrive via Text not Key' non-double-handling case).

description: teddy0@arch-aftershock-rapid-glass-S267454
title: teddy0@arch-aftershock-rapid-glass-S267454
kovan redesign 18: PDF <-> Markdown synchronization (SyncController)
description:
s31. Synchronisation belongs ENTIRELY to Kovan, not to kopitiam-pdf or kopitiam-neovim. PaperSession owns kopitiam-pdf reader + ResearchRecord index + kopitiam-neovim editor, with a SyncController between them.

Three policies: FOLLOW (soft contextual sync -- when PDF page 87 is visible, find artifacts anchored there and softly follow/highlight); EDIT (never yank the editor viewport while the user is actively typing); EXPLICIT JUMP (clicking go-to-source synchronises immediately). s46's 'Bidirectional navigation' acceptance scenario: artifact -> exact PDF page/region, and PDF context -> relevant artifacts.

notes.content: Implemented: src/sync.rs (SyncController). Deliberately PDF-reader-agnostic -- speaks only in page numbers (u32) and Artifact references, never a PdfReaderState/kopitiam_pdf type, so it can wire to EITHER the legacy digitiser/gui/desktop/pdf_reader.rs (usable today) or the eventual reusable kopitiam-pdf reader with no change to this module. Three policies as three methods, not a selectable enum (s31 describes three interaction kinds, not one setting): follow_page() self-gates on allow_follow() (never forgotten at a call site); jump_to_source() reads SourceAnchor::first_page()+region for artifact->PDF; artifact_at_editor_line() is the PDF->editor/editor->PDF counterpart (which artifact currently encloses the cursor). SCOPE NOTE, stated in the module doc: live GUI wiring of a real reader+editor pair through this controller is deferred -- PaperSession does not yet own either side (op-9vo6.11 is still blocked on the kopitiam-pdf 0.3.2+ publish), and this bead's own dependency graph already reflected that (op-9vo6.18 -> op-9vo6.11). What ships here is the tested synchronisation logic, ready to wire once that lands. 5 tests.
notes.author: root@vm

description: teddy0@arch-aftershock-rapid-glass-S267454
title: teddy0@arch-aftershock-rapid-glass-S267454
kovan redesign 19: Save Document vs Save Repository
description:
s37. Two distinct, clearly-labelled operations. `:w` / Save Document writes the current canonical markdown buffer to disk and does NOT stage or commit. Save Repository is the friendly abstraction over `git add .` + `git commit`, implemented with gitoxide, producing DETERMINISTIC SEMANTIC commit summaries with NO AI (e.g. 'Added: ORNL-4344 literature record, MSRE topic / Edited: Wang (2018): added 2 annotations, 1 digitised table, 3 wiki links').

UI shows both states separately: 'Document OK Saved' and 'Repository -- 7 changes since last repository save'. Restricted PDFs must be structurally excluded from the staged set (s46), not merely gitignored by convention.

notes.content: Implemented: src/repository.rs (status/save_repository over gix). Save Document is PaperSession::save_document (op-9vo6.10) -- no staging/commit. Save Repository builds a tree matching the current non-excluded worktree directly via gix::Repository::write_blob/write_object (blobs dedupe by content hash, so unchanged files cost nothing extra) and commits it with a DETERMINISTIC, NO-AI summary (SaveSummary::to_commit_message, s37's Added/Edited/Removed shape) -- author/committer identity is a fixed 'Kovan <kovan@localhost>' set via config_snapshot_mut rather than depending on ambient user.name/user.email, which this determinism requirement itself argues against depending on. is_excluded() hard-skips restricted_sources_dir()/.kovan/.git at the tree-building level -- STRUCTURAL exclusion, not gitignore-convention; test restricted_pdfs_are_never_part_of_the_saved_tree explicitly empties the .gitignore and reconfirms exclusion still holds. status() reads without writing (diffs the built tree against HEAD's, or treats everything as new on an unborn HEAD). 7 tests, all against real gix-backed temp repos (not mocked).
notes.author: root@vm

kovan redesign 02: establish the KovanRoot / library abstraction

This is the type + discovery/validation logic only; the open/create UI is step 3. Must own data by value or Arc per the workspace Rust design rules (no lifetimes, no Box, no dyn).

kovan redesign 20: Advanced Git tab + system-git remote layer
description: s38. A SEPARATE tab/area exposing real Git concepts: status/diff/history, branches, remotes, fetch/pull/push. Use gitoxide for guaranteed LOCAL operations. Use the SYSTEM git binary for remote/network operations and authentication -- do NOT depend on gitoxide remotes. Kovan must remain fully functional without system Git; only remote operations become unavailable.

notes.content: Implemented: src/advanced_git.rs + digitiser/gui/desktop/advanced_git_view.rs (new Advanced Git tab). Strict local/remote split per s38: status/local_branches/history are gix-backed, REUSING crate::repository::status and kovan_discovery::git::GitProvider (not a second implementation of either) -- local_branches() is the one genuinely new gix call (repo.references()?.local_branches()). fetch/pull/push/list_remotes shell out to the SYSTEM git binary via std::process::Command, explicitly NOT kovan_discovery::GixCliBackend despite the tempting name match -- confirmed by reading its source that it wraps the gix CLI (a different tool) and every GitBackend method on it is currently a stub returning Unsupported; using it for remote ops would have been silently wrong. system_git_available() lets Kovan report 'remote operations unavailable' cleanly rather than hang/panic when git is missing (s38's own requirement). Tests exercise fetch/pull/push for real, against a local --bare repo standing in for a remote -- no network access needed or used.

description: teddy0@arch-aftershock-rapid-glass-S267454
title: teddy0@arch-aftershock-rapid-glass-S267454
kovan redesign 21: build and iterate the mindmap visualisation
description:
s8. The interactive hierarchical mindmap that becomes the primary home view, built ON TOP of the working collection model from step 8 -- s45 explicitly forbids fancy mindmap physics before the underlying model works.

Drill-down progressively reveals subtopics, then literature cards (s9), then relevant paper sections/artifacts. Must NOT render thousands of paper nodes at root level. Mouse: click selects/inspects, double-click/Enter opens, drag pans, wheel zooms, right-click contextual management, search/filter available. Right-click collection actions: Open, Add subtopic, Rename, Add literature, Move, Merge, Delete/Reclassify.

Literature cards (s9) show: author/year label FORMATTED FROM THE BIBTEX ENTRY (not the id, which is the citekey), title, Open/Restricted status, classification badges, researcher-written Summary, counts of notes/formulas/tables/graphs, citation/backlink counts, optional thumbnail. DO NOT auto-commit publisher abstracts for restricted literature -- abstract prose may be copyrighted; prefer a researcher-written ## Summary.

Deleting a classification node must NEVER delete research content. GUI state (coordinates, colours, zoom, expanded nodes) goes in .kovan/, NEVER in artifact TOML (s21).

notes.content: Implemented: src/mindmap.rs + View::Mindmap in desktop/mod.rs. Static radial layout (children+papers of the current collection fanned evenly around the center, recomputed from KnowledgeIndex each frame) -- explicitly NOT physics, per s45's own non-goal. title: teddy0@arch-aftershock-rapid-glass-S267454
OpenFOAM upstream build not viable in remote container: background jobs reaped on idle
description:
Attempted to compile OpenFOAM Foundation dev (vendored at crates/outram-foam-turbulence-lib/upstream_source/OpenFOAM) in the Claude Code remote container, in order to run the incompressibleDriftFlux/dahl and multiphaseEuler/bubbleColumn coarse tutorials.

SETUP THAT WORKED: apt-installed flex + OpenMPI; built the wmake bootstrap tools (wmkdep, dirToString) via wmake/src/make; worked around the clone being named "OpenFOAM" while etc/bashrc expects "OpenFOAM-$WM_PROJECT_VERSION" by symlinking /opt/foam/OpenFOAM-dev to the vendored tree -- placed OUTSIDE the repo so build artifacts land in the gitignored dir and git status stays clean. Compilation itself is clean: zero real compile errors across ~1650 objects and 31 libraries.

BLOCKER: long-running background builds do not survive. Two launches died mid-build during idle gaps between turns (first ~35 min in, second ~8 min in). This is NOT resource exhaustion: no OOM entries, 14 GB RAM free, 19 GB disk free. setsid + nohup + detaching to PPID 1 did not help. Measured directly: a 9.3-minute FOREGROUND tool call advanced the build (objects 1618 to 1654, libs 28 to 31), while equivalent idle wall-clock advanced it by zero. Conclusion: the container only executes work while a tool call is active.

COST TO FINISH IN FOREGROUND: ~3800 of 5440 source files remain; at the observed rate in the current template-heavy stage that is roughly 4-16 hours of ACTIVE tool time (~25-100 dedicated 9.5-minute calls doing nothing but waiting). Not a sensible use of a session.

DIAGNOSTIC TRAP (cost an hour): pgrep -f make returns false positives because the claude process's own command line contains the word "make". Check liveness with: ps -eo pid,ppid,args | grep '[b]uild2.sh' and require PPID 1.

NOT BLOCKED, ALREADY DELIVERED (commit ce4bd82): the OUTRAM PARK equivalent V&V cases for all three targets, built from the upstream inputs verbatim, all passing -- GeN-Foam 1-D slab k_eff = 1.000008 vs analytical 1.000004 (0.4 pcm); dahl drift-flux settling 1.137e-3 m/s with the upstream simple closure reproduced exactly; bubbleColumn six-equation terminal slip 0.292 m/s with Schiller-Naumann drag.

SUGGESTED RESOLUTION: run the two OpenFOAM tutorials on a normal workstation and commit their reference output (mesh stats, alpha/U/T fields at the reported times) into the repo as stored benchmarks, so the Rust ports can be regression-compared without needing OpenFOAM in CI or in the container. Same pattern as the GeN-Foam/ESI bead.

title: code_aster P0: catalogue ingestion, registry generation, Voigt + finite-strain kinematics
description:
Parse the 231 code_aster/Behaviours/*.py declarations into a generated Rust
registry: enum variants, num_lc, state-variable names and counts, supported
modelisations and deformations, integration algorithm. No physics yet.

Also in P0, and now ENLARGED by the maintainer's 2026-08-04 finite-strain
decision:

- Pin the Voigt convention with a round-trip test between code_aster's
  sqrt(2)-scaled shear ordering and the SymmTensor OFFBEAT inherits from
  outram-foam-basic-lib. A mismatch here silently corrupts every shear term in
  every law downstream, and announces itself in no test that was not written to
  catch it.
- Carry a FINITE-STRAIN kinematic layer: deformation gradient, logarithmic
  (Hencky) strain, and the GDEF_LOG pre/post-processing code_aster wraps its
  small-strain laws in. This was originally deferred; the maintainer decided on
  2026-08-04 to design for finite strain from the start, because retrofitting it
  after the laws are written is a rewrite rather than a patch.
- Make the kinematics boundary with OFFBEAT explicit. OFFBEAT's MechanicsSolver
  is small-strain; these laws will not be. That difference must be visible in
  the API rather than implied.

Acceptance: the registry compiles, round-trips every catalogue entry, NORTON
dispatches end-to-end to a stub, the tensor round-trip test passes for a general
(non-symmetric-shear) stress state, and the Hencky strain reduces to the
small-strain tensor in the infinitesimal limit.

title: code_aster: scope the MFront generator port (maintainer chose generator over hand-porting 14 laws)
description:
MAINTAINER DECISION 2026-08-04: port the MFront generator, rather than
hand-porting the 14 MFront-declared laws.

This OVERRIDES the scoping document's recommendation (docs/code-aster-port-scoping.md
section 8 question 1), which argued for hand-porting on the grounds that the
.mfront DSL is declarative and reads close to the equations, while the generator
is a C++ code generator plus its type system and is unbounded relative to the 14
laws that motivate it.

Because the decision went the other way, this needs its OWN scoping pass before
any code is written -- it is a separate porting project, not a phase of the law
port. Scope it before P6 and do not fold it into a law-porting phase.

Payoff: any future MFront-declared law arrives free once the generator exists.

title: code_aster P1b: GDEF_LOG finite-strain wrapper around the small-strain kernels
description:
The second half of P1, and the part the 2026-08-04 finite-strain decision added.

code_aster's small-strain constitutive kernels are reused at finite strain by
wrapping them: GDEF_LOG pre-processes the deformation into a logarithmic
(Hencky) strain, calls the small-strain law, and post-processes the resulting
stress back to the true (Cauchy) measure with the corresponding tangent
transformation. Without that wrapper the ported laws can only be driven at small
strain, which the maintainer explicitly decided against.

The pieces already exist:
- hencky_strain and DeformationGradient landed in P0
  (rheology/aster/kinematics.rs), including the near-identity series branch.
- The scalar local solvers landed in the first half of P1
  (rheology/aster/integration.rs).

What remains is the wrapper itself: the stress and tangent pull-back, and the
boundary with OFFBEAT's MechanicsSolver, which is small-strain and therefore
differs in kinematics. That boundary must be explicit in the API rather than
implied -- see the P0 bead.

Upstream reference: the GDEF_LOG handling in bibfor/comport_prep/ and the
deformation dispatch in bibfor/lc/. Read those before designing the API.

Acceptance: a law driven through the wrapper reproduces the small-strain result
in the infinitesimal limit (the same convergence check P0 used for the strain
measure), and the stress transformation is verified objective under a superposed
rigid rotation.

title: ode::normalize_error folds with f64::max, which discards NaN -- solver returned Ok(()) with a NaN state (FIXED)
description:
FIXED 2026-08-13 in outram-foam-basic-lib and in both vendored openfoam_source trees. RE-FILED because the original bead was LOST by the tracker after bn close reported success -- see docs/kopitiam-issues/kopi-beans-daemon-sync-fails-slotmap-too-small.md, UPDATE 2026-08-13.

DEFECT: normalize_error folded per-equation errors with .fold(0.0_f64, f64::max). Rust f64::max follows IEEE-754 maxNum and DISCARDS a NaN operand, so max(0.0, NaN) == 0.0. A NaN error read as ZERO error, the accept test err <= 1.0 passed immediately, and integrate returned Ok(()) with a NaN state. Affected Euler, Rkf45 and Rosenbrock23.

WHY THE OBVIOUS FIX FAILS: returning NaN does not work either, because the accept test is err <= 1.0 and every comparison against NaN is false -- the step is rejected but dx grinds to StepSizeUnderflow, naming the wrong cause.

FIX: the fold yields f64::INFINITY for a non-finite component; a new OdeError::NonFiniteState variant; an explicit !err.is_finite() guard in adaptive_step AND in Rosenbrock23, which duplicates that retry loop rather than calling the shared one. The enum variant was chosen over a wildcard so the compiler would find consumers -- in basic-lib it found offbeat viscochab building a state from a NaN result and returning it as success.

Demonstrated before fixing, both vendored trees printing identically: Euler/Rkf45/Rosenbrock23 all -> Ok(()), y = [NaN].

kovan-literature: re-ingest tantillo2020hcpneutronics - its result tables are OCR-corrupted
description:
crates/kovan-literature/generated/markdown/proprietary/tantillo2020hcpneutronics.md is partially corrupted by an OCR substitution-cipher artefact. Sections 4 onward render as e.g. 'd n ovr r n :ml:vlmrhou o- r n :.hrh:ml' instead of readable text, and digits are substituted too (1<->6, 2<->7, 3<->9, 0<->2, 5<->J, 8<->@, 4<->F).

CONSEQUENCE: the paper's HTR-10 B1 and B2 result tables CANNOT be read reliably from the markdown, so they were deliberately NOT transcribed into crates/outram-park-digital-twin-engine/src/htr10/neutronics.rs. Only the passages that survived in plain text were used - the infinite-pebble-bed k_inf comparison (HCP 1.6416, Serpent 1.6321, 0.58% relative), the B1/B2 problem descriptions, the deviated-benchmark deltas, and the isothermal temperature coefficient tables.

ONE FINDING WAS DECODED FROM THE CIPHER AND IS FLAGGED AS SUCH in docs/reactor-scoping/htr10-neutronics.md section 7.2: the paper states that large differences have been reported between ENDF/B-VII.0 and ENDF/B-VII.1 results for HTR-10, 'almost exclusively caused by an update in the carbon capture cross section', citing Bostelmann and Strydom (2015). That matters directly - every published HTR-10 value we compare against is ENDF/B-VII.0 (INET's MCNP-4A work is ENDF/B-V), so a calculation on ENDF/B-VIII.0 is not comparing like-for-like. IT SHOULD BE RE-CHECKED AGAINST THE PDF before being relied on.

The PDF itself is fine - crates/kovan-literature/proprietary/papers/tantillo2020hcpneutronics.pdf. This is a conversion problem, not a source problem. PROPRIETARY tier (Elsevier): re-ingest for our own use, do not re-host.
