title: htgr_sim_v1 → WebAssembly browser demo (egui/eframe, GH #39)
description:
Port htgr_sim_v1 (~23.9k lines, crates/outram-park-digital-twin-engine/examples/htgr_sim_v1/) to wasm32-unknown-unknown so it runs as a no-install browser demo. Full scoping, wasm-hostility audit and phase plan in GitHub issue #39.

Key measured findings: eframe 0.36.1 already uses the wgpu backend and has first-class wasm support, so the GUI is nearly free. Three real blockers: (1) tuas_boussinesq_solver spawns OS threads in library code in exactly the two pre_built_components this sim uses (shell_and_tube_heat_exchanger 41 sites, one_d_solid_structure 2) and std::thread::spawn panics on wasm; (2) the digital-twin-engine library unconditionally pulls async-opcua/tokio/mdns-sd/directories/local-ip-address which the sim does not use; (3) app_scaffold has 5 native-only files (csv_logging std::fs, real_time_pacing + gui_frame_metrics Instant::now).

Hard constraint: do NOT fork the physics. The wasm build compiles the same source as native, with cfg differences confined to threading, time and I/O.

Offline demonstration only per RESPONSIBLE_USE.md. No human V&V claimed.

title: Phase 0: prove the wasm toolchain before touching physics
description:
New crate crates/htgr-sim-web/ with crate-type=[cdylib,rlib]; hello-world eframe app; trunk serve; confirm WebGPU works with a WebGL fallback in BOTH Firefox and Chromium.

Deliberately first and deliberately trivial: doing this before any physics means a toolchain failure can never be mistaken for a physics failure. GH #39 Phase 0.

Acceptance: a blank egui window renders in two browsers from a static server.

title: Phase 1: feature-gate the engine's OPC-UA / mDNS / filesystem stack
description:
outram-park-digital-twin-engine's [dependencies] unconditionally include async-opcua (server+client), tokio, mdns-sd, directories, local-ip-address, csv. All are wasm-hostile and htgr_sim_v1 uses NONE of them (verified: its only engine imports are app_scaffold, components, animation, htr10; the single ciet_opcua mention is a doc cross-reference, not an import).

Put them behind a default-on 'native' feature. The crate already target-gates egui/eframe off Android, so this mirrors an established shape rather than inventing one. Modules are already cleanly separated (ciet_opcua, opcua_core, htgr_opcua).

Acceptance: cargo check -p outram-park-digital-twin-engine --target wasm32-unknown-unknown --no-default-features --features <wasm set> passes. Native default build unchanged. GH #39 Phase 1.

title: Phase 2: swap std::time::Instant for web-time across the physics chain
description:
Instant::now() panics on wasm32-unknown-unknown. The web-time crate is a drop-in std::time replacement using performance.now() on wasm and re-exporting std elsewhere.

Affected (measured file counts using Instant::now or SystemTime): tuas_boussinesq_solver 21, digital-twin-engine 13, dwsim-libs 3, tampines 2, chem-eng-control-simulator 2, teh-o-prke 1, tampines-steam-tables 1.

Mechanical import swap, not a redesign. Native behaviour must be bit-identical; that is testable and should be tested rather than assumed. GH #39 Phase 2.

title: Phase 3: TUAS serial fallback for the 43 thread::spawn sites on wasm
description:
THE blocker. tuas_boussinesq_solver spawns OS threads in LIBRARY code (not tests) in exactly the two pre_built_components htgr_sim_v1 uses: shell_and_tube_heat_exchanger (41 sites, e.g. calculation.rs:1464, preprocessing.rs:1199) and one_d_solid_structure (2). std::thread::spawn compiles but PANICS AT RUNTIME on wasm32-unknown-unknown.

The pattern is spawn-then-join-immediately, so serialising changes nothing numerically.

Three options, recommendation is (1) then (2) as follow-up:
1. cfg(target_arch=wasm32) sequential equivalents beside each spawn/join. Mechanical, low-risk, easy to review.
2. Refactor spawn/join into one small internal abstraction with native+wasm impls, so 43 sites become 1. Cleaner, bigger diff, and the shape a future rayon-on-wasm story would want.
3. wasm-bindgen-rayon + SharedArrayBuffer. Real browser threads, but needs COOP/COEP cross-origin-isolation headers, which plain GitHub Pages cannot set. NOT recommended for a demo whose whole point is 'open a link'.

Acceptance: a native test asserting the threaded and serial paths agree BIT-FOR-BIT. They should, given join-immediately semantics; if they do not, that is a finding about TUAS worth its own bead. GH #39 Phase 3.

title: Phase 4: promote htgr_sim_v1 out of examples/ into a library target
description:
cargo cannot build an [[example]] as a cdylib, so wasm needs a real target. The sim's App type must become reachable as a library item; the existing example becomes a thin native main.

Coordinate with the EXISTING bead op-76hu ('promote reactor models / widgets from examples into the digital-twin-engine library once V&V'd'). The wasm port is a second, independent reason to do that promotion — sequence them together rather than solving it twice.

Open question for the maintainer (GH #39): is promotion acceptable now, or should the wasm crate reach into the example tree as a stopgap? GH #39 Phase 4.

title: Phase 5: web shell — index.html, trunk config, canvas sizing, blob CSV export
description:
The browser-side glue. index.html, Trunk.toml, canvas sizing/resize, a loading indicator (the wasm blob will not be small).

CSV export needs rethinking, not porting: app_scaffold's csv_logging writes through std::fs::File + PathBuf, which has no browser equivalent. htgr_sim_v1 imports CsvSnapshotPanel and CsvLogger so it cannot simply be dropped. Honest browser behaviour is an in-memory buffer the user downloads via a blob URL — nicer than dropping the panel, and a small amount of JS glue. GH #39 Phase 5.

title: Phase 6: real-time pacing against requestAnimationFrame, incl. backgrounded tabs
description:
The sim paces against a native wall clock (app_scaffold/real_time_pacing.rs). In a browser it must pace against requestAnimationFrame AND survive being backgrounded — browsers throttle inactive tabs to roughly 1 Hz.

Needs an explicit, documented decision rather than a default: wall-clock-locked (sim time tracks real time, tab throttling means the sim visibly stalls), or fixed-step-with-catch-up (sim advances a bounded number of steps on return, with a cap so a tab left open overnight does not attempt hours of catch-up on one frame).

Whichever is chosen, say so in the docs — a user who backgrounds a reactor transient and returns to a different answer than they expected deserves to know which model they are in. GH #39 Phase 6.

title: Phase 7: measure and reduce wasm bundle size / load time — report honestly
description:
A release wasm build of a workspace this size will be large. Apply wasm-opt -Oz, lto=fat, panic=abort, codegen-units=1, and MEASURE.

Record the actual number. If it is unacceptable for a browser demo, say so and consider trimming the demo scope (see the maintainer question in GH #39 about a full vs teaching-subset demo) rather than quietly shipping a 40 MB page. A measured 'this is too big' is a legitimate deliverable. GH #39 Phase 7.

title: Phase 8: deploy + mandatory responsible-use caveats on the page itself
description:
Static hosting, plus the caveats this workspace's own policy requires, VISIBLE IN THE PAGE and not merely in a README:
- offline demonstration only (RESPONSIBLE_USE.md: not for reactor operation, licensing, safety-critical or operational digital-twin use)
- AI-assisted draft physics, no human V&V
- not affiliated with any reactor operator or vendor

Blocked on understanding op-s47i (6 pre-existing htgr_sim_v1 test failures). Publishing a demo makes those failures public too. Maintainer question in GH #39: is that a blocker, or a disclose-and-ship? My view: at minimum it must be disclosed on the page. GH #39 Phase 8.

title: Steam generator widgets: bubble generation needs to be physically fussy
description:
Maintainer wants the boiling detail in the steam-generator widgets done carefully -- bubbles are the thing that gives away a boiling surface, and getting them wrong makes an otherwise good drawing read as decoration.

CURRENT STATE (b42df8f, crates/outram-park-digital-twin-engine/src/components/steam_generator.rs):
  - Horizontal U-tube (VVER): bubbles rise off the tube bundle.
  - Vertical U-tube (PWR): entrained droplets drawn in the steam space above the water level.
  - Helical coil: once-through, no level and no bubbles -- correct, leave alone.

Both are deterministic scatters seeded from a hash, which must stay true (the widget is rebuilt every repaint; a real RNG makes them shimmer).

WHAT 'FUSSY' SHOULD MEAN -- candidate list, to be refined by the maintainer:
  - Bubbles should NUCLEATE AT THE HEATED SURFACE, i.e. originate on the tubes, not appear uniformly in the water volume.
  - Bubble size should GROW as they rise -- coalescence plus falling static head. A uniform bubble size is the tell.
  - Void fraction should INCREASE UP THE BUNDLE in a recirculating SG, so the population should be denser and larger near the top of the heated length.
  - Density should scale with DUTY, so the bubble field responds to the power/temperature sliders rather than being static decoration.
  - Nothing below the level should be a droplet and nothing above it a bubble -- the two populations must not cross the free surface.
  - Rise should be plausible: roughly vertical, slight wobble, faster for larger bubbles.

NOT YET SPECIFIED: the maintainer has not said which of these bothers them most. Ask before doing all of it -- some are cheap and some (a real void profile) are not.

CONSTRAINT: this is offline demonstration ARTWORK, not a two-phase model. outram-foam-multiphase has real void/CHF/wall-boiling closures but they are not wired to anything and must not be dragged in for a drawing. Keep it a display heuristic and keep saying so in the docs.

title: OPCPFluidArray: pipe ends are now direction-switched advection terminals (TUAS convention), not OpenFOAM patches (DONE)
description:
IMPLEMENTED 2026-08-12 in crates/outram-park-fork-coolprop, per explicit maintainer decision.

DECISION. OPCPFluidArray is a PIPE: its ends are junctions with a flow network, not patches on a standalone 3-D domain. It therefore uses the TUAS boundary-condition convention (upwind advection terminals) rather than generic OpenFOAM zeroGradient/fixedValue patch semantics.

THE DEFECT THIS REPLACES. The explicit energy convection fvc::div evaluated every boundary face from its BC TYPE alone. Two failure modes, both reachable:
- zero-gradient on an INFLOW face advects the domain's own enthalpy inwards (h_face = h_owner): self-referential, and with zero-gradient at both ends there is no boundary through which energy can enter or leave, so mdot*(h_out - h_in) = Q cannot even be posed. This is the state the array was left in before the he BC re-stamp (op-2qsf), which restored the VALUE while leaving the FORMULATION direction-agnostic.
- fixed-value on an OUTFLOW face forces the enthalpy the domain is exporting, which the domain does not get to choose. This is what a flow reversal produces from a correctly-set-up forward case.

PORTED LOGIC. From tuas_boussinesq_solver/src/lib/single_control_vol/boundary_condition_interactions/advection_to_bcs.rs -- its advection_heat_rate takes h_a when mdot_{a->b} >= 0 and h_b otherwise, and its calculate_*_advection_set_temperature / _non_set_temperature pair supplies the boundary-side enthalpy either from a prescribed BC state or from a zero-gradient extrapolation. In FV terms, with phi positive OUT of the domain:
    phi_b >= 0 (outflow, interior upstream) -> psi_f = psi_owner
    phi_b <  0 (inflow,  boundary upstream) -> psi_f = BC-evaluated face value
Implemented in openfoam_source::fv_operators::fvc::div_limited. Equivalent to OpenFOAM's inletOutlet, and it matches the vendored IMPLICIT fvm::div, which already switched on the flux sign -- only the explicit operator did not.

NO FORMULATION MISMATCH. The concern that a matrix/patch FV formulation could not express a lumped control-volume convention did not materialise: the selection is per face per call inside the explicit convection operator, needs no matrix-structure change, and a zero-gradient patch degenerates exactly to TUAS's non-set-temperature terminal.

API (additive; no signature changes, no version bump):
  set_outlet_enthalpy / get_outlet_advected_enthalpy / get_inlet_advected_enthalpy
  set_inlet_enthalpy KEEPS its signature but changes MEANING: it is now the upstream state used only while fluid enters through that end, ignored on outflow (inletOutlet), where before it was an unconditional Dirichlet value. Documented on the method.

VERIFICATION. flow_reversal_keeps_enthalpy_bounded_by_both_end_states: 8 cells, seed 400 K, left-end state 300 K, right-end state 500 K, +/-0.5 m/s switching every 2500 steps, 4 phases (two full reversals). Worst overshoot and worst undershoot both +0.00 kJ/kg across all 10000 steps. Forward flow settles the inlet cell to 301.7 K (the 300 K left state); after reversal the far cell settles to 499.9 K (the 500 K right state) -- each end supplies its own prescribed state exactly when it is upstream.

COORDINATION. tampines-steam-tables' TampinesSteamArray needs the same change; another agent owns that crate.

title: root@vm
njoy LEAPR: regeneration cache key omits the generator, so a physics fix keeps serving stale tapes
description:
FOUND 2026-08-21 while fixing the LEAPR temperature-block-selection bug
(generate_tape used deck block 0 regardless of the requested temperature).

THE HAZARD. leapr::generate::cached_tape_path keys its on-disk cache
(~/.cache/outram-park/endf/leapr-generated/) on a GenerationRecipe made of:
material, deck source, deck sha256, evaluation date field, physical-constant
vintage, temperature, and elastic-channel choice. It does NOT include anything
identifying the GENERATOR -- no crate version, no build id, no hash of the
LEAPR code path. So when the port's own physics changes, every previously
cached tape stays valid by that key and keeps being served.

OBSERVED, concretely. After fixing the block-selection bug I re-measured
H-in-H2O at 293.6 K through thermal_scattering_tape() and got the OLD, wrong
numbers back (T_eff 1195.35 K). The tape being read was
HinH2O-293.6000K-d09297bc57c0de2f.endf, written 2026-08-19 23:47 -- before the
fix. Deleting it and regenerating gave T_eff 1194.33 K. Nothing warned; the
recipe hash was unchanged because the deck, constants and temperature were
unchanged. Only the code was different, and the code is not in the key.

WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND THIS ONE FIX. This is a silent-stale-result mechanism
that survives across sessions and machines: a developer who fixes a kernel bug,
re-runs the suite and sees it pass may be seeing pre-fix cached data. It also
cuts the other way -- a REGRESSION would be masked on any machine with a warm
cache. It is exactly the failure mode the crate's own porting notes warn about
(a plausible number rather than an error).

Note the tests still passed both before and after the fix here, because their
tolerances (2 %) were wider than the bug (0.6 %). That is luck, not protection.

SUGGESTED FIX (not done -- raising rather than guessing at the right key):
  1. Add a generator identity to GenerationRecipe. Cheapest credible version is
     env!("CARGO_PKG_VERSION") plus a manually-bumped GENERATOR_REVISION const
     that any change to the LEAPR generation path must increment. A build-script
     hash over src/leapr/ would be automatic but adds build complexity -- the
     maintainer should pick.
  2. Whichever is chosen, write it into the .recipe sidecar (already emitted)
     so a stale artifact is diagnosable by reading the file.
  3. Consider an escape hatch env var to bypass/purge the cache for a run.

WORKAROUND UNTIL THEN: rm -rf ~/.cache/outram-park/endf/leapr-generated/ after
any change to the LEAPR generation path, before trusting a measurement.

notes.content:
FIXED 2026-08-21, commit 5a91ecf7, per the maintainer's explicit design
(GH #27 comment): a CachePolicy enum, not an automatic key fix.

CachePolicy::{AlwaysRegenerate, UseCacheIfAvailable} on SabRequest.cache,
set via with_cache(). AlwaysRegenerate is the default -- every request
computes fresh and never touches the on-disk cache at all (no read, no
write). UseCacheIfAvailable reuses a hit (log::warn! naming the staleness
risk and pointing at #27 on every hit), and falls back to generating fresh
-- never an error -- on a miss, populating the cache for next time.

Also bumped GENERATOR_REVISION 2 -> 3: the temperature-block-selection fix
(1a904fc5) changed output for HInH2O/DInD2O/OInD2O and should have bumped
it then but didn't. Documented as the concrete case study in the
constant's own doc comment, since GENERATOR_REVISION still exists and
still matters for UseCacheIfAvailable users -- the new policy doesn't
replace it, it makes the risk that mechanism can't fully close an explicit
opt-in instead.

Two new tests prove the actual bug scenario: one plants a deliberately
invalid tape under the real cache key and confirms AlwaysRegenerate never
reads it; the other confirms UseCacheIfAvailable falls back gracefully on
a miss and populates the cache.

Full njoy suite green (0 failures, 24 targets); workspace check clean;
clippy clean on the change.

title: tampines-steam-tables: region router accepts p = 0 Pa and the B23 line contradicts its own doc
description:
Two smaller sharp edges found 2026-08-11 in the full range-literal audit of region_fwd_eqn_single_phase done for op-cv1c. Neither is the op-cv1c defect and neither was changed by its fix (behaviour-only scope), but both are real.

1. p = 0 Pa is ACCEPTED, not rejected. The Region-2 arm's disjuncts use (0.0..=p_sat_reg4_pascal) and (0.0..=p_boundary_23_pascal) and (0.0..=100e6) — all START-INCLUSIVE at zero. IF97 is defined for p > 0 (the ideal-gas part of the Region-2 Gibbs function contains ln(pi), which diverges at p = 0), so a p = 0 call returns a non-finite value rather than panicking or erroring. The bounds-checked facade interfaces::checked already rejects p <= 0, so this only bites callers of the raw functions.
   Suggested fix: exclusive lower edges in the Region-2 arms, so p = 0 hits the router panic like any other out-of-envelope input. Behaviour change, needs its own test.

2. Doc/code contradiction on the B23 line. The doc comment on p_boundary_2_3 (region_3_.../aux_eqn_boundary_region_2_and_region_3.rs:4) says 'note that points ON this line belong to region 2'. But the router's Region-3 arm is (p_boundary_23_pascal..=100e6), start-INCLUSIVE, and it is matched BEFORE the Region-2 arm — so for T in [623.15 K, 863.15 K) a point at exactly p = p_B23(T) routes to Region 3, not Region 2. (This start-inclusivity predates op-cv1c, which only closed the upper edge.) The measured practical effect is small — at (623.15 K, 100 MPa) the two region equations differ by 3.245e-6 in h and 1.769e-5 in v — but one of the two statements is wrong and should be settled against the IF97 release, then the loser corrected.

3. Minor contract mismatch, same audit: ps_flash_eqm/validity_range.rs::is_outside_pressure_range PANICS on an out-of-range pressure while its ph_flash_eqm twin RETURNS true. Both are named as predicates and both are called as 'if is_outside_pressure_range(p) { panic!(...) }', so the ps version can never return true and its caller's panic is dead code with a worse message.

title: kovan-cli: DESIGN -- keep rust-analyzer warm across invocations (daemon, avoid per-call cold-start)
description:
Found 2026-08-22 wiring op-l3uz's def/sig/refs: RustAnalyzerSession::connect_with_observed spawns a FRESH rust-analyzer and waits out the full index (up to KOVAN_RA_TIMEOUT_SECS, 180s default) on EVERY kovan-cli def/sig/refs invocation, then shuts it down -- no session reuse across separate CLI processes. Fine for a single one-shot query, wasteful for an agent making several in a session.

kopitiam-semantic already ships the right primitive for a long-lived host: AsyncRustAnalyzerSession (crates/kopitiam-semantic/src/async_session.rs) -- spawn_async() returns immediately, state()/is_ready() poll non-blockingly (LspState::Connecting/Ready/Failed), and definition/references/hover/rename/code_actions/apply_code_action all return RequestError::NotReady{state} instead of blocking. This is built for exactly a background-indexing daemon, not a one-shot CLI call.

PROPOSED SHAPE (not yet built, needs a design decision before implementation):
- A 'kovan-cli lsp-daemon' background process hosting one AsyncRustAnalyzerSession per (root, rust-analyzer) pair, listening on a local IPC channel. kovan-cli def/sig/refs (and the not-yet-built rename/code-actions, op-<rename-bead>) become thin clients: check for a live daemon, use it if present, else fall back to today's spawn-per-call path (never a hard dependency on the daemon existing).
- Precedent already dogfooded in this exact workspace: kopi-beans' own 'bn daemon run' (confirmed running via ps aux, 2026-08-22) -- same lazy-spawn / long-lived-background-process shape, so this is not a novel pattern here.
- Lazy spawn on first use, idle-timeout auto-shutdown (e.g. 10-15 min of no requests) so it does not linger forever or need explicit start/stop.
- IPC choice needs a decision: a Unix domain socket is the natural choice on Linux/Termux, but Windows has no Unix sockets (named pipes there) -- this workspace's Android/Windows-portability discipline (CLAUDE.md) means the IPC layer needs a cross-platform answer or an explicit Windows fallback (spawn-per-call, no daemon) before this ships, not an unstated gap.
- Alternative/complementary: kovan-tui, when a human has it open, is ALREADY a long-running process -- it could host the same daemon role, with kovan-cli preferring it if reachable. Doesn't help an agent-only session where nothing keeps kovan-tui open, so the standalone daemon is still needed as the primary path.

notes.content: IMPLEMENTED 2026-08-22, revised from the original design during implementation per maintainer direction: NO idle timeout -- the daemon runs until explicitly stopped (kovan-cli lsp-daemon-stop --root <root>), not until N minutes idle. Shipped: crates/kovan/src/commands/lsp_daemon.rs (Unix-domain-socket daemon holding one kopitiam_semantic::AsyncRustAnalyzerSession per workspace root, lazy-spawn-on-first-query via def/sig/refs, newline-delimited JSON request/response, stale-socket recovery on crash). kovan-cli lsp-daemon-serve (hidden, internal) runs it; kovan-cli lsp-daemon-stop (visible) stops it. Windows has no daemon (query() returns None, falls back to spawn-per-call) -- explicit, not silently degraded, per this bead's own original design note. Verified live: cold call ~35-54s (real rust-analyzer index), warm calls 0.1-1s, explicit stop confirmed (process exits, socket removed), stale-socket recovery exercised accidentally (a killed daemon's leftover socket file was correctly detected and replaced). Also found+fixed a real bug during testing: the daemon's original idle-timeout clock started at connection-ACCEPT not connection-FINISH, so a single slow first request (waiting out indexing) could make the daemon look 'idle' the instant it replied -- moot now that idle-timeout was removed entirely, but the fix is preserved in the commit history as a lesson (measure idle from when a request finishes, not when it starts, in any future daemon).

title: teddy0@arch-aftershock-rapid-glass-S267454
TUAS: remove .unwrap() from library paths so failures propagate gracefully instead of panicking
description:
Maintainer request, 2026-08-13 07:2x (filed outside active hours; no audit or code work done -- no unwrap count taken yet).

Motivation: the op-m1jz crash. A recoverable ThermophysicalPropertyTemperatureRangeError was .unwrap()ed in one_d_solid_array_with_lateral_coupling/calculation.rs:95, which killed the whole htgr_sim_v1 process and reported no material, no node, and no temperature. That single unwrap is a symptom; the maintainer wants the pattern removed across TUAS so the library fails gracefully and the caller can decide what to do.

STEP 0 -- AUDIT BEFORE EDITING. Count and classify every .unwrap() / .expect() in crates/tuas_boussinesq_solver/src/. Report the number and the breakdown before changing anything; the result decides whether this stays one bead or becomes an epic with per-module children.

CLASSIFICATION -- these are NOT all the same defect, and a blanket sed would be wrong:
  (a) Recoverable domain errors (property out of range, convergence failure, bad geometry, empty collection) -- THESE ARE THE TARGET. Propagate through TUAS's existing error enum; do not invent a parallel error type without checking what the crate already has.
  (b) Lock poisoning on RwLock/Mutex -- very common in this codebase's Arc<RwLock<T>> state. Decide a single consistent policy rather than case-by-case.
  (c) Genuinely infallible (a just-inserted key, a statically-known-nonempty vec). Leaving these is acceptable, but each should say WHY in a short comment, or be restructured so the invariant is visible.
  (d) Tests / examples -- OUT OF SCOPE. unwrap in a test is fine and should be left alone.

CONSTRAINTS:
- Replacing .unwrap() with .expect("...") is NOT a fix -- it still panics. Only better as a stopgap on category (c).
- Error messages must carry the diagnostic payload the panic lacked: which component/node, what value, what the allowed range was.
- Changing public fn signatures to return Result is a BREAKING API CHANGE for TUAS's dependents (tampines, teh-o-prke dev-deps, nee_soon, the digital-twin engine). Expect a compile cascade; that is the compiler doing its job, per the workspace rename guidance. Do NOT bump the crate version -- versions are only bumped when the maintainer explicitly asks.
- Callers that genuinely cannot recover (a GUI render loop) should surface the error to the user and keep running or shut down cleanly, not re-unwrap it one level up. Moving the panic up a frame is not the deliverable.
- Release-mode build/test rule applies: cargo check --workspace --lib --tests, cargo test --release.

Related: op-m1jz (the crash that motivated this).

notes.content:
AUDIT COMPLETE, 2026-08-13 (read-only agent; counts measured by a brace-depth-aware Python walk over src/, not eyeballed).

HEADLINE: 5025 raw occurrences, 4929 live (96 in commented-out code), across 203 files. But 3823 are TEST code and out of scope.
  (a) recoverable domain error ....... 833   <- the target
  (a/c) into()/try_into() HTE conv ... 245   <- genuinely ambiguous, needs type info to split
  (b) lock poisoning + join .......... 26
  (c) genuinely infallible ........... 2
Plus a second panic class the brief missed: 166 panicking MACROS in library paths (panic! x125, todo! x18, unimplemented! x2, unreachable! x0).
Work estimate for bucket (a): ~975 sites, up to 245 more depending on the conversion judgement.

MY BRIEF'S PREMISE ON LOCKS WAS WRONG. This crate contains ZERO RwLock (grep -c RwLock src/ = 0). The primitive is Arc<Mutex<T>>, and there are only 22 .lock().unwrap() sites, in four files -- three of which are inside functions literally named _advance_timestep_parallel_buggy. Bucket (b) is a rounding error, not a policy problem: one PoisonedLock variant plus a .map_err() helper covers all 26 including the 4 join() sites.

THE SINGLE HIGHEST-VALUE FINDING -- the error variant carries no payload.
  TuasLibError lives at src/lib/tuas_lib_error/mod.rs (NOT tuas_lib_error.rs), 9 variants.
  ThermophysicalPropertyTemperatureRangeError is a UNIT variant. That is precisely why the htgr_sim_v1 crash reported no
  material, no node and no temperature. Even a perfect ?-propagation pass would still produce an unactionable message.
  Adding fields to it is arguably worth more than removing any single unwrap, and it is non-API-breaking (constructed in
  ~40 places, all as a bare unit value).

THE MOTIVATING CRASH IS A FREE FIX -- ZERO API CHANGE.
  advance_timestep ALREADY returns Result<(), TuasLibError> in both array modules (one_d_solid_array/calculation.rs:21,
  one_d_fluid_array/calculation.rs:22). So calculation.rs:95 and its twin at one_d_fluid_array/calculation.rs:127 convert
  with no signature change at all.
  Shape caveat: Array1 does not have the Result FromIterator blanket impl, so it needs collect::<Result<Vec<_>,_>>()? then
  Array1::from_vec -- one extra allocation per node-array per timestep. Short-circuits, so not measurably slower, but
  worth benchmarking since it runs per node per timestep.

BLAST RADIUS (grep-based, no LSP available to the agent; downstream figures +/-30%).
  Of 1084 non-lock library sites: 85 pub fns ALREADY return Result (free), 16 private already Result (free),
  174 private plain-return (internal only), 809 pub plain-return (API-BREAKING).
  Of the 166 lib panic-macros, 60 are already inside Result-returning fns (free).
  => COMBINED FREE, NON-BREAKING WORK: ~187 sites, ~19% of the total, zero downstream impact.
  The 809 breaking sites live in 125 distinct pub fns, but only 25 of those are referenced downstream, and 95%+ of the
  ~499 downstream call sites are in examples/ and src/bin/, not downstream library code.
  Per crate: digital-twin-engine 377, tampines 43, tampines-steam-tables 40, teh-o-prke 39, nee_soon 0 (does not depend on TUAS).
  Three names dominate: pipe_fluid_array_temperature (191), advance_timestep (126), calibrate_insulation_thickness (101).
  DUPLICATION MULTIPLIER: examples/fhr_sim_v*/app/thermal_hydraulics_backend/mod.rs exists in FOUR near-identical copies
  (34 call sites each) across tampines, digital-twin-engine, teh-o-prke, tampines-steam-tables. Fixing one means fixing four.

MISSING ERROR VARIANTS for bucket (a): root-finding/convergence failure; lock poisoning; correlation validity-range
  (distinct from property-table range -- 95 panic! in nusselt_number_correlations/pipe_correlations.rs say things like
  'gnielinski Re > 1e6, too high'); nonphysical input (20 panic! in dimensionalisation.rs); general empty-collection
  (CourantMassFlowVectorEmpty is hyper-specific); singular matrix (MatrixError::Singular{col} exists at matrix.rs:39 but
  its one call site flattens it into GenericStringError, losing the column index).

ON op-t647 (the tampines-steam-tables Result facade): the agent recommends TUAS should NOT copy the facade pattern.
  That facade exists because its internals are a large panicking mass nobody wants to re-sign. TUAS is the opposite --
  its property layer ALREADY returns Result correctly (range_check works); the panics are entirely in CALLERS. A facade

title: HTR-10 rung 2->3 seam: bridge MGXS into GeN-Foam nuclearData (RBF-parameterised over states)
description:
Parent: op-841p. THE RUNG 2 TO RUNG 3 INTERFACE. Wire to op-p6p.4 (genfoam neutronics/XS nuclearData structures, In Progress); do not invent a parallel format.

WHAT WAS VERIFIED IN THE CODE 2026-08-11 (crates/outram-foam-appbuilder-lib/src/genfoam/):
- The whole genfoam subtree is 32,334 lines with 262 tests and NOT ONE todo!().
- neutronics/xs/ (2167 lines, 13 tests): CrossSectionData at xs/mod.rs:134, NuclearDataOneEnergy at xs/nuclear_data_one_energy.rs:63.
- GroupConstants at xs/group_constants.rs:59 IS THE LANDING STRUCT and is already uom-typed: diffusion_coefficient (m), nu_sigma_f (1/m), sigma_pow (J/m), sigma_removal (1/m), chi_prompt, chi_delayed, inverse_velocity (s/m), disc_factor. PrecursorConstants at :85 carries beta, beta_tot, lambda.

THE HARD PART, AND WHY THIS IS ITS OWN BEAD: GeN-Foam's nuclearData is NOT an njoy/OpenMC MGXS library. It is a dict PARAMETERISED BY FEEDBACK VARIABLES via polyharmonic-spline RBF interpolation across perturbed reactor states. So the bridge is not a format conversion - it is 'run rung 1 at N perturbed states (fuel temperature, moderator temperature, density) and fit the interpolant'. Design the perturbation matrix explicitly and record it in the run manifest.

HOMOGENISATION IS THE OTHER HALF, AND IT IS EXPENSIVE TO GET WRONG. Wang et al. (2014), Ann. Nucl. Energy 64, 1-7 (PROPRIETARY tier - cite, do not re-host) measured, against continuous-energy MCNP5 on the detailed HTR-10 model: INFHOMMEDIUM +2820 +/- 19 pcm, LATTICECELL +681 +/- 24, MULTIREGION +661 +/- 21, LATTICECELL(CELLMIX) +653 +/- 21, MULTIREGION(CELLMIX) +470 +/- 22, DOUBLEHET +276 +/- 20. Worst is 10.2x the best. A homogenised pebble-bed model cannot reach the ~200 pcm accuracy this benchmark needs - which is exactly why the rung 2->3 homogenisation must be MEASURED against rung 1, not assumed. Captured as typed data in outram_park_digital_twin_engine::htr10::neutronics::wang_2014_unit_cell_bias.

title: outram-mc-libs: run_keff_csg/run_keff_delta don't dispatch on ComputeType
description: Discovered while building crates/outram-mc-tui (op-z5q/op-4h8): only physics::keff::run_keff (the bare-sphere-only driver) branches on KeffSettings::compute (ComputeType::CpuSingleThread/CpuMultiThread/Gpu). physics::transport_csg::run_keff_csg and pebble_beds::keff_delta::run_keff_delta both ignore the field entirely and always run the single-thread CPU path (verified: neither file references ComputeType/rayon/GpuContext at all). This means outram-mc-tui's compute-backend selector (CPU-single/CPU-multi/GPU) is currently inert for every one of its presets, since all four route through run_keff_csg or run_keff_delta, not run_keff. Follow-up: add the same ComputeType dispatch (rayon-parallel histories, GPU Sigma_t lookup with CPU fallback) to run_keff_csg and run_keff_delta that run_keff already has, so CSG and delta-tracking runs can actually use multi-core/GPU acceleration.

V&V agreement tests added and passing: delta_multithread_agrees_with_single_thread (1.65 sigma) and csg_multithread_agrees_with_single_thread (0.47 sigma), both thread-count-invariant to the bit. chem-eng: rewrite transfer functions as O(1) recurrences — MEASURED 28 us/step plateau in TUAS
description:
MEASURED 2026-08-07 (this was previously an unverified grep-level claim; it has now been benchmarked). Release build, AMD Ryzen 5 5600, rustc 1.97.0, std::time::Instant, 200-step windows per checkpoint, two 5,000-step warm-ups discarded. The temporary benchmark was deleted afterwards and the tree left byte-identical.

MECHANISM (confirmed):
crates/chem-eng-real-time-process-control-simulator/src/lib/beta_testing/stable_transfer_functions/first_order_transfer_fn.rs -- and a byte-identical twin under alpha_nightly/, which is the tier TUAS actually imports:
  :16      pub(crate) response_vec: Vec<FirstOrderResponse>,
  :113     self.response_vec.push(new_response);   -- one entry per input change; a real PID error signal changes every step (the guard at :89-92 only compares to 9 dp)
  :134-138 re-sums the ENTIRE vector every step via .iter_mut().map(|r| r.calculate_response(current_time)).sum()
  :147-230 clear_first_order_response_vector prunes via repeated .position() + .remove(index), itself O(n) per removal.

CORRECTION TO THE ORIGINAL CLAIM -- growth is NOT unbounded in general. FirstOrderResponse::is_steady_state (:291-301) retires an entry once time_elapsed/process_time > 20.0, so the vector saturates at N = 20*tau/dt entries. Cost is linear in step index up to that horizon, then FLAT. It is unbounded only when the run never reaches 20*tau -- which is exactly what happened to teh-o-prke (tau1 ~ 80.8 s at 1 ms -> 1.6 M entries).

MEASURED per-step cost:
  A: TUAS's shipped PID, dt=0.04 s -- 5.33 us @100 -> 27.90 @1k -> 28.61 @10k -> 28.07 @39k   (total 1.13 s / 40k steps)
  B: PID, dt=0.1 s               -- 5.36 -> 11.34 -> 11.45 -> 11.46                            (0.46 s / 40k)
  C: PID, dt=0.001 s             -- 52.4 us @1k -> 259.3 @5k -> 528.3 @10k -> 1084.6 @20k -> 1131.3 @40k -> 1133.3 @79k  (79.5 s / 80k)
  D: bare ProportionalController -- 1.83 @100 -> 9.30 @1k -> 9.34 @39k                          (0.37 s / 40k)
  E: PID tau=1000 s, dt=0.04 s   -- 5.34 @100 -> 35.96 @1k -> 105.57 @5k -> 367.04 @20k -> 692.35 @39k, never plateaus (15.7 s / 40k)

O() CONCLUSION: per-step cost is O(min(n, 20*tau/dt)) -- linear in step index during the ramp, then a flat plateau. Case C is decisive: growth is exactly linear (5k->10k = 2.04x, 10k->20k = 2.05x against 2.00x step ratios) then goes flat at step 20,000 = exactly 20 s / 0.001 s, the retirement horizon. Case E, whose horizon (500,000 steps) is never reached, grows linearly for the whole run and never plateaus. So: O(n^2) total while ramping, O(n * 20*tau/dt) once saturated.
Cost per response term is constant at 9.3 / 9.5 / 9.3 / 9.4 ns/term for A/B/D/C -- which nails the mechanism quantitatively.

WHY IT STILL MATTERS EVEN THOUGH IT SATURATES: TUAS's SHIPPED config sits at a permanent flat 28 us/step for ONE PID, and it runs two PIDs plus a P block -- ~66 us/step of pure controller overhead, forever, for arithmetic that needs ~1 ns. Halving the timestep doubles it.

TWO AGGRAVATING FINDINGS:
- first_order_transfer_fn_with_zeroes.rs:27,29 carries TWO such vectors, so every first-order-with-zero block costs 2N terms.
- proportional_controller/mod.rs:29-44 implements a PURE GAIN G(s) = K_c as (K_c*s + K_c)/(s + 1) through the same machinery, so a P controller does O(20/dt) work per step. Its own doc at :58 says "probably overdoing it in terms of computation cost but that's not an issue ... yet".

TUAS PID PATH CONFIRMED (library code, not #[cfg(test)]):
crates/tuas_boussinesq_solver/src/lib/pre_built_components/ciet_three_branch_plus_dracs/ciet_educational_simulator_loop_prototypes/version_3/mod.rs:508-512 AnalogController::new_filtered_pid_controller(1.75, 1.75 s, 1.0 s, 1.0); second CTAH controller :521-525; ProportionalController delay block :533-536; timestep 0.04 s (:108). Also version_2.rs:482,495 and ~20 further sites in DRACS regression/validation tests, plus coupled_dracs_loop_tests/isolated_dracs_loop_resistance_calibration/mod.rs:331.

REMEDY -- copy what teh-o-prke already did. Commit 46194ba6 (2026-07-15, bead op-e46.4), single file, +229/-80: deleted the five TransferFnFirstOrder lags and replaced them with a fixed-size 5-element state array advanced by a closed-form backward-Euler recurrence (delayed_neutron_layer.rs:405-413):
    C_i^{n+1} = (C_i^n + dt*(beta_i/Lambda)*P) / (1 + dt*lambda_i)
No Vec, no history, public API unchanged, guarded by an O(1) regression test precursor_update_is_o1_per_step (:555). The precedent numbers are recorded in-tree and were verified: delayed_neutron_layer.rs:88-89 "measured ~49 us -> ~1.8 ms/step from step 1k to 40k"; :549 "Representative: ~0.7-1.0 ns/step, flat across blocks".

A first-order lag must carry ONE state variable, not a history of every input it has ever seen.

RELATED: op-e46.5 already tracks a latent second instance -- nordheim_fuchs::advance_with_reactivity_driver still takes a &mut TransferFnFirstOrder.

HARDWARE CAVEAT: absolute microsecond figures are specific to this CPU. Machine-independent are (a) the linear relation between per-step cost and step index in the ramp regime, (b) saturation landing exactly at 20*tau/dt steps, (c) cost scaling exactly with live-term count.

notes.content:
IMPLEMENTED 2026-08-11 (awaiting maintainer review; NOT closed by the agent).

APPROACH CHOSEN: option 1, the exact O(1) recurrence. Not time-bucketing. The recurrence reproduces the pre-existing semantics EXACTLY rather than approximating them, so bucketing was not implemented and no grouping error had to be quantified. It is the zero-order-hold / step-invariant discrete equivalent, exact for piecewise-constant input; module docs cite Astrom & Wittenmark, Seborg et al., Franklin/Powell/Workman, Ogata, Hochbruck & Ostermann, Oppenheim & Schafer, and Smith (open access). No editions/years/pages given -- none verified against a physical copy.

SCOPE: all FIVE vector-carrying block types, in BOTH tiers (alpha_nightly and beta_testing), not just the first-order one named in the original report:
  first_order_transfer_fn.rs                (1 vec -> 2 scalars)
  first_order_transfer_fn_with_zeroes.rs    (2 vecs -> 1 scalar)
  second_order_transfer_fn.rs               (1 vec -> 3 scalars, enum per damping regime)
  decaying_sinusoid.rs                      (1 vec -> 2 scalars, decaying rotation)
  decaying_exponentials.rs                  (1 vec -> 3 scalars; alpha_nightly only)
The two tiers are now byte-identical apart from the tier import path; previously they had drifted (beta_testing's decaying_sinusoid had a '>' vs '>=' heaviside that dropped the cosine value at t == start_time; unified on alpha's correct '>=').

MEASURED, same harness before and after (release, AMD Ryzen 5 5600, rustc 1.97.0, 200-step windows, two 5,000-step warm-ups discarded). Baseline reproduces this bead's original figures:
  A PID dt=0.04, 40k:   28.35 us/step plateau -> 0.17 us/step;  1.188 s -> 0.007 s
  B PID dt=0.10, 40k:   13.15 us/step         -> 0.17 us/step;  0.478 s -> 0.007 s
  C PID dt=0.001, 80k: 1176.11 us/step plateau -> 0.17 us/step; 83.280 s -> 0.015 s   (the decisive case)
  D P only dt=0.04:      9.42 us/step         -> 0.06 us/step;  0.379 s -> 0.002 s
  E PID tau_d=1000 dt=0.04: 736.86 us/step still rising -> 0.17 us/step; 15.167 s -> 0.007 s
  F PID tau_d=80.8 dt=0.001 (the PRKE shape): 2329.52 us/step still rising -> 0.17 us/step; 127.599 s -> 0.014 s
Per-step cost is now FLAT in the step index in every case, including E and F whose retirement horizons are never reached.

PHYSICS UNCHANGED: the summed output over each of the six runs is identical before and after to the three decimal places printed (e.g. case A sink 17175484.304 both times). The only intended difference is that the old code discarded exp(-20) = 2.06e-9 of each step response when it retired one; the recurrence carries that residual, so the new answer is marginally MORE accurate.

VERIFICATION (methodology + results in each test doc comment): each recurrence checked against the closed-form analytic superposition of the retained response structs, over 2000 steps, tolerance 1e-9. Max abs differences measured 2026-08-11: first order 6.33e-15; with zeroes 1.69e-15; second order 9.05e-15 / 5.11e-15 / 6.94e-15 (zeta = 0.35 / 1.0 / 2.4); decaying sinusoid 4.16e-16 sine, 4.86e-16 cosine; decaying exponential 8.60e-16 overdamped, 6.66e-16 critically damped; irregular time grid 7.99e-15; dead time 6.11e-15. All round-off, not discretisation error.

REGRESSION TESTS (would have caught the original defect):
  block_state_size_does_not_grow_with_step_index -- 100k steps at dt=0.001 with tau=80.8 s; state size identical at step 100 and step 99,999 ([2,1,3,2,3] alpha, [2,1,3,2] beta). Pre-0.2.0 the counts would have been 101 and 100,000.
  pid_step_cost_does_not_grow_with_step_index (alpha) -- filtered PID tau_d=80.8 s at dt=0.001: 0.172 us/step @5k -> 0.175 us/step @100k, ratio 1.02; bare P 0.059 -> 0.060, ratio 1.02.
  first_order_step_cost_does_not_grow_with_step_index (beta) -- 0.0550 -> 0.0570 us/step, ratio 1.04.

CAPABILITIES PRESERVED: irregular/arbitrary timesteps (the recurrence uses the actual elapsed time per call, verified by a dedicated test) and dead time (queued in a VecDeque bounded by delay/dt -- 26 entries for 0.25 s of dead time at dt=0.01, flat over a 2000-step run; empty when there is no dead time). htgr_sim_v1: the GUI stepped the plant at a rate no test drove, and it crashed
description:
FIXED 2026-08-12 in the same change that landed the nodalised steam generator, recorded because the CLASS of defect will recur.

WHAT HAPPENED. examples/htgr_sim_v1/app/mod.rs steps the plant at PHYSICS_DT_S = 1.0e-3 s, ten sub-steps per 10 ms tick, to keep the animation smooth. Every test in the suite steps at 0.05 s. The nodalised steam generator's fluid arrays are unstable BELOW about 0.005 s (the water side starts resolving its own acoustic transient and the IAPWS-IF97 (p,h) flash leaves Region 5 range and panics), so the whole suite was green while the simulator killed its physics thread within 30 s of launch:

  [physics thread panicked] htgr-physics failed in helium primary loop (circulator + hot gas duct): (p,h) point lies above the 1073.15 K isotherm. (p,h) flash into IAPWS-IF97 Region 5 (T > 1073.15 K) is unsupported.

FIX. SteamGeneratorConfig::substep is now a FIXED accumulate-and-advance clock rather than a 'subdivide to at most this' bound: the exchanger accumulates whatever dt the caller passes and advances the arrays in whole 0.0125 s steps, carrying the remainder. That makes it a multi-rate sub-model, which is also what its physics wants -- nothing in it moves on a millisecond scale.

REGRESSION TESTS ADDED (both would have caught it):
- physics::steam_generator::tests::the_gui_millisecond_timestep_reaches_the_same_state -- drives the exchanger over the same 100 s at 0.05 s and at 1 ms and asserts they agree. Measured: identical to 0.0000 K and +0.0000% on duty.
- physics::tests::the_whole_plant_steps_at_the_gui_timestep -- 20 000 plant steps at 1 ms, end to end.

THE GENERAL LESSON, worth acting on beyond this bug: a test suite that drives a plant at a timestep the application does not use is not testing the application. Any future sub-model with a stability window (and the coolprop / steam-tables arrays all have one) needs at least one test at the app's real rate. Consider making PHYSICS_DT_S visible to the physics module so a test can assert against it rather than hard-coding 1.0e-3 in two places.

title: TUAS Wakao fix: the BEFORE baseline was never measured, so calibration masking is unresolved
description:
The Wakao correlation was corrected on 2026-08-11 from the transposed `Nu = 2 + 1.1 Re^0.333 Pr^0.6` to the published `Nu = 2 + 1.1 Pr^(1/3) Re^0.6`. The implementing fleet captured AFTER numbers but stopped with the BEFORE baseline outstanding, so the question the whole task existed to answer is still open.

THE QUESTION. Wakao sits on a CALIBRATED CIET path — ciet_heater_v2, the porous-media components, the heater top/bottom heads. The crate CLAUDE.md records that CIET steady-state natural-circulation and isothermal tests agree with published Zweibaum (2015) and Zou et al. (2019) data to within ~6 percent. If a heat-transfer coefficient was calibrated against experiment WHILE the correlation was wrong, the calibration absorbed the error, and correcting the correlation should have moved that agreement.

So: did agreement change? Nobody measured. Three possibilities and they have very different consequences:
1. Agreement unchanged -> the calibrated path was insensitive to Wakao, or the calibration dominates it. Fine, but worth knowing.
2. Agreement degraded -> the calibration WAS masking the error, and re-calibrating against experiment with correct physics is a separate, larger job needing maintainer sign-off. Do NOT re-tune to hide it and do NOT revert the correlation to keep tests green.
3. The tests never exercise Wakao at all -> a coverage finding, and it would explain how a factor-5.84 error at Re = 1000 survived.

HOW TO GET IT. Run the CIET suite on a worktree at the pre-fix commit and compare against the post-fix numbers. Both runs are expensive: the full TUAS lib suite measured 2959.84 s (49 minutes) on this machine, and per CLAUDE.md it must run in PARALLEL, never with --test-threads=1. A killed run is neither a pass nor a fail.

COMPOUNDING FACTOR, see op-lmye: ciet_heater_v2 feeds a HYDRAULIC-diameter Reynolds number to Wakao, which is defined on PARTICLE diameter. So the calibrated path had TWO errors — a transposed correlation and a wrong length scale. Fixing one without the other may move agreement in a confusing direction, and any baseline comparison must say which fixes were in place for each run.

THIS IS A CLASS, NOT AN INCIDENT. The same audit filed op-ctbq (Pr_bulk/Pr_wall swapped in PipeGnielinskiCalibrated - the same transposition class, still latent), op-tidc (Sieder-Tate bounds inverted), op-i7od (LMTD ambient helper sign/panic), and op-a3yi. A correlation module with this many transposition and inversion defects deserves a systematic pass against the published forms, not one fix at a time.

title: kovan-gui: digitiser Auto-trace fails silently when reference values are unset/invalid
description: Maintainer report on GitHub issue #30 (comment posted 2026-08-22T03:42:59Z, right after the op-zfnh/op-8ixa/etc progress report): 'digitiser doesn't really autocalculate the points for me using the max and min x and y. I want the points to be calculated.' Root cause: the four axis-reference lines (op-zfnh's persistent draggable box) are seeded with pixel positions on image load, but their VALUES (ref_val[0..4], what those pixel positions mean in data units) start as empty strings. calibration() correctly rejects empty/non-numeric values, but auto_trace()'s failure path just sets self.message to a one-line string at the very bottom of a long scrollable side panel -- easy to miss entirely, especially with no visual distinction from the normal status line. Net effect: user drags the box, clicks Auto-trace, nothing visibly happens, no points appear. Fix: make calibration completeness/validity visible BEFORE the user even clicks Auto-trace (inline per-field validation) and make a failure message impossible to miss (prominent banner, not a buried label).

notes.content: Fixed: added DigitiseApp::message_is_error (set via new set_status/set_error helpers, replacing every raw self.message = assignment) plus (1) a prominent red banner duplicating any error message at the TOP of the side panel, right under the heading -- not just the easily-missed one-line status label at the bottom of a long scrollable panel; (2) live inline per-reference-value-field validation (green check / orange 'not set' / red 'not a number') so an incomplete calibration is visible before Auto-trace is even clicked; (3) auto_trace() now distinguishes 'traced 0 points' (shown as an actionable error suggesting threshold/curve-colour/box-placement) from a genuine pipeline error, instead of silently reporting '0 points' as if it were a normal success. Verified: cargo check clean both targets, cargo test --release -p kovan clean (160+15+17+7 passing).

title: tampines TwoFluid1d: no Dirichlet-pressure boundary (ReservoirInlet / PressureOutlet) -- needed before a Marviken-style vessel discharge
description:
Recorded 2026-08-12 as part of op-62vf so the Edwards/Marviken agent is not blocked by surprise.

TwoFluidBoundary currently has exactly three variants, all VELOCITY boundaries: Closed, PrescribedVelocity(u), ChokedOutlet{area_fraction, ambient_pressure}. A velocity face carries no pressure sensitivity, so it stays out of the pressure matrix entirely (d_k = 0) and the pressure floats on the compliance diagonal. That is right for a closed-vessel blowdown and wrong for a pipe fed from a plenum.

drift_flux::AxialBoundary already has the two missing variants and they have no counterpart here:
  - ReservoirInlet{stagnation_pressure, stagnation_enthalpy}
  - PressureOutlet{pressure}

WHAT ADDING THEM INVOLVES in the six-equation solver, which is more than in drift flux:
  1. A half-cell pressure coefficient d = dt/(rho_face * dx/2) per PHASE at the boundary face, obtained from the 2x2 PhaseCouplingBlock rather than from a single mixture density.
  2. A Dirichlet term area * m_k_face * d_k * p_boundary on the first/last cell's pressure RHS, weighted by 1/rho_k like every other flux term in that equation.
  3. A per-phase inflow donor state: the entering fluid needs alpha_g, rho_g, rho_l, h_g and h_l, not just a mixture (p, h). A stagnation (p0, h0) does not determine a six-equation inflow state; the boundary has to say what the phase split of the incoming fluid is, or assume equilibrium and document it.

Point 3 is the real design question and it should be decided deliberately, not defaulted.

Also missing and worth deciding at the same time: the ChokedOutlet imposes the SAME velocity on both phases (no slip at the break) and hands the HEM dispatcher a mass-weighted mixture enthalpy. Both are documented at the variant, both are modelling inconsistencies, and a Marviken case may care about the first.

title: code_aster: consolidate the two IsotropicHardening types
description:
damage::IsotropicHardening and isotropic::IsotropicHardening are distinct types written by different agents. The isotropic one is the VMIS_ISOT_*/VISC_ISOT_* curve driving the von Mises radial return; the damage one is the curve set used by Rousselier and GTN. Both names are defensible in their own module, so neither was renamed and damage's is left out of the aster re-export block. Consolidating them into one curve type is a design decision, not a mechanical rename. Also worth folding in: damage::equivalent_stress overlaps semantically with viscoplastic::von_mises_of_deviator (one takes full stress, one the deviator), and scale_tensor plus the deviator/mean reassembly are duplicated across viscoplastic.rs and metallurgy.rs.

njoy: SiC coherent elastic -- per-atom-type Debye-Waller (Zhu 'exact' option) + locate Zhu & Hawari ICNC 2015
description:
Split out of op-4daf when that bead's root-cause work closed (GitHub issue #28, 2026-08-21). Two residual items, neither blocking:

1. PER-ATOM-TYPE DEBYE-WALLER. After the evaluation's basis error is accounted for, ~1% of the SiC coherent-elastic residual remains, and it sits entirely in the weak |b_Si - b_C|^2 difference reflections (all-even hkl, h+k+l = 2 mod 4): +6.1% at n=20 rising monotonically to +23.5% at n=100. Growth with tau^2 confined to the difference reflections is the signature of a per-atom-type Debye-Waller factor inside the structure factor, F = sum_j b_j exp(-W_j tau^2) exp(i tau . r_j) -- Zhu 2014's 'exact Debye-Waller' option (card-5 iel=2 in the modified LEAPR) -- against the single compound coefficient this crate uses (Zhu's cubic approximation, iel=1, crystals::debye_waller_decks). Implementing the exact option would let the crate reproduce those reflections. Low value on its own since they are weak at the thermal point.

Related: the DW coefficients themselves differ, 4W' = 5.977/eV (tape, 300 K) vs 5.382/eV (this crate, 296 K), ~10% apart after temperature scaling. Not root-caused.

2. LITERATURE GAP. Zhu, Y. and Hawari, A. I. (2015), 'Implementation of a Generalized Coherent Elastic Scattering Formulation for Thermal Neutron Scattering Analysis', ICNC 2015, OSTI 23100909 -- the paper describing the in-house routine that actually produced the published MF=7/MT=2 (per reference-data/endf/tsl-SiinSiC.readme). No freely available copy located; NOT catalogued in kovan-literature. It is the document that would confirm or refute the basis finding in op-4daf. The 2014 MS thesis (the primary source actually used) IS catalogued: crates/kovan-literature/open/theses/zhu2014thermal.{json,pdf}.

See crates/njoy-outram-park-fork/docs/leapr-sic-coherent-elastic-vv.md.

notes.content:
ITEM 1 DONE 2026-08-21, commit 26395482. Per-atom-type Debye-Waller (Zhu's 'exact' option) implemented and measured; the shape argument that predicted it is confirmed.

MEASURED. Residual against the published tape, per difference reflection (all-even hkl, h+k+l = 2 mod 4):
  n     compound      per-atom
  4      +2.8 %        +2.0 %
  12     +4.8 %        +2.0 %
  20     +6.9 %        +1.9 %
  36    +11.1 %        +1.9 %
  44    +13.4 %        +1.9 %
  52    +15.7 %        +1.9 %
Compound residual grows 5.6x across the range; per-atom is FLAT to within 0.1 percentage point. The tau-dependent component is therefore fully accounted for.

THE HEADLINE NUMBER DID NOT IMPROVE. sigma(0.0253 eV) 2.85303 b (-2.98 %) -> 2.84387 b (-3.30 %) vs the tape's 2.94078 b. Expected: the difference reflections are weak, so the total is dominated by sum reflections and by the basis question this option does not touch. An assertion pins that so it cannot be misread later as an improvement. The option is opt-in (ElasticChannel::GenerateExactDebyeWaller), never the default, and reports NotValidatedAgainstReferenceTape.

NEW LEAD, AND IT IS ON OUR SIDE. The flat ~2 % offset that remains matches in size and sign the ~10 % difference in the fitted W' itself: 5.977 /eV (tape, 300 K) vs 5.382 /eV (this crate, 296 K) after temperature scaling. Unlike the basis question this is about THIS PORT, needs no outside expertise, and is the most likely place a real defect on our side is still hiding. That is now this bead's remaining technical work, alongside item 2.

IMPLEMENTATION. coher::general::coher_general_with_per_atom_debye_waller folds exp(-2 W'_j E_tau) into each atom's amplitude, shared inner sum keeps the compound path byte-identical, wrong-length slice falls back rather than misassigning. endout::ElasticOutput::CoherentPreWeighted stops the factor being applied twice -- added as an enum variant not a flag so the decision had to be made at every match site, which immediately caught a second dispatch site in the validation reporter. crystals::debye_waller_deck_for_species gives the per-species decomposition with a test that it and the compound deck list name the same set.

Two of the new tests initially failed on MY wrong expectations, not the code: W' set to 0.05 /eV where SiC's real value is ~1.35 /eV; and the synthetic final edge treated as a reflection when it is a duplicated histogram-extension edge (the two paths weight it differently by 3.0e-4, now excluded and documented rather than papered over).

ITEM 2 (locate Zhu & Hawari ICNC 2015) still open.

cargo fmt -p is destructive in this workspace: 222 files, +21057/-4495
description:
Found 2026-08-11 by the njoy/outram-mc agent while following the CLAUDE.md bookkeeping-pass routine, which tells agents to run `cargo fmt -p <crate>`.

MEASURED: `cargo fmt -p njoy-outram-park-fork -p outram-mc-libs` rewrote **222 files, +21 057 / -4 495 lines**. None of it was wanted; all of it was reverted and the real edits replayed by hand. The final semantic diff for that task was 4 files, +587/-48.

ROOT CAUSE: the repository is not rustfmt-clean and carries no `rustfmt.toml`, so `cargo fmt` reformats to upstream defaults across every file it touches, not just the ones being edited. The two conditions compound — no pinned style, and a large body of never-formatted legacy code.

WHY THIS MATTERS BEYOND ONE AGENT: the workspace CLAUDE.md "Bookkeeping pass" section instructs agents to run a formatter as part of a routine that is explicitly designed to be run per-crate by a fleet. Anyone who follows that instruction literally detonates a 20k-line diff into a branch, and if they do not notice, it lands. The instruction is currently a trap.

Also relevant: the same day, a `rustfmt --check` on four `tampines-steam-tables` files showed the legacy formatting problem directly — `ps_flash_eqm/validity_range.rs` would be substantially rewritten by rustfmt despite the change under review being three lines.

OPTIONS, maintainer's call:
1. Add a `rustfmt.toml` pinning the current style closely enough that a format pass is a no-op on untouched code, then format the workspace once in a single dedicated commit.
2. Format the workspace once, in its own commit, on a quiet branch, and accept the one-time churn — after which `cargo fmt -p` becomes safe and the CLAUDE.md instruction becomes true.
3. Amend CLAUDE.md to forbid `cargo fmt` and require `rustfmt` on individually named changed files only.

Until one of these is done, CLAUDE.md should carry a warning next to the bookkeeping-pass formatter step. Do NOT let an agent format the workspace as a side effect of unrelated work.

notes.content:
STEP 5 DONE 2026-08-14 -- the pebble-bed wiring, the majorant re-check, and the end-to-end number this bead demanded all now exist and are measured.

WHAT THE 'MOSTLY CLOSED' CLAIM MISSED. Commit e4afd51779 added tests/htr10_graphite_thermal_scattering_pebble_bed.rs and described it as closing most of this bead, but its k-eigenvalue test was #[ignore]d and therefore never ran. Un-ignoring it exposed TWO real defects:

1. THE STATED BLOCKER WAS NOT REAL. The ignore reason was that Nuclide::from_core("C12") fails with WmpData("nuclide C12 not in WMPL container"), attributed to a gap in the embedded WMPL blob and filed as op-wqk.21 (which was never actually created -- it is absent from the store). There is no data gap: the CORE library carries natural carbon as "C0" (ENDF/B-VII.1 ZA 006000, listed as 'C-nat | 006000' in wmp-nuclide-manifest.md). tests/thermal_graphite_elastic.rs:307 already used "C0" correctly. It was a wrong nuclide name, not missing data. No op-wqk.21 is needed.

2. THE ACTUAL WIRING DEFECT, which the ignored test was hiding. With C0 in place the free-gas and bound runs returned BIT-IDENTICAL k. Root cause: Nuclide::sample_thermal had exactly ONE caller in the crate, physics::transport_csg. Neither physics::keff (collide_batched, transport_history, transport_history_tabulated) nor pebble_beds::keff_delta called it. So xs_at_energy correctly substituted the BOUND cross section -- setting collision rates -- while secondary energy and angle were still drawn free-gas. Internally inconsistent, and it admits no up-scatter, so a graphite-moderated spectrum cannot equilibrate. All five collision sites now route through the bound-atom law below the table cutoff, mirroring transport_csg / OpenMC src/thermal.cpp ThermalData::sample. sample_thermal consumes no RNG when there is no table or the neutron is above cutoff, so every non-thermal nuclide is bit-identical -- full suite 265 passed / 0 failed confirms no regression.

3. THE TEST PROBLEM WAS ALSO FAST, independently. It mirrored triso.rs's HEU dispersion (pf 0.30, 1 cm3 box, k~2.08) where neutrons are absorbed long before thermalizing, so the law was never sampled BY CONSTRUCTION and a null result was uninterpretable. Added diagnose_thermal_spectrum_reach (ignored diagnostic, homogenized infinite-medium sweep) to measure this instead of assuming it: 34.41% of 20k fission-born neutrons reach below the 4 eV cutoff after a mean 67.4 scatters. Retuned the case to pf 5e-4 (C/U-235 ~ 3.8e3, order-of-magnitude of a real HTR-10 pebble ~1e4) in a 6 cm reflective cube. Sensitivity is real and was measured: at pf 5e-3 the comparison has no power at all (0.20 sigma).

MEASURED RESULTS (2026-08-14, release, this environment):
  - graphite_thermal_scattering_changes_pebble_bed_keff PASSES. Free-gas C-nat k = 1.08838 +/- 0.01851; bound graphite k = 1.95254 +/- 0.01407; separation 37 sigma (dk = 0.86416, combined sigma 0.02325), 300 particles / 8 inactive + 15 active, ~107 s. Confirming run at 800 particles / 10 + 25: 1.07579 +/- 0.00833 vs 1.94166 +/- 0.00626, 83 sigma, ~410 s. Direction is physically sensible -- the bound law holds a Maxwellian near 0.025 eV where U-235 fission dominates, while the free-gas kernel (stationary target, no up-scatter) lets neutrons slide below thermal into parasitic 1/v capture. This is the gap between a CORRECT and an INCORRECT treatment of the same system, not a design change.
  - MAJORANT RE-CHECK, which this bead's coordinator note explicitly demanded be measured and not assumed (a Woodcock majorant that under-bounds Sigma_t is a SILENT BIAS, not a crash): majorant_still_bounds_total_xs_with_bound_graphite PASSES. Worst Sigma_t/Sigma_maj = 0.909091 over 200k log-spaced points from 1e-4 to 4.2 eV across both materials -- exactly 1/1.1, i.e. the sampling grid captures the true per-bin peak and the entire 10% margin survives even against graphite's 221-edge Bragg sawtooth.
  - Also fixed a latent race in the test helper: the regenerated-tape temp file was named from the PID only, but cargo runs these tests as threads of ONE process, so concurrent callers wrote/read/deleted the same path -- EndfParse("unexpected end of section data"). Now uses a per-call atomic counter. It was invisible while only one test used the helper.

WHAT THIS DOES NOT ESTABLISH: no benchmark comparison. The reference throughout is this workspace's own njoy port, so these are internal-consistency gates, not an independent NJOY/OpenMC-ACE oracle. The geometry is a packed cube, not HTR-10 -- reproducing HTR-10's published k-effective still needs the real geometry/composition under op-6tz.35 / op-6tz.35.1. AI-assisted draft, human review still owed. Do not describe HTR-10 neutronics as validated on the strength of this.

tampines-steam-tables: x_ph_flash Region-3 saturated-liquid sub-region chain picks v_tp_3y below the critical pressure
description:
FOUND while building the steam_table_plotter GUI (op-eebe, GH issue #26), by
plotting the saturation dome that x_ph_flash's own branch logic implies.

WHERE
crates/tampines-steam-tables/src/interfaces/functional_programming/ph_flash_eqm/mod.rs,
in x_ph_flash, the t_sat > 623.15 K branch. The saturated-LIQUID specific
volume is selected as:

    if t_sat_kelvin <= 634.659 { v_tp_3c }
    else if t_sat_kelvin <= 643.15 { v_tp_3s }
    else if t_sat_kelvin <= 646.483 { v_tp_3u }
    else { v_tp_3y }

SYMPTOM
For t_sat in (646.483 K, 647.096 K) -- i.e. p_sat from about 21.93 MPa up to
the critical pressure 22.064 MPa -- the else-branch calls v_tp_3y. IAPWS-IF97's
sub-region 3y is defined ABOVE the critical pressure (roughly 22.064-22.11 MPa),
so below it the polynomial diverges. It does NOT return NaN; it returns a
finite, wildly wrong number.

MEASURED 2026-08-20
At t_sat = 646.503 K, p_sat = 21.906 MPa (a sample the plotter's dome sweep
landed on), the resulting saturated-liquid enthalpy came out as

    h_f = -1.108e21 kJ/kg     (s_f = -1.151e18 kJ/(kg K))

against a physical value of order 2000 kJ/kg. Because the value is finite it
passes any is_finite() filter. In the plotter it collapsed the entire enthalpy
axis of the p-h figure to a range of -1.1e21 .. 0 kJ/kg until it was caught.

CONSEQUENCE FOR THE LIBRARY
x_ph_flash returns x = (h - h_f)/(h_g - h_f). With h_f at -1e21 the quality
comes back as approximately 0.0 for essentially any h, and h_g computed through
the lever rule loses all precision to cancellation. So a (p,h) flash whose
saturation temperature lands in that ~0.6 K band silently reports a wrong
quality rather than erroring. Every consumer of x_ph_flash in the near-critical
band is affected: kappa_t_ph_eqm interpolates on it, and the choked-flow
dispatcher routes on it.

Note the saturated-VAPOUR chain in the same function may have the same shape of
problem (its thresholds are 640.691 / 643.15 / 646.599, then v_tp_3z); it was
not separately diagnosed here because the liquid divergence masked it.

SUGGESTED NEXT STEP (not done -- this is a library fix, out of scope for op-eebe)
Check the sub-region selection against the IAPWS-IF97 supplementary release for
backward equations v(p,T) in Region 3, specifically which sub-region covers the
saturated-liquid line between 21.93 MPa and p_crit. Add a verification test at
t_sat = 646.5 K asserting h_f is of order 2000 kJ/kg. Consider adding an
ordering guard (h_f <= h_g, s_f <= s_g) so a diverged polynomial cannot be
returned as a valid state.

WORKAROUND IN PLACE (plotter only, does NOT fix the library)
examples/steam_table_plotter/curves.rs::saturation_state tries v_tp_3u first in
that band, validates the resulting state with
SaturationState::is_physically_ordered (h_f <= h_g, s_f <= s_g, h_f >= -1 kJ/kg),
and falls back to the neighbouring sub-region, dropping the sample if neither
works. That keeps the figures honest; it does not touch x_ph_flash.

notes.content:
FIXED 2026-08-20. Root cause was narrower than first diagnosed: only
x_ph_flash's own copy of the sub-region chain was broken. The other three
functions with an identical-looking chain in the same file (v_ph_eqm,
u_ph_eqm, s_ph_eqm) already gated their final (t_sat > 643.15 K) branch on
PRESSURE (p_mpa <= 21.9010 / <= 21.9316), matching v_tp_3u/v_tp_3x/v_tp_3y/
v_tp_3z's own doc-commented validity windows in MPa. x_ph_flash's copy alone
used TEMPERATURE-only thresholds (t_sat_kelvin <= 646.599 / <= 646.483) for
that same branch, so it could and did fire v_tp_3y outside its valid pressure
window -- confirmed exactly at the bug's own measured case (t_sat=646.503K,
p=21.906 MPa): v_tp_3u there gives v=2.6124e-3 m3/kg -> h_f=1993.29 kJ/kg
(sane), v_tp_3y gives v=3.076e-5 m3/kg -> h_f=-5.64e21 kJ/kg (the recorded
garbage). Fix: copied the already-correct pressure-gated pattern from the
other three functions into x_ph_flash (crates/tampines-steam-tables/src/
interfaces/functional_programming/ph_flash_eqm/mod.rs).

FIRST ATTEMPT, reverted: I initially replaced the WHOLE chain in all four
functions with a general-dispatcher-plus-temperature-nudge scheme
(v_tp_3(t_sat +/- eps, p), leaning on the crate's own fully-correct near-
critical `subregion()` map in backward_eqn_pt_3). That version fixed the
measured -1e21 case too (h_f=1993.07 kJ/kg, matching), and self-consistency-
checked cleanly against several points -- but it also replaced ALREADY-
correct code (the other three functions' pressure-gated final branch, which
was never broken) and introduced new regressions verified against this
crate's own reference-table tests: at t_sat=643.15 K exactly (the row the
crate's own saturation_table_260_degc_to_crit_temp_373_946_degc.rs literally
comments "very near critical point, this kinda fails bad") a tiny eps=1e-6 K
nudge landed BOTH the liquid and vapour probes on the same sub-region (a
genuine corner where several named sub-regions meet), and larger eps values
that worked there caused wrong-side jumps at other points near 21.93 MPa.
No single fixed epsilon covered both. Rather than build a more elaborate
adaptive-epsilon scheme under time pressure, I fell back to the narrower fix
above, which is a one-line-pattern-copy from code the crate's own test suite
already validates, not new numerical machinery.

VERIFIED: full library suite (cargo test --release -p tampines-steam-tables
--lib) is 959 passed, 0 failed, 13 ignored -- unchanged pass count from
before this fix (confirms no regression), and the previously-recorded
sic... I mean the previously-recorded h_f=-1e21 case now returns h_f=1993.29
kJ/kg instead. cargo check --workspace --lib --tests also clean.

REMAINING (not done, follow-up if wanted): the two SAME-ISSUE gap tests in
outram-mc-libs's triso_shell tests are unrelated to this crate; not
applicable here. The near-critical quality-formula ill-conditioning noted
during investigation (h_g - h_f -> ~0.0007 kJ/kg within ~0.6 K of Tc, making
x = (h-h_f)/(h_g-h_f) numerically enormous for any h even slightly off) is
real physics already documented in this crate's own "Known accuracy
pitfalls" (CLAUDE.md: "Region 3 backward equations lose digits within ~0.5 K
of Tc"), not a defect introduced or left by this fix -- no clamp was added,
since that would be new scope beyond the diagnosed dispatch bug.

kovan: resilience — recover from corrupted TOML / file data, and merge-conflict management
description:
Maintainer request while dogfooding the PDF-reader page-context panel (2026-09-02).

Kovan's on-disk model is human-readable Markdown + fenced-TOML artifacts + BibTeX + Git (issue #35 north star). Two failure modes have no handling today:

1. **Corrupted / malformed data recovery.** A hand-edit or bad merge can leave a paper's Markdown with a broken fenced-TOML `[kovan]` block, a truncated `kovan.toml`, an unparseable `.bib` entry, or a half-written file. `artifact::parse_document` is already total (reports problems, keeps good artifacts) but there is no UI to surface those problems, no 'quarantine + keep going' for a broken `kovan.toml`, and no guided repair. Define the recovery behaviour for each tracked file type and expose it in the GUI/CLI.

2. **Merge-conflict management.** Because the store is Git-native and multi-clone, `<<<<<<< / ======= / >>>>>>>` markers will land in paper Markdown, `bibliography.bib`, and `kovan.toml`. Kovan should detect conflict markers, present the two sides at the artifact/entry level (not raw hunks), and let the user pick/merge without dropping to `git mergetool`. Ties into the Save Repository tab (op-9vo6.19/.20).

Scope: design doc first (what 'corrupted' means per file type, what recovery is safe/automatic vs. needs confirmation), then implement. Relates to op-9vo6 (issue #35 redesign) and the Save Repository work.

title: Zircaloy Poisson: possible WRONG SIGN in dnu/dT -- highest priority check
description:
FLAGGED 2026-08-05 during the op-6sl.7 validation-case work. NOT CONFIRMED — logged as a hypothesis to check, not a finding.

Search summaries of the abstract of Northwood, London & Bahen (1975), 'Elastic constants of zirconium alloys', J. Nucl. Mater. 55(3) 299-310, DOI 10.1016/0022-3115(75)90071-9, ADS 1975JNuM...55..299N, state that MEASURED Poisson's ratio DECREASES with temperature for Zircaloy-2.

The ported MATPRO correlation pair gives nu INCREASING with temperature throughout the alpha range — that is the whole mechanism by which it crosses 0.5 at 1354.84 K.

IF THE ABSTRACT IS RIGHT, this is a wrong-SIGN error across the entire alpha range, which is far more serious than the crossover the parent bead records. The crossover would then be a symptom rather than the disease.

THE PAPER WAS NOT READ. Every literature host was blocked by this container's egress policy — osti.gov, nrc.gov, pnnl.gov, digital.library.unt.edu, inis.iaea.org, sciencedirect.com, link.aps.org, doi.org, arxiv.org all refused at CONNECT with 403, and WebFetch is blocked session-wide. So this rests on a search-result summary of an abstract, which is exactly the kind of second-hand claim that should not be trusted.

TO RESOLVE, in order of value:
1. Read Northwood 1975 itself and record the measured dnu/dT sign with its temperature range.
2. Better, read Schwenk & Wheeler (1978), DOI 10.1016/0022-3115(78)90491-9 — it measures nu DIRECTLY on Zircaloy-4 over 297-589 K, so it settles the sign without going through E and G.
3. Cross-check against NUREG/CR-7024 / PNNL-19417 (Luscher & Geelhood, PNNL, 2011).

Tracked as VAL-3 in crates/outram-park-fork-offbeat/docs/validation/poisson_ratio_zircaloy.md and as GAP-7 in the sibling References.md.

Do NOT change the correlation numerics on the strength of this bead alone. If the sign is genuinely wrong upstream, the workspace rule is to REPRODUCE the defect and document it with a test that pins the discrepancy — not to silently correct it.

---

title: outram-foam-basic-lib: 24 broken intra-doc links in module docs; ComputeBackend::Auto does not exist
description:
Found 2026-08-13 while documenting op-yvj.4.8. Pre-existing, not introduced by
that change.

## 1. Broken intra-doc links (24, across at least 5 modules)

cargo doc -p outram-foam-basic-lib --no-deps --release emits 24
'unresolved link' warnings. Unique targets: ComputeBackend (and ::Serial,
::CpuMulti, ::Gpu, ::Auto, ::resolve), ThreadCount, select_backend,
gpu_adapter_present, LduMatrix, bicgstab, bicgstab_prepared, gmres,
gmres_prepared, derived_name, parallel, rayon::ThreadPool::install.

Root cause: lib.rs puts an OUTER /// doc comment on the 'pub mod X;'
declaration while X.rs carries INNER //! module docs. Rustdoc concatenates the
two and resolves the intra-doc links of the merged block in the scope of the
outer item (lib.rs), where none of those names are imported. Every module
carrying both forms is affected -- compute, krylov, ldu_matrix, fv_operators at
minimum.

Why it matters: this is a human-interface-layer defect in the sense the
workspace CLAUDE.md makes mandatory. The module docs are the map a new reader
meets first, and in the rendered docs every type name in them is dead text
rather than a link -- so 'navigable by a Rust developer using rust-analyzer
alone' fails exactly where navigation was supposed to start.

Two candidate fixes, maintainer's choice:
  (a) drop the outer /// summaries from lib.rs and move that text into each
      module's //! header, so links resolve in module scope; or
  (b) keep the lib.rs summaries but make every link in them a fully-qualified
      path (crate::compute::ComputeBackend).
(a) is the smaller diff and keeps one doc home per module; (b) preserves the
at-a-glance module table in lib.rs.

## 2. ComputeBackend::Auto is documented but does not exist

src/compute.rs module docs say callers 'pass [ComputeBackend::Auto]-style
resolution via [select_backend]'. The enum has exactly three variants --
Serial, CpuMulti, Gpu -- and no Auto. Confirmed by reading the enum body.
The sentence should name select_backend/resolve without inventing a variant.
This one is a correctness defect in the docs, not just a dead link, and would
mislead a reader looking for a variant to pass.

Verification: cargo doc -p outram-foam-basic-lib --no-deps --release 2>&1 |
grep -c 'unresolved link'  =>  24, both before and after the op-yvj.4.8 doc
change (checked via git stash).

description: Merge vertices closer than a tolerance into one (Blender's Mesh > Merge by Distance / bmo_remove_doubles / weld modifier). Spatial-hash bucketing for O(n); rebuild faces on the merged vertex set; drop faces that collapse to a degenerate (<3 distinct verts) after welding. Hardens boolean output and imported polygon soups before the CSG/polyMesh export bridges. New MeshOp::Weld { tolerance } variant + dispatch. V&V: coincident-duplicated cube welds 16->8 verts back to chi=2; a slit sphere seam welds to watertight; tolerance=0 is a no-op.

title: root@vm
outram-blender: fill holes (cap open boundary loops -> watertight)
description: Detect boundary loops (edges incident to exactly one face) and cap each with a centroid-fan triangulation, making an open surface watertight. Blender analogue: bmo_holes_fill / Fill Holes. Winding of each cap triangle is chosen opposite to the boundary directed edge so it stays consistent with the existing surface (adjacent faces traverse the shared edge in opposite directions). Directly serves the MC CSG bridge, which needs closed geometry. New MeshOp::FillHoles variant + dispatch. Pairs with weld (op-hzs.22): weld stitches near-coincident seams, fill-holes closes true gaps. V&V: cube with one face removed -> chi back to 2, watertight (every edge borders 2 faces); an already-closed mesh is a no-op.
