title: root@vm
outram-blender: solidify (shell thickness -> closed solid)
description: Give a surface thickness: offset a copy of every vertex inward along its area-weighted vertex normal by 'thickness', add the inner shell with reversed winding (cavity-facing), and bridge open boundary edges with rim quads. Blender analogue: MOD_solidify (simple mode). Turns a surface patch into a volume (CFD wall meshing) or a closed mesh into a hollow shell. Reuses the boundary directed-edge tracing from fill_holes and consistent-winding rules. New MeshOp::Solidify { thickness } variant. V&V: open grid -> closed slab chi=2, watertight; closed cube -> nested outer+inner shells (hollow box) chi=4, each shell watertight; thickness=0 collapses inner onto outer.
root@vm
title: root@vm
outram-blender: recalculate normals (make winding consistent + outward)
description: Blender's Recalculate Normals Outside (mesh.normals_make_consistent). BFS over face adjacency (shared undirected edges): flip any neighbour that traverses a shared edge in the SAME direction as its already-oriented neighbour, making each connected component consistently wound; then per component compute signed volume and flip the whole component if negative so normals point outward. Unlike boolean_general::orient_outward (which only whole-mesh-flips an ALREADY-consistent mesh by volume sign), this repairs an inconsistently-wound polygon soup -- foundational for boolean, the CSG inside-test, and solidify. New MeshOp::RecalculateNormals. V&V: a cube with a subset of faces reversed recovers full consistency + positive signed volume; an all-inward cube flips outward; an already-correct cube is unchanged.

outram-blender: triangulate operator (all-quad/ngon -> triangle Mesh)
description: Fan-triangulate every polygon face into triangles and rebuild a triangle-only Mesh. Distinct from export::triangulate, which yields a GPU-style IndexedTriangles index buffer, not a Mesh. A triangle Mesh is what Loop subdivision, QEM decimation, and the MC/CFD export bridges prefer. Winding preserved. New MeshOp::Triangulate. V&V: cube (6 quads) -> 12 triangles, V8 E18 F12 chi2 watertight; an already-triangulated mesh is unchanged in count.

title: root@vm
outram-blender: inset faces (per-face inset ring)
description: Blender's Inset Faces (bmo_inset, Individual mode): replace each face with a smaller inner copy shrunk toward the face centroid by a fraction, plus a ring of quads bridging the original boundary to the inner face. Independent inner vertices per face (individual mode). Winding kept outward/consistent. New MeshOp::Inset { amount } where amount in (0,1) is the fraction toward the centroid; amount<=0 is a no-op. V&V: cube inset 0.3 -> V32 F30 chi2 watertight; amount=0 no-op.
root@vm
title: root@vm
outram-blender: bisect (plane cut / half-space clip)
description: Blender's Bisect. Cut a mesh by a plane (point + normal) and keep the half where n.(x-point) <= 0, clipping every face against the half-space with Sutherland-Hodgman. New crossing vertices deduped per undirected original edge so adjacent faces share them. Leaves the cut open (composes with fill_holes to cap). Directly serves the CSG/MC half-space workflow. New MeshOp::Bisect { point, normal }. V&V: cube[-1,1]^3 bisected by z=0 (+z) -> open half-box; fill_holes(that) -> watertight chi=2 with signed volume = 4 (half of 8); plane fully outside keeps mesh unchanged; plane fully inside-out yields empty mesh.
root@vm
title: root@vm
outram-blender: revolve / spin (surface of revolution)
description: Blender's Spin. Sweep a profile polyline around an arbitrary axis (point + direction) by an angle in N segments (Rodrigues rotation), connecting consecutive rings with quads. Full 360deg closes the seam (wrap), a partial angle leaves it open. Off-axis profile points only in v1 (on-axis pole points documented as needing a subsequent weld). Generates pipes/tubes/vessels/cones -- surfaces of revolution, on-theme for reactor geometry. Free generator fn (like primitives), not a MeshOp. V&V: a 2-point off-axis segment revolved 360deg/16 -> open 16-gon tube V32 F16 chi0; fill_holes(that) -> closed prism chi2 with positive volume ~ 16-gon*height; a partial 180deg sweep leaves an open strip.

description:
outram-blender can already WRITE OpenFOAM polyMesh three ways (export::to_polymesh_text -> 5 ASCII strings; export::write_polymesh -> disk; feature-gated export::to_poly_mesh -> real outram_foam_basic_lib::io::poly_mesh::PolyMesh). It has NO reader, so a polyMesh cannot be loaded back into a Mesh. Add the import side to complete round-trip polyMesh I/O.

Recommended route (low-risk, no new parser): under the foam bridge feature, add export::from_poly_mesh(&outram_foam_basic_lib::io::poly_mesh::PolyMesh) -> Mesh that converts the PolyMesh points + faceList into the half-edge Mesh boundary surface (Mesh::from_polygons). The foam crate already provides PolyMesh::read(dir) (crates/outram-foam-basic-lib/src/io/poly_mesh.rs:212), so from_poly_mesh + PolyMesh::read gives full disk read for free. Optionally also a feature-free ASCII parser (points/faces only) for standalone use without the foam dependency.

Caveats to document: a polyMesh is a VOLUME mesh (points/faces/owner/neighbour/cells); outram-blender's Mesh is a boundary surface, so import reconstructs the face soup (all faces), not cells. Winding/owner-neighbour orientation may need a recalc_normals pass.

V&V: round-trip a primitive — write_polymesh(cube) or to_poly_mesh(cube) -> from_poly_mesh -> assert V/E/F/chi == original cube (8/12/6/2), watertight after an optional recalc_normals. Methodology + measured results in the test doc comment per the workspace V&V rule.

title: root@vm
outram-blender: multifidelity neutronics pipeline as a third solver bridge
description:
MAINTAINER REQUEST 2026-08-11: once the HTR-10 multifidelity neutronics pipeline lands, wire it into the outram-blender port.

THE PIPELINE: rigorous Monte Carlo -> MGXS -> deterministic multiphysics -> PRKE + decay heat. Each rung trades fidelity for speed and is validated against the rung above it. Scoped under op-jyyp (HTR-10 simulator); the scoping document is docs/reactor-scoping/htr10-neutronics.md.

WHY BLENDER IS THE RIGHT HOME. crates/outram-blender is the mesh-authoring frontend and ALREADY carries exactly this pattern twice over:
- an opt-in Monte Carlo bridge: mc-export -> sim -> MC Studio
- an OpenFOAM volume-meshing bridge: foam-mesh -> foam_mesh -> tet-dual Mesh Studio
The multifidelity pipeline becomes a THIRD bridge of the same shape — author the geometry, then drive the fidelity ladder from it. The existing MC bridge is the closest precedent and should be read first; rung 1 of the pipeline is the same Monte Carlo engine that bridge already targets, so this may extend that bridge rather than sit beside it. Decide which and record why.

DESIGN CONSTRAINT ALREADY COMMUNICATED UPSTREAM. The pipeline agent has been told to give the pipeline a HEADLESS, SCRIPTABLE entry point taking a geometry description plus a run configuration, rather than something only callable from a test — precisely so a frontend can drive it. If that constraint was not honoured, fixing the pipeline API is in scope here before wrapping it.

REPRODUCIBILITY CARRIES THROUGH THE BRIDGE. The pipeline must emit a run manifest recording the workspace commit, cross-section data and version, MC seed and batch counts, group structure and homogenisation choice. A frontend that drives the pipeline must PRESERVE and surface that manifest rather than hiding it behind a button — a result a user cannot trace back to its inputs is not usable as evidence. Same discipline as the graph digitiser bead op-5v5.8, which must record calibration with every export.

BLOCKED UNTIL THE PIPELINE LANDS. Do not start this before the rungs exist. Filed now so the intent is not lost, and so the pipeline is designed with a frontend consumer in mind rather than retrofitted.

Note outram-blender is GPL-3.0, a fork of Blender mesh architecture, and is NOT affiliated with the Blender Foundation — keep that framing intact in any docs added here.

title: outram-blender: Blender GUI CAD/modeling operator parity (survey, GH #37)
description: Umbrella for translating Blender's interactive GUI CAD toolset into outram-blender headless operators. Full survey + ground rules in GitHub issue #37 (theodoreOnzGit/outram-park-backend). Children are one operator family each; each becomes a parameterised, deterministic, Android-buildable operator (the GUI gesture's output values become explicit params). Concepts/algorithms only — not Blender source; GPL provenance header required for any literal transcription. AI-assisted draft until human-reviewed.

notes.content:
Closed. All 48 children done — and checking scope rather than the count, the survey they came from (GitHub issue #37) was itself the scope definition, so the child list is not a partial view of a larger ambition the way op-6w0's was.

What landed: ~15 new modules in crates/outram-blender covering sections A-J of the survey — selection/topology, loop cut/knife/slide, subdivide/bevel/extrude/inset, merge/rip/dissolve/bridge/fill/connect, transform + proportional + symmetry + spin/screw, numeric input + snapping + cursor/pivot + measure, normals/attributes/remesh/deform, curves + curve-surface + curve-mesh + NURBS surfaces, text-to-geometry, primitives + extra-objects + draw tool, LoopTools, snap-utilities-line, PDT, Bool Tool, F2/AutoMirror/Bsurfaces, object-mode ops, array patterns.

Test count went 167 -> 449 passing lib tests over the run. Clippy clean for every new module (15 pre-existing warnings elsewhere untouched). cargo check --all-targets and --examples clean throughout.

Provenance discipline held: concepts and documented behaviour only, no Blender source transcribed; every new module carries a GPL-3.0-only SPDX header and cites the upstream file whose behaviour it reimplements.

STILL AN AI-ASSISTED DRAFT PENDING HUMAN V&V. The crate README's Bookkeeping status axes are deliberately unchanged — both remain 'Not yet manually checked', and GitHub #37 was left OPEN for maintainer review rather than closed alongside this bead.

title: outram-blender: optional bridge to outram-foam-basic-lib sparse solvers (CG/GAMG)
description: Optional reuse path: wire outram-foam-basic-lib's LduMatrix + FvMatrix::solve_cg / solve_gamg (iterative sparse, FV face-addressing) as an ALTERNATIVE backend for outram-blender's large one-off sparse solves. Primary LA is faer (added 2026-07-17: dense + sparse Cholesky, better for interactive same-matrix/many-RHS mesh editing). The foam bridge is for code reuse within OUTRAM PARK on large iterative solves; note the impedance mismatch (foam ldu = cell-FACE addressing vs a vertex-vertex mesh Laplacian graph) and that foam has no sparse DIRECT factorization. Depends on the sparse-solve consumers existing first (op-hzs.1/.2 Laplacian/subdivision, plus future ARAP/parameterization).

notes.content: UNBLOCKED 2026-07-23: op-hzs.15 Laplacian smoothing is now a real sparse-solve consumer. Kept open as optional/low-value: the smoothing solve is symmetric, same-matrix, multi-RHS -> faer sparse Cholesky (direct) is the right fit and is implemented. foam LduMatrix is face-addressed, iterative-only (no direct factorization) -> impedance mismatch, strictly inferior here. Revisit only if internal solver code-reuse is specifically wanted.

title: teddy0@snrsi-arch-desktop
outram-mc: no regression gate stops a thermal-scattering law from being wired with no caller
description:
Prophylactic, from the op-hc2o post-mortem (2026-08-14).

Two defects in that bead's step 5 were the SAME class of failure: physics that is implemented, tested at unit level, and then never actually invoked by the path that matters.

- Nuclide::sample_thermal was implemented, had 7 green V&V tests at nuclide level, and had exactly ONE caller in the crate (physics::transport_csg). Both k-eigenvalue paths -- physics::keff and pebble_beds::keff_delta -- silently fell through to free-gas kinematics for 3.5 months.
- The one test that would have caught it was #[ignore]d for a reason that was itself wrong (a nuclide NAMING error, "C12" vs the real "C0", misdiagnosed as a missing-data gap and attributed to a bead that was never even filed).

Neither showed up as a failure. Everything was green the whole time.

WHAT TO ADD:
1. A test that asserts every collision path routes thermal scattering. Concretely: for each of the transport entry points (run_keff, run_keff_delta, transport_csg), run a short fixed case with a moderator nuclide carrying an S(alpha,beta) table and assert the result DIFFERS from the same case without it. A bit-identical result is the exact signature of a dead branch and is trivially detectable -- that is what caught this one.
2. A guard against silently-ignored tests. #[ignore] on a V&V test hid a defect for months. Options: a periodic '--ignored' sweep in the suite runner, or a rule that an #[ignore] reason naming a bead must reference a bead that EXISTS (op-wqk.21 did not).
3. Consider a general audit for other implemented-but-uncalled physics. grep for pub fns in src/physics/ and src/material/ whose only callers are tests. sample_thermal would have shown up.

Not urgent, but this class of bug is invisible to the existing gates by construction, and the workspace has now been bitten by it once at P1 severity on the HTR-10 critical path.

title: chem-eng: reconcile the new z_domain c2d port with the ZOH recurrences already in stable_transfer_functions
description:
FILED 2026-08-11. Two agents landed overlapping mathematics in this crate on the same day; they must be reconciled rather than left as duplicates.

WORK A (op-fm5, landed, uncommitted in tree): every transfer-function block in BOTH tiers now advances by the exact zero-order-hold / step-invariant discrete equivalent, hand-derived per block. Lives in:
  src/lib/alpha_nightly/stable_transfer_functions/{first_order_transfer_fn,first_order_transfer_fn_with_zeroes,second_order_transfer_fn,decaying_sinusoid,decaying_exponentials}.rs
  src/lib/beta_testing/stable_transfer_functions/{same, minus decaying_exponentials}.rs
  verification + O(1) regression tests: */stable_transfer_functions/recurrence_tests.rs
Each carries a module doc deriving Phi = exp(A T), Gamma = integral_0^T exp(A s) ds * B and citing Astrom & Wittenmark, Seborg et al., Franklin/Powell/Workman, Ogata, Hochbruck & Ostermann, Oppenheim & Schafer, and Smith (open access). No editions/years/pages -- none verified against a physical copy, and that constraint should be kept.

WORK B (concurrent, same day): a z_domain module ported from the GNU Octave control package (GPLv3-or-later), including c2d. That is the SAME transformation, generically implemented.

THE QUESTION TO SETTLE: should the hand-derived per-block recurrences call into z_domain::c2d, or stay as they are?
Arguments for keeping them as-is: they are exact closed forms specialised per block (2-3 scalars, no matrix algebra, no allocation), they are what makes the 0.17 us/step figure possible, and they are already verified against the analytic superposition to ~1e-15. Routing them through a general c2d would likely cost performance and would put an Octave-derived GPL port on the hot path of every controller step.
Arguments for reconciling: one source of truth for the discretisation, and z_domain::c2d could be VERIFIED AGAINST the per-block closed forms -- which is probably the real win here, and is cheap: the recurrence_tests.rs analytic-superposition harness can be pointed at c2d output directly.

RECOMMENDED: keep the specialised recurrences on the hot path; add a cross-check test that z_domain::c2d reproduces them for a first-order lag and for all three second-order damping regimes. That gives the shared-truth benefit with no performance cost.

ALSO CHECK: LICENCE PROVENANCE. The crate was relicensed Apache-2.0 -> GPL-3.0-only on 2026-08-11. The op-fm5 recurrences are original work (derived from textbook-standard mathematics, nothing copied) and carry no upstream provenance. The z_domain code IS an Octave port and needs its NOTICE/attribution-header treatment kept intact per the workspace rule. Do not let a later refactor blur which files are which.

title: tuas: LMTD ambient heat-flux helper has opposite sign conventions and panics when ambient hotter than fluid
description: Found 2026-08-11 by correlation audit during op-4542. crates/tuas_boussinesq_solver/src/lib/heat_transfer_correlations/parallel_heat_exchangers.rs:121-145. The equal-temperature early return computes U*A*(T_amb - T_fluid) (heat INTO fluid, matching the doc); the LMTD branch passes ambient as the cold pair and fluid as the hot pair, yielding T_fluid - T_amb (heat OUT of fluid) -- opposite sign convention between the two branches. Inline comment at L133-134 claims delta T = ambient - fluid, contradicting the actual argument order. Additionally log_mean_temperature_difference panics when hot < cold, so the function panics outright whenever ambient is hotter than the fluid -- the very heat-input case its doc describes.

title: chem-eng: z-domain follow-ups — d2c ZOH (matrix log), c2d foh/impulse-invariant, order > 2 support
description:
CONTEXT: on 2026-08-11 the crate was relicensed Apache-2.0 -> GPL-3.0-only (see crate NOTICE) and a SISO port of the GNU Octave control package's c2d/d2c/tf/filt core landed in src/lib/beta_testing/z_domain/ (upstream gnu-octave/pkg-control commit f39e2625bffc56864c3af746b4410bb71ce6bbb1, GPLv3-or-later side only; the BSD-3 SLICOT kernels were NOT ported). Implemented and verified (11 tests, methodology + measured results in verification_tests.rs doc comments): Zoh, Tustin, TustinPrewarp, MatchedPoleZero c2d; Tustin, TustinPrewarp, MatchedPoleZero d2c; O(1) DF2T discrete stepping.

DELIBERATELY LEFT OUT, in scope for this bead:
1. d2c by zero-order hold — upstream inst/@ss/__d2c__.m computes it with a matrix logarithm (logm of the augmented [A B; 0 I] matrix). Needs a general dense matrix log; not half-implemented.
2. c2d by first-order hold (foh) and impulse-invariant methods — upstream inst/@ss/__c2d__.m (foh via augmented matrix exponential) and imp_invar.m.
3. System order > 2 for Zoh and MatchedPoleZero — currently ZDomainError::UnsupportedOrder, because poles/zeros come from the quadratic formula. General order needs a polynomial root finder (companion-matrix eigenvalues) and/or a scaling-and-squaring expm. Tustin variants already handle any order.
4. Consider whether z_domain should be wired into the controllers layer (a discrete PID via c2d of the analog PID) and whether TUAS-facing alpha_nightly needs a twin — currently z_domain exists in beta_testing only, documented in crate CLAUDE.md.

LICENCE RULE for any follow-up: per-file provenance. If a follow-up ports SLICOT-derived material (anything under slicot-reference/ or the __sl_* kernels), that file's BSD 3-Clause notice must be carried verbatim; do not relabel it GPL. See crate NOTICE.

title: VERIFY CITATIONS: textbook references for the O(1) / ZOH recurrence were supplied from model knowledge, not checked
description:
ACTION: a human must verify these citations against the actual books before any of them appears in a publication, an arXiv draft, or anywhere the project asserts provenance.

WHAT HAPPENED. On 2026-08-11 an AI assistant supplied the literature basis for the exact zero-order-hold / step-invariant discretization used to replace the growing response vectors in chem-eng-real-time-process-control-simulator (bead op-fm5), and for the analytic exponential integration in crates/teh-o-prke/src/decay_heat.rs. The citations were produced FROM MODEL KNOWLEDGE while offline. Authors, titles and publishers are asserted with reasonable confidence. EDITIONS, YEARS, PAGE NUMBERS, CHAPTER NUMBERS AND EQUATION NUMBERS WERE NOT VERIFIED AND MUST NOT BE ASSUMED CORRECT.

This is exactly the failure mode RESEARCH_INTEGRITY_AND_PROVENANCE.md exists to prevent, and exactly the class of error AI_USAGE.md requires a human to catch. A plausible-looking but wrong citation is worse than no citation, because it survives review by looking right.

CITATIONS TO CHECK:

Sampled-data control theory (the primary basis - the discretization is EXACT, not an approximation, for piecewise-constant input):
1. Astrom, K. J. and Wittenmark, B., "Computer-Controlled Systems: Theory and Design", Prentice Hall. Claimed to derive x[k+1] = Phi x[k] + Gamma u[k] with Phi = exp(A*T) and Gamma = integral_0^T exp(A*s) ds * B in its sampling-of-continuous-systems chapter. VERIFY the chapter and that the result is stated as exact.
2. Seborg, D. E., Edgar, T. F., Mellichamp, D. A. and Doyle, F. J., "Process Dynamics and Control", Wiley.
3. Franklin, G. F., Powell, J. D. and Workman, M. L., "Digital Control of Dynamic Systems", Addison-Wesley.
4. Ogata, K., "Discrete-Time Control Systems", Prentice Hall.

Numerical ODE framing (used in decay_heat.rs, where the motivation is stiffness rather than sampling):
5. Hochbruck, M. and Ostermann, A., "Exponential integrators", Acta Numerica, volume 19 (2010), pages 209-286. The volume, year and page range are asserted and SHOULD BE CHECKED - a journal citation with a specific page range is the easiest of these to get wrong and the easiest to verify.

Signal-processing framing (one-pole IIR filter via impulse invariance):
6. Oppenheim, A. V. and Schafer, R. W., "Discrete-Time Signal Processing", Prentice Hall.
7. Smith, J. O. III, "Introduction to Digital Filters", W3K Publishing. Claimed to be freely available from Stanford CCRMA. If true this is the only OPEN-ACCESS item in the list and the one to prefer where a paywall-free citation is wanted - VERIFY the free availability and the exact title, which has appeared with an "with Audio Applications" subtitle.

ACCESS TIER. Items 1-6 are commercial textbooks and one paywalled journal - proprietary under DATA_POLICY.md. Do NOT ingest them into crates/kovan-literature/open/. The mathematical results are textbook-standard and freely implementable; only the publications are gated. Item 7, if the free availability checks out, may be catalogued open.

ACCEPTANCE: each citation either confirmed with its verified edition/year/pages recorded in the doc comment, or corrected, or removed. Until that is done, every doc comment carrying one of these must retain its unverified-citation disclaimer.

title: njoy endf::interp::terp1 had ENDF laws 3/4 swapped - FIXED 2026-08-11, needs human review
description: FOUND AND FIXED 2026-08-11 while wiring S(alpha,beta) temperature interpolation (op-1y4y/op-cjw.22 session; fix in working tree, not committed). DEFECT: src/endf/interp.rs terp1 attached the wrong formulas to ENDF INT codes 3 and 4: code 3 (LinLog) computed ln(y)-linear-in-x (which is ENDF law 4) and code 4 (LogLin) computed y-linear-in-ln(x) (which is ENDF law 3). Verified against ENDF-102 0.5.2 and upstream NJOY2016 endf.f90 terp1 (i=3: y=y1+log(x/x1)*(y2-y1)/log(x2/x1); i=4: y=y1*exp((x-x1)*log(y2/y1)/(x2-x1))). The unit tests only covered laws 1/2/5, which is how it slipped through. IMPACT: any TAB1 with INT=3 or INT=4 segments evaluated via terp1/eval_tab1 (reconr linearize, photon, nuclear_data/secondary, purr heating, groupr kinematics LEP) interpolated with the wrong law; most neutron XS tables are INT=2 so the blast radius is limited, but MF7 MT4 extra-temperature LISTs are LI=4 and would have been wrong. FIX: formulas swapped back to ENDF semantics, upstream-parity flat-segment short-circuit (y1==y2 -> y1) added, pinned unit tests for laws 3 and 4 added, reconr/linearize.rs midpoint_energy arm updated (geometric mean now for LinLog|LogLog) and its lin_log_adds_points test corrected to INT=4 (its comment always said 'linear in E but log in sigma'). 393 lib tests pass after the fix. REMAINING: human review; consider re-running any V&V gates for modules that consume INT=3/4 data (RECONR Doppler gates were green after the fix in this session's lib run).

title: HTGR Phase 4.3: HTTR LOFC transient (Tier 3, digitised from figures)
description:
Reproduce the HTTR 9 MW gas-circulator-trip loss-of-forced-cooling transient at 30% power.

SOURCE, Tier 3: digitise figures from JNST Vol 51 Issue 11-12 (2014), Takamatsu et al. Same technique already used for Kieffer 1977 in TAMPINES, and the workspace has kovan-digitise for exactly this - use the CLI path, not eyeballing.

WHAT ACTUALLY GOVERNS THE RESULT, per the maintainer: reactivity performance sets the converging power level and hence fuel temperature; graphite conduction and RPV-to-cavity radiation set the temperature transient. FORCED CONVECTION IS ABSENT BY DEFINITION - so helium properties matter far less here than conduction and radiation. Do not over-invest in the gas path for this case.

WATCH: xenon reactivity temperature dependence has been the subject of dedicated sensitivity studies. Expect it to matter.

Depends on the RCCS/cavity path (op-jyyp.7) and PRKE feedback (op-juve).
acceptance_criteria: Power decays to zero then re-criticality at roughly 8 h; peak fuel and RPV temperatures within digitisation error of the published curves. Docs state 'digitised from published figures' with the citation and the digitiser calibration record.

title: HTGR Phase 5: GTHTR300 direct helium Brayton balance of plant
description:
600 MWt, 850 degC core outlet (upgraded design 950 degC), NON-INTERCOOLED cycle chosen for simplicity. Baseline 45.6% net efficiency; upgraded design breaks 50%.

Components: recuperator, precooler, compressor, turbine.

THE PIECE THAT IS NOT A SIMPLE SERIES LOOP - RPV COOLING FLOW PATH: compressor outlet helium at ~550 degC from the recuperator flows UPWARD along the RPV inner surface to keep the vessel below the SA533 steel limit. It is a load-dependent bypass stream the in-core structure was designed around. Model it as such.

WHY THIS DESIGN IS WORTH SIMULATING: direct-cycle coupling means no steam generator decouples core from turbine, so a turbine trip propagates STRAIGHT into core flow. That is the interesting transient.

CAVEAT FOR DOCS: GTHTR300 is a PAPER DESIGN with no experimental validation. Validate physics against HTTR; use GTHTR300 only as a plant configuration. Zero GTHTR references exist in the workspace today (verified 2026-08-13).
acceptance_criteria: Design-point efficiency reproduced within 1 percentage point; turbine-trip transient runs stably in real time; docs state the paper-design caveat.

notes.content:
Cross-link from op-id3l.2 (helium fast path), maintainer note 2026-08-13.

(p,s) retains an extra iteration even in CoolProp's TABULAR backends -- and (p,s) is precisely what isentropic turbine and compressor expansion needs in this Brayton cycle. So the ONE place a hand-rolled backward relation for helium is likely to earn its keep is here in the BOP, not in the core.

Everywhere else, (p,h) and (p,T) are the tabular backends' native gridded inputs and are already fast. Do not write bespoke helium backward relations for the core path. -q

description: root@vm
title: root@vm
HTGR Phase 6 (stretch): GTHTR300C IHX — couple to the EXISTING distillation columns and hydrogen, not FCC
description:
REVISED 2026-08-13 on maintainer direction. GTHTR300C: 600 MWt at 950 degC, IHX between RPV and gas turbine system, 170 MW of IHX duty to process heat, balance to electricity.

FCC IS OUT OF SCOPE - settled, with a technical reason worth keeping: fluid catalytic cracking is AUTOTHERMAL. The regenerator coke burn both regenerates the catalyst and supplies the cracking endotherm, so there is no external heat demand for nuclear to displace. Do not model it.

WHAT TO COUPLE TO INSTEAD - the workspace already owns one half of this (verified 2026-08-13):
  - DISTILLATION COLUMNS ARE REAL AND SUBSTANTIAL: crates/outram-park-fork-dwsim-libs/src/columns/ is 11,355 lines across 15 modules - bubble_point, newton_raphson, sum_rates, tridiagonal, thermo_bridge, specs, profile, initial_estimates, solver, plus dynamic.rs (853 lines) and shortcut.rs landed 2026-08-12. Column reboiler duty is a genuine high-grade heat demand and is the natural first coupling target.
  - HYDROGEN IS NOT BUILT: the only 'hydrogen' hits in crates/ are NUCLEAR hydrogen (H-1 / ZrH thermal scattering in outram-mc), not process hydrogen. The steam-methane reformer exists only as bead op-1z3o.7 (Gibbs equilibrium block, Todo). Steam cracking (>850 degC, purely fired) and hydrogen production remain the real targets, but both are unbuilt.

So the deliverable is: an IHX component model, plus the secondary-side process load as a BOUNDARY CONDITION - and the first credible load to attach is the existing dwsim-libs column reboiler duty, not a from-scratch process. Full iodine-sulfur process chemistry stays out of scope.

Feeds op-1z3o.1 (refinery demonstration-scope DECISION): the FCC-autothermal reasoning above should inform it, and the columns are the asset that already exists.
acceptance_criteria: IHX duty split reproduced at the design point with the process side as a boundary condition; the first coupled load is an EXISTING dwsim-libs distillation column reboiler duty, not a new process model; op-1z3o.1 updated with the FCC-autothermal reasoning.

title: HTGR cross-cutting: validation-data ACCESS TIER taxonomy, tagged on every V&V claim
description:
Adopt and document a four-tier taxonomy for validation-data provenance, and tag every HTGR V&V claim with its tier. The failure this prevents: a Tier 3 comparison getting written up as if it were Tier 1.

  Tier 1  Open specification WITH tabulated experimental data
          e.g. IAEA-TECDOC-1382, TECDOC-1694, IRPhEP HTR10-GCR-RESR-001
  Tier 2  Open code-to-code benchmark, NO experimental data
          e.g. OECD MHTGR-350 -- VERIFICATION only, never validation
  Tier 3  Digitised from published figures
          e.g. HTTR LOFC plots in JNST 51(11-12) 2014
  Tier 4  GATED -- requires NEA framework membership
          e.g. OECD/NEA LOFC joint project, HTGR T/H (HTTF) benchmark

TIER 4 IS OUT OF SCOPE: Singapore is not an NEA member. Tier 4 requires a partner institution holding the agreement. Treat as out of scope until a collaboration exists.

This complements, and does not replace, the existing kovan open/proprietary split (which is about REDISTRIBUTION rights); the tier is about EVIDENTIAL strength.
acceptance_criteria: The taxonomy is written into the HTGR scoping docs, and every HTGR V&V write-up carries its tier tag.

title: HTGR OPEN QUESTION (maintainer, 2026-08-13): is 'the mapping' where wgpu pays off?
description:
Maintainer raised this at 02:30 SGT, OUTSIDE active working hours, so it is RECORDED HERE UNANSWERED rather than analysed. Answer it in a working window.

THE QUESTION AS ASKED: 'I suppose the mapping is where wgpu may pay off?'

'The mapping' is ambiguous in context and the reading must be settled before any analysis. At least three candidates, all live in this workspace:

  (a) PROPERTY-TABLE MAPPING (state -> properties), batch. Immediately preceding context was CoolProp tabular backends (op-id3l.2). Upstream CoolProp 8.0's fast_evaluate is explicitly a cache-bypassing, allocation-free BATCH API writing into a caller-allocated buffer - which is already the GPU-shaped workload. Per-cell property evaluation over a mesh is embarrassingly parallel.

  (b) CROSS-MESH MAPPING (meshToMesh / RBF non-conformal) in genfoam multi_region - 3,953 lines / 24 tests already implemented.

  (c) MGXS rung 2->3 SEAM (op-fhjn): GeN-Foam nuclearData is parameterised by feedback variables via polyharmonic-spline RBF interpolation across perturbed reactor states. That is a scattered-data interpolation mapping.

WHAT IS ALREADY GPU-CAPABLE (verified 2026-08-13, wgpu in 7 crate manifests): boon-lay, njoy-outram-park-fork, outram-blender, outram-foam-basic-lib, outram-mc-libs, outram-park-fork-pflotran, raffles. So the question is not 'can we' but 'which mapping is actually the bottleneck'.

DO NOT GUESS THE ANSWER. The workspace rule is profile-first, and op-id3l.2's acceptance already requires measuring per-call overhead before choosing an implementation. Any wgpu claim here needs a measured CPU baseline first, and the f32-GPU / f64-CPU precision tradeoff applies as it does everywhere else in this workspace.
acceptance_criteria: The intended reading of 'the mapping' is settled by the maintainer, a CPU baseline is measured for it, and the wgpu decision is made on that measurement rather than on expectation.

title: HTGR Phase 0.2: real-time helium fast path — port CoolProp's TABULAR backends (TTSE/BICUBIC)
description:
REVISED 2026-08-13 after maintainer correction. My original framing (fit Gibbs polynomials, write backward equations) was borrowed from the water/IF97 world and was wrong for helium. Corrected framing below.

WHY THE ORIGINAL FRAMING WAS WRONG:
True analytical backward equations exist ONLY for water - the IF97 backend has them because IAPWS-IF97 defines them as a standard. Helium has NO equivalent standard. Upstream CoolProp's substitute is TABULAR INTERPOLATION, and it reaches the same place practically.

VERIFIED IN THIS WORKSPACE 2026-08-13 (grep over crates/outram-park-fork-coolprop/):
  TTSE            0 files
  BICUBIC         0 files
  tabular         0 files
  fast_evaluate   0 files
  AbstractState   0 files
  'backward'      2 files - BOTH are forward/backward SWEEPS in the GAMG and conjugate-gradient linear solvers, i.e. unrelated to thermodynamics.
=> THE FORK IS HEOS-ONLY. It has the accuracy but not the fast path. By the maintainer's own decision rule, this bead STANDS - but as a tabular-backend port, not a polynomial fit.

WHAT TO ACTUALLY BUILD:
  - Port the tabular backends TTSE and BICUBIC. Native inputs are (p,h) and (p,T) - those are fastest because they are what the tables are gridded on. Two table sets get written: pressure-enthalpy and pressure-temperature, cached upstream under HOME/.CoolProp/Tables.
  - Accuracy is essentially free: for R245fa density, BICUBIC matches HEOS to about 9 significant figures.

THE (p,s) CATCH, AND WHERE A HAND-ROLLED RELATION ACTUALLY EARNS ITS KEEP:
(p,s) STILL requires an extra iteration even in the tabular backends, though the overhead is far less severe than the full EOS. And (p,s) is exactly what isentropic turbine and compressor expansion needs in the GTHTR300 Brayton cycle (op-id3l.12). So the one place a bespoke backward relation is justified is the BALANCE OF PLANT, not the core.

TWO PRACTICAL CONSTRAINTS FOR THE PORT:
  1. Table load is 80-140 ms per AbstractState construction. Instantiate ONCE and hold it - in Rust the property object lives in the solver struct, never created per call.
  2. CoolProp 8.0 added fast_evaluate: cache-bypassing, allocation-free batch evaluation writing into a caller-allocated buffer, because the per-call update()/keyed_output() machinery was dominating actual math cost for fast backends. Check which upstream version this fork descends from - an older lineage may have inherited that overhead.

FIRST ACTION IS TO PROFILE, not to write: confirm the per-call overhead is real in our port before choosing between a tabular port and anything bespoke.
acceptance_criteria: Tabular (TTSE/BICUBIC) helium path available with (p,h) and (p,T) native; agreement with the Phase 0.1 HEOS reference at tabular-interpolation accuracy (target: matches HEOS to ~9 significant figures, as upstream BICUBIC does for R245fa density); >= 20x speedup over the full EOS call measured, not assumed; zero heap allocation per call; the property object is constructed once and held, with the 80-140 ms construction cost paid at setup only. (p,s) overhead measured separately and reported, since it retains an iteration.

title: HTGR Phase 2.1: CoreFlowClosure and PowerConversion — HARD ENUM dispatch, no dyn
description:
ARCHITECTURE REQUIREMENT: the core flow closure is the ONLY thing that differs between the two HTGR geometries. Everything else is shared - TRISO fuel model, graphite conduction, decay heat, PRKE, helium properties, RCCS radiation. What differs: pressure drop, wall heat transfer, effective conductivity.

DISPATCH IS SETTLED (maintainer, 2026-08-13): HARD ENUM. No dyn as far as possible.

  enum CoreFlowClosure { PebbleBed(PebbleBedClosure), Prismatic(PrismaticClosure) }

  - A trait MAY be used as a compiler-enforced CONTRACT on each concrete struct, so the compiler verifies every closure implements the required methods.
  - The trait is NOT used for runtime dispatch. Match on the enum.
  - No Box<dyn>, no &dyn, no Arc<dyn>.

This matches the workspace Rust design rules (enums give exhaustiveness - adding a geometry becomes a compile error at every match site, not a runtime surprise - plus zero heap allocation and working go-to-definition, which dyn breaks).

Same applies to PowerConversion (steam Rankine vs direct Brayton), which is the BOP-side analogue and will gain a Brayton variant under op-id3l.12.

Gated on the TAMPINES transonic HEM critical-flow V&V (op-id3l.15).
acceptance_criteria: Swapping pebble bed for prismatic requires no change outside the closure impl, verified by a compile-time test instantiating both. Dispatch is an enum match; grep confirms no Box<dyn>/&dyn/Arc<dyn> introduced in the closure or PowerConversion path. Adding a third variant produces compile errors at every match site.

Discrete coolant channel model, block-level conduction, gap radiation for the prismatic HTTR core.

THE PRISMATIC GOTCHA, per the maintainer: BLOCK BYPASS FLOW. A meaningful fraction of total flow, load-dependent, and routinely the largest single source of code-to-experiment disagreement. Implement it EXPLICITLY, not as a lumped fudge factor.

Note the workspace history: htgr_sim_v1 was originally prismatic and is being retargeted to HTR-10 pebble bed under op-jyyp. This bead is the prismatic core coming BACK as a first-class geometry alongside the pebble bed, behind the Phase 2.1 closure trait - not a revert of op-jyyp.

Gated on Phase 2.1 and on the TAMPINES sequencing gate.
acceptance_criteria: Bypass fraction and outlet temperature consistent with HTTR published steady-state operating points at rated power / 850 degC outlet, with the bypass fraction reported as its own number.

title: tuas: no gas phase in the Material type system — blocks MELCOR-style CVH
description:
crates/tuas_boussinesq_solver has no gas phase in its type system.

- Material enum (src/lib/boussinesq_thermophysical_properties/mod.rs:14) has exactly 2 variants: Solid(SolidMaterial), Liquid(LiquidMaterial).
- LiquidMaterial (:126) has 7 variants: TherminolVP1, DowthermA, HITEC, YD325, FLiBe, FLiNaK, CustomLiquid(...). All six named fluids are single-phase heat-transfer oils or molten salts. No steam, water, water-vapour or air.
- SolidMaterial (:58) has 5 variants: SteelSS304L, Copper, Fiberglass, PyrogelHPS, CustomSolid(...).
- Crate-wide greps for GasMaterial, enum Gas, Material::Gas, VapourMaterial, SteamMaterial, LiquidMaterial::Steam return ZERO hits in src/. Greps for gas|vapou?r|superheat|two-phase|quality in the thermophysical-properties module return zero.

This is architecturally consistent -- the crate is named *Boussinesq*, i.e. incompressible single-phase by construction -- so treat it as a SCOPE BOUNDARY, not an oversight. But the practical consequence is real: MELCOR-style control-volume hydrodynamics (non-condensable gases, vapour/liquid pools, phase change) has no representation here, and adding one means a new Material arm plus every match site updated. Under the workspace no-trait-objects/enum-dispatch rule that is a breaking change to a published enum.

Decision needed from the maintainer: extend tuas, or build CVH in a separate lumped-parameter crate (see the MELCOR-lite epic) and leave tuas single-phase.

Verified 2026-08-07 against the working tree.

title: OPCPFluidArray: selectable implicit energy-balance mode via outram-foam fvm::div
description:
MAINTAINER INSTRUCTION, 2026-08-13: 'pls move the advection terms to implicit by default... do for both OPCPFluidArray and TampinesSteamArray, but use outram-foam FVM::div.'

THE TWO SITES:
  TampinesSteamArray -- crates/tampines-steam-tables/src/openfoam_algorithms/rhoPimpleFoam/mod.rs:1639
      let conv_he = fvc::div(&self.phi, &self.he);   // explicit div(phi h)/V
  OPCPFluidArray -- crates/outram-park-fork-coolprop/src/openfoam_algorithms/rhoPimpleFoam/mod.rs:1306
      fvc::div_limited(&self.phi, &self.he, self.he_convection_scheme.limiter());  // explicit

Use crates/outram-foam-basic-lib/src/fv_operators/fvm/div.rs:61  pub fn div(phi: &SurfaceScalarField, psi: &VolScalarField) -> FvMatrix

WHY: the energy convection is explicit while MOMENTUM in the same files is already implicit
(fvm::div_vec at :1351 and :986 respectively). The explicit energy term imposes a hard CFL limit that
NO number of PIMPLE outer correctors can lift -- the corrector loop is a Picard iteration whose contraction
factor IS the cell Courant number, so above Co = 1 it diverges however many are used. Measured on the HTGR
steam generator: hot-side cells 0.625 m, gas ~11 m/s, Co ~0.23 at the 0.0125 s substep and ~1.8 at a 0.1 s
plant step. That Courant limit is the sole reason the SG must substep 8x per plant step (op-6eqe).

PREMISE CORRECTION -- READ THIS, IT CHANGES THE WORK:
The maintainer believed TUAS's FluidArray already does implicit advection. IT DOES NOT. Verified 2026-08-13:
mass_flowrate NEVER enters coefficient_matrix in
.../one_d_fluid_array_with_lateral_coupling/calculation.rs (zero occurrences); every advection term lands in
power_source_vector built from last-timestep enthalpies, and the code says so -- 'we also consider outflow
using previous timestep temperature' (:437). The matrix holds only thermal inertia (rho_cp V/dt), lateral
conductance, and axial conduction (:337, :425, :620).
SO THERE IS NOTHING TO PORT. This is new work, not a copy of an existing TUAS implementation.

THE LIMITER PROBLEM -- do not do a naive swap:
fvc::div_limited applies a nonlinear flux limiter (Upwind/Linear/VanLeer/Minmod via fvc::Limiter). A nonlinear
limiter CANNOT go into a linear matrix, so fvc::div_limited -> fvm::div is not a like-for-like replacement and
would silently drop boundedness on the OPCP side.
Standard treatment, and what should be implemented: IMPLICIT UPWIND in the matrix (fvm::div) PLUS DEFERRED
CORRECTION -- carry (limited - upwind) as an explicit source. Unconditionally stable because upwind dominates
the matrix, while the deferred part recovers the limiter's accuracy. The deferred term is still Picard, but
well-behaved.

SCOPE: crates/tampines-steam-tables and crates/outram-park-fork-coolprop only. Do NOT change TUAS FluidArray
(CIET-validated regression path) and do NOT touch outram-park-digital-twin-engine.

ACCEPTANCE:
  - Both arrays stable at Courant numbers above 1; demonstrate with a test that FAILS on the old explicit path.
  - Boundedness preserved on the OPCP side -- show the limiter still does its job via deferred correction.
  - Before/after accuracy on an existing case; report any degradation honestly.
  - 'by default' per the maintainer: implicit is the default path, not an opt-in flag.

SEQUENCING: this SUPERSEDES part of op-6eqe. That bead's 8-substeps-per-plant-step conclusion exists only
because advection is explicit. Once this lands, revisit the SG substep count -- it should drop, possibly to 1.

notes.content:
SCOPE REDIRECTED by the maintainer, 2026-08-13: 'stop the Tampines steam array agent... let's make sure the OPCPFluidArray has the mode for implicit and explicit energy balance. as a selectable enum. I want you to redirect the opcp agent to implement this implicit mode.'

TampinesSteamArray is OUT of this bead. An agent had been started on it and was stopped before making any edits
(verified: crates/tampines-steam-tables has no changes beyond the unrelated f32 warning sweep). TUAS is also out --
'leave tuas alone do not correct it'.

WORK IS NOW: crates/outram-park-fork-coolprop only. The explicit path already exists
(rhoPimpleFoam/mod.rs:1306, fvc::div_limited with the EnergyConvectionScheme limiter enum at :276). Add the IMPLICIT
mode alongside it, selectable, using outram-foam-basic-lib fvm::div (fv_operators/fvm/div.rs:61).

DESIGN POINT handed to the agent: EnergyConvectionScheme's own doc comment says it is 'enum dispatch over the flux
limiter lambda(r)'. Implicit-vs-explicit is a TIME/MATRIX treatment, orthogonal to limiter choice -- you can want
van Leer with either. Recommended a SEPARATE enum (e.g. EnergyBalanceMode { Explicit, Implicit }) over adding
variants to the limiter enum, which would make that enum's documentation untrue. The agent owns the call and must
justify it.

BOUNDEDNESS: a nonlinear limiter cannot live in a linear matrix, so fvc::div_limited -> fvm::div is not like-for-like.
Specified implicit upwind in the matrix PLUS deferred correction carrying (limited - upwind) as an explicit source.
This matters more than usual here because op-1fyp documents dispersive over/undershoots on an advected thermal front
as a real MEASURED defect in this very array -- dropping boundedness would regress a bug that was deliberately fixed.

VALIDATION VEHICLE -- CHECKED, and Edwards is NOT available here. crates/outram-park-fork-coolprop has no Edwards
blowdown test; its tests/ are EOS/property tests (water_reference, helium_reference, single_cv_and_flash, ...). The
code REFERENCES Edwards-O'Brien at :355, :563, :761, :1652 but that case lives in tampines-steam-tables, now out of
scope. The agent must find the in-crate transient tests for the equal-timestep baseline and BUILD the primary
acceptance case: a run at cell Courant number above 1 where the explicit mode FAILS and the implicit mode succeeds.
A case that passes under both proves nothing.

RELATED, and should be reconciled after this lands:
  op-1fyp (P2, still Todo) -- the limiter fix for THIS array. The code at :1306 now calls fvc::div_limited citing
    that bead, so it looks done; either close it or record what remains.
  TampinesSteamArray has the SAME unfixed defect: its energy convection at
    crates/tampines-steam-tables/.../rhoPimpleFoam/mod.rs:1639 is still bare fvc::div, i.e. central differencing,
    unlimited, on an advection-dominated equation. op-1fyp never covered it. Filed separately.
notes.author: teddy0@arch-aftershock-rapid-glass-S267454

notes.content:
DONE 2026-08-13, pushed (8e97330d; SG wired at 68e35551).
EnergyBalanceMode { Explicit, Implicit } on OPCPFluidArray, kept separate from the EnergyConvectionScheme limiter
enum because measurement showed the axes are independent: explicit UPWIND also diverges at Co >= 1.25 while implicit
VAN LEER survives, so stability tracks the time treatment and accuracy tracks the limiter.
Deferred correction preserves boundedness -- verified, not assumed: fvm_div_matches_explicit_upwind_divergence
compares (M*h - S) against V*conv_upwind, worst mismatch 0 W EXACTLY against a 575 W largest cell term.
Co > 1 evidence: overshoot past the boundary value as % of span -- Co 1.25 gives +135.14% explicit vs +0.10%
implicit; Co 2.00 gives +47539% vs +1.19%. Attribution isolated: pressure and velocity stay finite in every diverged
explicit run.
Honest cost: implicit is LESS accurate at low Courant ((u dx/2)(1+Co) diffusion against explicit (1-Co)), so the
crate default stays Explicit + van Leer and the SG opts in explicitly.
Used the crate's OWN vendored fvm::div rather than outram-foam-basic-lib's, because Cargo.toml:29 and
openfoam_algorithms/CLAUDE.md:16 both document that the crate deliberately has no such dependency, for
Android-buildability. Deviation from the original instruction, flagged and accepted.

TUAS SolidColumn::new_cylindrical_shell builds its end control volumes from a SOLID rod of the bore
description:
FOUND 2026-08-12 while building the nodalised steam generator for htgr_sim_v1.

FILE: crates/tuas_boussinesq_solver/src/lib/array_control_vol_and_fluid_component_collections/one_d_solid_array_with_lateral_coupling/constructors.rs:226 (new_cylindrical_shell).

The constructor computes the array cross-section correctly as the annulus:
    let cross_sectional_area = PI*outer_diameter^2/4 - PI*inner_diameter^2/4;
but then builds its back/front boundary control volumes with
    SingleCVNode::new_cylinder(node_length, inner_diameter, ...)
which (single_control_vol/mod.rs:349) computes volume = PI*d^2/4 * z for a SOLID cylinder of the INNER diameter.

So back_single_cv.mass_control_volume and .volume are those of a solid rod of the bore, not of the tube wall. The error does not vanish as the wall thickness goes to zero -- it goes to the full bore volume. For a 19 mm OD / 14 mm ID tube the end CVs carry 1.19x the correct metal, and for a thinner wall it is unbounded.

SCOPE OF THE IMPACT: advance_timestep() solves the interior temperatures from rho_cp * volume_fraction * (total_length * xs_area), which uses the CORRECT annular xs_area, so the solved temperature array is unaffected. The wrong mass reaches only back_single_cv / front_single_cv, i.e. anything using the axial CV-to-CV or CV-to-BC linking in axial_connection/.

WORKAROUND USED: examples/htgr_sim_v1/physics/steam_generator.rs uses new_block() with an equivalent rectangular section carrying the aggregate annular metal area of the whole 90-tube bundle, which is also the physically meaningful number for a bundle.

SUGGESTED FIX: give SingleCVNode a new_cylindrical_shell constructor, or pass the annular volume through. NOT fixed here -- tuas_boussinesq_solver is outside the scope granted for that task.

notes.content:
Marviken drift-flux gates WRITTEN AND MEASURED, 2026-08-11 (~17:00 SGT). All work in crates/tampines/src/multiphase_1d/marviken_tests.rs; case setup taken verbatim from the sibling HEM reference per the maintainer instruction; compared against the BARE HEM maximum-mass-flux criterion baseline as instructed (dispatcher excluded, op-dqng).

EXPLORATION FIRST (marviken_drift_flux_explore, run before any assertion was written, at 5 stagnation points 2.829/3.150/3.725/4.772/4.975 MPa): NO interior maximum anywhere — the steady flux rises monotonically down to the 101.325 kPa containment pressure, as anticipated for a semi-implicit pressure-based scheme with no imposed choking criterion (the RELAP5 situation). 68/69 sweeps in the full gates have no interior maximum; the single exception (4.306 MPa, t24) wins by 0.3 % = plateau noise. What IS measurable is an effective plateau: over the lower half of the sweep (factor ~20 in receiver pressure) the flux moves by mean 4.9 % / worst 5.2 % (t23) and 3.2 % / 7.3 % (t24). Documented as a limitation of the method, not papered over. Sweep cost 2.9-12.4 s per point; no trimming of sweep, t_end or dt was needed or done.

GATE RESULTS (MarvikenCase::default: 8 cells, dt 20 us, t_end 12 ms, C0 1.13, Vgj 0.1, tau 1 ms; 897 marched transients, 0 refused steps, max Courant 0.326):
- Test 23 (3 K): mean |dev| 8.9 %, signed +2.8 %, max 19.7 %, 0/29 points outside +/-25 % -> VALIDATED (both criteria met). vs bare HEM 10.1 % / -10.1 % / 28.2 %: drift flux clearly wins; HEM's uniform -10.1 % saturated-branch bias becomes +2.8 % (the L/D<1.5 length-effect regime of NUREG/CR-2671 sec 9.2).
- Test 24 (33 K): mean |dev| 11.4 %, signed -9.7 %, max 28.8 %, 6/40 points outside +/-25 % -> NOT VALIDATED, kept as an honest CHARACTERISATION test (mean criterion met, per-point criterion missed; all 6 misses clustered in 3.121-3.418 MPa and the gate asserts that clustering). vs bare HEM 9.0 % / -1.8 % / 26.5 %: drift flux slightly loses.

FALSIFIABLE EXPECTATION (recorded here 04:26): (1) no gain on the deeply subcooled branch — SUPPORTED (11 points >= 4.00 MPa: mean 4.3 %, signed -2.3 % vs HEM -1.8 %); (2) gain at the t24 flashing-inception knee with the knee moving down and sharpening — REFUTED: the model removes HEM's over-prediction below 3.10 MPa (signed +0.1 % over 9 points vs HEM up to +26.5 %) but FLATTENS the knee, systematic -23.0 % across 3.10-3.46 MPa, worse than HEM's -18.2 % (measured envelope +143 % over 2.984-3.418 MPa, model +65 %); (3) gain on t23's saturated branch — SUPPORTED, and it is where the whole t23 win comes from.

Knee deficit deliberately NOT attributed: single-tau relaxation, the constant-area domain (no convergent inlet resolved) and the absent interfacial-area/wall-nucleation model are all live candidates this test set cannot separate. No coefficient (C0, Vgj, tau, DEEP_SUBCOOLING_RATIO), tolerance, reference constant or data array was changed; a tau study is explicitly deferred as fitting to the validation set.

WALL CLOCK: 98.1 s (t23) / 381 s (t24), separate #[test] fns so cargo parallelises them. Cleanup done: unused AvailableEnergy import removed, print_sweep wired into both gates, cargo check -p tampines --lib --tests --release clean with zero warnings.

Not closing this bead — maintainer decision.

description: root@vm
title: root@vm
outram-mc-libs: rng::lcg::prn omits OpenMC's PCG-RXS-M-XS output permutation
description:
`outram_mc_libs::rng::lcg::prn` (crates/outram-mc-libs/src/rng/lcg.rs:26) does NOT reproduce OpenMC's `prn`.

Upstream (/home/teddy0/Documents/research/openmc/src/random_lcg.cpp:32-44):

    *seed = (prn_mult * (*seed) + prn_add);
    uint64_t word = ((*seed >> ((*seed >> 59u) + 5u)) ^ *seed) * 12605985483714917081ull;
    uint64_t result = (word >> 43u) ^ word;
    return ldexp(result, -64);

i.e. a PCG-RXS-M-XS output permutation of the LCG state, scaled by 2^-64 (full 64-bit resolution).

Ours:

    *seed = seed.wrapping_mul(MULT).wrapping_add(INC);
    (*seed >> 12) as f64 * (1.0 / (1u64 << 52) as f64)

i.e. the raw top 52 bits of the state, no permutation. The doc comment claims 'Maps to double prn(uint64_t* seed) in OpenMC' — it does not.

MEASURED EVIDENCE (2026-08-06). From seed = 1, first five draws:
  ours:   0.423209170872713, 0.509407442883721, 0.648359393963430, 0.382863390508260, 0.795447749253532
  openmc: 0.710817359881671, 0.752996005805941, 0.330118988789542, 0.467186818550906, 0.046254968305997
The LCG STATE recurrence is identical on both sides (state after 5 draws = 0xCBA276B4B881A9F0 either way), so future_seed / jump-ahead / init_seed / the GPU integer-state mirror tests are all unaffected and remain correct. Only the state -> double output mapping diverges.

IMPACT. Our uniforms are a statistically reasonable generator (top bits of an LCG), so this is not a correctness catastrophe the way op-rbo was — but it does mean this crate can NEVER reproduce an OpenMC random sequence bit-for-bit, which undercuts the crate's stated purpose (CLAUDE.md: 'the crate's entire value is fidelity to OpenMC'). It also violates the mandatory porting rule: the current implementation is a re-derivation, not a port.

WHY NOT FIXED UNDER op-rbo (deliberate scoping decision, 2026-08-06). Blast radius is far larger than init_seed's:
  - every random number in the crate changes -> every k-eff, every V&V CSV, every openmc_notebook_comparison must be re-run;
  - the WGSL shaders (src/gpu/shaders/*, gpu::batched_flight / batched_event) derive their f32 uniform from the state with the port's formula and would need matching changes plus new GPU-vs-CPU mirror numbers;
  - crates/raffles consumes rng::lcg::prn directly (samplers.rs:315,437,541,1085) and its sampler outputs/recorded results would shift; that crate was explicitly out of bounds for the op-rbo agent.
This needs its own planned change with a full re-run of the crate's recorded statistics, not a drive-by.

ALSO NOTED while auditing rng/lcg.rs (no action taken):
  - future_seed matches upstream (random_lcg.cpp:91-120) exactly, including operation order. Verified.
  - MULT / INC / DEFAULT_STRIDE match prn_mult / prn_add / DEFAULT_STRIDE exactly. Verified.
  - NOT ported at all: future_prn (:50), advance_prn_seed (:82), init_particle_seeds (:70), and the N_STREAMS = 4 stream-index constants (random_lcg.h:12-16). init_particle_seeds in particular is the idiomatic upstream way to give one particle its four streams; callers here hand-roll it. Consider porting them for API parity.
  - Lcg64 is new work (an oorandom::Rand64 compat shim for boon-lay), not an OpenMC port; its rand_u64 returns the raw LCG state, whose low bits are weak. Fine as-is but should not be mistaken for an upstream-faithful API.

title: teddy0@arch-aftershock-rapid-glass-S267454
HTR-10: wire the graphite/moderator feedback channel into PRKE (remainder of op-jyyp.6)
description:
The graphite/moderator reactivity channel itself has landed as `crates/tampines/src/pebble_bed/feedback.rs` (GraphiteModeratorFeedback: own temperature state, own caller-supplied coefficient, lumped m*cp ODE step, thermal time constant; 6 tests green). What remains of op-jyyp.6 is the KINETICS WIRING, which deliberately did NOT go in the tampines library:

- The tampines library is free of teh-o-prke (it is only an Android-gated dev-dependency), so feedback.rs returns a plain dimensionless reactivity for a caller to sum with a fuel Doppler term and feed to a kinetics solver.
- The wiring therefore belongs in an example or in nee_soon, where a neutronics dependency is appropriate. Do not add teh-o-prke to the tampines library to close this.

Also outstanding, and the real blocker on any quantitative use: a MODERATOR-ONLY temperature coefficient. None is supplied, on purpose. The published HTR-10 figures in IAEA-TECDOC-1382 part 2 Table 4-33 (NRG -7.37e-5/-8.05e-5 per C; INET/VSOP -7.49e-5/-9.15e-5 per C) are ISOTHERMAL coefficients (fuel + moderator moved together); they are exposed in feedback.rs as clearly-labelled constants for validating a whole-core isothermal calculation, and using one as alpha_m would double-count fuel Doppler. A moderator-only coefficient has to come from a neutronics calculation that perturbs the moderator alone (rung 3 -> rung 4 hand-off, docs/reactor-scoping/htr10-neutronics.md section 5.4).

Measured supporting figure (2026-08-11, feedback.rs::graphite_thermal_time_constant_is_long): the derived HTR-10 pebble-graphite inventory of 5129.16 kg against a bed conductance of 97473.9 W/K gives a thermal time constant of 89.37 s - and that is the pebbles alone, excluding the 1 m side reflector. Against an effectively instantaneous fuel Doppler response, this is why the two channels must stay separate.

title: HTR-10 rung 1: pebble-bed Monte Carlo reference k_eff, with sigma and stated data provenance
description:
Parent: op-841p. Rung 1 is the reference every other rung is validated against, so its credibility is the pipeline's credibility.

TARGET SEQUENCE, cheapest first, each with a published number to hit:
1a. TRISO grain unit cell, infinite medium. DONE as a code exercise: crates/outram-mc-libs/examples/htr10_fuel_zone_kinf.rs (see comment on this bead for the measured numbers). Free-gas thermal scattering, so NOT a physics result.
1b. Infinite pebble-bed lattice k_inf vs Serpent 1.6321 / HCP 1.6416 (Tantillo et al. 2020, Nucl. Eng. Des. 362, 110603, PROPRIETARY tier - cite, do not re-host).
1c. BCC fuel + graphite ball lattice k_inf vs MCNP5 1.77078 +/- 0.00008 (Wang et al. 2014, config b, PROPRIETARY tier).
1d. B1 detailed core k_eff at the measured 16890-ball / 123.06 cm loading vs MCNP5 1.01620 +/- 0.00014 (Wang et al. 2014, config c).

Steps 1a-1c are reachable with the existing reflective-cube driver run_keff_delta. Step 1d needs run_keff_csg plus a bed model.

EVERY REPORTED k MUST CARRY: sigma, particles per generation, inactive and active generation counts, RNG seed, cross-section library and version, fidelity tier (from_core LOW vs from_endf HIGH), and the thermal-scattering treatment. A k_eff without sigma and without data provenance is not a result.

STATE WHICH PROBLEM: B1-as-defined (helium, 20 C, dummy balls 1.73 g/cm3 and 1.3 ppm boron) or B1-as-measured (humid air 0.1013 MPa at 15 C, water-vapour density 2.57e-5 g/cm3, dummy balls 1.84 g/cm3 and 0.125 ppm). They differ by about +1000 pcm - larger than the published code-to-code spread of 683 +/- 22 pcm. Conflating them invalidates the comparison against the measured 123.06 cm.

Benchmark specification is typed data at crates/outram-park-digital-twin-engine/src/htr10/neutronics.rs. Scoping: docs/reactor-scoping/htr10-neutronics.md section 4.1.

notes.content:
RUNG 1 STEP 1a COMPLETED as a code exercise, 2026-08-11. crates/outram-mc-libs/examples/htr10_fuel_zone_kinf.rs.

PROBLEM: HTR-10 fuel-zone infinite medium, run twice - kernels resolved explicitly as randomly packed spheres, then the same nuclide inventory homogenised. Atom densities straight from IAEA-TECDOC-1382 Table 4-38 (OPEN tier, part 2 line 1101). Kernel volume fraction of the fuelled zone = 8335 * (0.025/2.5)^3 = 8.335e-3.

MEASURED (main run, 400 particles/generation, 10 inactive + 40 active, RNG seed 1, packing seed 20260811, 1018 kernels of r = 0.025 cm in a reflective cube of half-width 1 cm, realized packing fraction 0.008328, T = 293.15 K, delta tracking with a bin-maximum bounding majorant):
  heterogeneous k_inf = 1.57269 +/- 0.00877
  homogenised   k_inf = 1.45189 +/- 0.00820
  delta k = -12081 +/- 1201 pcm; delta rho = -5291 +/- 526 pcm; 10.1 sigma
A smoke run at 200/8/25 gave 1.60870 +/- 0.02031 and 1.47273 +/- 0.01489, agreeing with the main run to 1.6 sigma on the heterogeneous case.

SIGN IS A PHYSICS CHECK AND IT PASSES: resolving the kernels depresses the flux inside each lump at the U-238 resonance energies, so fewer resonance absorptions per U-238 atom and k rises; homogenising removes the depression so it must come out lower. It does.

THIS IS NOT A PHYSICS RESULT AND NOT AN HTR-10 CRITICALITY RESULT:
- Thermal scattering is FREE GAS. Graphite S(alpha,beta) does not reach the transport path (crates/outram-mc-libs/src/material/thermal.rs:24-26). On a graphite-moderated thermal system this alone disqualifies the absolute number.
- It is a fuel-zone infinite medium - no shell, no dummy ball, no bed, no reflector, no leakage. NO published HTR-10 value corresponds to this problem, so the absolute k_inf cannot be compared to the literature at all.
- TRISO coatings unresolved (op-6tz.35). LOW fidelity tier (flat nu-bar, Watt chi stand-in, ~+500 pcm on Godiva). k_std is a generation-batch SEM with no inter-generation correlation correction. op-rbo and op-jis inherited.
- The delta k is NOT comparable to Wang et al.'s unit-cell biases: theirs are multigroup XS PROCESSING biases against a CE reference on the full model and run the other way (+2820 pcm for INFHOMMEDIUM). This is a CE GEOMETRIC effect on a different problem.

WHAT IT DOES ESTABLISH: the rung-1 chain runs end to end on this reactor's real materials, reproducibly from a stated seed, with a correctly signed self-shielding effect.

COST WARNING for step 1d: thermal neutrons in graphite scatter hundreds of times per history. The 400/10/40 run took roughly 20 minutes for 40,000 histories. Budget compute accordingly.

Full write-up: docs/reactor-scoping/htr10-neutronics.md section 11.

description: FINDING 2026-08-11, from implementing the analytic ZBS closure (op-jyyp.3). The 18-point pebble-bed effective-conductivity tabulation in reference-data/virtual_test_bed/htgr/generic-pbr/pbr.i block keff_pebble_bed (300-2000 K, 11.94-44.95 W/(m K)) -- transcribed as the reference table in crates/outram-park-digital-twin-engine/src/htr10/zbs.rs and named the acceptance target for the analytic ZBS -- CANNOT be produced by the Zehner-Bauer-Schlunder correlation with the deck's own stated inputs (eps=0.39, d_pebble=0.06 m, emissivity=0.8, graphite k_s=26 W/(m K), helium at 6 MPa). Evidence, all computed 2026-08-11: (1) full ZBS (van Antwerpen 2010 form, contact phi=0.0077, C=1.25) with helium k_f from the KTA 3102.1 correlation gives 2.08 W/(m K) at 300 K vs the table's 11.94 (-83%), 10.5 vs 27.3 at 1000 K, 29.0 vs 45.0 at 2000 K; (2) inverting for the fluid conductivity the table would require gives k_f = 3.8 W/(m K) at 300 K rising past 40 at 1300 K -- no gas has this; (3) physically, stagnant-helium graphite pebble-bed effective conductivity at ambient is order 1-2 W/(m K) (SANA/HTTU-class experiments), so 11.94 at 300 K is not a physical stagnant-bed value under any correlation. The generating configuration is unknown -- SAM is closed-source, and the ANL reports (ANL/NSE-19/46, the NT24-115 SAM thermal-fluids paper, ANL pebble-temperature paper) cite the ZBS model but do not print the evaluation that produced this table. The analytic ZBS in crates/tampines/src/pebble_bed/zbs.rs carries a documented-discrepancy test recording the full 18-point comparison. CONSEQUENCE: the zbs.rs module doc in the digital-twin-engine frames this table as 'the published reference an analytic ZBS implementation must reproduce' -- that framing needs revisiting by the maintainer (that crate is owned by another agent; not edited). The table remains a faithful transcription of what the VTB/SAM model USED; the question is whether it is what ZBS PRODUCES. Options: keep the table as the interim bed conductivity (it is what the VTB transient models ran with), use the analytic ZBS, or obtain the full NEA PBMR-400 spec / SAM documentation to resolve the generating inputs.

title: root@vm
tampines: drift-flux and two-fluid pressure equations linearise DIFFERENT compressibilities -- measured 45% disagreement in the single-phase limit, undecided which is right
description:
Found 2026-08-12 while cross-checking the new six-equation solver against the four-equation one (op-62vf). Pinned by two_fluid_tests::the_two_solvers_disagree_in_the_single_phase_limit_and_the_compliance_ratio_explains_it.

THE FINDING. Run both 1-D solvers on the SAME single-phase subcooled state (7 MPa, 500 K, 1 m x 0.05 m pipe, 8 cells, closed left, 0.05 m/s prescribed outflow, dt = 100 us, 100 steps), with the drift-flux drift velocity set to zero and the two-fluid drag set to 1e12 so the no-slip limit is exact (measured slip 2.428613e-17 m/s). They should reduce to the same equations. They do not:

  drift-flux pressure drop = 4.273288e5 Pa
  two-fluid  pressure drop = 7.813506e5 Pa
  ratio                    = 1.828453
  worst discrepancy        = 45.4 % of the pressure change

THE CAUSE, MEASURED. The two pressure equations linearise different derivatives:
  - drift_flux uses psi_h = d(rho_m)/dp at FIXED ENTHALPY, on the argument that a segregated solve freezes h while it corrects p.
  - two_fluid uses d(rho_k)/dp along the ISENTROPIC path dh_k = dp/rho_k, on the argument that the energy equation applies the reversible work term alpha_k dp/dt in the SAME step, so that is the path the state actually takes.

Measured at 7 MPa / 500 K: psi_h = 9.764946e-7, psi_s = 6.313400e-7 s^2/m^2, ratio 1.546702. A smaller compliance gives a larger pressure change, so the direction is predicted and 82 % of the magnitude is accounted for.

WHAT IS UNRESOLVED, AND MUST NOT BE ASSERTED EITHER WAY:
1. WHICH ONE IS RIGHT. The isentropic derivative is the one an acoustic response should carry, and BOTH solvers apply the work term in their energy equations, which is an argument that drift_flux is the inconsistent one. That is an argument, not a result. Nothing has been compared against an analytic water-hammer solution, a speed-of-sound measurement, or an experiment.
2. THE REMAINING 18 %. The compliance ratio 1.547 does not fully account for the observed 1.828. Two unchecked candidates: the compliances are evaluated once at the initial state whereas both solvers re-evaluate theirs as p falls (drift flux switching to a secant after its first corrector), and the two reach their end state through different numbers of outer correctors. Instrument the per-step compliance of both rather than reasoning about it.

DO NOT 'FIX' drift_flux ON THE STRENGTH OF THIS. Its gated Edwards-O'Brien benchmark (edwards_drift_flux_gs1_pressure_history: RMSE 29.0 psia, plateau 354.3 psia inside the experimental band) was measured with psi_h. Changing its compliance changes that result and would invalidate the recorded numbers. The correct order is: settle 1 above against a reference first, then change one solver, then re-measure Edwards.

SUGGESTED NEXT STEP: a closed-form check. A rigid closed pipe of subcooled water with a small prescribed outflow has an analytic acoustic response p(t) set by 1/(rho c^2). Compare both solvers against IF97's own speed of sound (tampines_steam_tables w_tp / w_tpx_eqm) rather than against each other.

CROSS-REFERENCE from the API scoping work (op-375p / gh:#41), plus two things worth acting on inside this epic.

description:

CORRECTED CITATIONS. File 1: crates/boon-lay/src/lagrangian_decay_simulator/lagrangian_diffusion/single_particle_simulator/release_fraction_crp_6_case_1a_1b.rs
  - :50 is a println!, NOT the defect (the old citation pointed here)

  release_fraction_analytical_solution.rs, catch_unwind at :192,
  assert_relative_eq! against 0.53 at :200.

The 1600 degC companion test is clean.

FIX SHAPE (not applied): delete the catch_unwind and let the range assertion run. If it then fails, that is the real, useful result -- the model disagrees with CRP-6 by roughly 6-17% and that discrepancy needs investigating or documenting, not hiding. HTR-10 V&V: PBMR-400 coupled benchmark first, then HTR-10 criticality and safety demonstration tests
description:
Per docs/reactor-scoping/htr10.md section 5: target PBMR-400 BEFORE HTR-10. It is the most completely specified open pebble-bed benchmark and it exercises exactly the coupling that has to be built. Reaching HTR-10 measured transients with an unvalidated bed model would be guessing.

SEQUENCE:
1. PBMR-400 OECD/NEA coupled benchmark — steady state, then depressurised and pressurised loss of cooling, then rod withdrawal.
2. HTR-10 initial criticality (critical loading height) from the IAEA HTGR benchmark programme.
3. HTR-10 safety demonstration tests — loss of forced cooling without scram, and control-rod withdrawal without scram. Expect digitised plots rather than tabulated data, and record the digitisation procedure and its uncertainty as part of provenance.

Per the V&V rule, documentation must carry BOTH methodology and results: the reference, the inputs, the pass criterion, AND the measured numbers with uncertainty and the date taken. Depends on the bed closures and the graphite feedback channel.

Report disagreement honestly. A documented mismatch is a result; a quietly loosened tolerance is not.

notes.content:
HTR-10 thermal-hydraulic V&V targets, extracted 2026-08-11 from Gao, Z. and Shi, L. (2002), Thermal hydraulic calculation of the HTR-10 for the initial and equilibrium core, Nucl. Eng. Des. 218, 51-64, doi 10.1016/S0029-5493(02)00198-X. PROPRIETARY (Elsevier, all rights reserved) - catalogued at crates/kovan-literature/proprietary/papers/gao2002htr10th.json, gitignored. Cite it and implement from it; do NOT re-host the PDF.

This paper closes the gap that the VTB cannot: docs/reactor-scoping/vtb-findings.md records that VTB has NO HTR-10 thermal hydraulics at all. Gao and Shi supply calculated power, temperature and flow distributions for BOTH the initial and the equilibrium core.

QUANTITATIVE TARGETS TO VALIDATE AGAINST:
- Maximum fuel temperature 1046 C at 120 percent overload. This is the headline number to reproduce.
- HTR-10 maximum fuel temperature LIMIT is 1230 C under normal and accident conditions, per the experiment specification. NOTE this is NOT the 1600 C figure that appears throughout the modular-HTR literature (including the JRC book kugeler2017vhtr) - 1600 C is the generic coated-particle retention limit, 1230 C is HTR-10 own specified limit. Do not conflate them.
- Bypass flow through the gaps between graphite components is under 10 percent of rated flow. Any bed model that ignores bypass is therefore making a 10 percent error in core flow.
- Uncertainties the paper explicitly carries into the peak fuel temperature: non-uniform burnup, power distribution deviation, manufacturing deviation of fuel elements, graphite balls mixed with fuel balls in the initial core, and heat-transfer calculation deviation. A V&V comparison that ignores these is comparing a best-estimate to a conservative number.
- Initial core contains graphite balls mixed uniformly with fuel balls to suppress excess reactivity; the equilibrium core has none. These are two DIFFERENT validation cases, not one.

Confirms the operating point already taken from the IAEA benchmark: 10 MW, 3.0 MPa, 4.3 kg/s, 700 C outlet, 250 C inlet, feedwater 104 C, steam 440 C at 4.0 MPa.

description: teddy0@arch-aftershock-rapid-glass-S267454
title: teddy0@arch-aftershock-rapid-glass-S267454
tampines: gas-phase component layer for the HTR-10 helium primary circuit
description:
Replaces the mistaken op-jyyp.4, which proposed adding a gas arm to the TUAS Material enum. Maintainer ruling 2026-08-11: TUAS is for SALT solvers only and must never gain a gas arm; gas belongs in tampines.

THE NEED. An HTR-10 primary circuit is a helium loop at 3.0 MPa flowing 4.3 kg/s between 250 C and 700 C. Nothing in the workspace can currently model that with prebuilt components: TUAS has the component library but is salt-scoped, and tampines has the composition role but its component layer returns not-implemented for everything except Pipe::step.

WHAT TO BUILD. A gas-phase component layer in crates/tampines that can represent a forced-convection helium circuit: pipe/duct pressure drop and heat transfer for a compressible gas, the pebble-bed core as a porous component, and the circulator. Properties come from crates/outram-park-fork-coolprop, which already carries a full Helmholtz EOS for helium plus real NIST-lineage viscosity and thermal-conductivity correlations tested against tabulated reference states — consume those, do not reimplement or hardcode.

KNOWN DEFECT TO FIX WHILE HERE. htgr_sim_v1 currently hardcodes a constant helium viscosity despite the real correlation existing one crate away in coolprop. That shortcut should not survive into the gas layer.

RELATED WORK ALREADY LANDED. crates/outram-park-digital-twin-engine/src/htr10/ carries the cited HTR-10 design point and a verified KTA packed-bed pressure-drop implementation (reproduces the VTB gold values to every quoted digit). The gas layer should consume that rather than re-deriving it.

ALSO NOTE op-ql8 — tampines already has an open bead to wire the tested dwsim flash and finish the NotYetImplemented component wrappers. These two overlap; sequence them together rather than in conflict.

Do not widen TUAS. If a change appears to require touching tuas_boussinesq_solver Material enum, stop and reconsider the design.

notes.content:
SCOPE REFINEMENT from the maintainer, 2026-08-11: TUAS is not salt-only — it also does LIQUID METAL, even though salt was the original intent. So the boundary that matters is PHASE, not chemistry: TUAS covers LIQUIDS (molten salts and liquid metals), and GAS is the excluded phase.

That makes the ruling sharper rather than weaker. Do not read the earlier note on op-jyyp.4 as 'TUAS is for salt' — read it as 'TUAS is for liquids, and helium is not a liquid'. Adding a liquid-metal coolant to TUAS would be in scope; adding a gas arm is not, and that is why the HTR-10 helium circuit belongs in tampines.

Practical consequence for whoever implements this bead: do not try to generalise the TUAS Material enum into a phase-generic abstraction as a way of sneaking gas in. The liquid assumption is baked into the solver itself — TUAS is the Thermo-hydraulic Uniphase Advection and Convection Solver built on the Boussinesq approximation, which assumes small density variation. Helium at 3.0 MPa over a 250-700 C range varies in density by roughly a factor of two across the core, so the Boussinesq assumption does not hold for it. The exclusion is physical, not merely organisational.
notes.author: teddy0@arch-aftershock-rapid-glass-S267454

notes.content:
FINAL SCOPE FRAMING from the maintainer, 2026-08-11 — supersedes the two notes above, which were successively too narrow:

TUAS handles anything SINGLE-PHASE and NEARLY INCOMPRESSIBLE. That is liquids in practice — molten salts and liquid metals. An incompressible gas would technically fit the solver, but that restriction is severe enough that the maintainer explicitly does NOT want gas promised as a TUAS capability. Treat gas as out of scope for TUAS, full stop.

TAMPINES IS THE SUPERSET THAT INCLUDES TUAS. That is the architectural point and it resolves the whole question: gas support does not require widening TUAS, because tampines already sits above it and composes it alongside outram-park-fork-coolprop, tampines-steam-tables, outram-foam-basic-lib and chem-eng. Adding a gas layer at the tampines level is the natural place for it, not a workaround.

So the correct reading of this bead is not 'TUAS cannot do it, so find somewhere else'. It is 'tampines is where the superset lives, and a compressible helium circuit is a superset capability'.

Physical justification, unchanged: helium at 3.0 MPa across 250-700 C varies in density by roughly a factor of two through the core, so the nearly-incompressible assumption TUAS is built on genuinely does not hold for the HTR-10 primary circuit.
