description: teddy0@arch-aftershock-rapid-glass-S267454
title: teddy0@arch-aftershock-rapid-glass-S267454
Build the Haiku API-dogfooding harness and take a baseline
description:
Standing rule added to CLAUDE.md 2026-09-04 (Human interface layer > 'Verifying it: dogfood the API on a small model'). This bead is the harness that makes the rule runnable, plus the first baseline.

WHY. A strong model is the wrong instrument for API usability: when a call is unguessable it reads the Rust and compensates, so the defect never shows up in the result. Measured the same day, an Opus session writing short scripts against our own wheel -- WITH source access and grep -- guessed wrong ten times across six scripts (Sphere's arity, HalfSpaceSense vs bool, k_eff vs k_mean, stage_temperature singular/plural, TrisoRadii/TrisoMaterials wrappers, TrayHydraulics not constructible, ControlDict's thirteen positional args, FvSolution not constructible at all). A model that cannot read the source recovers from none of those, which is exactly why it is the honest probe.

WHAT TO BUILD.
  * A runner that starts a Haiku agent with a FIXED context: the wheel installed and nothing else. No repo, no .pyi, no source. The moment the stubs are in context it is testing something else.
  * A fixed task list spanning the tiers. Proposed: (a) k-eff of a bare HEU sphere; (b) run the pimpleFoam cavity case from a case directory; (c) reconstruct Pu-239 cross sections from an ENDF tape and Doppler-broaden them; (d) sweep reflux ratio on the rigorous MESH column; (e) something needing the low-level CSG types directly.
  * Per task: record round trips to a working script, and log EVERY exception with its message.
  * Aggregate the exception log across tasks, ranked by frequency. That ranked list is the backlog, and it is the deliverable -- same technique as outram-park/codegen/blocked.md one level up, which is what surfaced the generic-alias bug nobody had suspected.

TAKE THE BASELINE BEFORE CHANGING ANYTHING. The error-message and constructor work already discussed (self-describing enum errors, did-you-mean on attributes, Geometry::sphere/slab/box constructors, making mc_keff_of_actinide_sphere compose over run_keff_csg) should be measured against this baseline, not asserted.

NOT IN SCOPE. This measures discoverability, not physics. A script can run and be nonsense; the V&V tests remain the only check on correctness. A failure unique to the small model is likely its own priors rather than our API -- the tell is whether a different model trips on the same call.

notes.content:
SCOPE EXTENDED 2026-09-04 — two additions.

1. RUST-SIDE CUSTOM DIAGNOSTICS, same principle one layer down.

A confusing trait-bound error is the compiler's version of an undiscoverable API. `#[diagnostic::on_unimplemented]` is stable since Rust 1.78 and works on our 1.98 toolchain — verified here:

    #[diagnostic::on_unimplemented(
        message = "`{Self}` is not a valid solver state",
        label = "needs an OdeSystem",
        note = "construct one with `MySystem::new(..)`"
    )]
    trait OdeSystem {}

produces `error[E0277]: `u32` is not a valid solver state` with our label and note, in place of the default "the trait bound is not satisfied". `#[diagnostic::do_not_recommend]` (stable 1.85) suppresses a blanket impl the compiler would otherwise suggest unhelpfully.

The workspace has 65 public traits and, as of today, zero carry either attribute. Any trait whose bound a caller can plausibly fail should. Work item: audit the 65, annotate the ones with non-obvious bounds, starting with those a downstream crate actually names in a generic signature.

BE CLEAR ABOUT WHO THIS SERVES. on_unimplemented helps RUST callers and does nothing whatsoever for a Python user holding the wheel — the compiler is not in their loop. The Python-side equivalent is the pyo3 runtime error: an enum error that names its constructors, a wrong-attribute error that suggests the right one. Same design idea, two different layers, and the harness only measures the second. Do not conflate them or count one as progress on the other.

2. LITERATURE. The method has a lineage worth citing rather than reinventing.

  * API usability evaluation is a mature field — a systematic mapping covers 47 primary studies (Rauf et al. 2019, Comput. Sci. Rev.). The dominant instrument is the Cognitive Dimensions Framework questionnaire (Wijayarathna et al. 2017/2019; Piccioni et al. 2013, ESEM, 120 citations). The CD questionnaire is a ready-made structure for this bead's task list — use it rather than inventing categories.
  * Piccioni et al. found the top empirical issues to be 'the difficulty of finding good names for API features and of discovering relations between API types'. That is exactly what the Opus session hit here (two distinct Sphere types; having to discover that RegionToken relates to HalfSpaceSense), which is evidence the failures are the field's known dominant modes rather than anything exotic.
  * LLM-as-evaluator is very new: 'Lessons from API Usability Analyses Using an LLM' (John et al., CHI 2026 EA) uses a custom GPT to APPLY the CD framework on the designer's behalf — the model is the analyst, not the subject.
  * Nearest agentic work: 'ADK Arena: Evaluating Agent Development Kits via LLM-as-a-Developer' (arXiv 2606.05548); 'Diagnosing Knowledge Gaps in LLM Tool Use: An Agentic Benchmark for Novel API Acquisition' (2606.03657); 'ZhuLong: Execution-Grounded LLM Agent for EDA Scripting with Offline API Self-Exploration' (2608.07925).
  * NOT FOUND in two searches: the deliberate capability downgrade as the measurement principle — choosing a weaker model BECAUSE a stronger one masks the defect by reading source — with the ranked exception log as the defect backlog. Stated as not-found, not as novel; two searches is not a systematic review.

The framing that makes it defensible: usability testing requires representative users, not experts. Opus with grep is the expert who routes around the defect; Haiku with only the wheel is the representative user. The principle is old, the observation that model capability IS the expert/novice axis is the new part.
notes.author: teddy0@snrsi-arch-desktop

notes.content:
The Rust-side diagnostics work in the comment above is now split out as its own bead: op-wiep, 'Annotate public traits with #[diagnostic::on_unimplemented]'.

It belongs apart because the audiences differ — on_unimplemented serves Rust callers and is invisible to a Python user holding the wheel. Keeping them in one bead invited exactly the conflation this bead's own text warns against: closing the trait audit would have looked like progress on the Python harness, and it is not.

This bead (op-m2mj) stays scoped to the Haiku harness, the fixed task list, the baseline, and the exception log. op-wiep carries the 65-trait audit and its priority ranking.

tampines-steam-tables: pt_flash_eqm region classifier panics on exact float equality at the Region-4 line
description:
Found 2026-08-12 while implementing crates/tampines/src/multiphase_1d/two_fluid.rs (op-62vf).

DEFECT. interfaces/functional_programming/pt_flash_eqm/mod.rs:134 classifies a (T,p) point as the two-phase Region 4 with an EXACT float equality:

    (temp, pres) if (273.15..647.096).contains(&temp) && pres == p_sat_reg4_pascal => FwdEqnRegion::Region4

and every Region-4 arm of that module then panic!s (cp at :211, h at :171, s at :198, v at :242, w at :256, ...), because (T,p) cannot resolve a saturated mixture without a quality.

CONSEQUENCE. tampines::multiphase_1d::properties::SaturatedTransport::at(p) evaluates lambda_tp_eqm_two_phase at exactly (T_sat(p), p); the critical-enhancement term calls cp_tp_eqm_single_phase; so SaturatedTransport::at PANICS for every pressure p that round-trips bit-exactly through sat_pressure_4(sat_temp_4(p)).

MEASURED (2026-08-12, release), geometric sweep of 10790 pressures from 1.0e5 Pa to 2.2e7 Pa at ratio 1.0005:
  - SaturatedTransport::at panics: 105 (about 1 percent), scattered rather than banded
  - predicted by the bit-exact round-trip: 105, with ZERO false positives and ZERO false negatives
  - SaturatedProperties::at panics: 0 (it never routes through the classifier)

A blowdown sweeps continuously through pressure, so hitting one is a certainty, and it aborts the whole march with a panic rather than a Result.

TWO SEPARATE PROBLEMS:
1. A panic where an error belongs. interfaces/checked exists; the functional path should return Result rather than panic, or SaturatedTransport should use a quality-explicit entry point.
2. An exact float comparison on a region boundary. Even setting the panic aside, 'pres == p_sat_reg4_pascal' is not a defensible region test.

WORKAROUND IN PLACE (consumer side, not a fix): tampines::multiphase_1d::two_fluid::region_4_safe_pressure nudges p by a relative 4e-12 when and only when the bit-exact round-trip fires. Pinned by two_fluid_tests::region_4_safe_pressure_removes_the_upstream_classifier_panic, which re-measures the sweep and asserts zero mispredictions and zero surviving panics. Remove the workaround only after fixing the library and re-running that test.

WHAT HAPPENED: `cargo test -p outram-mc-libs --lib --tests --release` exited non-zero with

That run was executing CONCURRENTLY with `cargo test -p njoy-outram-park-fork --lib --tests --release` in a separate process, both started at the same moment on the same machine.

WHY THE NAME IS MISSING: the invocation was piped through `grep -E '^(test result:|failures:|error|...)'`, which filtered out the per-test FAILED line before it was written to the log. My mistake in the harness, not the test's.

DID NOT REPRODUCE. Three subsequent runs with nothing else building:
- `cargo test -p outram-mc-libs --lib --release` -> 212 passed, 0 failed, 3 ignored (twice)
- `cargo test -p outram-mc-libs --lib --tests --release` -> 212 + 5 + 30 + 7 = 254 passed, 0 failed

PLAUSIBLE BUT UNPROVEN: the lib target holds the GPU tests (`gpu::surface_distance`, `gpu::xs_interp`, `gpu::batched_flight`, `gpu::union_grid`), and this host has a single NVIDIA RTX 3050. A second heavy build competing for CPU and memory, or two processes contending for the one GPU device, is the obvious suspect. But njoy's suite has no GPU tests, so a pure GPU-contention story is not clean, and a plain build-lock/CPU-starvation timeout is equally consistent with the evidence. Do not write either into a doc as the cause.

NEXT STEP IF IT RECURS: re-run WITHOUT a grep filter, capture the full log, and get the failing test name. Then decide whether the GPU tests need serialising (a test-level mutex or a `--test-threads` carve-out for the gpu module only — NOT for the whole suite, per the workspace rule against serialising slow suites).

title: distillation_sim_v1 — transient distillation column GUI simulator in digital-twin-engine
description:
User request 2026-08-15: a transient distillation column GUI simulator in outram-park-digital-twin-engine, built on the existing htgr_sim_v1 example as a structural template, with a restart button like htgr_sim_v1's.

  - The TRANSIENT column physics already exists and is validated: crates/outram-park-fork-dwsim-libs/src/columns/dynamic.rs (866 lines), bead op-6rhz, status Done. DynamicColumn::from_solver_input + step_rk4 + integrate_to_steady; its own test (dynamic_column_relaxes_to_steady_mesh_solution) relaxes an 8-stage benzene/toluene column to the independently-computed steady MESH solution to 4e-4 K / 9.3e-6 mole fraction / 1e-3 mol/s product split.   examples/distillation_sim_v1/
    main.rs                    -- eframe entry + Android no-op stub
    app/mod.rs                 -- DistColSimApp, start_simulation()/restart_simulation(), crash-modal wiring, frame layout

Default plant is deliberately the SAME benzene/toluene 8-stage case op-6rhz's V&V test already validates against the independent steady MESH solve -- not a new, unverified configuration.

Children below split the work by module boundary. See each child for detail.

DONE 2026-08-15. All four children closed (op-mp9d, op-l6q9, op-akkj, op-81pb). Summary of what shipped, what was reused vs newly built, and what is honestly still unverified:

DELIVERED: crates/outram-park-digital-twin-engine/examples/distillation_sim_v1/ -- a working, tested interactive simulator for an 8-stage benzene/toluene distillation column, structured as a close mirror of htgr_sim_v1 (same app-scaffold patterns, same restart-on-crash flow). tampines components/: add gas-phase variants so gas_phase components slot into the Pipe/Pump component layer
description:
tampines::gas_phase landed 2026-08-11 (op-jyyp.12) with three working component models -- GasDuct (Churchill friction + Gnielinski/Dittus-Boelter heat transfer, low-Mach compressible), KtaBed (KTA 3102.3 packed-bed pressure drop) and Circulator (idealised fixed-rise/fixed-ratio compression). They are deliberately NOT wired into src/components/, which bead op-ql8 owns.

Interface notes for whoever does that wiring:

1. PipeBackend (components/pipe.rs) is an enum over stateful fluid ARRAYS (SinglePhaseFluidArray, CompressibleFluidArray, TampinesSteamArray, InsulatedFluidComponent). gas_phase::GasDuct is a different shape: it is stateless plain-data geometry plus a one-shot steady solve(mass_flow, T_in, p_in, boundary) -> GasDuctResult. It is NOT a drop-in PipeBackend variant.
   Suggested resolution: add a separate `SteadyGas(GasDuct)` variant, and accept that Pipe's methods split into a transient path (the array backends) and a steady path (this one), rather than forcing GasDuct to carry cell state it does not have.

2. KtaBed has no components/ counterpart at all -- a porous/packed-bed component struct would be new. It composes cleanly with crate::pebble_bed::zbs::ZbsBed (friction side + conduction side of the same bed).

3. Circulator is the gas analogue of components::Pump. Pump is currently a NotYetImplemented wrapper, so the cleanest move is probably a `PumpBackend` enum with a `GasCirculator(Circulator)` variant, mirroring PipeBackend.

4. All three take/return uom types and use crate::TampinesError, so error and unit conventions already match components/.

5. gas_phase exposes two public uom aliases -- MassFlux (kg/(m^2 s)) and PressureGradient (Pa/m) -- because uom ships no named types for those dimensions. If components/ needs them, re-export rather than redefining; note outram-park-digital-twin-engine/src/htr10/kta.rs independently defines identical aliases.

Blocked on op-ql8 finishing the NotYetImplemented wrapper pass.

STATE: crates/outram-mc-libs/src/material/thermal.rs is explicit at lines 24-26: 'Scope. Only the incoherent-*inelastic* channel — the one H-in-H2O needs (light water has no thermal elastic). Coherent / incoherent-elastic bound scattering (graphite, ZrH) is deliberately not wired here yet.'

The struct holds only xs_e/xs_sigma (sigma_inel) and emit_tables. Nuclide::with_thermal_scattering (src/material/nuclide.rs:221) attaches one ThermalScattering, and nuclide.rs:331-339 REPLACES the free-gas elastic channel with sigma_inel below the cutoff. For a scatterer whose thermal elastic is non-zero that substitution is doubly wrong: it drops the dominant channel AND removes the free-gas stand-in for it.

WHY IT MATTERS (HTR-10 critical path): for graphite at 0.0253 eV, measured through the njoy port against ENDF/B-VIII.0 tsl-crystalline-graphite (MAT=30): sigma_coh_el = 4.55 b, sigma_inel = 0.49 b. Wiring only the inelastic channel would give a graphite pebble ~11% of its true thermal scattering cross section — a materially wrong thermal spectrum and k_eff, and worse than the free-gas treatment it replaces.

WORK: extend ThermalScattering to carry an optional elastic channel (coherent: pre-tabulated sigma_coh_el(E) plus the Bragg (mu, weight) table per incident energy; incoherent: sigma(E,T) plus equiprobable cosines). At a thermal collision, choose elastic vs inelastic in proportion to their cross sections; an elastic scatter keeps E and samples mu from the Bragg weights (lab frame, no CM transform). Mirror OpenMC src/thermal.cpp ThermalData::sample, which does exactly this elastic/inelastic split. Depends on op-u5ju for the njoy-side surface.

SIZE: medium. Mostly plumbing + one sampling branch, but it changes the ThermalScattering shape and the nuclide.rs cross-section substitution, and needs a test.

notes.content:
IMPLEMENTED 2026-08-11 (this session; AI-assisted draft, NOT human-reviewed, NOT committed - coordinator holds the diff).

WHAT LANDED
- crates/outram-mc-libs/src/material/thermal.rs: new pub enum ThermalElastic {None, Coherent(CoherentElasticTable), Incoherent(IncoherentElasticTable)} (enum dispatch, no trait objects/Box/lifetimes). ThermalScattering now owns an elastic channel alongside the inelastic one, with elastic_xs(E), total_xs(E) and elastic() accessors. from_endf_file() reads the ENDF tape ONCE and DETECTS the elastic law from the evaluation (MT=2 LTHR=1/3 -> coherent, LTHR=2/3 -> incoherent, absent -> None); its signature is unchanged so every existing caller is source-compatible. NjoyError::NotPorted from a channel constructor is treated as 'this evaluation has no such section'; every other error, notably TemperatureOutOfRange, is propagated rather than silently dropping graphite's dominant channel.
- ThermalScattering::sample() now splits elastic vs inelastic with probability sigma_el/sigma_thermal, mirroring OpenMC src/thermal.cpp:296-302 ThermalData::sample_dist. The coherent branch mirrors src/secondary_thermal.cpp:34-54 CoherentElasticAE::sample (invert the cumulative structure factor, mu = 1 - 2 E_k/E, E_out = E_in).
- COHERENT IS STORED EXACTLY, NOT RESAMPLED. sigma_coh_el(E) is a 1/E sawtooth with 221 discontinuities for graphite, so a log-grid resample would smear every Bragg edge. CoherentElasticTable holds the Bragg-edge table itself (221 (E,sigma) pairs, ~3.5 kB - cheaper than the resample AND exact). Incoherent elastic IS resampled (it is smooth); grid sized by measurement at 400 points.
- crates/njoy-outram-park-fork/src/thermr/scattering.rs: added CoherentElasticScattering::bragg_edge_table() -> Vec<(NeutronEnergy, CrossSection)>, the uom-typed accessor that makes the exact storage possible. Mirrors the OpenMC CoherentElasticXS::bragg_edges()/factors() pair. This is the ONLY njoy-side change; the data/transport boundary is intact (outram-mc still parses no ENDF).
- crates/outram-mc-libs/src/material/nuclide.rs: xs_at_energy's thermal substitution now swaps in th.total_xs(e) = sigma_inel + sigma_el, not sigma_inel alone. THIS IS THE ACTUAL DEFECT THIS BEAD NAMED.

MEASURED (ENDF/B-VIII.0, release mode, 2026-08-11; full methodology + results in the module header of crates/outram-mc-libs/tests/thermal_graphite_elastic.rs, 7 tests, all green)
- Graphite MAT 30, 296 K, barn per carbon atom at 0.0253 eV: sigma_coh_el 4.5514, sigma_inel 0.4863, elastic fraction 0.9035. Confirms the ~90 % figure this bead was filed on.
- Exactness: worst relative deviation of the stored Bragg table vs the njoy surface = 7.67e-16 over 21199 points spanning 1e-4 to 4 eV. Bragg cutoff 1.822327e-3 eV (graphite (002)); sigma_el exactly 0.0 below it.
- Nuclide-level, C0 + graphite table vs bare C0, MicroXS::elastic at 0.0253 eV: free-gas 4.9398, bound-new 5.0378, bound-OLD (inel only) 0.4863. The pre-fix path gave graphite 9.8 % of its free-gas scattering; the fixed path gives 102.0 %.
- Sampling, 200000 draws at 0.0253 eV seed 1: elastic fraction 0.90340 vs cross-section prediction 0.90346 (0.09 sigma on a 6.6e-4 binomial sigma). Mean Bragg cosine -0.02357 vs the analytic sum p_i mu_i = -0.02497 over the 17 open reflections (1.17 sigma on SEM 1.20e-3).
- HTR-10 temperatures at 0.0253 eV: 293.15 K snaps to 296 K (NJOY tolerance) -> 4.5514/0.4863; 393.15 K interpolated -> 4.3849/0.6779; 523.15 K interpolated -> 4.1672/0.9445; 1073.15 K interpolated -> 3.3592/2.0373. Monotone Debye-Waller suppression; 100 K and 2200 K are hard TemperatureOutOfRange refusals.
- LIGHT-WATER REGRESSION: tsl-HinH2O MAT 1 at 293.6 K reports channel 'none', sigma_el identically 0, total_xs == inelastic_xs bit-identical, sigma_inel(0.0253) = 52.1420 b. The existing thermal pincell case is unaffected.
- ZrH MAT 7 (the OTHER elastic law, NOT on the HTR-10 path): channel 'incoherent elastic', sigma_el 55.0151 b/H vs sigma_inel 2.8804 b/H; log-grid resample error 2.61e-4 at 400 points (1.05e-3 at 200 - the grid was sized by this measurement); sampled mean cosine 0.13817 vs the njoy equiprobable-cosine mean 0.14142 (1.26 sigma), forward-peaked as the law requires.

GATES RUN: cargo test -p outram-mc-libs --lib --tests --release = 254 tests, 0 failed. njoy scripts/test.sh full suite = 393 lib + all integration, 0 failed. cargo check -p njoy-outram-park-fork -p outram-mc-libs --all-targets --target aarch64-linux-android --release = clean (NDK-free proxy; no native Termux run was done). cargo doc introduces no new broken intra-doc links.

WHAT THIS DOES NOT ESTABLISH: no k_eff has been computed with the elastic channel in place, and nothing is wired into pebble_beds yet - that is op-hc2o step 5, still open. The reference for the exactness and cosine gates is this workspace's own njoy port, so they are internal-consistency gates, not an independent NJOY/OpenMC-ACE oracle. NOT closing - human review owed.

notes.content:
Stagnation inflow BC now EXERCISED AND VERIFIED for the single-phase subcooled steady path, 2026-08-11 (~17:00 SGT). Items 2, 3, 4 of this bead are done; item 1 (land vs hold) stays a maintainer decision.

NEW TEST: reservoir_inlet_reaches_the_bernoulli_limit_in_subcooled_water in crates/tampines/src/multiphase_1d/tests.rs (+~390 lines incl. V&V doc). Closed form derived from the DISCRETE steady state of the scheme's own momentum balances (not the continuum limit): p0 - p_out = rho u^2/2 + rho F L with Darcy F, giving u = sqrt(2 dp / (rho (1 + f L/D))), friction incorporated (not neglected) via the code's own laminar-64/Re / Blasius closure. Case: p0 1.000 MPa -> p_out 0.980 MPa, T 300 K (~153 K subcooled), L 0.5 m, D 0.1 m, 20 cells, dt 0.5 ms, 3000 steps; all solver knobs at defaults.

MEASURED: closed-form u 6.225884 m/s vs measured steady inlet u 6.225891 m/s -> relative error +1.12e-6 against a 1.0 % tolerance PRE-COMMITTED in the doc comment before the first run (a-priori budget ~0.1 %, gated 10x looser because reference f is evaluated once at (p_out, mu_f)). Frictionless Bernoulli would be 6.334222 m/s; measured sits 1.7102 % below, matching the friction correction. Continuity |mdot_in - mdot_out|/mdot 1.28e-6; steadiness 3.3e-7; max Courant 0.125; alpha = 0 exactly throughout; ~6-7 s wall clock. Strongest evidence: the three pressure terms match INDIVIDUALLY (p[0] 980661.291 predicted vs 980661.29 measured; interior drop 644.376 vs 644.33; outflow face 16.957 vs 16.96), separately confirming the conservative half-cell inlet convection, the half-cell Dirichlet coefficient dt/(rho dx/2), and friction charged over exactly L. No defect found; the non-conservative alternative the BC doc warns about would sit at ~4.48 m/s (-28 %) and nothing near that appears.

DOCS: AxialBoundary::ReservoirInlet public doc now states both standing assumptions (zero inlet drift velocity; infinite non-depleting plenum) plus a V&V status block — doc-comment-only edits to drift_flux.rs, no code/signature/constant changed.

ALSO EXERCISED INDIRECTLY: the Marviken gates (op-ja3t) drive this BC through 897 marched two-phase transients with 0 refused steps.

STILL UNVERIFIED (stated in the test doc and the ReservoirInlet V&V block): two-phase inflow (InflowState::void_fraction and rho_g never exercised, alpha = 0 throughout the direct test), the h0 - u^2/2 static-enthalpy split only probed at 2e-4 relative head, backflow through either boundary, and transient behaviour. upwind_scalar has no direct unit test — it is private to drift_flux and tests.rs is a sibling module, so it needs a pub(super) visibility change first; filed as a follow-up bead (see op tracker, filed today). Note also Blasius is applied at Re ~ 4.1e6, beyond its nominal ~1e5 range — a property of the code under test, reproduced not corrected. Not closing this bead — maintainer decision.

title: teddy0@arch-aftershock-rapid-glass-S267454
OPCPFluidArray: boundary face flux phi is never pressure-corrected -- first-order outlet mass-balance deficit
description:
MEASURED 2026-08-12 in crates/outram-park-fork-coolprop, while adding the flow-rate inlet BC (op-2qsf). NOT fixed.

SYMPTOM. In step()'s pressure corrector, the mass-flux correction phi -= rho_f*rAU_f*snGrad(p)*|Sf| is applied to INTERNAL faces only; boundary faces keep the predictor value phi_HbyA. A prescribed-velocity (or prescribed-mass-flow) inlet is unaffected -- its boundary flux is written back explicitly from the BC -- but a fixed-pressure outlet's boundary flux is the uncorrected predictor.

MEASUREMENT. 1.0 g/s prescribed at the inlet (exact by construction), 200 W uniformly distributed, run to steady state, outlet flux read from phi's outlet patch:
  n =  8 cells: m_out = 9.929649e-4 kg/s, -0.7035 % against the inlet
  n = 16 cells: m_out = 9.968502e-4 kg/s, -0.3150 %
  n = 32 cells: m_out = 9.985182e-4 kg/s, -0.1482 %
Halving with each refinement => FIRST-ORDER TRUNCATION, not a conservation bug. Chief cause is the zero-gradient extrapolation of the outlet face velocity from the last cell centre while the flow is still accelerating through that half cell. The steady ENERGY balance closes far tighter over the same runs (200.0574 / 200.0002 / 200.0000 W against a 200 W source).

TRIED AND REJECTED. Recomputing the non-fixed-velocity boundary fluxes from the corrected U after the pressure correction moves n = 8 from -0.7035 % to -0.5364 % only -- it is not the dominant term, and it perturbs every existing test's numbers for a fraction of the error. Not worth taking on those terms without a proper look at the outlet face-value reconstruction.

Documented in the accuracy caveat on OPCPFluidArray::get_outlet_mass_flowrate_actual and in the doc comment of lateral_coupling::tests::mass_flow_inlet_closes_the_steady_energy_balance.

title: outram-foam-multiphase: port the virtual-mass closure so tampines can consume it instead of transcribing it
description:
Raised 2026-08-12 from op-62vf.

InterfacialForce::VirtualMass in crates/outram-foam-multiphase/src/two_fluid.rs is a documented scaffold whose momentum_coefficient returns MultiphaseError::NotImplemented. Beads op-dt3.12/.13 require the 1-D closures to TRACE BACK to this crate rather than be invented, and every other closure the new six-equation solver uses does: drag through DragModel::k_d, heat transfer through InterfacialHeatTransfer::volumetric_coefficient_si.

Virtual mass is the one exception, and it is the exception that matters most, because it IS the regularisation the whole six-equation model rests on (see crates/tampines/docs/six-equation-regularisation.md). tampines::multiphase_1d::two_fluid::virtual_mass_coefficient therefore writes the formula down locally:

    K_vm = max(alpha_d, alpha_res) * C_vm * rho_c

transcribed from OpenFOAM dispersedVirtualMassModel.C:51-67 and constantVirtualMassCoefficient.C:71-79 via the source study, with the deviation stated in that function's doc comment rather than hidden.

TO CLOSE: port the dispersedVirtualMassModel chain into outram-foam-multiphase -- the constantCoefficient arm at minimum, and the Lamb aspect-ratio arm (Lamb.C:69-77) if the aspect ratio is available -- so InterfacialForce::VirtualMass returns a real coefficient. Then replace the body of tampines::multiphase_1d::two_fluid::virtual_mass_coefficient with a call into it. Nothing else in the 1-D solver changes; the function exists precisely so that is a one-place edit.

Pinned meanwhile by two_fluid_tests::virtual_mass_coefficient_matches_the_transcribed_upstream_form, which checks the floored and role-swapped forms against hand arithmetic, so a ported version can be diffed against a known-good transcription rather than against nothing.

title: htgr_sim_v1: nodalised implicit counter-flow steam generator (helium/metal/water)
description:
BLOCKED 2026-08-12 by op-289n. See that bead for the reproductions.

Three designs were attempted, in the order the maintainer directed:
1. Hand-rolled implicit 3-stream matrix + Picard on the IF97 (p,h) nonlinearity, solved with outram-foam-basic-lib's dense LU SquareMatrix. WORKED end to end (three zones resolved, metal time constant real, energy balance closed to round-off) but was superseded and has been DELETED per explicit instruction.
2. Direct use of outram-foam-basic-lib fvm:: operators. Not built: FvMatrix is a single-field LDU matrix, so a monolithic 3-field coupled system is not expressible without either abusing the mesh topology (3N cells with synthetic film faces, writable via the public ldu.upper/lower/diag) or a partitioned outer iteration. Superseded before implementation.
3. Composition of OPCPFluidArray (helium) <-> SolidColumn (tube metal) <-> TampinesSteamArray (water/steam) via lateral_link_new_temperature_vector_avg_conductance. BUILT AND COMPILING, but BLOCKED: TampinesSteamArray ignores its inlet enthalpy boundary condition (op-289n), so the cold stream can never be given a feedwater inlet, has no axial temperature profile, and the exchanger cannot be driven.

VERIFIED WORKING in design 3 before the blocker: OPCPFluidArray advects its inlet enthalpy correctly; SolidColumn couples and advances; the lateral-conductance formulation gives the no-cross property structurally (q_i = UA_i*(T_up_i - T_down_i) at local temperatures, sign-correct by construction, nothing clamped); SolidMaterial::SteelSS304L supplies real density and cp so the metal mass is derived from geometry rather than invented; cost is ~0.35 ms per array step, so three 8-cell arrays at a few substeps per 0.05 s plant step is affordable.

TREE STATE: reverted to HEAD. examples/htgr_sim_v1 is unchanged and the suite is green (267 lib / 19 fhr_sim_v2 / 31 htgr_sim_v1 / 15 widget_studio, 0 failed). The ORIGINAL DEFECT IS THEREFORE STILL PRESENT: primary_loop.rs computes duty as eps*C*(T_helium - T_saturation) against an isothermal saturation sink, which over-predicts duty because the superheater driving difference never collapses. That is model error, not a timestep artefact.

NEEDS A MAINTAINER DECISION: fixing op-289n means editing tampines-steam-tables, which is outside the scope granted for this task (examples/htgr_sim_v1/physics/ only) and is a published crate.

=== UPDATE 2026-08-12: DELIVERED. ===
Design 3 (OPCPFluidArray <-> SolidColumn <-> TampinesSteamArray via lateral_link_new_temperature_vector_avg_conductance) is BUILT, WIRED INTO THE PLANT AND TESTED, in examples/htgr_sim_v1/physics/steam_generator.rs. The op-289n blocker is fixed and the inlet enthalpy BC works.

MEASURED AT THE DESIGN POINT (2026-08-12):
- Steam outlet 441.25 degC against the published 440 degC (+1.25 K), in the coupled plant with the feedwater controller in the loop. The maintainer-visible 'steam far too hot' symptom is gone.
- Hot-end driving temperature difference 263.80 K, against 470.4 K for the isothermal-saturation-sink model it replaces -- the old model over-predicted it by 78%.
- Zero node-by-node temperature cross at every step of every run (worst 0.000000 K), structurally rather than by clamping.
- max_absorbable_duty no longer binds: peak Q_offered/Q_max 0.8807 in normal operation, 0.9088 including start-up.
- Tube metal 3184.3 kg DERIVED from geometry via SolidMaterial::SteelSS304L (8030 kg/m3), C = 1.6366e6 J/K, tau = C/UA = 38.42 s. A 100 K duty step moves the steam outlet 0.0005% in the first 0.05 s.
- Energy balance closes to +0.34% (converged; it is an explicit Lie-split coupling, so O(dt) -- 1.72% at a 0.025 s substep, 0.35% at 0.00625 s).
- Helium terminals sit ~21 K above published (720.7/272.9 degC vs 700/250). REPORTED, NOT TUNED OUT.

Suite: 285 lib / 19 fhr_sim_v2 / 53 htgr_sim_v1 / 21 widget_studio, 0 failed. Example launches and runs clean.

title: root@vm
chem-eng: ProportionalController still routes a pure gain through the full first-order machinery
description:
Follow-up from op-fm5 (fixed 2026-08-11). No longer a performance emergency, but still wasteful and still the thing its own doc comment apologises for.

ProportionalController::new (alpha_nightly/controllers/proportional_controller/mod.rs) realises G(s) = K_c as the first-order transfer function (K_c s + K_c)/(s + 1), so a pure multiply goes through a TransferFnFirstOrder, i.e. TWO blocks (FirstOrderStableTransferFnNoZeroes + FirstOrderStableTransferFnForZeroes), three state variables, three exp() calls and the 9-decimal-place input-change guard, every step. Its Default doc at :58 already says 'This is probably overdoing it in terms of computation cost but that is not an issue ... yet ...'.

MEASURED 2026-08-11 (release, AMD Ryzen 5 5600, rustc 1.97.0), after the op-fm5 O(1) rewrite: a bare ProportionalController costs 0.06 us/step, against roughly 1 ns for the multiply it actually represents -- so about 60x overhead, flat. Before the rewrite it was 9.42 us/step. So the fire is out; what is left is tidiness.

PROPOSED: give ProportionalController a direct multiply path (output = K_c * input + offset) and keep the transfer-function representation only where a dead time is actually set, since dead time is the one thing the plain multiply cannot express. Watch out: the current form is NOT exactly a pure gain when a dead time is applied, so check what set_dead_time is expected to do here before simplifying.

Not urgent. Filed so the apology in the doc comment has somewhere to point.

title: kovan-literature: lit import defaults visibility to Open when the source PDF is outside open/ or proprietary/ (staging imports)
description:
Observed 2026-08-11 during the librarian pass, kovan CLI built from workspace at target/release/kovan (08:40 build).

REPRODUCTION (actually run):
./target/release/kovan lit import 'kovan_import/decay heat tobias.pdf' --json-out crates/kovan-literature/proprietary/papers/tobias1980decay.json --markdown-out crates/kovan-literature/generated/markdown/proprietary/tobias1980decay.md

OBSERVED: the summary printed 'visibility: Open' and the JSON was written with visibility Open — even though both --json-out and --markdown-out point into proprietary/ trees. The path-based visibility inference (storage::visibility_from_path per DECISIONS.md) evidently looks only at the SOURCE path (kovan_import/...), which contains neither open/ nor proprietary/, and the fallback default is Open.

WHY THIS MATTERS: the normal workflow (kovan_import/README.md) imports FROM staging, so every proprietary import gets visibility Open by default. That is the expensive failure direction — DECISIONS.md itself says the design goal was 'proprietary material can't be mislabelled open by accident', and this defeats it. The same run also imported an open document correctly, so only the default is wrong.

SUGGESTED FIX DIRECTION: infer visibility from the --json-out destination path when the source path is indeterminate, and/or default to Proprietary (the cheap failure direction) instead of Open, and/or print a loud warning when falling back.

The tobias1980decay.json record was hand-patched to Proprietary the same day; no mislabelled record remains.

notes.content:
FIXED 2026-08-11, pending maintainer verification. Maintainer decision: 'for lit import, visibilty should be closed by default. And open if explicitly stated.'

Implemented in crates/kovan-literature/src/lib.rs, storage::visibility_from_path. A document is now Open ONLY when its path contains an explicit open/ component; everything else, including a path with neither marker, is Proprietary.

WHY THE OLD TEST DID NOT CATCH IT: the existing test asserted exactly two cases, open/papers/x.pdf and proprietary/reports/x.pdf. Both pass under the OLD rule and the NEW one, because neither exercises the unmarked path. The defect lived entirely in the case nobody wrote a test for. The replacement test now covers a bare filename, a kovan_import/ staging path, an absolute Downloads path, case-insensitive OPEN/, and a substring trap (openfoam_cases/ must NOT be read as an open marker). 69 lib tests pass.

title: kovan discover emits mixed path separators on Windows
description:
Found incidentally on 2026-08-13 while adding kovan-metrics; NOT caused by that change.

'kovan discover --root crates/kovan-metrics --kind source' prints paths like:

  crates/kovan-metrics\src\baseline.rs

The root portion keeps the forward slashes it was given, while the walked portion uses Windows backslashes. The existing e2e test crates/kovan-cli/tests/cli_e2e.rs:63 asserts the output ends with 'src/lib.rs' and therefore FAILS on Windows -- a pre-existing platform failure, currently the only failing test in kovan-cli (16 pass, 1 fails).

Why it matters beyond the test: kovan-cli is the AGENT-facing interface, and its contract is line-oriented parseable output. Mixed separators in a single path make naive downstream splitting unreliable.

Options: normalise discovery output to forward slashes on all platforms (best for an agent-facing contract, and makes the test pass as written), or make the test platform-aware (cheaper, leaves the mixed-separator output). Prefer the former.

Do NOT 'fix' this by loosening the assertion without deciding the output contract first.

title: workspace: wasm32-unknown-unknown as a supported target for every crate
description:
GOAL: 'cargo check -p <crate> --lib --target wasm32-unknown-unknown' passes for all 36 workspace members, and stays passing.

MEASURED BASELINE 2026-09-04 (wasm32-unknown-unknown target installed, --lib, default features): 20 PASS / 16 FAIL.

PASS (20): chem-eng-real-time-process-control-simulator, kovan-codegen, kovan-common, kovan-literature, outram-foam-appbuilder-lib, outram-foam-basic-lib, outram-foam-cli, outram-foam-mesh, outram-foam-multiphase, outram-foam-turbulence-lib, outram-park-fork-cfmesh, outram-park-fork-coolprop, outram-park-fork-dwsim-libs, outram-park-fork-liggghts, outram-park-fork-moltres, outram-park-fork-offbeat, outram-park-fork-onix, outram-park-fork-thermochimica, tampines-steam-tables, teh-o-prke.

FAIL (16), in six distinct classes — one child bead per class:
  A. rayon/rayon-core does not build on wasm ('cannot find module or crate sys'): boon-lay, nee_soon, njoy-outram-park-fork, outram-mc-libs, raffles
  B. faer default features pull rayon -> spindle -> atomic-wait ('cannot find module or crate platform'): bedok, outram-blender
  C. getrandom/uuid need an explicit wasm randomness backend: kovan, outram-park-digital-twin-engine, tampines, tuas_boussinesq_solver
  D. std::os::unix used directly: kovan-discovery, kovan-metrics, kovan-semantics
  E. 64-bit usize assumptions (E0080 shift overflow — wasm32 usize is 32-bit): outram-park-fork-pflotran, outram-park-mpi
  F. keep it from regressing (CI gate)

*** CRITICAL SCOPE CAVEAT — COMPILES IS NOT RUNS. ***
This epic's acceptance is COMPILATION only, and that must not be overstated. std::thread::spawn, std::fs and Instant::now all COMPILE for wasm32 and fail only at RUNTIME (spawn and Instant panic; fs errors). chem-eng-real-time-process-control-simulator is the proof: it PASSES the compile check today while containing 5 thread::spawn sites and 10 files using std::fs.

Non-exhaustive runtime-hostility census (src/ only, excluding tests), for the crates that will actually need to RUN in a browser:
  tuas_boussinesq_solver         spawn=27 instant=21 fs=2
  outram-park-digital-twin-engine spawn=7  instant=13 fs=2
  chem-eng-...-control-simulator spawn=5  instant=2  fs=10
  kovan                          spawn=2  instant=6  fs=36
  njoy-outram-park-fork          spawn=0  instant=1  fs=16

Making a crate RUN on wasm is per-crate work tracked separately — see epic op-eeqw (htgr_sim_v1 browser demo, GH #39), whose Phase 2 and Phase 3 are exactly that job for the htgr dependency chain. Do not close this epic claiming browser-readiness.

Established in-workspace precedent to copy rather than reinvent: outram-foam-basic-lib already passes because its rayon sits behind an off-by-default 'parallel' feature (bead op-yvj.4.1 / GH #10). That is the shape class A should adopt.

Also note this is a NEW target, not a replacement: nothing here may break the existing aarch64-linux-android gates (epic op-zfr).

notes.content:
Done, with the scope the maintainer set on 2026-09-04.

RESULT: scripts/check-wasm.sh reports 30 ok, 0 failed, 6 excluded. Every in-scope workspace member's library compiles for wasm32-unknown-unknown, and a gate plus a CLAUDE.md section keep it that way. Baseline at the start of the epic was 20/36.

Checking SCOPE rather than child count, per the lesson from op-6w0: 4 of 6 children delivered, 2 cancelled as out of scope by maintainer decision (bedok/outram-blender on faer; the four filesystem-bound kovan crates). The remaining scope IS complete for the crates that are in it.

What the classes turned into:
  A rayon        DONE — 5 crates. Target-gated off wasm ONLY, never feature-gated and never off Android, because rayon is pure Rust and Android-in-scope. Serial wasm_par shims where needed; numerically exact for these crates.
  B faer         CANCELLED — bedok/outram-blender excluded.
  C getrandom    DONE — two different getrandom majors needing two different mechanisms; one satisfied via .cargo/config.toml, one CUT by gating async-opcua off wasm.
  D std::os::unix CANCELLED — kovan crates excluded; kovan-codegen/-common/-literature kept in the gate since they already pass.
  E 32-bit usize DONE — a real latent bug, see below.
  F gate + docs  DONE.

THE MOST VALUABLE THING THIS EPIC FOUND was not a wasm issue at all. outram-park-mpi's 'COLL_CONTEXT_OFFSET: usize = 1 << 40' is a compile-time overflow on ANY 32-bit target. Fixed by widening to u64 rather than truncating, because it is a namespace tag and not a memory size. It would equally have failed on armv7-linux-androideabi and i686-linux-android — targets CLAUDE.md claims to support but whose acceptance command names only aarch64. Filed against op-zfr; I expect more width assumptions there.

Second finding, recorded in CLAUDE.md: wgpu's WebGPU backend holds Rc<Cell<u32>> and is therefore !Send on wasm, so the 'static OnceLock<Option<GpuContext>>' pattern this workspace uses in several crates cannot compile there. It needs thread_local!, which is a real change rather than a gate. Currently sidestepped by gating GPU modules off wasm.

THE CAVEAT THAT MUST TRAVEL WITH THIS RESULT: compiling is not running. thread::spawn, Instant::now and std::fs all compile for wasm and fail at run time. chem-eng-real-time-process-control-simulator passes the gate today with 5 spawn sites and 10 std::fs files. Nobody should read '30/30' as browser-readiness — the actual runtime work is epic op-eeqw (GH #39). This is stated in the epic, in the script header and at the top of the CLAUDE.md section, deliberately in all three places.

No human V&V is claimed.

wasm class A: put rayon behind an off-by-default feature (5 crates)
description:
rayon-core does not build for wasm32-unknown-unknown at all — it needs OS threads, and fails with 'cannot find module or crate sys'. Five crates depend on it unconditionally:
  boon-lay, nee_soon, njoy-outram-park-fork, outram-mc-libs, raffles
(nee_soon and raffles inherit it transitively via njoy-outram-park-fork / outram-mc-libs.)

COPY THE EXISTING PRECEDENT, do not invent a new shape: outram-foam-basic-lib already passes the wasm check because its rayon sits behind an off-by-default 'parallel' Cargo feature (op-yvj.4.1 / GH #10), with ComputeBackend::CpuMulti degrading to Serial when the feature is off. Its compute.rs module header documents the reasoning. Same treatment here.

Note the deliberate asymmetry with Android: rayon IS Android-clean (pure Rust, no system component) and is correctly NOT target-gated for it. So the gate must be a FEATURE, not cfg(not(target_arch=wasm32)) — otherwise Termux loses multi-core for no reason. outram-foam-basic-lib's Cargo.toml comments already spell this out.

Acceptance: cargo check -p <each> --lib --target wasm32-unknown-unknown passes; native default build keeps rayon and is unchanged; cargo check --all-targets --target aarch64-linux-android still clean.

notes.content:
Done, landed in 56fba8fc00. Left In Progress by oversight when the epic was closed — the work shipped with the epic.

Five crates: njoy-outram-park-fork, outram-mc-libs and boon-lay declared rayon directly; nee_soon and raffles inherited it transitively and went green for free once those three were fixed.

MECHANISM, chosen deliberately and not the obvious one: TARGET-gated off wasm ONLY — not feature-gated, and not gated off Android. rayon is pure Rust with no system component and is Android-in-scope, so feature-gating it (the shape outram-foam-basic-lib uses, which this bead originally pointed at) would have cost Termux its multi-core path for nothing. Same reasoning applied to ratatui/crossterm.

On wasm the call sites use a small in-crate wasm_par module — serial stand-ins for exactly the three or four rayon adapters each crate actually uses, plus a ThreadPool/install stand-in for the two crates that build explicit pools. The module docs state plainly that it is NOT parallelism. For these crates the serial path is numerically exact rather than a degraded fallback: the Monte Carlo drivers seed per history and document thread-count-independent eigenvalues, and boon-lay's CPU Walk-on-Spheres path is already the trusted reference its GPU path is validated against.

That exactness is now TESTED, not just asserted — see op-okqo.7, which runs the shim paths under WASI and compares against the native rayon build.

description: teddy0@snrsi-arch-desktop
title: teddy0@snrsi-arch-desktop
wasm class C: getrandom/uuid wasm randomness backend (4 crates)
description:
Two related errors, same root cause — the rand/getrandom stack refuses to build for wasm32-unknown-unknown without being told where entropy comes from, because the bare wasm32-unknown-unknown target has no OS:

  kovan, outram-park-digital-twin-engine:
    'to use uuid on wasm32-unknown-unknown, specify a source of randomness using one of the js/rng feature flags'
  tampines, tuas_boussinesq_solver:
    'The wasm32-unknown-unknown targets are not supported by default; you may need to enable the js feature'

Fix is a target-gated feature, e.g. for getrandom 0.2 the 'js' feature, or for 0.3 the wasm_js backend plus the matching RUSTFLAGS cfg. CHECK WHICH MAJOR VERSION the tree actually resolves before choosing — getrandom changed this mechanism between 0.2 and 0.3 and the wrong advice is a common time sink.

Add only under [target.'cfg(target_arch = "wasm32")'.dependencies] so native and Android builds are untouched.

Question worth answering rather than assuming: does the crate actually NEED randomness on wasm, or is uuid/rand pulled in by something that could itself be feature-gated off? Cutting the dependency is better than satisfying it. tampines and tuas in particular should be checked — a thermal-hydraulics solver wanting entropy at all is worth a second look.

Acceptance: all four pass the wasm --lib check; native and Android unchanged.

notes.content:
Done. tampines, tuas_boussinesq_solver and outram-park-digital-twin-engine all pass the wasm --lib check.

Two DIFFERENT getrandom majors were in play, needing different mechanisms — the bead warned about exactly this and it was worth checking rather than assuming:

  getrandom 0.3 (tampines, tuas, via peroxide -> rand):
    Needs BOTH the 'wasm_js' feature AND --cfg getrandom_backend="wasm_js".
    The feature alone is insufficient and getrandom errors saying so. The cfg
    now lives in a new .cargo/config.toml scoped to [target.wasm32-unknown-unknown],
    so a plain 'cargo check --target wasm32-unknown-unknown' works with no extra
    environment — which is what the gate runs.

  getrandom 0.2 + uuid (digital-twin-engine, via async-opcua):
    NOT satisfied. CUT instead, which is what this bead said to prefer.

On the bead's own question — 'does the crate actually NEED randomness, or is it pulled in by something that could be gated off?':

  tampines/tuas: it comes from peroxide, which depends on rand UNCONDITIONALLY with no feature to disable it. Cutting would mean replacing peroxide's CubicSpline across ~39 sites in tuas — its own job, not this one. So satisfying it was the smaller correct change here, and the reasoning is recorded in .cargo/config.toml rather than left as a mystery flag.

  digital-twin-engine: it came from async-opcua, which a browser cannot use at all. Target-gating the whole OPC-UA/mDNS/filesystem stack off wasm (async-opcua, tokio, mdns-sd, directories, local-ip-address, env_logger) removed getrandom 0.2 AND uuid outright, and took the crate from 57 errors to 0. The ciet_opcua / opcua_core / htgr_opcua modules are gated to match.

That last one also DELIVERS op-eeqw.2 (GH #39 Phase 1), which asked for exactly this gating for the htgr browser demo. Two epics, one change.

All gates are wasm-only: async-opcua was verified Android-clean on 2026-07-28 and stays ungated there.

Verification: all three pass wasm --lib; all three pass native --lib and aarch64-linux-android --lib with 0 errors; cargo check --workspace --lib native has 0 errors.

description: teddy0@snrsi-arch-desktop
title: teddy0@snrsi-arch-desktop
wasm class D: std::os::unix in three kovan crates
description:
kovan-discovery, kovan-metrics and kovan-semantics use std::os::unix directly and fail with 'cannot find unix in os'.

Likely candidates: PermissionsExt (file modes), OsStrExt, CommandExt, or symlink handling in the fd/ripgrep walker.

Fix: cfg-gate the unix-specific code and provide a portable fallback, OR gate the whole capability off wasm where it makes no sense. Worth asking per site which it is — a file-permission check has no meaning in a browser, whereas a path-to-bytes conversion does and should use the portable API.

NOTE the honest question behind this one: kovan is a local-first developer CLI/TUI that walks the filesystem and shells out to language servers. kovan itself already shows 36 files using std::fs. 'Compiles for wasm' is therefore close to meaningless for these three crates in isolation — nothing about them would FUNCTION in a browser.

So decide explicitly, and record the decision:
  (a) make them compile for wasm anyway, for uniformity and to keep the CI gate simple; or
  (b) declare them out of scope, exclude them from the gate with a stated reason.
Option (b) is defensible and may be the honest answer. What is NOT acceptable is quietly making them compile and letting a future reader infer they work.

notes.content:
CANCELLED — EXCLUDED by maintainer decision, 2026-09-04: the kovan crates are out of scope for wasm.

This bead put the question rather than assuming, and option (b) — 'declare them out of scope with a stated reason' — is the answer. kovan is a local-first developer CLI/TUI that walks the filesystem and shells out to language servers; kovan itself has 36 files using std::fs. wasm class E: 64-bit usize assumptions — real portability bug (pflotran, outram-park-mpi)
description:
THE MOST VALUABLE FINDING OF THE WASM AUDIT. This is a genuine latent bug, not a build-config issue, and it would bite any 32-bit target — not just wasm.

  crates/outram-park-mpi/src/communicator.rs:53
    pub(crate) const COLL_CONTEXT_OFFSET: usize = 1 << 40;
  error[E0080]: attempt to shift left by 40_i32, which would overflow

wasm32 has a 32-BIT usize, so '1 << 40' as usize is a compile-time overflow. outram-park-fork-pflotran fails the same way (2 errors).

The code silently assumes 64-bit usize. On a 64-bit host it works; on wasm32 (and on armv7-linux-androideabi and i686-linux-android — both of which the Android rule nominally covers!) it does not. Worth checking whether the armv7/i686 Android targets were ever actually built, because this would have failed there too.

Fix is not merely 'make it compile': decide what the constant MEANS. If it is a tag/offset needing 40 bits of range, it must be u64 and the surrounding arithmetic must be u64, not usize. Widening the type is correct; truncating the constant to fit 32 bits would silently change behaviour and is the wrong fix.

Audit both crates for other width assumptions while in there — grep for 'as usize', '1 <<', and size_of::<usize>().

Acceptance: both pass the wasm --lib check; the constant's semantics are preserved and documented; add a test pinning the intended range.

notes.content:
Fixed. Both crates now pass cargo check --lib --target wasm32-unknown-unknown.

Root cause was as suspected — a genuine 64-bit usize assumption, not a build-config issue:
  crates/outram-park-mpi/src/communicator.rs:53
    pub(crate) const COLL_CONTEXT_OFFSET: usize = 1 << 40;
wasm32 has a 32-bit usize, so this was a compile-time overflow.

Fix: WIDENED the communicator context id to u64 throughout rather than truncating the constant, because the value is a numeric namespace tag and not a memory size — truncating to fit 32 bits would have silently collapsed the 40-bit separation the collective/point-to-point isolation argument depends on. Sites changed: WORLD_COMM_ID, COLL_CONTEXT_OFFSET, Communicator::comm_id field + accessor, coll_ctx(), alloc_context(), send_ctx/recv_ctx ctx params, Envelope::comm_id, Transport::next_comm_id (AtomicUsize -> AtomicU64), alloc_comm_id(), agree_new_context(), the split() context-map decode, and the transport test helper. A doc block on the constant now records why it is u64.

outram-park-fork-pflotran needed NO separate fix — its 2 errors were the same constant reached through its outram-park-mpi dependency, and it went green as soon as mpi did.

Verification: cargo check --lib --target wasm32-unknown-unknown 0 errors for both; cargo check --all-targets native 0 errors; cargo test --release -p outram-park-mpi 35 passed.

WIDER FINDING worth acting on separately: this would equally have failed on armv7-linux-androideabi and i686-linux-android, which the workspace Android rule nominally covers. That strongly suggests the 32-bit Android targets have never actually been built — the rule's acceptance command names aarch64 only. Worth a bead against epic op-zfr.

title: root@vm
chem-eng: step-cost regression tests use wall-clock assertions and flake under load
description:
Observed twice on 2026-08-11. The tests alpha_nightly::stable_transfer_functions::recurrence_tests::pid_step_cost_does_not_grow_with_step_index and its beta_testing sibling assert on measured wall-clock per-step cost. Both failed once and passed on immediate rerun while four other agents were compiling on the same machine.

WHY THIS MATTERS MORE THAN A USUAL FLAKE. These tests exist to defend the op-fm5 fix — they are the regression guard proving the response vectors no longer grow without bound. A guard that cries wolf gets muted, and the defect it guards against (a plateau at ~28 us/step at dt=0.04, degrading to ~1133 us/step at dt=0.001) is exactly the kind that creeps back in silently.

THE UNDERLYING ISSUE: wall-clock time is not the property under test. The property is that per-step cost is O(1) in the step index, i.e. that internal state does not grow. Wall-clock is a proxy for that, and a poor one on a shared machine.

SUGGESTED FIX: assert on the invariant directly rather than its timing shadow. Assert the internal state SIZE is constant between step 100 and step 100000 — a first-order recurrence keeps a fixed number of coefficients regardless of how many inputs it has seen. That is deterministic, machine-independent, fast, and it fails for the right reason. Note first_order_transfer_fn.rs already gained a state_size() method today (currently dead_code); that is the accessor this needs.

Keep a wall-clock benchmark if it is useful, but make it a benchmark that reports rather than a test that fails.

notes.content:
SUBSTANTIALLY FIXED 2026-08-11 (agent stopped at session end mid-verification; needs a review pass).

The wall-clock flakiness was addressed by changing WHAT is asserted rather than loosening a threshold. The tests now measure a mean-cost window at step 5,000 and again at step 100,000 and assert the RATIO, with a deliberately loose 5x pass criterion. The ratio is machine-independent; the absolute microseconds are not. Measured on AMD Ryzen 5 5600, rustc 1.97.0, release: filtered PID with tau_d = 80.8 s gives 0.279 us/step at both windows, ratio 1.00; a bare P controller 0.105 -> 0.104 us/step, ratio 1.00. Stable across three consecutive runs (32/32 each, ratios 1.00-1.03).

The doc comment now states explicitly that those figures were taken under heavy concurrent build load, which is why they sit above the 0.17 us/step measured on an idle machine — recorded rather than hidden, so a future reader is not confused by the discrepancy. For contrast it also records the pre-0.2.0 behaviour on the same machine: 58.2 us/step at step 1,000 rising to 2329.5 us/step at step 79,000, a ratio of 40 and still climbing.

REMAINING: the agent was stopped with the message 'Let me update the recorded V&V numbers to match the new methodology and re-verify.' The alpha_nightly tier doc comment was verified complete during the session-end sweep; the beta_testing tier was NOT individually inspected. Both files were modified and 32/32 tests pass, so nothing is broken, but the beta tier's recorded numbers should be read against its actual methodology before this bead is closed.

Also still open as originally filed: asserting on internal STATE SIZE rather than timing at all would be strictly better — deterministic, machine-independent, and it fails for the right reason. first_order_transfer_fn.rs has a state_size() method (currently dead_code) which is the accessor for it.

title: tampines: Edwards-O'Brien and Marviken two-fluid (6-eqn) cases -- API is ready, read the two blocker beads first
description:
Filed 2026-08-12 on completing the TwoFluid1d solver core (op-62vf), as a hand-off to whoever writes the six-equation benchmark cases (op-s1a0).

WHAT THE SOLVER OFFERS. crates/tampines/src/multiphase_1d/two_fluid.rs:
  TwoFluid1d::new(pipe, exchange, pressure, temperature, dt) -> Result<Self>
  TwoFluid1d::bubbly(pipe, pressure, temperature, dt)  -- Schiller-Naumann + Ranz-Marshall + spherical, 1 mm
  set_temperature_profile(&[ThermodynamicTemperature])  -- for the Hendrie non-isothermal profile
  set_left_boundary / set_right_boundary (TwoFluidBoundary::{Closed, PrescribedVelocity, ChokedOutlet})
  set_virtual_mass_coefficient / set_initial_void_fraction / set_residual_alpha / set_outer_correctors / set_pressure_under_relaxation
  step() -> Result<TwoFluidReport>
  read-only: pressure, void_fraction, liquid_fraction, vapour_/liquid_density, vapour_/liquid_enthalpy, vapour_/liquid_temperature, saturation_temperature, vapour_/liquid_face_velocity, slip_velocity, mixture_density, inventory, total_enthalpy, outlet_mass_flow

TwoFluidReport carries time, outlet_mass_flow, max/min_void_fraction, max_thermal_nonequilibrium, max_slip, inventory, max_courant, max_volume_residual, outer_correctors_used, outlet_choked, mass_transfer_limited_cells, residual_alpha_floor_events.

READ THESE BEFORE STARTING, both filed 2026-08-12:
1. 'low-void starts refuse -- vapour cannot shed its expansion work'. Edwards-O'Brien starts 57 K SUBCOOLED, which is exactly the regime that refuses after 10-15 steps. A two-fluid Edwards case is BLOCKED on that, not merely unwritten. Do not work around it by tuning the initial void fraction until it runs -- that is choosing a model parameter to get a benchmark to pass.
2. 'no Dirichlet-pressure boundary'. There is no ReservoirInlet or PressureOutlet, so a Marviken-style vessel discharge has no inlet boundary to use.

WHAT IS OBLIGATORY IF A CASE IS WRITTEN, per crates/tampines/docs/six-equation-regularisation.md section 9.5:
  - a grid-refinement study, with the observed order -- the system is NOT known to be well posed, so refinement may not improve the answer, and reporting a single-mesh number would be misleading;
  - a sensitivity of the headline result to C_vm over at least [0, 0.5]. two_fluid_tests::the_answer_moves_with_c_vm_and_the_sensitivity_is_reported shows how, and measured on the demonstrator case: 8.4 % spread in max |T_g - T_l|, 1.1 % in slip, 0.16 % in outlet mass flow;
  - the same for the initial void fraction, which is a model parameter with no measured provenance.

A WORKING STARTING POINT EXISTS: two_fluid_tests::a_two_phase_blowdown_marches_without_refusing runs the Edwards geometry from a SATURATED two-phase state and completes -- 667 steps at 8 cells, and 10002 steps (full 300 ms) at 24 cells, reaching 19.3 K of thermal non-equilibrium and 1.46 m/s of slip. That is not Edwards (wrong initial condition) but it is the harness shape a case would reuse.

columns/dynamic: interior-stage energy sweep was enthalpy-reference dependent
description:
FOUND AND FIXED 2026-09-04 while doing op-190j.4.

DynamicColumn::profiles computed interior-stage vapour flows as v[j] = rest / hv[j] — dividing by an ABSOLUTE molar enthalpy. Absolute enthalpies are defined only up to the reference state, so the answer depended on where the enthalpy scale is zeroed.

Benzene/toluene at ~360 K sits on the positive side of this crate's reference and worked, which is why op-6rhz's V&V never saw it. Heavy petroleum pseudo-components at CDU temperatures sit on the NEGATIVE side: hv = -914.8 J/mol at stage 10 of the reference crude column. Two symptoms followed:

  * check_latent(hv[j]) rejected the column outright ('energy-balance denominator -914.8 J/mol is non-physical'). That check is correct for the reboiler, whose divisor hv-hl IS a latent heat, and wrong for the interior stages, whose divisor is not.
  * With the check relaxed, the sweep returned a NEGATIVE vapour flow and hence a negative distillate (-0.228 mol/s), then diverged: inventory 1.6e3 -> 4.8e3 -> 1.9e19 -> 8.2e38 within 30 steps. Larger holdups only delayed it. Measured with AND without side draws, so side draws were not implicated.

FIX: rewrite the interior-stage balance in enthalpy DIFFERENCES relative to that stage's own liquid, which is the textbook form and the one the reboiler balance already used. Subtracting h^L_j x (stage mass balance) removes the reference; the divisor becomes the latent heat h^V_j - h^L_j, positive and order thousands of J/mol whatever the reference. Added check_enthalpy_divisor (finite, |.| > 1) for the stage-1 divisor, which mixes absolute terms and legitimately can be negative; check_latent keeps its original meaning at the reboiler.

EVIDENCE IT IS RIGHT:
  * The benzene V&V test (op-6rhz, distillation_sim_v1) still passes unchanged — the fix does not move the validated case.
  * The crude plant now holds its steady seed for 200+ steps at every inventory tried (tau 30/90/300 s, vessel 50/400/2000 mol), distillate 0.3376 mol/s in all of them. Independence from the inventory is the signature of the reference term being gone; before the fix the divergence rate tracked the holdup.
  * Regression test: crude_plant::tests::the_steady_answer_does_not_depend_on_the_inventory.

Related: op-190j.5 (the steady bubble-point defects), op-190j.4 (the crude sim this blocked).

Tutor: rhoPimpleFoam stability issues (teaching doc for OutramFoam/tampines)
description: User wants a step-by-step, teacher-to-student explanation of the rhoPimpleFoam pressure-velocity stability issues discovered 2026-07-14, written as durable documentation in the OutramFoam rhoPimpleFoam solver folder (crates/outram-foam-appbuilder-lib/src/solvers/rho_pimple_foam/), and referenced from tampines docs. Should walk through, pedagogically: (1) why compressible PISO couples p and U and how the pEqn is assembled from the momentum diagonal (rAU) + laplacian + psi*V/dt compressibility term; (2) the pressure-source clobbering bug -- fvm::laplacian puts the FixedValue-pressure Dirichlet source (coeff*p_bc) into the matrix source, and overwriting it (p_eqn.source = ...) kept the diagonal but dropped the source, silently imposing p_bc=0 and blowing up any fixed-pressure outlet even from equilibrium; the fix is to ADD not overwrite; (3) the phi_hbya boundary write-back for FixedValue velocity patches; (4) stiff-liquid water-hammer: near-incompressible liquid + impulsive inlet -> Joukowsky surge rho*c*du, reflection undershoots to negative absolute pressure -> out of EOS range; why gas (large psi) is well-conditioned but liquid (tiny psi) is stiff; (5) the standard fixes -- OpenFOAM pressureControl pMin/pMax bounding (limit pressure not density for complex EOS), PISO vs SIMPLE vs PIMPLE and under-relaxation, acoustic CFL dt<dx/c, and velocity ramping; (6) BC well-posedness (fixed-velocity inlet + fixed-pressure outlet, inletOutlet for backflow). Cite the OpenFOAM pressureControl source and the rhoSimpleFoam complex-EOS commit. This is the durable pedagogical companion to bead op-21g.12.

fhr_sim_v2 steam generator: temperature cross must be impossible
description:
Maintainer, 2026-08-12: 'for the fhr_sim_v2, i want the steam generator never to have temperature cross, it is superbly annoying'.

A TEMPERATURE CROSS IS THERMODYNAMICALLY IMPOSSIBLE, so this is a physics defect and not a display nuisance. In a counter-flow exchanger the cold stream may approach the hot stream's inlet temperature but can never exceed the local hot-stream temperature — heat would have to flow up a temperature gradient. If the simulator shows steam leaving hotter than the salt heating it, the model has violated the second law and any duty it reports is meaningless.

WHERE TO LOOK: crates/outram-park-digital-twin-engine/examples/fhr_sim_v2/app/thermal_hydraulics_backend/secondary_loop/ and the steam-generator duty path. Note (recorded during the 2026-08-06 audit) that the SG duty in fhr_sim_v2 is a USER-SLIDER UA — 'user_specified_secondary_loop_ua_watt_per_kelvin' — rather than a computed exchanger. An unconstrained UA slider is the most likely mechanism: drive UA high enough and a lumped model will happily transfer more heat than the pinch allows.

LIKELY FIXES, in order of honesty:
  1. Clamp the transferred duty to the thermodynamic maximum, Q_max = C_min * (T_hot_in - T_cold_in), i.e. an effectiveness-NTU formulation where effectiveness cannot exceed 1. This makes the cross impossible BY CONSTRUCTION rather than by post-hoc correction.
  2. If a lumped mean-temperature-difference form is kept, enforce a minimum pinch and clamp UA to whatever satisfies it.
  3. Do NOT simply clamp the DISPLAYED temperature — that hides the violation while leaving the reported duty wrong.

ACCEPTANCE: a test that sweeps the UA slider (and mass flows) across its full range and asserts the second law holds at every point — steam outlet never exceeds salt inlet, salt outlet never falls below feedwater inlet, and effectiveness stays within [0, 1]. That test is the deliverable as much as the fix, because it is what stops the defect returning.

Applies to fhr_sim_v2. Check whether htgr_sim_v1's secondary loop shares the mechanism.

title: tampines TwoFluid1d: low-void starts refuse -- vapour cannot shed its expansion work without a nucleation / interfacial-area model
description:
Found and diagnosed 2026-08-12 while implementing the six-equation solver (op-62vf). Recorded as a KNOWN LIMITATION with a measured boundary, not as a mystery.

SYMPTOM. TwoFluid1d marches a two-phase blowdown (saturated 7 MPa, alpha_g = 0.1, 1 mm bubbles, 24 cells, dt = 30 us) for the full 300 ms -- 10002 steps, p falls 7.0 MPa -> 0.494 MPa, alpha_g -> 0.993, |T_g - T_l| = 5.93 K, slip 0.279 m/s. The SAME transient started at alpha_g = 1e-4 refuses after 5-11 steps.

MECHANISM (diagnosed, not guessed). Each phase energy equation carries the reversible work term alpha_k dp/dt, i.e. dh_k = dp / rho_k per unit mass of that phase. In a depressurisation this cools the vapour along very nearly an isentrope. The only thing that heats it back toward T_sat(p) is interfacial heat transfer, whose volumetric coefficient scales as 6 alpha_d lambda Nu / d^2 -- proportional to interfacial area and hence to void fraction. At small alpha_g there is almost no area, the vapour cools faster than T_sat falls, and within a few steps it is more than MAX_METASTABLE_VAPOUR_SUBCOOLING (30 K) below saturation, where PhaseState::vapour_at refuses. The mirror case is a saturated start where flashing outruns the same area and the LIQUID leaves its 30 K superheat bound.

MEASURED (2026-08-12, release, 24 cells, dt = 30 us, ramped 87% break):
  57 K subcooled, alpha_g=1e-4, d=1 mm  : 11 steps, vapour past 30 K subcooling
  57 K subcooled, alpha_g=1e-4, d=0.1 mm: 10 steps, same
  57 K subcooled, alpha_g=1e-4, d=10 um :  5 steps, same
  saturated,      alpha_g=1e-4, d=1 mm  : 10 steps, liquid past 30 K superheat
  saturated,      alpha_g=1e-4, d=10 um : 11 steps, volume residual 1.23e-3 (see the separate bead)
  saturated,      alpha_g=0.1 , d=1 mm  : 10002 steps, full 300 ms, completed

NOT FIXED BY REFINEMENT. A smaller timestep does not help: the isentropic cooling per unit PRESSURE drop is a thermodynamic fact and the pressure drop is set by the transient, not by dt.

WHAT WOULD ACTUALLY FIX IT, in rough order of honesty:
  1. A wall/bulk nucleation source and an interfacial-area-concentration transport equation, so alpha_d and d respond to the flow instead of being prescribed. This is the real answer and it is a substantial piece of work.
  2. Failing that, treating the vapour work term with an implicit coupling to the interfacial heat transfer, so the two are solved together rather than sequentially.
  3. NOT acceptable: widening MAX_METASTABLE_VAPOUR_SUBCOOLING. The property layer is refusing correctly; the state really is outside what IF97 Region 2 can be extrapolated to.

CONSEQUENCE FOR THE EDWARDS CASE (op-s1a0). Edwards-O'Brien starts 57 K SUBCOOLED, which is exactly the regime that refuses. A two-fluid Edwards case is therefore blocked on this, not merely unwritten. Whoever picks it up should read this bead first rather than tuning the initial void fraction until it runs.

RECORDED IN CODE: two_fluid_tests::six_equation_march_refuses_where_a_phase_cannot_shed_its_expansion_work pins the boundary and carries the measured table; DEFAULT_INITIAL_VOID_FRACTION documents the stand-in.

description: From the 2026-08-07 bookkeeping pass of outram-foam-appbuilder-lib. Per the workspace V&V rule (methodology AND measured results), six gaps remain open after the pass: (1) tests/foam_vv_cases/main.rs test exact_riemann_matches_sod_table_ii has NO recorded result anywhere, yet it defines the faithful-station classification the primary Sod gate consumes -- run it and record the numbers in its doc comment; (2) no test in the crate records measurement uncertainty, and four say 'this machine' without identifying it -- add rustc version + CPU to each Results block; (3) Sod DATE CONFLICT: module doc and README say measured 2026-07-06, RESULTS.md and REVIEW_MANIFEST.md say 2026-07-17 for the same case -- determine which run produced the Table II numbers and reconcile; (4) tests/sod_shock_tube_validation/README.md appendix is character-corrupted from 'Step 3' on (~230 lines, '*' substituted into prose where '*' is also the star-state notation, so automated repair is unsafe) -- restore the derivation by hand against Toro (2013); a warning banner and the fixed DOI are already in place; (5) REVIEW_MANIFEST.md's human-verify checklist is entirely unchecked three weeks on -- maintainer action; (6) verification_and_validation/README.md mandates one .md per benchmark but only Sod has one. NOTE the pass already fixed a genuine numerical error (analytical k_eff 1.000010 -> 1.000004, confirmed by hand and by test output) and transcribed real measured results into three previously number-free Results sections (k_eff = 1.000008, +0.4 pcm; drift-flux u_settle = 1.1372e-3 m/s; bubble-column slip 0.2922 m/s; 2026-08-07, rustc 1.97.0).

notes.content:
DETECTION METHOD, added 2026-08-11. Item (4), the character-corrupted Sod appendix, is caught automatically by the workspace's own mandated README check:

  pandoc -f gfm+tex_math_dollars -t html --mathml <file> > /dev/null

It reports: [WARNING] Could not convert TeX math p / \*ho^\gamma = \text{const}. That is a corrupted \rho.

A full sweep of all 118 git-tracked README.md files on 2026-08-11 with pandoc 3.6.1 produced exactly ONE warning across the whole workspace, and it was this file. Every other README, including the ten that carry LaTeX math, converts cleanly with zero warnings and exit 0. So this is the sole outstanding markdown defect in the repository, which makes it cheap to confirm fixed later — re-run the sweep and expect zero warnings.

CONFIRMING THE BEAD'S OWN WARNING against a fresh look: automated repair really is unsafe. The file contains 160 '*' characters. Legitimate ones are the star-state notation (\rho^*_L, \rho^*_R, pStar) and ordinary markdown emphasis; corrupted ones are single characters substituted at random positions. Observed substitutions include a space in 'rarefaction*relation' and 'a*Riemann', 'i' in 'rarefaction *s' and 'rat*o', 'r' in '\*ho' and '*atio', 's' in 'post-*hock', a backslash in '\sqrt{*gamma', 'n' in 'ha*dy', 'o' in '*f', 'c' in 'post-rarefa*tion', and an underscore in '\rho^**L'. The replaced characters follow no pattern, so there is no rule that separates corruption from notation. Hand restoration against Toro (2013) remains the only safe route.

Only the pandoc-visible math error is machine-detectable; the corrupted PROSE is invisible to every automated check, so a clean pandoc run after a partial fix would NOT mean the appendix is restored.

2. UNCITED CLAIM. On 2026-08-11 this was flagged in-file as an uncited recollection, NOT checked against any source. It must be either given a real citation (source, tier, URL/DOI, date accessed per DATA_POLICY.md) or removed. None of the measured numbers in the module depend on it.

Also note the near-wall profile coefficients (1.36, 5.0) in ZbsBed::wall_region_porosity carry the same unverified-coefficient caveat.

title: Simulator GUI: user-toggleable temperature display units (degC / K)
description:
Maintainer request, 2026-08-13 07:1x (filed outside active hours; no code work done).

Add a toggle in the simulator GUI to switch temperature readouts between degrees Celsius and Kelvin.

DESIGN CONSTRAINT (important -- do not get this wrong):
- This is a DISPLAY-LAYER concern only. Internal state stays uom-typed (ThermodynamicTemperature) and is never converted to a bare f64 'current display unit'. The toggle selects which uom accessor is called at render time (get::<degree_celsius>() vs get::<kelvin>()), nothing more.
- Do NOT introduce a units field into the physics/plant state, and do NOT let the display unit reach any correlation, controller, or solver input. A display toggle that leaks into the model is exactly the silent unit error the uom typing exists to prevent.
- Label every readout with its unit; the toggle changes the label as well as the number.

- htgr_sim_v1 specifically, or
- all the egui simulators in outram-park-digital-twin-engine (fhr_sim_v2, CIET, etc.)?
If it is more than one, the toggle belongs as a shared widget/state in the digital-twin engine rather than being copy-pasted per example -- check what already exists there before adding it (search-before-building rule).

Also confirm: temperature only, or a general unit-preference system (pressure bar/MPa/psi, flow kg/s vs L/min)? Scoping it as temperature-only now is fine, but the shared-widget decision above depends on the answer.

Related: op-szmi.5 (finish the htgr_sim_v1 GUI to CIET v2 standard).
