LICENCE: choo2023criticality is in open/ and committed to a public repo, but carries no redistribution grant
description:
Found 2026-08-14 when the maintainer asked whether https://inis.iaea.org/records/9cr77-d5t43 could be placed under open/. It is ALREADY there, and by this workspace's own rule it should not be.

THE DOCUMENT. Choo, A. J. Y. and Xiao, S. (2023), 'Criticality Analysis of HTR-10 Using the High-Temperature Gas-Cooled Reactor Code Package', VINANST-15, INIS-VN-006, INIS record 9cr77-d5t43.

WHAT WAS CHECKED, 2026-08-14:
- The PDF contains NO copyright, licence, rights or permission statement anywhere. Full-text grep for copyright/(c)/all rights/licen/reproduc/permission returns nothing.
- The INIS record page states 'Copyright (c) 2026 International Atomic Energy Agency. All rights reserved.' Its 'open access' marking means freely READABLE, not freely redistributable.
- The files ARE tracked in git: crates/kovan-literature/open/papers/choo-htr10-criticality.{pdf,json}, added in 89100a934a, and origin is the PUBLIC github.com/theodoreOnzGit/outram-park-backend.

WHY THIS IS THE WRONG TIER, per CLAUDE.md verbatim: 'Decide the access tier BEFORE cataloguing, from the document's own copyright page -- not from where it was downloaded. Public hosting (INIS, gen-4.org, a lab's website) grants no redistribution rights. Unsure means proprietary; that failure direction is recoverable and the other is a licence violation in a public repository.' No statement in the document means unsure, which means proprietary. INIS is named explicitly as granting nothing.

The catalogue entry ALREADY SAYS SO in its own provenance note -- 'No licence statement in the document -- cite and use; do not assume redistribution rights beyond the INIS public copy' -- and the file was filed as open regardless. The note and the placement contradict each other.

A SECOND, SEPARATE INCONSISTENCY. The same document exists twice under different tiers and different years: open/papers/choo-htr10-criticality.{json,pdf} (tracked) versus generated/markdown/proprietary/choo2024criticality.{md,json} and generated/bibtex/proprietary/choo2024criticality.bib (untracked, and under the extractor's wrong 2024 guess). Deduplicate whichever way the tier decision lands.

MAINTAINER DECISION NEEDED, NOT AN AGENT FIX. Removing a tracked PDF from a published repository does not remove it from git history, so 'just move it' is not a complete remedy and the choice of remedy is the maintainer's. Note also that the authors are the maintainer's supervisor (Xiao) and a former colleague (Choo), so PERMISSION MAY WELL EXIST -- it simply is not recorded anywhere. Asking them and recording the grant in the catalogue entry would resolve this in the open direction, legitimately.

OPTIONS: (a) obtain and record written permission from the authors, keep it open; (b) move to proprietary/ and accept that history retains the blob; (c) move to proprietary/ and purge from history, which rewrites public history; (d) keep only the metadata and citation in open/, drop the PDF.

notes.content:
MAINTAINER DECISION 2026-08-14: keep it in open/. Grounds given: Anders Choo and Sicong Xiao are the maintainer's own colleagues at SNRSI.

Recorded rather than assumed -- the catalogue entry now carries a 'Tier decision' note stating that this is a DELIBERATE EXCEPTION to the workspace default (no licence statement means proprietary), who made it, and on what grounds.

The note also records the caveat the maintainer was given and accepted: no written grant is on file, and the copyright asserted on the INIS record is the IAEA's rather than the authors'. VINANST-15 is conference proceedings, whose copyright is commonly assigned to the organiser, so a permission from the authors would not by itself settle the redistribution right. If an explicit grant is ever obtained, the note says to upgrade it naming who granted it and when.

STILL OPEN, and unrelated to the tier: the same document exists twice under two tiers and two years. Filed separately as a cleanup chore.

Tampines steam tables: explicit backward equations — Region 5 T(p,h)/T(p,s) and Region 4 near-critical (h,s) flash
description:
IAPWS-IF97 Region 5 requires explicit backward equations to compute temperature from pressure and enthalpy, and from pressure and entropy. These equations are currently missing from tampines-steam-tables. This issue also covers a related explicit near-critical Region 4 (h,s) flash, to replace the iterative pressure fallback near the critical point.

Scope:
1. Region 5 backward equations - T(p,h) and T(p,s) for high-temperature water/steam.
2. Region 4 near-critical (h,s) flash - explicit p(h,s), Tsat(p), and vapor-quality x(h,s) for 623.15 <= Tsat <= 647.04 K, replacing the iterative pressure-fallback path in that near-critical band.

Three prototypes (ChatGPT/NUS ChatGPT Edu-assisted) posted as comments on GitHub issue #34:
- Python prototype: Region 5 forward equations + T_ph_5/T_ps_5 Chebyshev fit + validate() routine
- region5_backward_explicit.rs: direct Rust transcription of the Region 5 backward fit
- region4_hs_nearcritical_explicit.rs: p_hs_4_nearcritical, tsat_p_4, x_hs_4_nearcritical

Fit domains:
- Region 5: 1e-4 <= p <= 50 MPa, 1073.15 <= T <= 2273.15 K
- Region 4 near-critical: 623.15 <= Tsat <= 647.04 K

Not an official IAPWS supplementary release - needs review, integration into the Rust crate, and independent validation against IAPWS-IF97 reference data before it can be trusted.

Follow-up work:
- Port the fitted Chebyshev coefficients / evaluation logic into crates/tampines-steam-tables as Rust
- Add unit tests validating against forward equations and published IAPWS-IF97 reference data where available
- Document methodology + results per the workspace V&V documentation rule

  450 C: mu = 3.676616e-5 Pa s
  700 C: mu = 4.531067e-5 Pa s
The hardcoded 3.5e-5 is therefore ~19 % high at the core inlet and ~23 % low at the core outlet -- it is not a defensible constant across the HTR-10 core range. (Unlike c_p, which really does vary by only 0.0034 % over the same range.)

Fix: replace the constant with tampines::gas_phase::properties::helium_viscosity, or use gas_phase::pipe::GasDuct directly, which does the friction and heat transfer with real properties.

Scope note: this bead is about the digital-twin-engine crate only; the tampines-side replacement path already exists and is tested. Related to op-wqk.9.1, which covers the broader placeholder-correlation cleanup in that example.

title: outram-mc-libs: init_seed derives streams 1 step apart, not 1 stride apart
description:
`outram_mc_libs::rng::lcg::init_seed(id, offset, master_seed)` (crates/outram-mc-libs/src/rng/lcg.rs:90) computes:

    let base = future_seed(DEFAULT_STRIDE, master_seed as u64);
    future_seed((id + offset) as u64, base)

i.e. future_seed(DEFAULT_STRIDE + id + offset, master). Consecutive ids therefore land ONE LCG step apart.

OpenMC's own init_seed (canonical source, /home/teddy0/Documents/research/openmc/src/random_lcg.cpp:60) is:

    return future_seed(static_cast<uint64_t>(id) * prn_stride, master_seed + offset);

i.e. id * STRIDE steps apart. The port drops the multiplication.

IMPACT: any caller using init_seed for per-particle / per-stream separation gets streams that are a one-draw shift of each other rather than independent — the exact opposite of the reproducible-parallel-MC guarantee the doc comment claims ('Each particle gets a unique starting seed by striding from the master seed'). Two particles' histories would be near-perfectly correlated. Needs checking against the actual transport call sites: if init_seed is used to seed particle streams, k-eff statistics may be affected.

FOUND BY: the raffles samplers port (op-vjw.2), which needs independent per-dimension streams for Latin hypercube sampling. raffles works around it by calling future_seed(stream * DEFAULT_STRIDE, master) directly with OpenMC's semantics; the workaround and the discrepancy are documented in crates/raffles/src/samplers.rs (stream_seed) and crates/raffles/CLAUDE.md.

SUGGESTED FIX: future_seed((id + offset) as u64 * DEFAULT_STRIDE, master_seed as u64), plus a regression test asserting that init_seed(k) and init_seed(k+1) are DEFAULT_STRIDE steps apart. Verify against the C++ before changing — the offset placement differs too (OpenMC adds offset to the master seed, this port adds it to the id).

notes.content:
FIX IMPLEMENTED 2026-08-06 (uncommitted, awaiting maintainer review — AI output is untrusted draft per RESPONSIBLE_USE.md).

crates/outram-mc-libs/src/rng/lcg.rs now mirrors /home/teddy0/Documents/research/openmc/src/random_lcg.cpp:60-64:

    pub fn init_seed(id: i64, offset: i64, master_seed: i64) -> u64 {
        future_seed(
            (id as u64).wrapping_mul(DEFAULT_STRIDE),
            master_seed.wrapping_add(offset) as u64,
        )
    }

Both defects in this bead are fixed: id now MULTIPLIES the stride (streams 152917 draws apart, not 1), and offset is added to the MASTER SEED (independent run, not a shift within one). Signature kept per the maintainer's instruction; the master_seed parameter is documented as a deliberate deviation from OpenMC's global.

BLAST RADIUS (measured, not assumed): init_seed had ZERO library call sites. Its only users are 5 sites in examples/triso_stochastic_gpu.rs. All library transport code (physics::keff, pebble_beds::keff_delta, physics::transport_csg, gpu::batched_*) already calls future_seed(idx * STRIDE, base) directly with correct OpenMC semantics, so no k-eff or transport statistic was ever produced through the bug.

TESTS: 4 new regression tests in rng::lcg::tests, each verified to FAIL against the old implementation:
  - init_seed_consecutive_ids_are_one_full_stride_apart
  - init_seed_matches_openmc_golden_values (5 golden seeds computed by an independent Python implementation of the upstream recurrence)
  - init_seed_streams_do_not_overlap (old impl: 4095/4095 lag-1 exact matches — stream 1 WAS stream 0 shifted one draw)
  - init_seed_offset_selects_an_independent_run
Suite: 234 -> 238 passing, 0 failed, 0 pre-existing test moved.

RECORDED RESULTS: verification_and_validation/gpu_benchmarks/triso_stochastic_cls_gpu.csv was stale (produced 2026-07-21 through the bug). Re-run 2026-08-06 on an RTX A5000; CSV regenerated and the example's V&V doc block updated with the new measured values plus an explicit supersession note. CPU f64 reference moved 0.7013826 -> 0.7014103 (+0.0000277, 0.04 sigma) — the central value was barely biased; what was invalid was the quoted binomial sigma, since neighbouring histories were not independent samples.

SIBLING DEFECT FOUND, NOT FIXED HERE: rng::lcg::prn omits OpenMC's PCG-RXS-M-XS output permutation -> filed as op-jis (P1). Larger blast radius (all recorded stats + WGSL shaders + raffles), needs its own planned change.
ALSO: 2 pre-existing doctest failures in geometry::surface unrelated to this -> op-keh (P2).

tuas: parallel-branch flow solver panics via todo!() on non-convergence (:1347)
description:
In crates/tuas_boussinesq_solver/src/lib/array_control_vol_and_fluid_component_collections/fluid_component_collection/super_collection_series_and_parallel_functions.rs, the fn calculate_pressure_change_using_guessed_branch_mass_flowrate (declared :1184) sets SimpleConvergency { eps: 1e-9, max_iter: 70 } (:1310), tries find_root_brent (:1315), falls through its Err arm with only a dbg!, tries find_root_regula_falsi (:1332), falls through that Err arm with only a dbg!, and then reaches:

    todo!("debugging: all root finding methods used not successful");   // :1347

This ABORTS THE PROCESS on ordinary non-convergence. With max_iter 70 and eps 1e-9 that is a routine runtime outcome for a hard parallel network, not a theoretical one. The crate already has a TuasLibError type in scope, so returning Err is available.

Call sites: 5 in this file (:870, :993, :1027, :1075, :1098) plus 4 on a same-named sibling in collection_series_and_parallel_functions.rs (:620, :724, :758, :806).

This is the only todo!() in the file. (The crate has ~100 crate-wide, but those are overwhelmingly in test/calibration modules, not the library dispatch path -- this one is notable precisely because it is in the hot path.)

Fix: change the signature to return Result<Pressure, TuasLibError> and propagate, or return the best-effort bracket with a diagnostic error.

description:

    cargo +nightly doc -p <pkg> --no-deps -Z unstable-options --output-format json

with NO --features and no --all-features. So any feature-gated public module is still absent from the generated crates/<crate>/docs/<crate>-api.md mirror.

Concretely, outram-blender's mirror still omits `sim` (mc-export) and `foam_mesh` (foam-mesh) — the crate's two solver bridges, i.e. its most consequential public surface. Affects every crate with opt-in bridges.

Consider whether --all-features is safe given Android-hostile optional deps (outram-foam-basic-lib's `gpu` pulls wgpu; outram-blender's `mc-export` pulls the nuclear-data chain) — the mirror is generated on a desktop so it is probably fine, but the choice should be deliberate and documented rather than incidental.

Note the parity-gate lesson from op-w44a.7 applies in reverse here: that port DID gate parity by diffing the Python-generated api.md against the Rust one, and it passed — because both were equally wrong in this respect. A byte-identical port faithfully reproduced the bug.

description:

Fortran oracle (NJOY2016 leapr.f90, commit ac5adf5f): for b7>0 the scatterer loop runs ONCE (line 398 'if (nss.eq.0.or.b7.gt.zero.or.isecs.gt.0) idone=1'), the ssm merge is skipped (3018 requires b7.le.zero), dwpix takes the normal principal /awr path (3035), and no secondary Teff table is written (3578 requires b7.le.zero). The ONLY difference from a single-scatterer deck is the MT=4 LIST head: NI=6*(nss+1)=12 (3307), NS=nss (3308), B(7)=b7, B(8)=mss*sps, B(9)=aws, B(10)=B(11)=0, B(12)=mss (3315-3321).

Scope: emit those constants in endout, thread the deck card-6 fields through generate_tape, and narrow the unsupported_features gate from 'nss!=0' to 'nss!=0 && b7<=0'.

title: root@vm
TampinesSteamArray energy convection is unlimited central differencing -- the op-1fyp defect, never filed for this array
description:
Found 2026-08-13 while scoping op-j2oq. This is the sibling-crate counterpart of op-1fyp, and it was never filed.

THE DEFECT. crates/tampines-steam-tables/src/openfoam_algorithms/rhoPimpleFoam/mod.rs:1639

    let conv_he = fvc::div(&self.phi, &self.he);   // explicit div(phi h)/V

fvc::div interpolates the convected scalar with fvc::interpolate, i.e. LINEAR (central) interpolation, unlimited.
The energy equation is advection-dominated (cell Peclet >> 1), so an advancing thermal front carries dispersive
over- and undershoots. That is verbatim the symptom op-1fyp records -- for OPCPFluidArray.

THE ASYMMETRY. The coolprop sibling was FIXED: crates/outram-park-fork-coolprop/.../rhoPimpleFoam/mod.rs:1306 now
calls fvc::div_limited with an EnergyConvectionScheme limiter enum (:276, VanLeer default / Minmod / Upwind /
Linear), and its comment cites op-1fyp. TampinesSteamArray never received the same treatment. Momentum in BOTH
files is already implicit (fvm::div_vec at :1351 and :986 respectively) -- only the energy side differs.

This is exactly the failure mode the root CLAUDE.md warns about: 'Ports often exist in pairs; a defect or a feature
in one usually has a counterpart in the other.' A fix was applied to one lineage and its twin was left behind.

DO NOT CONFUSE with the OTHER limiter in the same file. Line 2203 does use fvc::Limiter::VanLeer, but that is the
central-upwind (Kurganov-Tadmor) reconstruct_pos_neg path for rho/he/p/c -- a DIFFERENT solver path, not the PIMPLE
energy equation. So the array is limited in one path and unlimited in the other, which is worth resolving
deliberately rather than by accident.

SUGGESTED FIX: mirror the coolprop treatment -- an EnergyConvectionScheme-equivalent limiter enum and
fvc::div_limited. Whether it should also gain the implicit mode being built for OPCPFluidArray under op-j2oq is a
separate decision; the maintainer deliberately stopped an agent that was starting that work here, so do not assume it.

Consider whether op-1fyp should be widened to cover both arrays, or this kept separate and both closed together.

title: scripts/push-beads-store.sh printed a false 'beads remain local only' warning
description:
Observed once, 2026-08-11 ~15:16 SGT, on develop.

WHAT HAPPENED, exactly:
  $ ./scripts/push-beads-store.sh
  warning: could not push beads store ref to origin; beads remain local only

Immediately afterwards, by hand:
  $ git push origin refs/heads/beads/store:refs/heads/beads/store
  Everything up-to-date
  $ git rev-parse refs/heads/beads/store
  4beb401e2abc278df219140a944edc7d60eacbfe
  $ git ls-remote origin refs/heads/beads/store
  4beb401e2abc278df219140a944edc7d60eacbfe  refs/heads/beads/store
  $ git show refs/heads/beads/store:state.jsonl | grep -c op-nik1
  1

So the ref WAS published, including the bead created minutes earlier — the warning was false. No beads were actually stranded.

WHY THIS MATTERS: the whole point of the Stop-hook carve-out is that beads filed in a session are never left on one machine. A warning that cries wolf trains the reader to ignore the one time it is real.

SUSPECTED CAUSE, not confirmed: the script compares `git rev-parse` against `git ls-remote` and only pushes on a mismatch. Two plausible races, both consistent with what was seen — (a) the kopi-beans daemon was mid-flush, so local_sha moved between the rev-parse and the push; (b) a concurrent push (the Stop hook firing alongside the manual invocation) held the ref lock, so `git push` exited nonzero even though the ref reached origin. `git push` output is sent to /dev/null, so there is no evidence either way.

SUGGESTED FIX: capture the push's stderr instead of discarding it and include it in the warning, and re-check `git ls-remote` before warning — if the remote now matches the local ref, the push effectively succeeded and the warning should not fire. Do not silence the warning outright; make it accurate.

title: tampines: Edwards-O'Brien two-fluid (6-eqn) test -- blocked until op-dt3.13/op-dt3.19 deliver the solver
description:
BLOCKED on the six-equation solver existing. Placeholder test already landed: multiphase_1d::edwards_tests::two_fluid_step_still_refuses_to_pretend pins the documented contract that TwoFluid1d::step() returns NotYetImplemented, and its doc comment describes the Edwards case to write once the solver exists.

Test-ownership split (maintainer instruction, 2026-08-11): tampines-steam-tables tests own the HEM models; tampines tests own drift flux and the six-equation model.

Landed on 2026-08-11 in crates/tampines/src/multiphase_1d/edwards_tests.rs:
- edwards_drift_flux_gs1_pressure_history (ACTIVE gate, 36-39 s): full 600 ms Edwards-O'Brien blowdown on DriftFlux1d, 24 cells, dt = 30 us, Hendrie non-isothermal IC, HEM-choked break through 0.87 A with the 1 ms rupture-disc ramp. Measured: GS-1 pressure RMSE 29.0 psia vs the digitised Edwards curve over 16 points (0-0.30 s), worst +52.0 psia at t = 0.100 s, flashing plateau 354.3 psia (experimental band ~350-367), break peak 101.0 lbm/s, 99.7 % drained, no cold tail (min 372.6 K) and +0.0 psia rebound.
- edwards_drift_flux_slip_and_tau_sensitivity (#[ignore], 132 s) and edwards_drift_flux_explore (#[ignore] scratch runner).

Key finding for the future six-equation case: turning the slip closure off entirely (C0 = 1, Vgj = 0) changes GS-1 pressure by at most 1.44 psia even though peak |v_g - v_l| goes 57.6 m/s -> 0. Edwards-O'Brien GS-1 pressure is therefore a poor discriminator of MECHANICAL non-equilibrium; a six-equation Edwards case should be judged on whether THERMAL non-equilibrium (max_thermal_nonequilibrium) changes anything, not on pressure RMSE alone. Mesh refinement (48 cells) moves GS-1 more (6.89 psia) than any model parameter does.

DoD: once TwoFluid1d::step() computes, write the Edwards two-fluid case in edwards_tests.rs mirroring run_edwards(), report max_thermal_nonequilibrium alongside the GS-1 pressure comparison, and record methodology + measured results per the workspace V&V doc rule.

title: TampinesSteamArray: outlet-anchored odd-even enthalpy oscillation, ~40% of span, NOT mesh-convergent
description:
MEASURED 2026-08-12, and PRE-EXISTING (byte-identical on d9abc55616 and on the TUAS-convention branch, so not introduced by the boundary work).

SETUP. Forward-only advected thermal front, no reversal. L=4 m, A=0.02 m2, 4 MPa water seeded 400 K, inlet junction 450 K, prescribed 3.2 kg/s inlet, fixed 4 MPa outlet pressure, PIMPLE(3,2) at 0.3 under-relaxation, dt=5 ms, 12000 steps.

SYMPTOM. A single-cell enthalpy spike parks at the SECOND-TO-LAST cell (the outlet-adjacent neighbour) and does not decay. Worst overshoot above the inlet junction enthalpy, as a fraction of the 215.4 kJ/kg span between seed and inlet:
  n=8   39.20%  (profile tail ... 748.1, 750.6, 835.3, 750.5)
  n=16  41.36%
  n=32  42.33%  (tail ... 785.7, 777.3, 842.1, 777.1)
  n=64  42.61%  (tail ... 801.3, 787.1, 842.6, 786.9)

KEY POINT: it does NOT converge with mesh refinement - it SATURATES at ~42.6%. A dispersive truncation error would shrink. The spike is always at index n-2 and is a classic odd-even/checkerboard mode anchored at the fixed-pressure outlet.

DISTINCT FROM op-1fyp. op-1fyp records fvc::div(phi,he) as pure central differencing giving 10-15% over/undershoot at an advected front. That is a travelling-front effect and is mesh-convergent. This is boundary-localised, 3-4x larger, and mesh-INVARIANT, so it is a separate defect - most likely the outlet pressure/velocity BC pairing (boundary phi is never pressure-corrected, cf op-nnqi) rather than the interior scheme.

WHY IT MATTERS. For a boiling stream an enthalpy overshoot of this size can push a (p,h) flash out of range and panic. It also sets the floor on any enthalpy-boundedness assertion: the reversal V&V test flow_reversal_keeps_enthalpy_bounded_between_terminals has to carry a forward-only control arm and assert relative to it, because the scheme violates boundedness by ~39% before any reversal is involved.

REPRO: crates/tampines-steam-tables, tests::flow_reversal_keeps_enthalpy_bounded_between_terminals (forward-only control arm).

scripts/push-beads-store.sh: stale local ref reported as a push rejection, misleading callers
description:
OBSERVED 2026-09-03, and it caused two incorrect public statements before being diagnosed.

The kopi-beans daemon publishes refs/heads/beads/store on its own (CLAUDE.md records this as verified since 0.1.3, kopitiam#19). The daemon's pushes advance the REMOTE ref without advancing this clone's LOCAL refs/heads/beads/store. scripts/push-beads-store.sh then tries to push the stale local ref, git rejects it as non-fast-forward, and the script prints:

    warning: could not push beads store ref to origin; beads remain local only

That message is false in this situation. The beads are not local only — the daemon already published them. The local ref is merely behind.

Impact: during this session the warning was taken at face value and reported twice on public GitHub issues (#17, #39) as 'bead changes are local only'. Both had to be corrected after fetching the remote ref and reading state.jsonl to confirm every change was in fact published.

Suggested fix: before warning, fetch the remote ref and compare. If the local ref is a strict ANCESTOR of the remote (git rev-list --left-right --count gives 0 ahead / N behind), that is the daemon-has-already-published case — fast-forward the local ref and exit 0 silently, or say 'already published by the daemon'. Reserve the warning for a genuine fork (both ahead and behind), which is the only case a human needs to act on.

Low priority as a defect — the script is documented as a non-load-bearing fallback — but the message actively misleads, which is worse than being unhelpful.

description:
In crates/kovan-literature/open/reports/nureg-cr-2671-marviken.pdf, report p.21 / PDF p.37, Table 4:2 row 7 'Initial temperature at nozzle inlet ~ degC' returns only two digits for tests 23 and 24 ('19' and '27') where every neighbouring column is three digits (T19=167, T20=181, T21=184, T22=168, T25=189, T26=135, T27=167). Both pdftotext -layout and -raw give the same truncation, so the text layer is at fault, not the extraction command. Physically the values must be three-digit.

Impact today: none. The Marviken V&V in crates/tampines-steam-tables (bead op-21g.16) does not need row 7 — it builds the stagnation state from row 6 'Min fluid temperature in the vessel' (260 degC for test 23, 230 degC for test 24), which is readable and consistent with row 5's nominal subcooling (3 K and 33 K) and with the universal stagnation qualities of Table 8:3.

Impact later: a model that wants the discharge-pipe inlet temperature rather than the vessel bulk temperature will need row 7. Fix by re-OCRing PDF p.37 at higher resolution, or by reading the page visually and recording the two values in the KovanDocument metadata. Do not guess them.

title: kovan-literature: lit import metadata extraction is unreliable on EU/JRC report PDFs
description:
Observed 2026-08-11 ingesting EUR 28712 EN (JRC HTR safety book, 264 pages) with kovan lit import. Command run:

./target/release/kovan lit import ~/Downloads/kjna28712enn.pdf --json-out crates/kovan-literature/open/reports/vhtr-modul-safety-jrc.json --markdown-out crates/kovan-literature/generated/markdown/open/vhtr-modul-safety-jrc.md

The Markdown body extraction was GOOD — 264 pages, 5373 lines, 498k chars, content intact. The METADATA was wrong in five ways, all of which had to be hand-patched afterwards:

1. TITLE TRUNCATED AT A LINE BREAK. Got "The High Temperature"; the actual title is "The High Temperature Gas-cooled Reactor: Safety considerations of the (V)HTR-Modul". The cover sets the title across three lines and only the first was taken.
2. EDITOR MISTAKEN FOR AUTHOR. Got authors = [Scheuermann, Walter], who is the first EDITOR. The actual authors are Kugeler, K., Nabielek, H. and Buckthorpe, D., listed above the editors on the cover. There is no editor field in KovanDocument at all, which is part of the problem — consider adding one.
3. document_type = Other, though the document carries strong Report markers: an EUR number, a JRC catalogue number, an ISSN and a Publications Office imprint. A heuristic on "EUR NNNNN EN" or "JRC NNNNNN" would catch this class.
4. source_sha256 left null even though the tool has the file open. It should hash what it ingests — provenance under DATA_POLICY.md wants it, and it is free to compute.
5. slug derived from the wrong author, giving scheuermann2017the — which also shows the truncated-title bug feeding into slug generation.

Also note: doi, year, page_count and visibility were all extracted CORRECTLY, so the extractor is not broadly broken, just weak on multi-line cover layouts and author/editor blocks.

SUGGESTED FIX DIRECTION: for the title, join consecutive large-font cover lines rather than taking the first. For authors, prefer the block above an "Editors:" label when one is present. For document_type, add report-identifier heuristics. Always populate source_sha256.

Not urgent — hand-patching the JSON is quick and lit bibtex round-trips correctly afterwards. But every ingested document currently needs a manual metadata pass, which will not scale.

title: htgr_sim_v1: full HTR-10 simulator — GUI + OPC-UA server and client
description:
Bring htgr_sim_v1 up to the standard the CIET educational simulator v2 sets: a real GUI, an OPC-UA server exposing plant state, and a client that reads it.

TARGET SHAPE, from src/bin/ciet_educational_simulator_v2/: main.rs + cli.rs + headless.rs + opcua_startup.rs + a simulator subdir, backed by an OPC-UA layer.

CURRENT STATE (46482b4): htgr_sim_v1 is an EXAMPLE, not a bin — examples/htgr_sim_v1/{app/{mod,panels,schematic,state}.rs, physics/{kinetics,primary_loop,secondary_loop}.rs}. Working GUI, 12 passing tests, honest lumped physics with explicit 'what is real / what is illustrative' contracts. No OPC-UA at all.

THE ARCHITECTURAL DECISION: src/ciet_opcua/ is 4206 lines, heavily CIET-specific (109 CIET references in server.rs, 90 in node_map.rs), but its transport scaffolding is generic — OpcuaServerConfig, OpcuaEndpointInfo, OpcuaServerHandle, OpcuaServerError, spawn_opcua_server_thread, plus pki_paths.rs (333 lines) and discovery.rs (631 lines).

Extract the generic layer so CIET and HTGR each supply their own node map and state, rather than copy-pasting. Extraction is right — a second simulator is exactly when duplication becomes permanent — but it refactors WORKING, TESTED code (CIET v2 has 37 passing tests) and must not regress them.

SEPARATE DECISION, not assumed here: htgr_sim_v1 is a PRISMATIC-BLOCK HTGR today, not a pebble bed (docs/reactor-scoping/htr10.md). A true HTR-10 core is a rewrite, not a retune. The GUI/OPC-UA work is orthogonal and can proceed either way.

title: teddy0@snrsi-arch-desktop
GUI lag in BOTH simulators: 19,874 circles/frame from the shared pebble-bed artwork
description:
Maintainer reports both fhr_sim_v2 and htgr_sim_v1 feel laggy (2026-08-12). Bearable, so deferred.

RULED OUT (measured, release build): physics (TH loop <20000 us against a 100000 us budget = 20% duty; PRKE <10 us); lock contention (app/mod.rs:134 drops the guard immediately); unbounded growth (plot buffers capped at NUM_DATA_PTS_IN_PLOTS); debug build (confirmed --release).

WHY BOTH SIMS: they share crates/outram-park-digital-twin-engine/src/components/. This demotes op-szmi.9 (per-frame FHRState clone) -- htgr_sim_v1 does not do that clone and lags anyway.

QUANTIFIED LEAD: src/components/pebble_packing.rs bakes 523 pebbles in PACKED_PEBBLES. Each is drawn as one body circle plus a TRISO speckle whose count is triso_dot_count(radius), clamped to 4..=18 (htr10_reactor_vessel.rs:389). So a fully-zoomed vessel emits roughly 523 * 19 = ~10000 circles PER VESSEL PER FRAME, each tessellated to triangles by egui every repaint. Both vessel widgets use this table.

NOTE a doc/code discrepancy found while measuring: pebble_packing.rs module docs (line 124) say each pebble carries 'of order 50 dots, so the circle count is ~50x the pebble count'. The code clamps to 18. Either the doc is stale or the generator and the widget disagree -- worth resolving, since the doc is what a reader sizes the cost from.

FIRST STEP: promote GuiFrameMetrics (examples/fhr_sim_v2/app/gui_frame_metrics.rs, added 2026-08-12) into src/app_scaffold/ so both examples share it, then read the split. Small update() CPU with a long frame interval means the cost is egui tessellation/paint of those circles, and the fix is fewer shapes -- bake the static bed to a texture, or cull occluded pebbles -- NOT optimising our ui() body. Read the split before choosing.

notes.content:
DESIGN AGREED WITH MAINTAINER 2026-08-12 -- bake to a texture, tint at draw.

Key enabling fact: triso_dot_offset is deterministic by construction (htr10_reactor_vessel.rs:431 documents this explicitly -- it exists to stop the speckle shimmering between frames). The artwork is therefore STATIC across frames. Re-drawing it every repaint is pure waste, not animation.

Do NOT snapshot the finished coloured picture -- temperature changes every frame and would invalidate the cache immediately, buying nothing.

Instead: rasterise the depth-shaded bed ONCE into an egui ColorImage as luminance/alpha, upload via ctx.load_texture, and paint it as a SINGLE textured quad with the temperature colour applied as a multiply tint. Temperature then never invalidates the cache. Per-frame cost goes from ~10000 circles to 4 vertices.

Fill level composes as a CLIP RECT at draw time, not a cache key -- bake the full bed, clip to the fill line.

Cache key: physical pixel size (rect * pixels_per_point), so it re-bakes only on resize or DPI/monitor change.

Cheaper half-measure if the texture route stalls: cache a pre-tessellated egui::Mesh. Skips CPU tessellation but still uploads ~120k vertices per frame. Strictly worse; note it only as a fallback.

Known tradeoff to accept or mitigate: a texture is raster and will resample on resize where the current vector path stays crisp. Keying the bake on PHYSICAL pixels avoids this in the steady state.

Still do the measurement first (promote GuiFrameMetrics to src/app_scaffold/) so the before/after is a number, not a claim.

title: htgr_sim_v1: nodalise the pebble bed onto 15-25 tet cells
description:
Maintainer decision 2026-08-12: replace the single lumped bed control volume with a genuine unstructured TETRAHEDRAL mesh of 15-25 cells.

RATIONALE (maintainer, and it is the deciding one): this is a stepping stone to COARSE-MESH GEN-FOAM AND NODAL METHODS on this geometry. The tet cells are not chosen for rendering or for accuracy at 20 cells -- they are the data structure the FV/nodal machinery will need. Judged against 'is 20 tets an accurate bed' this looks over-engineered; judged against 'does this give GeN-Foam something to stand on' it is the right call.

This retires an earlier caveat I recorded: I flagged that KTA and ZBS have no published face-based tet formulation and would have to be derived. That is too strong for the target approach -- GeN-Foam's POROUS-MEDIUM formulation applies 1-D friction closures like KTA as per-cell momentum sink terms, which is standard practice, not an invention. Maintainer confirmed KTA and ZBS are fine to carry over.

COST IS NOT THE ISSUE: ~20 zone balances at the 10 Hz timestep is ~200 zone-updates/s on a thermal-hydraulics thread currently at 20% duty. The GUI is doing ~600000 circle tessellations/s by comparison (op-szmi.12). Tet physics is roughly 3000x cheaper than what the renderer already does, and lands on a different thread.

SEQUENCING: do this AFTER op-szmi.12 (the pebble-bed texture bake), because the bake's per-vertex tint seam is being built specifically so an axially/spatially varying bed can be painted as a handful of quads with interpolated vertex colours rather than 10000 recoloured circles. Landing the mesh first would mean painting per-zone colour through the slow path.

MUST NOT REGRESS: the honesty contracts. A resolved mesh removes the 'one control volume' caveat but NOT the others -- still no momentum equation feeding pressure drop back on flow, still no natural circulation, unless those are actually implemented. Update the contracts to what is true after the change, neither over- nor under-stating.

title: Promote the nodalised steam generator into tampines for fhr_sim_v2 reuse
description:
Maintainer intent 2026-08-12: the nodalised counter-flow steam generator being built for htgr_sim_v1 is to be reused by fhr_sim_v2.

ARCHITECTURE CONSTRAINT: it cannot live in outram-park-digital-twin-engine/src/ -- that crate's CLAUDE.md states its library is PRESENTATION ONLY, 'no new physics'. And duplicating it across two examples would guarantee drift. The correct home is most likely the tampines crate, the central TH framework that already composes tuas / coolprop / tampines-steam-tables.

It is being BUILT inside examples/htgr_sim_v1/physics/ for now, deliberately written so promotion is a file move plus an import fix rather than a rewrite: no crate:: paths back into the example, no dependency on HtgrSnapshot or app/, self-contained public API, and all geometry / UA / metal mass / fluids as constructor parameters rather than constants read from Htr10DesignPoint.

The hot side must not assume helium -- fhr_sim_v2 will pass a molten salt. Both are CoolProp-side, so OPCPFluidArray covers both; the fluid must be a parameter (enum, never a trait object).

BLOCKER TO CHECK BEFORE MOVING: tampines is a PUBLISHED crate, so this is a cross-crate decision for the maintainer, not an agent's. Confirm tampines can reach SolidColumn (currently in tuas_boussinesq_solver) without creating a dependency edge the workspace does not want -- the tampines library is deliberately TUAS-free today, with TUAS only a dev-dependency for its examples.

Composition: OPCPFluidArray (hot fluid) <-> SolidColumn (tube metal) <-> TampinesSteamArray (water/steam), joined by lateral_link_new_temperature_vector_avg_conductance. No temperature cross by construction, since lateral heat flow is evaluated at local node temperatures and simply changes sign rather than violating the second law.

title: htgr_sim_v1: temperature coefficient is 2.1x too weak — derive it from TECDOC-1382 B2
description:
The kinetics layer uses an ILLUSTRATIVE alpha_f = -4.0e-5 /K (kinetics.rs, TemperatureCoefficient::new::<per_kelvin>(-4.0e-5)). The published HTR-10 value is derivable and is roughly TWICE as strong.

DERIVATION (IAEA-TECDOC-1382 part 2, problem B2, original benchmark, VSOP; full core, helium, no rods). The document gives k_eff at three core temperatures, so rho = (k-1)/k gives the isothermal temperature coefficient directly:

  T degC     k_eff       rho (dk/k)
    20.0   1.119747    0.1069411
   120.0   1.110435    0.0994520
   250.0   1.095961    0.0875588

  20 -> 120 degC :  -7.49 pcm/K
 120 -> 250 degC :  -9.15 pcm/K
  20 -> 250 degC :  -8.43 pcm/K   <- use this as the linear value

So -8.427e-5 /K, versus the -4.0e-5 /K in the model: the model's feedback is 2.11x TOO WEAK. At beta = 0.0065 that is -0.01296 $/K published against -0.00615 $/K modelled.

NOTE THE COEFFICIENT IS NOT LINEAR -- it strengthens with temperature (-7.49 -> -9.15 pcm/K). A single linear alpha understates the feedback exactly where it matters most, at high temperature. Worth considering a two-point or piecewise form rather than one constant.

CAVEAT ON WHAT THIS IS: B2 is an ISOTHERMAL coefficient (whole core at one temperature), not a fuel-only Doppler coefficient. It bundles fuel, moderator and reflector. For a point-kinetics model whose single lumped node represents the whole core, the isothermal value is arguably the MORE appropriate one -- but the doc comment must say which it is, because calling an isothermal coefficient 'Doppler' would be wrong.

SECOND FINDING, and it matters for expectations: even with the correct coefficient, nulling the +16.45 $ cold clean excess needs a 1269 K temperature rise (against 2673 K with the illustrative value). Both are past the 1230 degC fuel limit. So fixing alpha does NOT make the model survive an instantaneous full-bank withdrawal.

The real HTR-10 safety demonstration test (control-rod withdrawal WITHOUT scram, docs/reactor-scoping/htr10.md line 144) therefore cannot be an instantaneous full-bank withdrawal -- it must be a rate-limited withdrawal of part of the bank. That is what the rod DRIVE SPEED represents, and the drive speed currently in the widget is itself illustrative and unsourced (op-qeih). Sourcing the actual test procedure and rod speed is what would let this simulator attempt that benchmark.

title: htgr_sim_v1 still feels laggy AFTER the texture bake — and it cannot measure itself
description:
Maintainer reports htgr_sim_v1 still feels laggy on 2026-08-12, AFTER the pebble-bed texture bake landed (541a38ef33). Deferred by the maintainer, not pursued that day.

WHAT IS ALREADY DONE, so this is not a duplicate of op-szmi.12:
The bake IS wired into the HTR-10 vessel -- htr10_reactor_vessel.rs:44 imports draw_bed/BedTint from components::pebble_bed_texture. Measured for that widget: 19910 shapes / 1.73 ms per frame -> 39 shapes / 0.014 ms, the bed's own share going 19874 circles -> 3 quads. So the single largest known cost is gone and the lag is something else.

THE FIRST PROBLEM IS THAT WE ARE BLIND. **htgr_sim_v1 has NO frame-time readout.** grep for GuiFrameMetrics / frame_interval / update_cpu_time in examples/htgr_sim_v1/ returns nothing. fhr_sim_v2 has had one since 2026-08-12 (four side-panel rows: update() CPU time, peak CPU, frame interval, FPS), and GuiFrameMetrics was PROMOTED to src/app_scaffold/gui_frame_metrics.rs specifically so both simulators could share it. htgr_sim_v1 was never wired to it.

DO THAT FIRST. Do not guess at a cause -- that mistake has already been made once on this exact symptom, where physics was blamed before measurement showed it was at 20% duty. The readout distinguishes:
  - small update() CPU inside a ~16.7 ms interval  -> vsync-limited, healthy, look elsewhere
  - CPU approaching the interval                   -> our ui() body is the bottleneck
  - CPU peak >> CPU mean                           -> intermittent hitching, not uniform slowness
  - long interval with small CPU                   -> cost is in egui tessellation / GPU / compositor

CANDIDATES, in rough order, NONE verified:
1. Per-frame animation now running that was not before: the turbine rotor spins from a real torque balance (00a776be12) and the schematic drives flow tracers. Both are cheap in principle; measure rather than assume.
2. The schematic composes many widgets -- vessel, steam generator, turbine, condenser, pipes, bends, legend, instrumentation. Their combined shape count has never been measured the way the vessel's was.
3. op-szmi.9's sibling defect: fhr_sim_v2 clones its whole state twice per frame. Check whether htgr_sim_v1's HtgrSnapshot clone is comparable -- it now carries ~39 fields.
4. Whether the bake is actually HITTING its cache in this simulator, or re-baking. A re-bake costs 2.4 ms and is meant to be paid once per size; if the cache key is being invalidated every frame the bake would be a net loss. This is worth checking early because it would be a defect rather than a cost.

BLOCKED ON: examples/htgr_sim_v1/ was owned by the steam-generator agent as of 2026-08-12. Wire the readout after that lands.

title: teddy0@snrsi-arch-desktop
SolidColumn steel property tables panic above 1000 K — the SG kills the sim too easily
description:
Maintainer report 2026-08-12: htgr_sim_v1 fails too easily because of the steel temperature ceiling in the new nodalised steam generator.

THE LIMIT. TUAS's SolidMaterial::SteelSS304L property tables are tabulated to 1000 K and TUAS PANICS above that rather than returning an error or clamping. The steam generator's tube metal is SteelSS304L, so any transient that drives a metal node past 1000 K kills the physics thread.

MARGIN AT DESIGN: metal sits near 765 K, so about 235 K of headroom. That sounds generous and is not, because the reachable excursions are much larger than 235 K -- a full control-rod withdrawal exposes +16.45 dollars, and with the protection system disarmed (which is currently the DEFAULT, see the RPS toggle) nothing terminates it. The agent that built the exchanger documented this as a known unguarded failure rather than fixing it.

WHY IT FEELS LIKE THE SIMULATOR IS FRAGILE: the failure presents as a hard panic and the restart modal, so an operator exploring a transient gets a dead simulator with no explanation of what they did. That is exactly the class of failure the crash-component reporting and the salt-freeze guard were built to avoid elsewhere -- a recoverable excursion out of the model's valid envelope should PAUSE and explain, not crash.

WHAT A FIX SHOULD LOOK LIKE, in rough order of value:

1. GUARD THE PROPERTY CALL, do not silently clamp. Detect a metal node approaching 1000 K BEFORE calling the property, and park the physics thread with a modal naming the component and the temperature -- the same pattern as salt_freeze_guard in fhr_sim_v2 (detect on the previous step's state, pause, explain, offer recovery). Silently clamping would be worse: it would keep running while the model is outside its data.

2. Consider whether 1000 K is the right ceiling at all. It is a PROPERTY TABLE limit, not a material limit -- 304L stainless does not cease to exist at 727 degC, it just is not tabulated there in TUAS. Extending the table, or using a material whose data covers the range, may be more honest than guarding. Check what TUAS actually carries before assuming.

3. Feed it back into the protection system. A high metal temperature is a legitimate trip signal on a real plant, and the RPS (physics/protection.rs) already has the structure -- it trips on measurable signals with a latching scram. Metal temperature is arguably measurable in a way fuel temperature is not.

NOTE THE INTERACTION WITH THE RPS DEFAULT. The protection system is currently DISARMED by default (maintainer decision, so the steam generator could be studied without a trip cutting transients short). Re-arming it would mask this failure rather than fix it, and the two decisions should be revisited together.

RELATED: the same class of defect was found in the IF97 (p,h) flash, which panics out of Region 5 rather than erroring -- that is what the GUI-timestep bug surfaced. Property libraries in this workspace panic rather than return Result at roughly 40 sites; guarding call sites one at a time is the current approach.

notes.content:
MEASUREMENT CORRECTION from the op-ffg6 audit, 2026-08-13 (read-only, counted by script, not eyeballed).

This bead states property libraries panic 'at roughly 40 sites'. For TUAS's boussinesq_thermophysical_properties/
specifically the measured figure is 99 LIBRARY-PATH PANICKING SITES -- 58 .unwrap()/.expect(, 29 panic!, 12 todo!
(excluding 62 in tests and 12 in doc examples). About 2.5x. The 40 figure may have been about tampines-steam-tables,
where op-t647 quotes the same number.

TWO FINDINGS THAT CHANGE THE FIX FRAMING ON THIS BEAD:

1. ss_304_l.rs is NOT the offender. It calls range_check(..., 250.0, 1000.0) in seven places and ALREADY RETURNS Result
   CORRECTLY -- the 1000 K ceiling is honestly reported by the property layer. The panic is introduced entirely by
   CALLERS unwrapping it. So this bead's fix item 1 ('guard the property call') is right, but the guard belongs at the
   caller, and the deeper fix is that callers stop unwrapping (op-ffg6.2).

2. THE CRASH FIX IS FREE. advance_timestep already returns Result<(), TuasLibError> in both array modules
   (one_d_solid_array/calculation.rs:21, one_d_fluid_array/calculation.rs:22), so calculation.rs:95 and its twin at
   one_d_fluid_array/calculation.rs:127 convert with ZERO API change. Tracked as op-ffg6.2.

RELATED, on this bead's IF97 remark: tuas_boussinesq_solver has NO IF97 or steam-table dependency at all (deps are
approx, csv, ndarray, peroxide, roots, thiserror, uom; grep -ri 'if97|steam' src/ returns nothing). The coupling is one
level up -- examples/htgr_sim_v1/physics/steam_generator.rs imports BOTH TUAS and the steam tables. So widening the
steel range relocates the panic ACROSS A CRATE BOUNDARY into the app's steam side, where TUAS's error type has no reach.
Making htgr_sim_v1 excursion-safe needs op-t647 to land AND the app to handle both error channels.

title: htgr_sim_v1: replace invented piping and secondary-loop geometry with sourced HTR-10 values
description:
The HTR-10 simulator's piping and secondary-loop geometry are INVENTED PLACEHOLDERS, by maintainer's decision 2026-08-12: 'for now, let's just invent placeholders'. This bead is to replace them with sourced figures later.

WHAT WE ACTUALLY HAVE, from IAEA-TECDOC-1382 (ingested at crates/kovan-literature/generated/markdown/open/iaea-tecdoc-1382-part1.md and part2, PDFs alongside in crates/kovan-literature/open/reports/):

  primary helium      3.0 MPa, 250 degC in / 700 degC out, 4.3 kg/s, 10 MWth
  main steam          440 degC at 4.0 MPa, 12.5 t/hr
  feedwater           104 degC
  steam generator     once-through modular HELICAL tube type, in a SEPARATE
                      vessel 11.3 m tall x 2.5 m ID, ~70 t, with the helium
                      circulator mounted ABOVE the SG in that same vessel
  hot gas duct        900 mm opening in the RPV wall joining the two vessels
  RPV                 4.2 m ID x 11.1 m, ~142 t

WHAT IS MISSING, and therefore invented in the simulator:

  - SG tube diameter, wall thickness, coil pitch, number of tube modules
  - hot gas duct inner/outer diameter and the coaxial arrangement
  - primary loop pipe sizes and lengths
  - the turbine/condenser side beyond the steam conditions above
  - feedwater pump and any secondary pressure drops

WHY IT IS MISSING: TECDOC-1382 is a NEUTRONICS BENCHMARK. Its detail is core
physics — criticality, control-rod worths, temperature coefficients — so it
carries almost no plant piping. This is a limitation of the source, not of the
ingestion.

WHERE TO LOOK NEXT:
  - crates/kovan-literature/generated/markdown/open/vhtr-modul-safety-jrc.md
    (JRC VHTR-MODUL safety report, also newly ingested) may carry more
    plant-side engineering than a neutronics benchmark does.
  - The Wu, Lin & Zhong HTR-10 design-features paper in Nuclear Engineering and
    Design (~2002) is the standard open source for the plant arrangement — see
    docs/reactor-scoping/htr10.md, which lists it at high confidence.
  - reference-data/virtual_test_bed/htgr/htr10/ is neutronics only and has NO
    thermal hydraulics (recorded in docs/reactor-scoping/vtb-findings.md), so
    it will not supply this.

ACCEPTANCE: every invented dimension either replaced by a sourced figure with
its citation, or explicitly marked in the module docs as illustrative and not
from any specific design. Do NOT leave an invented number looking sourced —
that is the failure mode RESPONSIBLE_USE.md exists to prevent.

title: htgr_sim_v1 kinetics: control-rod insertion control + sourced feedback coefficient
description:
Two related changes to the HTR-10 kinetics, both AFTER the rustfmt standardisation pass. Maintainer, 2026-08-12.

=== 1. CONTROL-ROD INSERTION, NOT A REACTIVITY SLIDER ===

'you shouldn't give me a slider for reactivity, but rather control rod insertion. This should be similar to fhr_sim_v2'

Today panels.rs exposes external reactivity directly, which is a DERIVED quantity no operator ever sets. An operator moves rods; reactivity is what results. An operator-facing twin should expose the real control.

Follow fhr_sim_v2, which already has control-rod insertion fractions driving its kinetics (see its side panel and prke_backend).

WHAT HTR-10 ACTUALLY HAS, from IAEA-TECDOC-1382 (ingested):
  - 10 control rods, IN THE SIDE REFLECTOR, not in the core. They drop by
    gravity for shutdown.
  - 7 small absorber ball units, also in the side reflector, as the second
    independent shutdown system.
  - Rod worth: TECDOC-1382 carries CONTROL ROD WORTH as one of its three
    benchmark cases, so a sourced worth curve is available rather than invented.

TOOL ALREADY IN THE WORKSPACE: crates/teh-o-prke/src/control_rod_feedback.rs has
obtain_rod_worth_cylinder, a Lamarsh S-curve worth
rho(x) = rho_H * [x/H - sin(2*pi*x/H)/(2*pi)]. That is the right shape — worth
accumulates fastest near mid-insertion — and is already unit-tested at half
insertion.

Note the widget library's reactor vessels already TAKE a rod insertion fraction
and draw the rods at depth, so the GUI half is largely wired: the vessel art
will show insertion once the control drives it.

=== 2. SOURCED FUEL-TEMPERATURE FEEDBACK COEFFICIENT ===

kinetics.rs:116 currently uses TemperatureCoefficient::new::<per_kelvin>(-4.0e-5),
an ILLUSTRATIVE value carried over from when this simulator was a generic
~200 MWth HTGR. Its own doc comment says so. The plant has since been rescaled to
the real HTR-10 (10 MWth, 4.3 kg/s) against TECDOC-1382, so this constant is now
the odd one out.

TECDOC-1382's three benchmark cases are initial criticality, CONTROL ROD WORTH,
and the TEMPERATURE COEFFICIENT — so the sourced coefficient is already in the
ingested document. Replace the invented value and cite it.

Watch for the sign and basis: a benchmark may quote a coefficient for fuel,
moderator or the whole core, and this model carries a SINGLE lumped fuel node.
Do not silently apply a whole-core coefficient to a fuel-only node — state which
was used and why.

=== ACCEPTANCE ===

Rod insertion drives reactivity through a worth curve; the reactivity slider is
gone from the operator panel; the feedback coefficient is sourced and cited; and
the Nordheim-Fuchs excursion remains self-limiting (negative alpha) with a test
proving a rod withdrawal produces a bounded power rise rather than a runaway.

Nordheim-Fuchs feedback itself is ALREADY PRESENT and correct — kinetics.rs
composes NordheimFuchsExactTimestepper with a five-group delayed bank under a
documented Lie split. This bead does not add it; it makes its inputs real.

notes.content:
Closed 2026-08-14 on the maintainer's report that control-rod sensitivity has been changed.

VERIFIABLE IN THE CODE: part 1 of this bead is done. The GUI commands control-rod INSERTION FRACTION, not reactivity -- HtgrSnapshot::control_rod_insertion_fraction (0.0 withdrawn to 1.0 inserted), clamped at the stops by crate::physics::control_rods, with reactivity published back as external_reactivity_dollars purely for display. Its doc comment states the design explicitly: 'reactivity is a consequence of rod position, not something commanded directly'. GUI_INITIAL_ROD_INSERTION opens near the critical position implied by the published bank worth.

NOT VERIFIED BY ME: the feedback coefficient's sourcing, which was part 2 of this bead. I have not checked what value is now used or what it is sourced from. If that half is still open, it wants its own bead rather than living on in a closed one.

htgr_sim_v1 duplicates src/htr10/ instead of using it — KTA and ZBS already exist, unwired
description:
Found 2026-08-12. The simulator says it lacks correlations the library next door already implements.

THE SITUATION:

  crates/outram-park-digital-twin-engine/src/htr10/  (arrived via the pull)
    kta.rs        kta_friction_factor, kta_pressure_gradient,
                  packed_bed_reynolds, superficial_mass_flux
                  -> REAL KTA packed-bed friction, tested against published Re
    zbs.rs        zbs_effective_conductivity + an 18-point table
                  -> REAL Zehner-Bauer-Schlunder effective bed conductivity
    design.rs     Htr10DesignPoint, Htr10FuelTemperatureLimits
    neutronics.rs

  crates/outram-park-digital-twin-engine/examples/htgr_sim_v1/physics/
    module docs state, in these words: 'no packed-bed friction correlation, no
    effective bed conductivity'. Uses instead a quadratic loss anchored to the
    published circulator head, and an INVENTED overall pebble-to-helium HTC of
    160 W/m2K. Re-derives HTR-10 design constants that design.rs already holds.

NOTHING IN THE WORKSPACE USES src/htr10/ — a grep for 'htr10::' finds only doc
mentions in src/htgr_opcua/. It is declared in lib.rs and otherwise inert.

CAUSE, recorded so it is not repeated: when briefing the pebble-bed work I only
inspected examples/htgr_sim_v1/ and never checked src/. I then explicitly told
the agent to DROP KTA and ZBS as over-scoped. Both already existed. The agent
followed the brief correctly; the brief was wrong.

WHAT TO DO:

  1. Wire physics/primary_loop.rs to htr10::kta for the bed pressure drop,
     replacing the anchored quadratic. The KTA path can be verified against the
     gold pressure drop recorded in docs/reactor-scoping/vtb-findings.md
     section 5 — a real gate, not a plausibility check.
  2. Wire the bed thermal resistance to htr10::zbs instead of the invented HTC,
     or state clearly why a lumped HTC is still preferred at this fidelity.
  3. Replace duplicated design constants with htr10::design::Htr10DesignPoint
     so there is ONE source of truth for the operating point. Two copies WILL
     drift.
  4. Update the 'what is real / what is illustrative' contracts afterwards —
     they will then be understating what the model does, which is the opposite
     error but still wrong.

CAUTION: keep the honest contracts accurate at every step. Wiring KTA makes the

title: Graceful degradation when the private literature submodule is missing/uninitialized/inaccessible
description: Part of op-72hy. Direct requirement from the comment: 'When a private submodule is unavailable, uninitialized, or inaccessible, papers must remain visible in Wiki/Mindmap and their Markdown/BibTeX knowledge must remain usable; KOVAN should simply report that the source PDF is unavailable locally.' Wiki/Mindmap paper listing, classification, bibliography, and any code path that currently assumes a PrivateSubmodule-mode paper's PDF is present on disk (op-q1qj's PDF-reader active-paper wiring is the most likely place this bites) must degrade to 'source PDF unavailable locally' rather than erroring or hiding the paper. Depends on op-dlv8/op-xq8t existing first (nothing to degrade gracefully from until the submodule mode itself exists).

notes.content: Investigation found Wiki/Mindmap paper visibility and Markdown/BibTeX usability were ALREADY unconditionally independent of PDF presence -- KnowledgeIndex/KnowledgeGraph build entirely from kovan.toml + Markdown (confirmed by grep across wiki.rs/mindmap.rs turning up zero PDF-existence-gated logic), and DigitiseApp::activate_paper already had a pre-existing '.filter(|path| path.is_file())' graceful-degradation path (op-sr4n) explicitly built for exactly this class of problem ('a clone of the repo without the submodule/proprietary content pulled' per its own comment) -- that mechanism transparently covers an unready private submodule with zero submodule-specific code needed, since root.restricted_sources_dir() is just an empty/uninitialised directory in that case. The one real, concrete gap: activation reported a generic 'opened {citekey}' status regardless of whether the PDF was found, never actually telling the user the PDF was unavailable. Fixed: ActivePaper gained a pdf_unavailable: bool field (true only when kovan.toml records a source PDF that wasn't found locally -- distinct from a metadata-only paper that never had one), activate_paper_and_navigate's status message now says 'source PDF unavailable locally', with an additional private_submodule_hint() suffix naming 'private literature submodule not checked out' specifically when that's the configured-but-unready cause (silent otherwise, so an ordinary moved/deleted PDF doesn't imply a submodule problem that doesn't exist). 6 new tests: pdf_unavailable flagging (both directions), the status message text, the submodule-specific hint (present/absent as appropriate), and an end-to-end 'PrivateSubmodule-mode paper with an unready submodule still indexes and activates cleanly' test. Verified: cargo check -p kovan --all-targets --all-features clean; cargo test -p kovan --lib --release: 375 passed (was 370), 0 failed.

description: root@vm
title: root@vm
njoy LEAPR: no SiC coherent-elastic -- stock LEAPR cannot generate it, so the TRISO SiC layer has no usable S(alpha,beta)
description:
FOUND 2026-08-14 while doing op-6tz.35.1 (TRISO shell S(alpha,beta) wiring). Confirmed from the decks themselves, not inferred.

SYMPTOM. Regenerating tsl-CinSiC (MAT 44) and tsl-SiinSiC (MAT 43) from their embedded decks via leapr::generate::generate_tape with ElasticChannel::Generate yields laws with elastic_xs identically 0.0. Measured at 0.0253 eV, barn per principal atom:
  C in graphite : elastic 4.55555 + inelastic 0.48162 = 5.03717   (free-gas C0 4.9382 -> bound 5.0372, +2.01%)
  C in SiC      : elastic 0.00000 + inelastic 0.13291 = 0.13291   (free-gas C0 4.9382 -> bound 0.1329, -97.31%)
  Si in SiC     : elastic 0.00000 + inelastic 0.06367 = 0.06367   (free-gas Si28 1.9914 -> bound 0.0637, -96.80%)

A bound crystalline solid scattering 97% LESS than the free gas it replaces is not physical. It is exactly the failure mode op-nhoa named for graphite -- an inelastic-only law missing its dominant elastic channel -- so a caller who wired this in would give the SiC layer ~2.7% of its true thermal scattering and get a plausible wrong k, not a crash.

ROOT CAUSE, from the deck files in crates/njoy-outram-park-fork/src/leapr/decks/:
  1. Card 4 (awr spr npr iel ncold): tsl-crystalline-graphite has iel=1 (NJOY built-in graphite lattice); tsl-CinSiC and tsl-SiinSiC have iel=0, i.e. NO built-in lattice, so stock LEAPR emits no coherent-elastic section.
  2. Both SiC decks' own comment cards state that 'modifications to the LEAPR source code were made to calculate the coherent elastic', citing Y. Zhu and A. Hawari, 'Implementation of a Generalized Coherent Elastic Scattering Formulation for Thermal Neutron Scattering'.

So this is NOT a defect in this workspace's LEAPR port. The port faithfully reproduces stock NJOY LEAPR, which carries built-in lattices only for graphite / Be / BeO and cannot produce a general crystal structure factor. It is a capability gap.

OPTIONS, in rough order of cost:
  (a) Obtain the official ENDF/B-VIII.0 tsl-CinSiC / tsl-SiinSiC TAPES rather than regenerating from decks. The tapes carry the evaluator's coherent-elastic MF=7/MT=2 already, so ThermalScattering::from_endf_file would pick it up with no new physics. Cheapest by far. Note this reintroduces an external-data dependency the embedded decks removed, so it likely wants the acquire/cache path (op-6tz.28) rather than a hardcoded path.
  (b) Implement the generalized coherent-elastic formulation (Zhu and Hawari) in the LEAPR port -- a general structure factor from lattice parameters instead of the three hardcoded lattices. Correct and reusable for every non-built-in crystalline scatterer, but real work and needs its own V&V.
  (c) Leave the SiC layer free-gas and DOCUMENT it as a known modelling limitation. Currently the honest default, and what the code says today.

DO NOT substitute the graphite law for the SiC layer. Carbon bound in silicon carbide is a different lattice from carbon bound in graphite; the two laws are measurably different (97.36% apart at 0.0253 eV, though that figure is inflated by this very gap).

CURRENT STATE IN TREE. tests/triso_shell_thermal_scattering.rs asserts this gap deliberately -- sic_carbon_elastic_channel_is_missing_from_the_embedded_deck and sic_silicon_elastic_channel_is_missing_from_the_embedded_deck assert elastic == 0.0, so if the capability lands they FAIL and force the docs and this bead to be updated rather than letting inelastic-only data stay silently in use. geometry/triso_particle.rs's module doc records the limitation where a reader meets it.

Blocks a physically correct TRISO shell-resolved thermal transport case (op-6tz.35).

notes.content:
2026-08-17: option (a) is now available and MEASURED. The maintainer committed the official ENDF/B-VIII.0 tsl-CinSiC tape (MAT 44, 7.2 MB, commit ffef0fb76f); it now lives at reference-data/endf/tsl-CinSiC.endf after op-mixd moved tapes out of crates/.

The tape carries MF=7/MT=2 LTHR=1: 685 Bragg edges over 8 temperatures. Read through the existing SabSource::EndfTape path (no new physics needed), measured at 0.0253 eV / 296 K, barn per principal atom:

  C in SiC, regenerated from deck : elastic 0.00000 + inelastic 0.13291 = 0.13291  (free-gas C0 4.9382 -> -97.3%)
  C in SiC, from the committed tape: elastic 2.94078 + inelastic 0.13880 = 3.07957  (free-gas C0 4.9382 -> -37.6%)
  C in graphite, for scale         : elastic 4.55142 + inelastic 0.48634 = 5.03776
  Bragg cutoff, C in SiC: 1.066463e-3 eV (graphite: 1.822327e-3 eV)

So the tape gives 23x the total thermal cross section the deck path gives, and the -37.6% bound-vs-free figure is physically plausible where -97.3% was not.

NOT YET DONE, so this bead stays open:
  - The two GAP tests in outram-mc-libs/tests/triso_shell_thermal_scattering.rs still assert elastic == 0.0. They are designed to fail when the gap closes; they have not been flipped, because nothing yet routes the SiC layer at the tape.
  - tsl-SiinSiC.endf (MAT 43) was NOT committed -- only CinSiC plus three graphite grades. The silicon half of the SiC layer is still inelastic-only. Maintainer says they will upload it.
  - geometry/triso_particle.rs module doc still records the limitation.

MAINTAINER DIRECTION 2026-08-17: option (b) -- implement the Zhu and Hawari generalized coherent-elastic formulation in coher.rs -- was chosen over wiring the tape alone, so the capability is wanted regardless. Prerequisite: neither Zhu 2014 (MS thesis, NCSU) nor Zhu and Hawari 2015 (ICNC) is in crates/kovan-literature; per the workspace literature HARD RULE they must be catalogued before their formulation is used. The committed tsl-CinSiC MT=2 (685 edges, 8 temperatures) is then a real published oracle to validate the implementation against, and reproducing the six built-in NJOY lattices through the general path is a second free gate.
notes.author: root@vm

notes.content:
2026-08-17 (2): the silicon half is now supplied too (op-84v6). Both SiC tapes live in reference-data/endf/. Measured at 0.0253 eV / 296 K, barn per principal atom:

  C in SiC  (MAT 44): elastic 2.94078 + inelastic 0.13880 = 3.07957  (free-gas C 4.9382 -> -37.6%)
  Si in SiC (MAT 43): elastic 2.94078 + inelastic 0.06615 = 3.00693  (free-gas Si-28 1.9914 -> +51.0%)

CRITICAL for wiring: those two elastic figures are identical because MAT 43 and MAT 44 carry byte-identical MF=7/MT=2 sections (1044 records each; only the header ZA/AWR differs). Coherent elastic is a lattice property of 3C-SiC, not a per-sublattice one. So summing the elastic channels of both materials double-counts Bragg scattering -- MT=2 must be attributed to the compound once. This is a real trap: it would give a plausible wrong k rather than a crash, the same failure mode this bead was opened about.

Also: the evaluator's tsl-SiinSiC.readme (shipped with the tape, now in reference-data/endf/) states in its own words that the coherent elastic 'was generated using an in-house routine [1]', citing Zhu and Hawari, ICNC 2015. That is independent corroboration of this bead's root-cause analysis, from the evaluation itself rather than inferred from card 4's iel=0.

Still open, unchanged: the two GAP tests in outram-mc-libs/tests/triso_shell_thermal_scattering.rs still assert elastic == 0.0 (they test the DECK path, which remains correctly elastic-free); nothing yet routes the SiC layer at the tapes; and the maintainer's chosen path is option (b), implementing the Zhu-Hawari generalized formulation, for which the two papers are still not in kovan-literature.
notes.author: root@vm

notes.content:
2026-08-21 -- the "Si in SiC inelastic is 3.7% short" figure recorded in this
bead is RETRACTED as an artefact. It was a temperature mismatch, not physics.

The deck was regenerated at 293.6 K (outram-mc-libs' TEMPERATURE_K) and
compared against a tape read at 296 K, which NJOY's T/1000+5 = 5.296 K match
tolerance snaps to the tape's 300 K block. Two different temperatures.

Measured like-for-like (commit 1a904fc5), sigma at 0.0253 eV, b/atom:
  deck @ 293.6 K : inelastic 0.063673
  deck @ 300   K : inelastic 0.066150
  tape @ 300   K : inelastic 0.066150   <- 0.0000% difference
The whole -3.74% was the 6.4 K gap.

Stronger statement, now committed as
tests/leapr_temperature_block_selection.rs::
si_in_sic_kernel_reproduces_the_published_evaluation_at_every_temperature:
regenerating S(alpha,beta) from tsl-SiinSiC.leapr reproduces
reference-data/endf/tsl-SiinSiC.endf at ALL 8 declared temperatures --
306,033 tabulated points, worst deviation 0.0000% (ENDF's 6-digit write
precision), T_eff exact at every temperature. The Si-in-SiC INELASTIC kernel
is validated against the published evaluation.

What remains open in this bead is only the ELASTIC side: deck-regenerated
coherent elastic is 2.85169 b at 300 K against the tape's 2.94078 b, -3.03%.
That is the residual from the generalized coherent-elastic implementation
(op-jw4a) and is tracked in op-4daf, not here.
notes.author: root@vm

notes.content:
CLOSING 2026-08-21. The capability gap this bead names is closed.

The symptom was elastic_xs identically 0.0 for both SiC materials, i.e. a
bound crystalline solid scattering 97% LESS than the free gas it replaces.
Option (b) -- implement the Zhu & Hawari generalized coherent-elastic
formulation -- was the maintainer's choice (2026-08-17) and is implemented
(op-jw4a, commit 8933cdbf).

Measured now, 0.0253 eV / 300 K, b per principal atom, like-for-like against
reference-data/endf/tsl-SiinSiC.endf:
  elastic    2.85169  vs tape 2.94078   (-3.03%)   -- was 0.00000
  inelastic  0.066150 vs tape 0.066150  (+0.0000%)

and the earlier "-3.7% inelastic" figure in this bead is retracted as a
temperature artefact (see the previous comment).

Both "do not work around it" warnings this bead raised still stand and are
recorded where a reader meets them (outram-mc-libs/src/geometry/
triso_particle.rs module doc): do not substitute the graphite law for SiC, and
do not sum both SiC materials' elastic channels for one region -- they carry
the identical compound structure factor by design, so summing double-counts
Bragg scattering. The second is pinned by a test.

REMAINING, tracked in op-4daf (not lost by this close): the -3.03% elastic
residual, the edge-by-edge MT=2 comparison, and rewriting the two #[ignore]d
gap tests in outram-mc-libs/tests/triso_shell_thermal_scattering.rs to real
tolerance-based assertions.

Note for op-6tz.35, which this blocked: the SiC layer is now modellable, but
with a stated ~3% elastic bias. Whether that is good enough for a shell-
resolved TRISO transport case is a judgement call for whoever picks it up --
it is no longer a 97% error, and it is no longer zero.

title: tuas: Sieder-Tate Reynolds validity bounds inverted (accepts only 4000-10000, rejects Re > 1e4 where it is valid)
description: Found 2026-08-11 by correlation audit during op-4542. crates/tuas_boussinesq_solver/src/lib/heat_transfer_correlations/nusselt_number_correlations/pipe_correlations.rs:246-248 panics on Re > 10000, and the doc at ~L183-187 states 4000 < Re_D < 10000. Sieder & Tate (1936) is a turbulent correlation valid for Re > 1e4 -- 10000 is the LOWER bound, not the upper. Combined with the Re < 4000 panic below it, the function accepts only 4000-10000, a window almost entirely outside the correlation's validity, and refuses every Reynolds number where it is actually valid. The algebra itself (0.027 Re^0.8 Pr^(1/3) (mu_b/mu_w)^0.14) is correct.

title: htgr_sim_v1: the feedwater controller is feedforward, and the coupled plant limit-cycles
description:
MEASURED 2026-08-12 in crates/outram-park-digital-twin-engine/examples/htgr_sim_v1.

Once the steam generator became a resolved exchanger with a real 38 s tube-metal time constant, the secondary's feedwater controller started producing a slow limit cycle: the steam outlet swings roughly 698-718 K with a period near 100 s at the 10 MWth design point, and the loop is still visibly moving at 300 s. The published 440 degC sits inside the swing (settled 441.25 degC at 300 s).

CAUSE: secondary_loop::step's controller is FEEDFORWARD, not feedback. It sets the target flow from the duty being offered, target_flow = Q/(h_target - h_feed), and first-order-lags the actual flow toward it with a 10 s constant. There is no error term on the steam temperature at all. Feedforward against a plant with a 38 s lag oscillates.

This was invisible before 2026-08-12 because the secondary had no thermal inertia to oscillate against: the steam-generator outlet was the algebraic h_feed + Q/mdot, so the controller acted on a plant with no lag.

FIX: replace the feedforward law with real feedback on steam temperature (or enthalpy) -- the workspace already has chem-eng-real-time-process-control-simulator with PID and transfer-function blocks, which is the obvious thing to reach for and is already a dependency of outram-park-digital-twin-engine.

NOT a blocker: the plant settles inside a few K of the published steam condition and the oscillation is bounded. Recorded so it is not mistaken for exchanger noise.

htgr_sim_v1 opens SLIGHTLY SUPERCRITICAL: rod insertion 0.6035 vs critical 0.604535 (+28.3 pcm)
description:
Surfaced 2026-08-13 by a new test comparing the literal against critical_insertion_fraction. PRE-EXISTING, not introduced by the secondary-controls work. Documented on the constant and deliberately NOT changed.

GUI_INITIAL_ROD_INSERTION = 0.6035. A bisection puts critical at 0.604535. So the simulator's opening state commands
+0.0435 dollars = +28.3 pcm of excess reactivity -- the plant is very slightly supercritical the moment it opens,
rather than sitting at the critical insertion the constant's name implies.

Far below prompt critical, so it is not a stability problem; it means the opening state drifts up slowly instead of
holding, and anyone reading the constant reasonably assumes it is the critical value.

WHY IT WAS LEFT ALONE, and why this is a maintainer decision rather than an obvious fix: every V&V number recorded
against the opening state was measured AT 0.6035. Changing it to 0.604535 moves the whole-plant smoke test, the
20 s timing test, the 150 s run, the corrector sweep and the command-envelope corners. That is a coordinated
re-measurement, not a one-character edit.

TWO WAYS TO RESOLVE, pick one:
  (a) Set the constant to the computed critical insertion and re-measure every V&V figure that references the
      opening state, updating each doc comment with the new number and date.
  (b) Keep 0.6035 and RENAME it so it stops implying criticality (e.g. GUI_INITIAL_ROD_INSERTION_SLIGHTLY_SUPERCRITICAL),
      documenting the +28.3 pcm as deliberate -- a plant opening with a little excess reactivity is a defensible
      teaching state.
Either is fine; the current situation -- a name that claims critical and a value that is not -- is the part worth
fixing.

Related: op-szmi.7 (control-rod insertion control + sourced feedback coefficient), op-szmi.15 (temperature
coefficient 2.1x too weak).

title: root@vm
njoy THERMR: no consumer surface for the thermal ELASTIC channels — thermr::scattering exposes incoherent-inelastic only
description:
VERIFIED 2026-08-11 by code inspection + a live parse of ENDF/B-VIII.0 graphite.

STATE: src/thermr/scattering.rs is the documented 'hand-off' surface that outram-mc-libs consumes, but it exposes exactly one type, IncoherentInelasticScattering, covering MF=7/MT=4 only. The two ELASTIC channels are implemented as bare impl blocks on the raw parser structs:
  - CoherentElastic::cross_section / ::bragg_reflections  (src/thermr/coherent.rs:29,53)
  - IncoherentElastic::cross_section / ::equiprobable_cosines / ::debye_waller  (src/thermr/incoherent_elastic.rs:36,64,83)
Neither has a uom-typed, temperature-selecting, pre-tabulated consumer struct analogous to IncoherentInelasticScattering, and grep shows the ONLY in-tree consumer of either is src/acer/thermal.rs (the ACE writer). No transport crate can reach them through the documented surface.

WHY IT MATTERS (HTR-10 critical path): graphite (tsl-crystalline-graphite MAT=30, tsl-reactor-graphite-10P MAT=31, -30P MAT=32) is coherent-elastic + incoherent-inelastic, with NO incoherent-elastic (verified: parse_mf7 reports coherent_elastic=true, incoherent_elastic=false, incoherent_inelastic=true for all three). Coherent elastic is ~90% of graphite thermal scattering at 0.0253 eV. So the one channel that dominates the HTR-10 moderator is the one with no consumer surface.

WORK: add a CoherentElasticScattering consumer struct in thermr::scattering mirroring IncoherentInelasticScattering — from_endf_file(path, mat, temperature), uom-typed cross_section(E), and a sample-a-Bragg-reflection method returning (E_out = E_in, mu) from bragg_reflections' (mu, weight) pairs. Do the same for IncoherentElastic (needed later for ZrH, not for graphite). Depends on op-1y4y for correct temperature behaviour.

SIZE: small. The physics is already implemented and tested; this is a typed wrapper + temperature selection.

notes.content: DONE 2026-08-11 (this session; unverified-by-human, not committed yet). thermr::scattering now exposes all three channels: CoherentElasticScattering (from_endf_file/from_tape at a uom Temperature; uom cross_section(E) per principal atom; bragg_cutoff() = first edge with nonzero S, 1.8223 meV for graphite; bragg_reflections(E) normalised-probability (mu,p) list, zero-weight grid points filtered; sample(E, xi)->(E_out=E_in, mu) with caller-owned RNG) and IncoherentElasticScattering (cross_section(E), equiprobable_cosines(E,nbin); constructor refuses temps outside the W'(T) table range) alongside IncoherentInelasticScattering. All re-exported from thermr. Temperature resolution at construction per the shared mf7 policy (tolerance/interpolate/refuse). Consumer-surface consistency V&V in tests/thermal_graphite_coherent.rs passes (surface == mf7-level to machine precision; probabilities sum to 1; sampling elastic). Downstream MC wiring (op-nhoa/op-hc2o) untouched per scope.
notes.author: teddy0@arch-aftershock-rapid-glass-S267454

notes.content:
One addition to this surface, 2026-08-11 (uncommitted), made while implementing op-nhoa: CoherentElasticScattering::bragg_edge_table() -> Vec<(NeutronEnergy, CrossSection)>, one uom-typed pair per tabulated Bragg edge (221 for ENDF/B-VIII.0 crystalline graphite), where sigma_i = S(E_i,T)/(E_i*natom) is the value cross_section() takes throughout [E_i, E_{i+1}).

WHY IT WAS NEEDED: sigma_coh_el(E) is a 1/E sawtooth with a discontinuity at every edge. A consumer that pre-tabulates it on its own log grid - which outram-mc must do, to keep the transport hot loop cheap - smears all 221 edges. Exposing the step table lets the consumer cache the channel EXACTLY instead: measured worst relative deviation of outram-mc's cached copy vs this surface is 7.67e-16 over 21199 points from 1e-4 to 4 eV, and the whole table is ~3.5 kB, cheaper than the resample it replaces. Everything else (the cumulative structure factor S_i/natom = sigma_i*E_i, and each edge's sampling weight as its increment) is recoverable from the pairs exactly.

It mirrors the CoherentElasticXS::bragg_edges() / ::factors() pair that OpenMC's CoherentElasticAE::sample consumes (src/secondary_thermal.cpp:34-54), so it is a port move rather than an invention. No behaviour change to any existing method. njoy full suite green after it (393 lib tests + all integration, scripts/test.sh, release). Not closing - human review still owed on this bead's original work too.
