title: kovan-cli: rename + code-actions commands (rust-analyzer-backed) -- fills the gap the harness's read-only LSP tool leaves
description:
The workspace CLAUDE.md's own 'Workflow rules' section already names this gap: the harness's built-in rust-analyzer LSP tool is READ-ONLY (goToDefinition/findReferences/hover/documentSymbol/workspaceSymbol/call hierarchy) and explicitly does NOT expose rename/code-action/applyEdit -- an agent using only that tool has no way to drive an actual refactor, and CLAUDE.md currently tells an agent to reach for 'kopitiam rename'/'kopitiam code-actions' to fill it (with the caveat that kopitiam rename is itself broken upstream right now -- kopitiam#30, 'Client does not support rename capability').

kopitiam-semantic's RustAnalyzerSession (already a kovan-cli dependency as of op-l3uz's def/sig/refs work) already has the session-level methods needed: rename(file, line, character, new_name) -> Vec<FileEdit>, code_actions(file, line, character) -> Vec<CodeAction>, apply_code_action(action) -> Vec<FileEdit>. kopitiam's own apps/cli/src/rename.rs and code_actions.rs are the reference CLI wiring (diff-preview by default, --apply to write, per this workspace's own kopitiam-rename-preference note in CLAUDE.md).

PROPOSED SHAPE (not yet built):
- kovan-cli rename <symbol> --file <file> --new-name <name> [--apply] -- name-based like def/sig/refs (resolve via document_symbols, same as op-l3uz), diff preview unless --apply.
- kovan-cli code-actions <file> <line> <character> [--apply <index>] -- list available code actions at a position, apply one by index with --apply.
- WATCH: kopitiam's own rename is currently broken upstream (kopitiam#30 -- rust-analyzer rejects the rename request with LSP error -32803, 'Client does not support rename capability', because kopitiam-semantic's initialize handshake doesn't declare the textDocument.rename client capability). Since kovan-cli would depend on the SAME kopitiam-semantic crate and its LspClient, this exact bug is very likely inherited unchanged -- verify against a live session BEFORE claiming this feature works, don't assume it's fine just because it's a different CLI wrapping the same library. If it reproduces here, this bead is blocked on that upstream fix landing (kopitiam#30), not implementable as a workaround from this workspace (kopitiam is consume-binaries/libraries-only, never patched here).
- Depends on the keep-warm daemon design (sibling bead) being at least considered together, since rename/code-actions are exactly the kind of interactive, multi-step workflow (list actions, then apply one) where a cold rust-analyzer restart per step would be worst.

notes.content: VERIFIED 2026-08-22 (before this bead's speculative caveat was written, corrected here): tested kopitiam_semantic::RustAnalyzerSession::rename directly (a throwaway example, computed-only -- rename() never writes to disk per its own doc comment, confirmed via git status showing zero changes) against this workspace's rust-analyzer. It WORKS -- 2 file edits computed successfully, no LSP -32803 capability error. kopitiam#30's 'Client does not support rename capability' bug is therefore specific to the kopitiam CLI BINARY's own session/capability setup (apps/cli's layer), NOT to kopitiam-semantic::RustAnalyzerSession itself, which kovan-cli would call directly. Correction to this bead's original description: do NOT assume kovan-cli rename is blocked on kopitiam#30 -- it is not, verified. The 'WATCH' paragraph in this bead's original description is superseded by this note.

basic-lib: add traction (sigma.n=0) BC on D and anisotropic (tensor-coeff) laplacian for thermo-mechanics
description: Follow-ups surfaced by genfoam thermoMechanics mesh solve (op-p6p.11). (1) fvm::laplacian_vec only takes a scalar coefficient (2mu+lambda); an anisotropic stiffness needs a tensor-coefficient laplacian operator. (2) The field boundary layer offers only Dirichlet (FixedValue) and zero-gradient on D; a traction boundary condition (sigma.n = given, e.g. stress-free surface under thermal load where dD/dn != 0) is not expressible, so the stress-free free-thermal-expansion case can only be reached via a non-uniform temperature with Dirichlet ends. (3) fvc::grad_vec sets a zero-gradient output boundary, so the compact-normal-stress divSigmaExp correction carries no boundary-gradient info (exact on 1-D columns, approximate near 2-D/3-D boundaries). (4) No non-orthogonal gradient correction. See src/genfoam/thermo_mechanics/mesh_solve.rs limitations note.

title: GeN-Foam build blocked in container: ESI OpenFOAM v2506 unreachable
description:
GeN-Foam (gitlab.com/foam-for-nuclear/GeN-Foam, cloned OK to /opt/foam/GeN-Foam) declares in its README that it is built on the OpenFOAM ESI/OpenCFD distribution, currently v2506 (openfoam.com) — NOT the OpenFOAM Foundation 'dev' distribution (openfoam.org) that this repo vendors at crates/outram-foam-turbulence-lib/upstream_source/OpenFOAM. The two distributions are API-incompatible for a solver as deeply integrated as GeN-Foam.

Blocker: the remote-execution container's network policy denies both dl.openfoam.com and develop.openfoam.com (agent proxy returns 403 to CONNECT). github.com and gitlab.com ARE reachable. There is no official ESI mirror on those hosts, and pulling an unofficial third-party mirror was deliberately NOT done — provenance/licence review is required per RESEARCH_INTEGRITY_AND_PROVENANCE.md, so an unverified mirror is not acceptable for this project.

Consequence: GeN-Foam cannot be compiled or run in this container. This is an environment constraint, not a code defect.

What WAS delivered instead (commit ce4bd82): the OUTRAM PARK equivalent V&V case for GeN-Foam's Tutorials/guidedCases/1_reactorSlab_1D_1Gr_neutronicDiffusion, built from that tutorial's nuclearData verbatim (D=0.1275, sigmaRemoval=5.0082, nuSigmaEff=5.5675, P0 scatter 0.1, IV, 6-group beta/lambda) on a 151-cell 1.5 m slab. It verifies against the closed-form one-group bare-slab solution: k_eff = 1.000008 vs analytical 1.000004 (0.4 pcm), and reproduces the k_inf = 1.111677 quoted in the upstream README — confirming the in-group-scattering convention matches.

To unblock: either (a) allowlist dl.openfoam.com / develop.openfoam.com for this environment, or (b) build on a machine with ESI OpenFOAM v2506 already installed, or (c) run the GeN-Foam tutorial elsewhere and commit its reference output as a stored benchmark for regression comparison.

tampines-steam-tables: promote the golden-section search out of the crate; 4 copies, one of which evaluates twice per iteration
description:
Found while implementing op-yvj.4.3 (batched golden section in
outram-foam-basic-lib). RECOMMENDATION ONLY -- no edit was made to
tampines-steam-tables, because its callers sit on the gated Marviken V&V path
and changing them is a maintainer decision.

## Finding 1 -- there are FOUR copies of the same golden-section loop in one crate

All in crates/tampines-steam-tables/src/steam_turbine_equations/
converging_diverging_nozzles/choked_flow/:

  1. stagnation_point_outside_vle_ph_dome_multiphase.rs:67
     fn golden_section_max_g(...)  -- the factored-out one
  2. stagnation_point_outside_vle_ph_dome_multiphase.rs:~160
     the same loop written out inline inside
     get_critical_pressure_and_mass_flux_subcooled_liquid_ph, NOT calling (1)
  3. stagnation_point_within_vle_ph_dome_multiphase.rs:~67
     the same loop again, inline
  4. mod.rs:~426, inside dome_crossing_interior_choke, the same loop again

They already differ in incidental detail while being the same algorithm. This is
the drift risk the CLAUDE.md "Search the workspace before building anything"
rule describes, inside a single crate.

## Finding 2 -- all four evaluate the objective TWICE per iteration

Golden section's whole point is that the contraction constant makes one probe of
the new bracket coincide with a probe of the old one, so each iteration after the
first costs ONE objective evaluation. All four copies recompute both c and d and
evaluate both. The doc comment in copy (3) actually claims the property --
"costing one G-evaluation per iteration" -- while the code below it does two.

Cost: roughly 2x the objective evaluations. The objective here is
h_ps_eqm/v_ps_eqm, i.e. an IF97 flash, so this is not free. ~40 iterations per
solve means ~40 wasted flashes per choke point.

## Finding 3 -- a fifth implementation family exists elsewhere in the workspace

Brent parabolic-interpolation minimisers (golden-section fallback):
  crates/outram-park-fork-dwsim-libs/src/petroleum/fitting.rs:104
    pub fn brent_minimize(...)  -- independent impl from Brent (1973) ch.5
  crates/outram-park-fork-dwsim-libs/src/columns/shortcut.rs:~1006
    fn brent_minimize(...)  -- faithful port of DWSIM BrentMinimize.vb:176-295

## Proposed resolution

crates/outram-foam-basic-lib/src/math/minimise.rs now exists (op-yvj.4.3):
golden_section_batch(), Sense::{Minimise,Maximise}, abs+rel bracket tolerance,
per-lane status, backend dispatch, probe reuse (one evaluation per iteration).
It is the natural canonical home -- outram-foam-basic-lib sits BELOW both
tampines-steam-tables and dwsim-libs, so the dependency can only flow this way.

Suggested steps, maintainer to decide:
  a) point the four steam-tables call sites at
     outram_foam_basic_lib::math::minimise::golden_section_batch with
     Sense::Maximise and MinSettings { x_tol_abs: 1.0, x_tol_rel: 0.0, .. }
     (the existing 1 Pa rule expressed exactly);
  b) re-run the gated Marviken + Zaloudek tests and record the deltas.

Expected behaviour change, stated up front so it is not a surprise: probe reuse
is not bit-identical to recompute-both, so choke pressures will move in the last
bits. The steam-tables stopping rule is a 1 Pa bracket, ~13 orders above that,
so no gate should move -- but this MUST be demonstrated by running the gated
tests, not assumed.

Also worth deciding separately: whether a batched Brent minimiser should live in
outram-foam-basic-lib and the two dwsim-libs copies become callers. Deliberately
NOT written during op-yvj.4.3 rather than adding a third Brent.

notes.content:
2026-08-13 (agent, bead op-uyi3 work session).

FINDING 1 VERIFIED. Four copies confirmed at the cited locations, all evaluating the objective twice per iteration.

DEPENDENCY DECISION: NOT ADDED. outram-foam-basic-lib was NOT added as a dependency of tampines-steam-tables. Reasons, in order of weight:
 (a) tampines-steam-tables already VENDORS outram-foam-basic-lib. src/openfoam_algorithms/openfoam_source/ is 23489 lines of it, and src/openfoam_algorithms/CLAUDE.md states the vendoring is deliberate: 'The outram-foam-basic-lib primitives ... are already committed to tampines-steam-tables as Rust source ... do not attempt to fetch, copy, or reorganise them.' Adding a live dependency would put the same crate in the build twice, with FV primitives coming from the vendored copy and the minimiser from the live one. That is worse duplication than the one being fixed, and reversing the vendoring is a maintainer architecture decision.
 (b) The crate CLAUDE.md states its dependencies are exactly approx/ndarray/thiserror/uom.
 (c) Android-buildability was NOT the blocker. outram-foam-basic-lib default features pull only thiserror+uom+ndarray, all already present; rayon/wgpu are off by default and wgpu is target-gated off Android. On that axis alone the dependency would have been acceptable.

WHAT WAS DONE INSTEAD (strictly local, no dependency-graph change): the three inline copies now call the existing golden_section_max_g (visibility fn -> pub(crate); verified NOT in the public rustdoc, so no crates.io API change), and golden_section_max_g was rewritten to reuse the retained probe.

MEASURED (2026-08-13, release, all numbers printed by code that was run):
 - objective evaluations on the regression bracket: 69 -> 37 (1.86x).
 - probe reuse vs the retired recompute-both form, 158 real IF97 searches over all three bracket shapes: worst |dp_crit| = 5.990479e-1 Pa (stopping rule is 1 Pa), worst relative 4.604111e-8, worst |dG|/G = 3.429708e-13.
 - Marviken: 6 passed, output BYTE-IDENTICAL. Test 23 mean|dev| 12.6%/max 23.1%; test 24 mean|dev| 48.6%/max 70.2%, still NOT validated, unchanged.
 - Moody: 13 passed, output BYTE-IDENTICAL.
 - Zaloudek: 88 passed / 1 ignored. 14 lines of 6993 moved, all in p_crit_calc only (G_calc identical in all 14); largest move 3 Pa on 10356.041 kPa = 2.9e-7 relative, against Zaloudek's 0.005 relative tolerance.
 - cargo test --release -p tampines-steam-tables --lib: 959 passed, 0 failed, 13 ignored (was 955/0/13; +4 new tests in tests/golden_section_shared_search.rs).
 - cargo check --workspace --lib --release: clean.

IMPORTANT CORRECTION to the error analysis in outram-foam-basic-lib/src/math/minimise.rs: that module reasons the probe-reuse deviation stays ~1e-16 relative. Measured here, the located ABSCISSA can move by up to about the stopping-bracket width (0.6 Pa in the oracle sweep, 3 Pa observed in the Zaloudek suite), because a last-bit probe difference can flip a comparison on a near-flat objective or change which iteration first trips the stopping test. The conclusion (no gate moves) holds; the stated magnitude does not. Worth reflecting in minimise.rs, which this session was not permitted to edit.

STILL OPEN, MAINTAINER DECISION: whether to promote the search to outram-foam-basic-lib at all. That is now entangled with the separate, larger question of whether tampines-steam-tables should keep vendoring outram-foam-basic-lib or depend on it. Also unresolved: the two Brent minimisers in outram-park-fork-dwsim-libs (Finding 3) were not touched.

htgr_sim_v1: physics thread cannot reach real time -- fixed sleep after compute, not a deadline
description:
The htgr_sim_v1 physics thread in examples/htgr_sim_v1/app/mod.rs advances 10 substeps of PHYSICS_DT_S = 1 ms (10 ms simulated) and then calls thread::sleep(PHYSICS_TICK) with PHYSICS_TICK = 10 ms UNCONDITIONALLY, after the work.

Wall period is therefore compute + 10 ms for 10 ms of simulated time. Real-time ratio = 10/(10+compute_ms). Any nonzero compute makes the sim slower than real time; 1:1 is structurally unreachable, not a tuning question.

Two comments in the file assert the opposite and are wrong:
  - line 42: 'Physics substeps advanced per wall tick (a mild real-time speed-up).'
  - line 159: 'The physics thread runs ~1:1 with wall time (10 substeps of 1 ms per 10 ms tick)'
The tracer animation on line 161-162 is clocked off GUI frame time on the strength of that claim, so tracers run faster than the plant they depict.

Fix: deadline pacing -- record Instant at tick start, sleep PHYSICS_TICK.saturating_sub(elapsed). Also decide and document what should happen when compute exceeds the tick budget (drop to slower-than-real-time and say so in the GUI, vs. reduce SUBSTEPS_PER_TICK).

Why it started mattering today: before edbb2bd7 the steam generator was an algebraic eps-NTU sink and compute was negligible, so the defect was invisible. That commit replaced it with three coupled arrays (OPCPFluidArray + SolidColumn + TampinesSteamArray, 8 nodes, implicit solve, IF97 flashes) on a 0.0125 s substep clock. NOT YET MEASURED: the actual per-tick compute cost, and hence how far off real time it is. Measure before choosing the fix -- the existing test physics::tests::the_whole_plant_steps_at_the_gui_timestep does 20 s of simulated time at 1 ms and its wall clock is a direct read on this.

notes.content: Cross-link: op-szmi.16 tracks htgr_sim_v1 GUI frame-time lag and is a DIFFERENT symptom -- rendering speed, not sim-clock rate. Do not merge them. That bead records physics previously measured 'at 20% duty', which if it means 2.5 ms compute against the 10 ms sleep already implies a 0.8x real-time ratio; recover the original figure when op-775s runs.
notes.author: teddy0@arch-aftershock-rapid-glass-S267454

notes.content:
DEADLINE PACING LANDED 2026-08-13, following the fhr_sim_v2 pattern per maintainer instruction.

Implementation: new shared crates/outram-park-digital-twin-engine/src/app_scaffold/real_time_pacing.rs. Cumulative
plant-clock-vs-wall-clock comparison; ahead -> sleep out the tick budget; behind -> 5 us token sleep and press on.
The cumulative comparison is the valuable part: a stall is WORKED OFF rather than lost. One deliberate deviation from
fhr_sim_v2: the original does not sleep at all on the behind branch, which spins the physics thread against the GUI.

Also fixed here: the two false comments at app/mod.rs:42 and :159, and the tracer animation, which was clocked off GUI
frame time on the strength of the false 1:1 claim and so ran FASTER than the plant it depicts. Tracers now advance on
the delta of snapshot.sim_time_s, which is exact and self-correcting.

Over-budget policy, decided and documented: fall behind, work it off, and SAY SO. Skipping sim time would fabricate
state; growing dt would change the integration. Since panels.rs was reserved for op-qpgw, the readout went on the
schematic -- a 'real-time 0.41x' instrument plus an amber 'SLOWER THAN REAL TIME -- plant clock N.N s behind' line.

Pacer tests (5 new, passing): overrun 25 ms against a 10 ms budget -> 0 ms sleep + 15 ms overrun, where the OLD formula
slept 14 ms; boundary sweep 7-13 ms gave sleeps 3,2,1,0,0,0,0 and overruns 0,0,0,0,1,2,3 with no wrap; a 500 ms stall
cleared in exactly 62 catch-up ticks then resumed sleeping 8 ms.

RESULT: ratio 0.29-0.32 -> 0.41-0.48. DOES NOT REACH 1:1 and cannot -- see op-775s (closed) for the measurement and the
new global-0.1s-timestep bead for the actual route. Not closing this until someone confirms on a display.
notes.author: teddy0@arch-aftershock-rapid-glass-S267454

notes.content:
MAINTAINER CONFIRMED ON SCREEN, 2026-08-13: 'it's still slower than real-time, i see the schematic and it works.'

So the INSTRUMENTATION is verified by a human: the real-time ratio readout and the amber 'SLOWER THAN REAL TIME' line
render and report correctly. That was the last thing the headless agent could not check.

DELIBERATELY LEFT OPEN. The defect this bead names -- a fixed sleep after the compute instead of a deadline -- IS
fixed (ratio 0.29-0.32 -> 0.41-0.48). But the bead's title claims the physics thread cannot reach real time, and that
is still TRUE: 1:1 is unreachable at dt = 1 ms because the physics costs 2.09-2.45 ms per 1 ms of plant time (op-775s).
Closing it now would read, to anyone scanning closed beads, as though real time had been achieved.

Close this when op-6eqe (global 0.1 s timestep with outer correctors) lands and the measured ratio actually reaches
1:1 -- or reframe the title to name the fixed-sleep defect alone and close it then.

description: teddy0@arch-aftershock-rapid-glass-S267454
title: teddy0@arch-aftershock-rapid-glass-S267454
tampines TwoFluid1d: outer-corrector Newton fails to converge the volume constraint at small bubble diameter -- UNDIAGNOSED
description:
Found 2026-08-12 (op-62vf). Recorded as UNRESOLVED rather than guessed at.

SYMPTOM. With a saturated 7 MPa start, alpha_g = 1e-4 and a 10 um bubble diameter, the ramped blowdown survives 11 steps and then fails with:

  TAMPINES numerical failure: volume constraint alpha_g + alpha_l = 1 is violated by
  0.0012295274121916222 after 20 outer correctors at t = 0.00036 s, above the 1e-4 limit

i.e. the outer-corrector Newton iteration on the volume residual stops converging. The same configuration at 1 mm bubbles fails differently (the metastable-bound refusal, separate bead), and the 10 um run is otherwise BETTER behaved -- the phase-temperature difference falls from 49.8 K to 5.74 K, which is the interfacial closures working as intended.

WHAT IS KNOWN.
- The Newton system is the correct quasi-Jacobian: M = -(V/dt) dR/dp, assembled from the compliance C_i = sum_k alpha_k psi_k / rho_k on the diagonal and the pressure-corrected face fluxes off it. It is strictly diagonally dominant.
- The compressibilities psi_k are taken along the isentropic path (dh_k = dp/rho_k), which is the path the step actually takes; using the fixed-enthalpy derivative instead was measured to stall the correctors and was fixed on 2026-08-12.
- Under-relaxation is 0.7 and 20 correctors were allowed.

LEADING HYPOTHESIS, NOT VERIFIED. The residual R(p) is not smooth in p once the mass-transfer rate limiter (MAX_MASS_TRANSFER_FRACTION_PER_STEP) and the residual-alpha phase floor (PHASE_FLOOR_TRIGGER) switch on and off between correctors. Newton on a piecewise residual does not converge. The failing run showed those branches firing on most cells (lim = 22-24, floor = 30 of 24 cells over both stages). If that is right, the fix is to make the branch decisions once per STEP rather than once per corrector, or to smooth the limiter.

DO NOT paper over this by raising MAX_VOLUME_RESIDUAL. The refusal is correct: a step whose phases do not fill the cell to better than 1e-4 has not converged, and returning it would give a density field wrong by the residual.

NEXT STEP: instrument the corrector loop to print R and max|dp| per corrector for the failing step, and check whether the limiter/floor branch set changes between correctors.

title: kovan-gui: PDF reader continuous-scroll mode (view all pages in one flow)
description: GitHub issue #30 comment 2026-08-25: 'To scroll thru the pdfs in continuous mode' -- an Okular-style continuous page-flow view instead of one-page-at-a-time. Pages stack vertically, scrollable as one document; per-page full-res textures rasterized lazily (only pages intersecting the viewport), page size for layout purposes derived cheaply from the existing thumbnail-DPI cache (avoids adding a new page-size-only API call). Toggleable against the existing single-page mode; draw-box/select-text/annotation interactions stay single-page-mode-only for this pass (documented scope cut) -- continuous mode is a reading view.

notes.content:
Implemented. crates/kovan/src/digitiser/gui/desktop/pdf_reader.rs:
- New "Continuous scroll" toggle (default ON per the explicit ask), checkbox in the toolbar.
- `continuous_pages_ui`: all pages stacked vertically in one scrollable canvas. Layout size per page comes cheaply from the already-cached thumbnail texture (op-0y4k) scaled from THUMBNAIL_DPI up to RENDER_DPI, avoiding a full rasterization just to learn dimensions. Actual full-res textures (`full_res_texture`, cached in a new `page_textures` map) are only rasterized for pages intersecting the viewport -- off-screen pages get a placeholder rect, so opening a long document stays cheap.
- Existing saved annotations are shown read-only as an overlay in continuous mode.
- `page_index` auto-tracks whichever page has the most viewport overlap each frame, so the toolbar's "page N/M" readout and single-page mode (if toggled back) stay in sync with scroll position.
- Thumbnail-strip clicks now work correctly in continuous mode too: a new `scroll_to_page` field, consumed via egui's `scroll_to_rect`, jumps the continuous view to the clicked page (previously would have just been silently overwritten by the per-frame visible-page tracking).

Deliberate scope cut, documented in the code: continuous mode is VIEW-ONLY -- draw-box/select-text/annotation *creation* tools stay single-page-mode-only. Re-deriving "which page, and where on it" a click/drag landed across a whole scrolling flow is materially more work than the single-page coordinate math the tools already use, and the ask here was about reading, not digitising.

title: kovan-literature: BibTeX parser (read .bib -> KovanDocument-ish entries), needed for kovan.toml's bib-key document join
description: Follow-up from op-b1y5. The 'kovan folder' project format design (docs/kovan-folder-format.md, op-63u0) specifies kovan.toml's document.id as the .bib entry's cite key, joining bib/PDF/markdown by that key. op-b1y5's v1 implementation (crates/kovan/src/project.rs) cannot do this join today because this workspace has no BibTeX PARSER anywhere -- kovan_literature::bibtex::to_bibtex only renders a KovanDocument INTO BibTeX (one-way), there is no read path for an arbitrary user-authored .bib file. v1 instead joins pdf/<stem>.pdf <-> markdown/<stem>.md by shared filename stem, which works but does not match the design doc's spec and cannot associate a document with its actual bib entry. Natural home: kovan-literature (alongside bibtex.rs). Scope: parse a .bib file into a list of (cite_key, fields) entries -- does not need to produce a full KovanDocument, just enough to drive project.rs's regenerate() to join on cite key instead of filename stem.

notes.content:
Implemented. Natural home confirmed and used: `kovan-literature/src/bibtex.rs` (alongside `to_bibtex`).

What shipped:
- `kovan_literature::parse_bib_entries(&str) -> Result<Vec<BibEntry>, BibParseError>` -- a hand-rolled, offline, brace-balanced parser (no new dependency; consistent with this workspace's offline-deterministic style). Handles `@type{key, field = {value}, ...}` and `field = "value"`/bare (`year = 2020`) forms, nested braces inside a `{...}` value, trailing commas, and `%`-commented/blank text between entries. `@string`/`@preamble`/`@comment` blocks are brace-balanced past and dropped (not citable entries).
- `BibEntry { entry_type, cite_key, fields: BTreeMap<String, String> }` -- deliberately shallow, per this bead's own scope note: no attempt to reconstruct a `KovanDocument`, just enough for an exact-match cite-key join. Field values keep their TeX escapes as written (not unescaped) -- documented as a known limitation in the module doc.
- Both re-exported at the `kovan-literature` crate root.

Consumer wired in the same pass (closes the gap `op-b1y5`'s v1 flagged): `crates/kovan/src/project.rs`'s `regenerate()` now parses the project's `.bib` file and joins by cite key (design doc's actual spec) instead of by filename stem alone -- a document exists only when a `.bib` entry's cite key has both a matching `pdf/<key>.pdf` and `markdown/<key>.md` on disk. Added `ProjectError::Bib` for a malformed `.bib` file. Updated the module doc's "known v1 scoping limitation" note to reflect this is now closed, and fixed 3 existing tests whose fixture `.bib` cite keys didn't match their pdf/markdown stems (previously harmless since the join ignored the bib file's content entirely).

Verified:
- `kovan-literature`: 18 bibtex tests (13 new), 52 lib tests total, all passing.
- `kovan`: 4 new project.rs tests (mainline join, stem-with-no-cite-key skip, cite-key-with-no-files skip, malformed .bib error) + all 12 pre-existing project tests (3 fixture-updated), 181 lib tests total, all passing.
- `cargo check --all-targets` clean on both crates, native and `--target aarch64-linux-android`.
- `cargo doc --no-deps`: no new warnings on either crate.
- Regenerated both crates' `docs/<crate>-api.md` mirrors via `kovan-cli api-docs`.

Not implemented (correctly out of scope for this bead, tracked separately): the actual JabRef-like bibliography *editor* UI (op-9vml's other half) -- this bead only unblocks it by providing the read path. op-9vml itself is left as-is; a comment there notes the unblock.

Not committed/pushed yet per this workspace's never-auto-commit rule.

title: root@vm
kovan: DECISION -- projective/parallelogram axis calibration for off-centre plots
description: Issue #30 comment 2026-08-22 03:06 UTC floats a parallelogram (not just axis-aligned box) calibration for plots photographed/scanned off-axis. crates/kovan/src/digitiser/calibration.rs's PlotCalibration is strictly axis-aligned today (AxisCalibration per axis, pixel = column for x / row for y; see module doc + tests) -- there is no 2D projective or affine-from-4-points transform anywhere in the digitiser. Adding one is a DigitisedDataset schema change (DATASET_SCHEMA_VERSION bump in dataset.rs), since PlotCalibration is serialized to the on-disk JSON. Needs a maintainer call before implementation: is this in scope now, and if so does the new calibration variant coexist with the axis-aligned one (enum-dispatched, per the workspace's no-trait-objects rule) or replace it. Blocks nothing else in the op-9c2e tree; the axis-aligned persistent-box UX (sibling bead) ships independently.

notes.content:
RECOMMENDATION, not a decision -- flagging this as a genuine blocker for the maintainer rather than deciding unilaterally, per the criteria that make it different from op-6ez3/op-9bvi (which I did decide): this one (a) changes a persisted on-disk schema (DATASET_SCHEMA_VERSION bump, PlotCalibration becomes an enum with a new variant) affecting every previously-exported dataset's re-readability, and (b) blocks nothing else in the op-9c2e tree today -- the axis-aligned persistent draggable box (op-zfnh, shipped) already solves the bulk of the practical complaint (no more one-click-per-corner), and per the bead's own description a parallelogram variant would coexist with, not replace, axis-aligned calibration.

My recommendation, for whenever the maintainer wants to pick this up: enum-dispatch per the workspace's no-trait-objects rule --

  pub enum PlotCalibration {
      AxisAligned(AxisCalibration, AxisCalibration),  // today's shape, renamed as a variant
      Parallelogram { corners: [PixelPoint; 4], data_corners: [(f64, f64); 4] },
  }

with point_at() matching on the variant (axis-aligned: today's per-axis linear/log interpolation, unchanged; parallelogram: a bilinear or full 2D projective (homography) map from the pixel quadrilateral to the data-space quadrilateral -- projective is the more correct choice if the plot was genuinely photographed at an angle with perspective foreshortening, bilinear is simpler and adequate for a merely-skewed-but-not-perspective scan). DATASET_SCHEMA_VERSION -> 2, with read_json handling both old (implicit AxisAligned) and new records for backward read compatibility -- write path always emits the new shape.

Not implemented. Left open pending maintainer input on: (1) is this worth the schema churn given op-zfnh already shipped, (2) bilinear vs full projective, (3) whether AxisAligned stays the default/only option for existing UX and Parallelogram is opt-in via a toggle, or whether the draggable box should just always be a freely-skewable quadrilateral (simpler UI, but changes existing muscle memory for the common axis-aligned case).
notes.author: root@vm

notes.content:
Implemented. Per explicit maintainer instruction: "parallelogram mode and rectangle mode should be selectable enums. so that we don't break old code" -- exactly the enum-dispatched shape recommended in the earlier comment, now built.

crates/kovan/src/digitiser/calibration.rs:
- `PlotCalibration` is now an enum: `AxisAligned { x, y }` (the original shape, unchanged behaviour) and `Parallelogram(ParallelogramCalibration)` (new).
- **Backward compatibility via `#[serde(untagged)]`**: `AxisAligned` serialises to byte-identical `{"x": ..., "y": ...}` JSON -- every dataset already on disk under `DATASET_SCHEMA_VERSION` 1 still deserialises unchanged, no migration, no version bump needed (verified: `read_json`'s schema_version check is a top-level dataset field untouched by this change). Test: `old_flat_json_still_deserialises_as_axis_aligned`.
- `ParallelogramCalibration`: 4 pixel-space corners mapped to the unit square via a 2D projective transform (homography, solved via an 8x8 Gauss-Jordan linear system -- the standard "photographed rectangle" perspective-correction map), then the *same* per-axis linear/log interpolation `AxisCalibration` already implements and tests. Validated constructor (`new`) rejects degenerate corners, non-finite/coincident values, and non-positive log-axis references, mirroring `AxisCalibration::new`'s own rules. 12 new calibration tests: round-trip, corner-to-reference-value mapping, log-axis correctness, degenerate-input rejection, and a sanity check that a parallelogram over an actual rectangle reproduces `AxisAligned`'s numbers exactly.
- `xy_uncertainty_interval` (dataset.rs) generalises the existing per-axis `uncertainty_interval` to the enum: `AxisAligned` delegates unchanged (byte-identical behaviour); `Parallelogram` perturbs column/row and reads the value spread off `point_at` (documented simplification, same "treat x/y as independent" spirit the original already has).

GUI (crates/kovan/src/digitiser/gui/desktop/mod.rs): a real, working "selectable" surface, not just internal plumbing --
- New "Calibration shape" toggle (Rectangle | Parallelogram) in the side panel.
- Rectangle mode: completely unchanged (same 4 lines, same corner-drag from the earlier round).
- Parallelogram mode: 4 freely-draggable corners (no rectilinear constraint), drawn as a skewed quad outline with the same corner-handle styling: drag any corner independently to skew the box to match an off-angle photo.
- Same 4 data-value text fields reused in both modes (X1/X2/Y1/Y2 -- left/right/bottom/top).
- Auto-trace correctly rejects Parallelogram mode with a clear message (the automatic column/row scan is inherently axis-aligned -- same boundary as the CLI/TUI automatic pipeline in `auto.rs`, now documented there too) and points the operator at hand-placing points instead.

Downstream call sites fixed to keep AxisAligned behaviour byte-identical: `auto.rs` (CLI/TUI automatic pipeline, stays AxisAligned-only by design), `synthetic.rs` (test-fixture generator, AxisAligned-only), `tui/digitiser.rs` (hand-placed point nudging, now calibration-shape-agnostic via the new PlotCalibration-level `pixel_at`/`xy_uncertainty_interval` methods), `dataset.rs` (CSV provenance header now branches on variant to describe either shape).

Verified: `cargo check --all-targets` clean (native + aarch64-linux-android). `cargo test --release`: 201 kovan lib tests passing (10 new calibration tests, all digitiser_synthetic integration tests still green, confirming the real end-to-end JSON pipeline is unaffected for AxisAligned data). `cargo doc --no-deps`: no new warnings. GUI binary rebuilt and smoke-tested under xvfb-run (same known no-GPU sandbox limitation as every other round this session). Regenerating the API doc mirror now. Not committed yet.

kovan agent-docs-gen: bundle Outram Park API docs for an external 200k-context agent
description:
Maintainer request 2026-08-14. The maintainer chats with Opus through NUS AI Know (200k context) and wants to hand it the Outram Park API markdown so it can advise on how to code in, scaffold and structure solutions for this workspace.

THE BINDING CONSTRAINTS, measured 2026-08-14:
- The upload dialog takes MULTIPLE FILES but NOT FOLDERS. Output must therefore be FLAT -- one file per crate, no subdirectories.
- Budget is 200k tokens. The 13 existing crates/<crate>/docs/api.md mirrors total 5,154,447 bytes ~= 1.29 M tokens by the chars/4 estimate -- 6.5x over. outram-park-fork-offbeat alone is 928,045 bytes ~= 232k, over budget BY ITSELF. So flatten-and-copy is not a design that can work.
- Only 13 of 37 crates have an api.md at all. Missing include tampines, tuas_boussinesq_solver, teh-o-prke, njoy-outram-park-fork, chem-eng-real-time-process-control-simulator, outram-park-digital-twin-engine, bedok -- i.e. most of what a plant-modelling question would need.

MAINTAINER DECISIONS (asked and answered 2026-08-14):
1. Budget strategy: BOTH -- a condensed signature index covering ALL crates (always emitted, one file) PLUS verbatim api.md for the crates named on the command line.
2. Missing api.md: REGENERATE them first, via scripts/gen_api_docs.py.
3. Layout: ONE FLAT FILE PER CRATE.

NOTE ON DECISION 2 AND KOVAN'S CHARTER. Regenerating shells out to python3 + nightly rustdoc + rustdoc-md: not offline, not deterministic, and it would add ~2.4 MB to an already over-budget corpus. That was put to the maintainer and chosen anyway. It is reconciled by making regeneration an EXPLICIT OPT-IN FLAG that is off by default, exactly as 'kovan setup' already handles its online cargo-install path ('never run automatically, and has no bearing on the rest of kovan's offline/Android-clean operation'). The default invocation stays deterministic and offline.

PLACEMENT: logic in kovan-semantics as a new agent_docs module (repository-understanding artifact, sibling to outputs::repository_summary_markdown); kovan-cli stays a thin clap wrapper, per the workspace 'ports as modules, not new crates' rule.

OUTPUT: /agent-docs/ at the workspace root, regenerable and gitignored.

title: agent-docs: crate inventory + token estimator
description:
Walk crates/*/, read each Cargo.toml package name, record whether docs/api.md, README.md and CLAUDE.md exist and their byte sizes.

TOKEN ESTIMATOR. KOVAN has no tokenizer and must not gain one (offline/deterministic, no ML). Estimate as ceil(chars/4) and DOCUMENT IT AS AN ESTIMATE everywhere it is printed -- never call it a token count. Print bytes alongside so the maintainer can sanity-check. The chars/4 ratio is a convention for English+code, and technical markdown with heavy punctuation and identifiers runs denser, so the estimate is optimistic; treat the budget as soft and say so in the output.
teddy0@snrsi-arch-desktop
title: teddy0@snrsi-arch-desktop
agent-docs: condensed signature index over ALL crates
description:
The always-emitted _INDEX.md giving the external agent a map of the whole workspace.

Deterministic markdown transform of each docs/api.md: keep the module/item headings and the fenced 'pub ...' signature lines plus each item's FIRST doc line; drop prose bodies, examples, status tables. rustdoc-md emits flat headings (a submodule gets the same heading level as its parent -- recorded in scripts/gen_api_docs.py's own docstring), so the module tree CANNOT be reconstructed from heading depth. Do not try; carry the module path from the '# Module `x`' headings instead.

MUST be reproducible byte-for-byte from the same inputs -- no timestamps, no HashMap iteration order, no absolute paths in the output.

notes.content:
DESIGN CHANGED DURING BUILD, on measurement. The approved design was ONE _INDEX.md holding a condensed signature index of every crate. Built and measured 2026-08-14 on the real workspace, that file came to 535,580 bytes = ~134k estimated tokens -- 67% of the 200k budget spent before a single crate's real documentation was uploaded. Composition was evenly spread (headings 25%, signatures 44%, descriptions 29%), so no single trim rescued it.

Split into a three-tier ladder instead, all flat, nothing lost: _INDEX.md is now a ~3.4 KB roster of all 37 crates; <crate>.index.md (~7-105 KB each) carries the condensed index for one crate; <crate>.api.md is the full rustdoc. Uploading every .index.md reproduces the old single file exactly, so the content is identical -- it just became optional. A crate whose full api.md is in the core set gets no .index.md, since that would pay twice for one crate out of one budget.

agent-docs: hardcoded AGENTS.md generator (the workspace rules for a remote agent)
description:
The instruction file uploaded alongside the API docs, telling the external agent how to write code for this workspace. Hardcoded in Rust (a const/template), not read from the workspace CLAUDE.md -- the root CLAUDE.md is ~600 lines of Claude Code harness policy (beads, hooks, working hours, push rules) that is noise to a chat agent and would eat the budget.

MUST CARRY (the rules that change the CODE it writes):
- Rust design rules: NO trait objects (Box<dyn>/&dyn/Arc<dyn>) -- enums for dispatch; NO Box<T>; NO lifetime parameters -- own by value or Arc<T>; Arc<RwLock<T>> for shared mutable state, Arc<T> for read-only, RwLock over Mutex, no channels for simulation state.
- uom typing throughout, with named type aliases rather than raw Quantity<...>.
- Human interface layer: every public item documented, what physical quantity, valid ranges, units spelled out even when uom-typed.
- V&V documentation: any test checking physics against a reference must state METHODOLOGY AND MEASURED RESULTS with uncertainty and date.
- Release mode for builds/tests.
- Reuse before writing: this is a 40-crate workspace and the prior is 'it already exists'.
- Intended use is education/research/V&V ONLY -- never reactor operation, control, licensing, or safety-critical decisions.
- AI output is untrusted draft until a human reviews it.

MUST STATE WHAT THE AGENT HAS NOT BEEN GIVEN -- the crates whose api.md is absent from the bundle, by name. An agent told nothing about them will infer they do not exist and invent APIs.

MUST NOT include: beads/kopi-beans workflow, git hooks, token accounting, the working-hours guardrail, push policy. None of it applies to a chat agent.

description:
Maintainer instruction 2026-08-14: 'just retire gen api docs'.

WHY. The call chain was kovan (Rust) -> python3 -> cargo + rustdoc-md: a Rust binary spawning an interpreter to spawn Rust tooling. That inverts the direction epic op-yz7b already set, which deleted docs/historian/*.py and token_usage.py and replaced them with kovan-metrics so the toolchain needs no Python. The rationale recorded in .githooks/kovan-bin.sh is concrete: on Windows 'python3' resolves to a Microsoft Store alias stub that prints an advert and exits, which silently turned the token hooks into no-ops.

NOT THE LAST PYTHON, contrary to what was said in chat. scripts/ still holds kloc_accounting.py and gen_aster_behaviour_registry.py. This retires the doc-generation one only.

WHAT NIGHTLY IS FOR, since it keeps being misread: rustdoc-md is an ordinary STABLE binary that reads a JSON file. The nightly requirement belongs to rustdoc's '--output-format json', still gated behind -Z unstable-options. Verified 2026-08-14: 'cargo +stable doc --output-format json' -> 'unexpected argument'. It is build tooling only; nothing shipped needs nightly and the workspace still builds, tests and publishes on stable.

PLACEMENT. The port goes in kovan-cli (crates/kovan-cli/src/commands/api_docs.rs), NOT kovan-semantics. It spawns cargo, so it is desktop-scope and neither offline nor deterministic; kovan-semantics must stay Android-clean and offline. This mirrors 'kovan setup', whose cargo-install spawn lives in the CLI layer for the same reason.

SCOPE: 14 references to update -- CLAUDE.md x2, six crates/*/docs/README.md, docs/reactor-scoping/htr10.md, and three Rust doc comments. Delete the script last.

notes.content:
Done and verified 2026-08-14. Ported to crates/kovan-cli/src/commands/api_docs.rs as 'kovan api-docs <crate> [--private]'; scripts/gen_api_docs.py deleted; all 14 references updated (CLAUDE.md x2, six crates/*/docs/README.md, docs/reactor-scoping/htr10.md, three Rust doc comments). agent-docs-gen's --regenerate-missing now calls generate() IN PROCESS -- no interpreter in the chain at all.

ONE DELIBERATE BEHAVIOUR CHANGE. The Python silently ran 'cargo install rustdoc-md --locked' when the binary was absent. The Rust does NOT; it errors with the exact command to run. A surprise network fetch inside a documentation regeneration is the kind of implicit side effect this workspace's tooling avoids, and the new CLAUDE.md 'API-doc toolchain' rule already requires the tool to be installed deliberately.

Verified: 42 kovan-semantics + kovan-cli tests pass, cargo check --workspace --lib --tests clean, and both crates check for aarch64-linux-android with --all-targets.

title: Annotate public traits with #[diagnostic::on_unimplemented]
description:
Split out of op-m2mj, where it was only a comment. Same principle as that bead — an interface should be usable without reading its source — but a DIFFERENT audience, and the two must not be counted against each other.

op-m2mj measures the PYTHON surface with a Haiku agent. This bead is the RUST surface: a confusing trait-bound error is the compiler's version of an undiscoverable API, and the compiler is not in a Python caller's loop at all. Progress here is not progress there.

WHAT IS AVAILABLE. `#[diagnostic::on_unimplemented]` stable since Rust 1.78; `#[diagnostic::do_not_recommend]` stable since 1.85. Both work on this workspace's 1.98 toolchain — verified 2026-09-04 rather than assumed:

    #[diagnostic::on_unimplemented(
        message = "`{Self}` is not a valid solver state",
        label = "needs an OdeSystem",
        note = "construct one with `MySystem::new(..)`"
    )]
    trait OdeSystem {}

yields `error[E0277]: `u32` is not a valid solver state` carrying our label and note, replacing the default 'the trait bound `u32: OdeSystem` is not satisfied'. `do_not_recommend` suppresses a blanket impl the compiler would otherwise suggest unhelpfully.

CURRENT STATE. 65 public traits across the workspace; zero carry either attribute.

SCOPE, IN PRIORITY ORDER. Annotate the traits a caller can plausibly fail a bound on — ranked by how often each is actually named as a bound:

     91  EquationOfState                  (dwsim-libs / coolprop)
     89  ThermoModel
     53  FluidComponentTrait              (tuas_boussinesq_solver)
     36  TransportModel
     35  TransferFnTraits                 (chem-eng)
     32  OdeSystem                        (outram-foam-basic-lib)
     30  FluidComponentCollectionMethods
     19  MpiPrimitive
     14  Filter
     10  UnitOpEvaluator
      9  TurbulenceModel
      9  OpcuaVariable

The top six cover the bulk. A trait used once internally and never named in a public generic signature does not need this; the test is whether a downstream caller can hit the bound.

WHAT A GOOD MESSAGE SAYS. Not a restatement of the bound. Name the concrete types that DO implement it, or the constructor to call — 'implemented by PengRobinson, Srk, PengRobinson1978' is worth more than 'the trait bound is not satisfied', because it turns a search through the source into a choice from a list. That is the same standard op-m2mj applies to the Python enums.

NOT IN SCOPE. Adding traits, changing bounds, or introducing trait objects to make errors nicer — the workspace's enums-over-dyn rule stands. This is annotation only.

VERIFICATION. For each annotated trait, a compile-fail check that the custom message actually appears (trybuild, or a doc example) — an on_unimplemented that silently stops matching after a refactor is worse than none, because it reads as done.

description: root@vm
title: root@vm
Validation pipeline per test reactor: ENDF -> MC -> MGXS+feedback -> deterministic -> ROM -> digital twin
description:
EPIC. Maintainer ask 2026-09-04: for each well-documented test reactor we validate against, a small agent (Haiku, or ChatGPT with a Python interpreter and shell) should be able to drive the whole chain through the outram-park-backend Python API, within reasonable compute.

THE PIPELINE, and where each stage stands. Surveyed 2026-09-04, not assumed.

  1. ENDF -> pointwise data. njoy-outram-park-fork. Tape::read_file, reconr, doppler_broaden all reach Python as of 5cab9ef. EndfCache can fetch. STATUS: seams exist; DATA does not (see below).
  2. Monte Carlo. outram-mc-libs. run_keff_csg on arbitrary CSG, run_keff_mg, run_fixed_source, TRISO into_geometry, CRP pebble packing, delta tracking. STATUS: works — a Godiva-like sphere assembled from Python gives k = 1.00485 +/- 0.00541.
  3a. MGXS. STATUS: DOES NOT EXIST. Mgxs::new has no call site outside its own definition; there are no MGXS tallies; Mgxs and genfoam GroupConstants are different types with no converter. Split out as op-84bc / gh:#42.
  3b. Feedback coefficients. teh-o-prke has Nordheim-Fuchs, Doppler, control-rod and moderator-density feedback. STATUS: NordheimFuchs is NOT exposed to Python (confirmed missing from the wheel). Doppler/rod feedback partially.
  4. Deterministic. genfoam neutronics (diffusion/SP3/SN/point-kinetics on FvMesh), bedok nodal, moltres for circulating fuel. STATUS: present in Rust; Python coverage thin (moltres 14 classes / 1 function, onix 10 / 1).
  5. ROM / surrogate. raffles. STATUS: **surrogate.rs is 54 lines with NO pub items — a stub.** sensitivity.rs has Sobol layout, Pearson/Spearman correlation and Sobol sampling, but there is no surrogate model of any kind: no GP, no polynomial chaos, no POD. THIS STAGE DOES NOT EXIST AND BLOCKS EVERY REACTOR.
  6. Digital twin. outram-park-digital-twin-engine. STATUS: exists, but plant models live in example trees (11,531 lines for htgr_sim_v1) and are reachable from nothing — see the placement note on op-jyyp.

TWO FINDINGS THAT SHAPE THE WHOLE EPIC.

FINDING A — stage 5 is a stub. The pipeline as described has a hole in the middle-late position. Either implement a surrogate in raffles (the sampling and sensitivity halves are already there, so this is the model itself: GP or polynomial chaos over the state grid), or drop stage 5 from the near-term chain and go straight from deterministic to twin. That is a maintainer decision and should be made before any reactor child starts, because it changes every one of them.

FINDING B — we do not have the nuclear data. reference-data/endf holds 12 files: U-235, U-238, H-2, He-4, Ar-37, and TSLs for Al-27, C-in-SiC, Si-in-SiC, crystalline graphite, reactor graphite 10P/30P, H-in-ZrH. MISSING for the named reactors: O-16 (every oxide fuel), H-1 (all light water), Zr, Fe/Cr/Ni, B-10, Pu-239/240/241, Na-23, Li-7/Be-9/F-19 (MSRE salt), Th-232/U-233. Stage 1 is therefore a real per-reactor task, not a formality; EndfCache is the seam to drive it.

COMPUTE BUDGET IS PART OF THE SPEC. 'Reasonable compute' has to be written down per reactor or a small agent will launch something that never finishes. Each child must state a target: particles x generations for the MC stage, group structure and state-grid size for MGXS, and a wall-clock ceiling. A pebble bed with double heterogeneity is orders of magnitude past a bare sphere and cannot be scoped by analogy to one.

REACTORS, and the existing work each must NOT duplicate:
  HTR-10   -> op-jyyp (18 children, 0 done), docs/reactor-scoping/htr10*.md
  HTTR     -> op-id3l.4 (first criticality + rod worth), .9 (core TH), .11 (LOFC)
  MSRE     -> op-6w0 (digital twin epic), docs/reactor-scoping/msre.md
  EBR-II   -> docs/reactor-scoping/ebr2.md
  EBR-I    -> nothing yet
  LWR      -> op-wqk.10 (ipwr_sim_v1), op-wqk.11 (abwr_sim_v1), docs ipwr.md / bwr.md
  HWR      -> nothing yet

Children are the per-reactor validation runs. They are validation and API-exercise tasks, NOT simulator-construction tasks — the simulators are the epics above and this epic depends on them rather than replacing them.

NO V&V IS CLAIMED BY THIS EPIC. Producing a number for a benchmark is not validating against it; each child names its published reference and its acceptance band explicitly, and a child that runs but misses its band is a finding, not a pass.

Related: op-375p / gh:#41 (neutronics API scope), op-84bc / gh:#42 (MGXS), op-m2mj (Haiku harness).

title: tampines-steam-tables: choked-flow and Joule-Thomson solvers should return Result, not panic on non-convergence
description:
Found while doing op-dt3.26 (extending interfaces::checked). These panics are NOT envelope violations, so no bounds-checking facade can exclude them - the honest fix is in the solvers themselves.

PANIC SITES (traced 2026-08-11):
  - steam_turbine_equations/converging_diverging_nozzles/choked_flow/mod.rs:241
    panic!('unable to find bracket for critical mass flux root finding') - fires when
    the downward pressure scan from p0 finds no sign change in
    (g_energy - g_hem). Reached from get_critical_pressure_and_mass_flux_multiphase_ph
    and thus from TampinesSteamTableCV::get_crit_pressure_and_massflux.
  - converging_diverging_nozzles/joule_thomson.rs:157 panic!('bounds are same sign!')
  - converging_diverging_nozzles/joule_thomson.rs:201 panic!('Joule-Thomson algorithm:
    failed to converge')

WHY A FACADE CANNOT HELP. Whether a bracket exists is a property of the function over
the whole scan interval, not of the stagnation state (p0, h0). Deciding it requires
running the scan - at which point you have done the work and can just return the
failure. A checked wrapper that gated only the (p,h) envelope of the stagnation state
would claim a safety it does not provide, which op-dt3.26's no-half-gating rule
forbids. So interfaces::checked deliberately leaves these alone and says so in its
'Known gaps' section.

WHAT op-dt3.26 DID COVER in this area: ps::try_mass_flux_ps_eqm_throat, which is a
genuine envelope check - the unchecked mass_flux_ps_eqm_throat differentiates v(p,s)
by finite difference (dp = p*1e-5), so it evaluates the (p,s) flash at p, p+dp and
max(p-dp, floor). Near 100 MPa and near the 1073.15 K isotherm the step walks out of
the envelope and the raw function panics; the checked version re-runs the envelope
check at all three pressures (and gates the s_tp_eqm_two_phase bubble-point lookup)
and rejects instead. Verified: 162 394 accepted points, zero leaked panics.

PROPOSED FIX (needs maintainer sign-off - it CHANGES PUBLIC SIGNATURES and so was out
of scope for op-dt3.26's additive-only remit):
  - a NonConvergent-style error variant (the crate CLAUDE.md already forbids papering
    over NonConvergent with a default value, so an error type is the intended shape)
  - get_critical_pressure_and_mass_flux_* -> Result
  - the Joule-Thomson root finder -> Result
  - TampinesSteamTableCV::get_crit_pressure_and_massflux gets a try_ sibling
Alternatively keep the panicking functions and add try_ siblings that return Result,
which would stay additive.

description:
Found 2026-07-28 while porting to v2. v1's GUI does: clone CIETState early in the egui repaint, mutate a couple of control fields on the clone, then overwrite_state(clone) at the end -- a full-struct store from a stale snapshot, ~20x/second. Sites: examples/ciet_educational_simulator/ciet_simulator_v1/app/panels_and_pages/main_page.rs:109 and :1194, and the frequency-response block in app.rs.

Impact in v1: mild and self-healing. CIETState is a publication surface, not the solver's internal state -- the physics thread recomputes temperatures from its own tuas component objects each timestep, so clobbered OUTPUTS are restored within one step. That is presumably why this was never noticed.

Impact in v2: NOT benign. CIETState also carries the CONTROLS the solver reads each timestep (heater power, pump pressure, set points). With OPC-UA writes arriving from remote clients at arbitrary times, a client write landing between the GUI's clone and its store is silently discarded -- remote control would appear to randomly not take effect, and would be near-impossible to diagnose from the client side.

Fixed in v2 by writing only the specific fields the GUI actually changed, under a short write guard, instead of overwriting the whole struct (main_page.rs:134 and :1236).

Consequence for port equivalence (op-wqk.13.6): v1 and v2 will NOT agree step-for-step with a GUI running, because v1 discards updates and v2 does not. The comparison must therefore be run HEADLESS on both sides to be meaningful.

No fix proposed for v1 itself -- out of scope for the v2 request, and v1 is the maintainer-validated reference. Flagging for his decision.

A gallery/dogfooding app in outram-park-digital-twin-engine that displays every visual component on one screen with live controls, so each widget can be built and quality-controlled ONE AT A TIME (maintainer's framing, 2026-08-03: 'construct widget by widget so there is some quality control').

SCOPE: gallery only. An authoring tool (compose a plant schematic interactively) is explicitly deferred to a future epic.

WHY: the components/ layer is far weaker than its bead history suggests. Inventory 2026-08-03 -- 1 genuine widget (PipeVisual, 281 lines, per-FV-cell colouring + tracers), 1 modest (ReactorVesselVisual), 4 single-rectangle colour-only (cooling tower, steam generator, turbine, valve), and 4 with NO state-derived detail at all (pump, condenser, heat exchanger, instrumentation -- flat circles/rects). op-wqk.3 is closed, but it delivered wrappers, not good widgets.

DESIGN BAR (maintainer, 2026-08-03/04): a widget's look must derive from the real dimensions and design of the component -- turbine sizing, pipe bore and run -- not from arbitrary screen coordinates. Aesthetically: pipes connect smoothly, thickness reflects cross-sectional area, displayed length is proportional to real length, and angle follows elevation so natural-circulation loops read correctly. Avoid over-detailing; too much may confuse the end user.

title: TurbineVisual: per-stage blade angulation from the physical turbine model (replace placeholders)
description:
Maintainer, 2026-08-04: 'the turbine blades are reaction + impulse. They are angled differently at each stage. Have placeholder angles for those. When detailed turbine design lands (and it should later), then take the angulation from the physical turbine model.'

INTERIM (done under op-wqk.14.3): stator + rotor blades are drawn with a PLACEHOLDER per-stage angle schedule. These are illustrative only and MUST be labelled as such in the doc comments -- they are not derived from any turbine design and must never be presented as if they were.

THE PHYSICS THEY STAND IN FOR:
  - Degree of reaction is the fraction of the stage enthalpy drop taken across the ROTOR. Impulse ~ 0% (all expansion in the fixed nozzle/stator, rotor just turns the flow); reaction typically ~50% (expansion split between stator and rotor).
  - Classic steam-turbine practice puts impulse stages at the HP inlet (Rateau/Curtis) and reaction stages toward the LP exhaust (Parsons), so a multi-stage machine is a MIXTURE and the blade angles vary stage by stage -- which is exactly why one fixed angle for all rows is wrong.
  - The blade SHAPES differ too, not just the angles: impulse rotor blades are near-symmetric buckets; reaction blades are asymmetric aerofoils. If the drawing is to distinguish stage types honestly, shape should follow angle.

WHEN THIS IS DONE: the angles must come from the real turbine model rather than the placeholder schedule -- stator exit angle alpha and rotor inlet/outlet angles beta per stage, plus the degree of reaction per stage. That model does not exist yet; it arrives with the detailed turbine design work (see op-dt3.18, the TampinesSteamArray-coupled turbine). Wire the dependency and delete the placeholder schedule at that point; do not leave both paths live.

title: Widget library: standard PWR HP and LP turbines (single-flow vs double-flow)
description:
Maintainer, 2026-08-04: 'we should have a standard HP and LP turbine as it is for the PWR plants' -- in the widget library.

CORRECTION THIS CARRIES. On 2026-08-04 the mirrored 'hourglass' silhouette inherited from fhr_sim_v2 was called an artwork defect and replaced with monotonic inlet-to-exhaust blade growth (commit b44f549). That was only half right. A PWR LP turbine is normally DOUBLE-FLOW: steam admits at the centre and expands outward in BOTH directions, so its rotor genuinely is mirrored about the mid-plane. The real defect was applying one silhouette unconditionally, plus proportions that collapsed at wide aspect ratios. Flow path is a property of the machine, not a drawing style.

WHAT TO BUILD:
  - Single-flow: monotonic expansion, inlet one end, exhaust the other. Typical HP.
  - Double-flow: centre admission, mirrored expansion to an exhaust at each end. Typical PWR LP, and how the original fhr_sim_v2 artwork was actually shaped.

Closed set -> enum dispatch, per the workspace no-trait-objects rule.

STANDARD PWR SECONDARY ARRANGEMENT to represent:
  - Steam generators deliver SATURATED (not superheated) steam, roughly 6-7 MPa.
  - HP turbine expands to roughly 1 MPa. Wet steam throughout, so erosion matters.
  - A moisture separator reheater (MSR) sits between HP and LP -- it is a distinct component and is NOT currently in the widget library at all. Worth its own bead.
  - Typically two or three double-flow LP turbines exhaust to the condenser at vacuum (~5 kPa).
  - LP last-stage blades are very long; the annulus area ratio between HP and LP is large and should be visible when the two widgets are shown side by side.

RELATION TO OTHER BEADS: per-stage blade angulation and the impulse/reaction mix are op-wqk.14.11 (placeholders now, real angles when the physical turbine model lands, op-dt3.18). Physical envelope dimensions remain blocked on op-dt3.17.1. This bead is about the FLOW PATH and the HP/LP presets, which are independent of both.

DO NOT present the presets as a specific vendor's or plant's design -- they are illustrative standard-arrangement values per RESPONSIBLE_USE.md, and the data policy forbids using any actual plant data.

notes.content:
DECIDED 2026-08-04 (maintainer): DOUBLE-FLOW IS THE DEFAULT for turbine widgets. Single-flow remains available as the other enum variant, but a TurbineVisual built without specifying a flow path draws double-flow.

This matches large-PWR practice rather than being merely a drawing preference: at PWR secondary-side volumetric flows, the HP turbine is commonly double-flow as well as the LP set (a typical large PWR turbine-generator is one double-flow HP plus two or three double-flow LP cylinders). So double-flow is the right default for BOTH presets, not just LP.

Practical consequence for the implementation: the mirrored silhouette from the original fhr_sim_v2 artwork becomes the DEFAULT rendering again, with centre admission and an exhaust at each end -- but now with the pitch-derived proportions from b44f549 so it no longer collapses at wide aspect ratios, and with the blade-height growth running outward from the centre admission plane toward both exhausts (not inward, and not mirrored-by-accident as before).

description: teddy0@snrsi-arch-desktop
title: teddy0@snrsi-arch-desktop
TurbineVisual: settle stator/rotor blade lean direction (deferred)
description:
Deferred by the maintainer 2026-08-04 after several rounds of on-screen iteration. The turbine looks acceptable; the blade LEAN convention is not settled and should be decided against a proper reference rather than by eye.

WHAT IS SETTLED (do not redo):
  - Blade HEIGHT mirrors about the admission plane for double flow. Enforced by the test double_flow_geometry_is_symmetric_about_the_admission_plane. The rotor radius must blend from the LESS-EXPANDED neighbour (nearer admission), not from row+1 -- +x is downstream on one half and upstream on the other, and blending toward row+1 on both halves broke the symmetry.
  - Blades are rooted at the hub, run radially to the tip, and project root and tip by the same cos(phi) so they shorten onto the shaft edge-on.
  - Blades are cambered quadratic Beziers; camber runs in OPPOSITE senses for stator and rotor. That opposition is what turns the flow and extracts work.
  - The stator ring is drawn whole; only the ROTOR hides its far half (that is what reads as rotation).

WHAT IS NOT SETTLED -- the lean (overall slant), as distinct from the camber:
  - Attempt 1: lean applied in a fixed x direction. Maintainer: rotor blades not symmetric.
  - Attempt 2: lean mirrored with flow direction via a flow_sign helper. Maintainer: stator wrong on the left, rotor wrong on the right. Those four observations are only satisfiable by uniform lean with the rotor base inverted, so flow_sign was removed.
  - Attempt 3 (current): lean uniform across the machine; stator negative (angles down, maintainer-verified for SINGLE flow), rotor negative. Consequence: the two rows now lean the SAME way, and only the camber opposes.

OPEN QUESTIONS:
  1. Should lean mirror with flow direction on a double-flow machine, or stay uniform because the shaft turns one way along its whole length? Physical argument exists both ways: mirrored blades are what cancel axial thrust in a double-flow rotor, but rotation sense is common.
  2. Is it right that stator and rotor lean the same way and only the camber opposes?
  3. Double flow has NOT been re-checked since the stator lean was flipped on 2026-08-04; the earlier 'stator looks right on the right half' judgement predates that flip.

HOW TO SETTLE IT: against a published turbine velocity-triangle / blade-profile reference, not by eye. Anything adopted must be documented with its source per the workspace provenance rule. Note the angles themselves are still placeholders (op-wqk.14.11) and become real when the physical turbine model lands (op-dt3.18) -- it may be cheapest to settle lean and angles together at that point.

title: color_maps: add a perceptually-uniform temperature colour map (licence-clean)
description:
Maintainer asked 2026-08-05 about using the NASA GISS Panoply colorbars (https://www.giss.nasa.gov/tools/panoply/colorbars/) for temperature colouring, and flagged uncertainty about the copyright. That uncertainty was correct.

FINDING -- DO NOT ADOPT PANOPLY'S SET IN BULK (checked 2026-08-05):
The Panoply colorbars page carries NO licence, terms of use, or redistribution statement of any kind. The tables are explicitly third-party in origin, by the page's own attribution text:
  CB*   -> ColorBrewer2.org, Cynthia A. Brewer
  NCL*  -> NCL Graphics Color Table Gallery, UCAR
  GMT*  -> Generic Mapping Tools, SOEST, University of Hawai'i
  EO/NEO-> NASA Earth Observatory / NASA Earth Observations
  plus NOAA, UK Met Office, Scientific Visualization Studio, and individual researchers (e.g. Joshua Stevens)

So 'it is NASA, therefore public domain' does not hold: US Government works are public domain only for the parts NASA actually authored, and the page does not mark which those are. Taking the CB* tables via Panoply would additionally STRIP the attribution notice ColorBrewer's own licence requires. This fails RESEARCH_INTEGRITY_AND_PROVENANCE.md (documented source/author/licence/URL/date) and the CLAUDE.md rule against introducing code whose licence has not been checked.

TWO VERIFIED, GPL-3.0-COMPATIBLE ALTERNATIVES:

1. RECOMMENDED -- Scientific colour maps, Fabio Crameri.
   Licence: MIT (verified on the Zenodo record, v8.0.1, published 2023-10-05).
   DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.1243862 ; https://www.fabiocrameri.ch/colourmaps/
   Built for scientific data: perceptually uniform (equal steps in temperature look like equal steps in colour) and readable with colour-vision deficiency. Diverging hot/cold candidates: vik, roma. Sequential: lajolla, lipari. Citable, which suits the V&V write-ups.

2. ColorBrewer. Licence: Apache-2.0, (c) 2002 Cynthia Brewer, Mark Harrower, The Pennsylvania State University.
   GPL-3.0-compatible (NOT GPL-2-compatible). Conditions: retain the copyright notice; end-user documentation must acknowledge 'This product includes color specifications and designs developed by Cynthia Brewer (http://colorbrewer.org/)'; the ColorBrewer name may not be used to endorse derivatives.

HOW TO IMPLEMENT WHEN PICKED UP:
  - ADD alongside the existing maps, never replace them. crates/outram-park-digital-twin-engine/src/color_maps/ is documented as already-validated code whose exact values call sites depend on. hot_to_cold_colour_mark_1 stays.
  - New map gets a provenance header (project, author, version/DOI, licence, URL, date accessed) and a References.md entry.
  - If ColorBrewer is chosen, the attribution string above must appear in user-facing docs, not just source.

Callers that would benefit: PipeVisual cell fills, TurbineVisual casing, and the per-stage steam-quality tint (which currently reuses steam_quality_colour_mark_1 normalised over a display range).

notes.content:
COLORBREWER SOURCE CLARIFICATION (checked 2026-08-06, prompted by the maintainer asking whether github.com/axismaps/colorbrewer is 'the' ColorBrewer):

Yes -- axismaps/colorbrewer is the official repository behind colorbrewer2.org, maintained by Axis Maps, with the schemes based on Dr Cynthia Brewer's research.

BUT THE TWO LICENCE FILES ARE NOT INTERCHANGEABLE:
  - github.com/axismaps/colorbrewer/LICENCE.txt is the STOCK Apache-2.0 boilerplate with the placeholders left unfilled ('Copyright {yyyy} {name of copyright owner}'). It names no copyright holder and carries no acknowledgement clause. It governs Axis Maps' website/software.
  - colorbrewer2.org/export/LICENSE.txt is Apache-2.0 WITH the copyright filled in -- (c) 2002 Cynthia Brewer, Mark Harrower, The Pennsylvania State University -- and the specific condition that end-user documentation acknowledge: 'This product includes color specifications and designs developed by Cynthia Brewer (http://colorbrewer.org/)'. It also forbids using the ColorBrewer name to endorse derivatives.

The colour SPECIFICATIONS are the part this project would use, so the export licence is the authoritative one to cite. Taking the GitHub boilerplate instead would mean redistributing the colour data with no named copyright holder and no attribution -- the same defect as taking them via Panoply.

Unchanged recommendation: Crameri's Scientific colour maps (MIT, DOI 10.5281/zenodo.1243862) remain the simpler choice, with no attribution clause to carry and better suitability for scientific data. ColorBrewer stays viable if its acknowledgement is honoured in user-facing docs.
notes.author: teddy0@snrsi-arch-desktop

notes.content:
DECIDED 2026-08-06 (maintainer): use CRAMERI'S SCIENTIFIC COLOUR MAPS. ColorBrewer is not being adopted; the licence comparison above is retained only as the record of why.

Licence: MIT. Verified on the Zenodo record, v8.0.1, published 2023-10-05.
Cite: Crameri, F. (2018). Scientific colour maps. Zenodo. DOI 10.5281/zenodo.1243862
Home: https://www.fabiocrameri.ch/colourmaps/  Supporting paper: Geoscientific Model Development (2018).
MIT is compatible with this workspace's GPL-3.0-only and carries no attribution clause to thread through user-facing docs.

WHY CRAMERI RATHER THAN COLORBREWER (the reason is technical, not preference):
ColorBrewer's schemes were designed to make DISCRETE choropleth classes distinguishable and are NOT perceptually uniform. Stretched across a continuous field they manufacture apparent banding -- fast-changing stretches read as steep gradients and flat stretches as isothermal, when the underlying data is smooth. For widgets whose stated premise is that rendering derives directly from physics state, a colour map that invents structure is actively wrong. Crameri's are perceptually uniform by construction: equal steps in the quantity read as equal steps in colour.

Two further properties that matter here:
  - Greyscale-safe: stays readable printed black-and-white, which the V&V write-ups will need.
  - CYCLIC maps (romaO, vikO, ...). ColorBrewer has no equivalent, and the turbine rotor angle is a cyclic quantity -- a cyclic map is the correct way to colour one.

ColorBrewer's qualitative sets remain the more battle-tested option IF categorical palettes are ever wanted (flow regimes, component types, material IDs). Revisit only for that.

MAP SELECTION (suggested, confirm when implementing):
  - temperature / hot-cold, diverging: vik or roma
  - sequential (quality, burnup, flux): lajolla, lipari, or batlow
  - cyclic (rotor angle, phase): romaO or vikO

IMPLEMENTATION CONSTRAINTS (unchanged):
  - ADD alongside the existing maps; never replace them. crates/outram-park-digital-twin-engine/src/color_maps/ is documented as already-validated code whose exact values call sites depend on. hot_to_cold_colour_mark_1 and steam_quality_colour_mark_1 both stay.
  - Provenance header on the new module (project, author, version, DOI, licence, URL, date accessed) plus a References.md entry, per RESEARCH_INTEGRITY_AND_PROVENANCE.md.
  - Vendor only the specific map tables used, with their MIT notice, rather than the whole suite.
  - Callers that would benefit: PipeVisual cell fills, TurbineVisual casing, the per-stage steam-quality tint.

notes.content:
NEUTRAL-MIDPOINT ALTERNATIVES (measured 2026-08-06, from the official archive). Maintainer asked whether anything other than white could carry 'neither hot nor cold'; decision was to KEEP WHITE (vik). Recorded so the option is not re-derived.

Diverging maps in the suite, sampled at t=0 / t=0.5 / t=1 with Rec.601 luma at the midpoint:
  vik      (  0, 18, 97) (236,229,224) ( 89,  0,  8)  mid-luma 230.5   <- in use
  broc     ( 44, 26, 76) (235,238,236) ( 38, 38,  0)  236.9
  cork     ( 44, 25, 76) (230,237,236) ( 15, 41,  3)  234.8
  bam      (101,  2, 75) (246,241,240) ( 13, 76,  0)  242.4
  roma     (126, 23,  0) (192,234,195) (  3, 49,152)  217.0
  berlin   (158,176,255) ( 25, 12,  9) (255,173,173)   15.5   <- dark neutral
  lisbon   (230,229,255) ( 23, 25, 25) (255,255,217)   24.4
  tofino   (222,217,255) ( 13, 22, 19) (219,230,155)   19.0
  vanimo   (255,205,253) ( 26, 21, 19) (190,253,165)   22.3
  managua  (255,207,103) ( 87, 41, 73) (129,231,255)   58.4

berlin is the direct drop-in if a dark neutral is ever wanted: same blue-cold / red-hot semantics, but the midpoint recedes on a dark UI instead of being the brightest thing on screen.

WHY WHITE WAS KEPT: berlin and the other dark-neutral maps invert the intensity relationship -- extremes become light, the middle dark -- so they read oddly printed or on a light background. vik behaves sensibly either way, which matters if studio output ends up in figures. Switching is a one-line change in components::temperature_colour; the blue/white/red convention test would need updating with it.

description:
The studio frame everything else plugs into. An eframe app (target-gated off Android per the windowing exemption, like mesh_studio/mc_studio) with: a list/picker of every visual component, a live-state control panel (sliders for temperature, flow, opening fraction, etc.) so a widget can be driven across its full range by hand, and a panel showing the widget's derived geometry inputs so it is obvious what drives what.

Follow the crate's existing example-app conventions (examples/ with required-features, app_scaffold/ for shared panels). Tracer state is APPLICATION-owned and advanced once per frame, then copied into the widget at build time -- widgets are rebuilt every repaint, so a train owned by a widget resets its phase each frame (crate CLAUDE.md).

Parent: the Widget Studio bead.

title: Widget Studio: plant-space layout layer — metres to screen transform, node graph, elevation
description:
The substrate that makes the aesthetic bar achievable, and the missing abstraction today. PipeVisual currently takes screen_position: Pos2 + screen_vector: Vec2 in raw SCREEN POINTS, hardcodes PIPE_STROKE_WIDTH = 4.0, and has no elevation and no connection concept -- so every endpoint is hand-placed by the app and nothing about the drawing is derived.

Needed: a layout module owning a plant-space (metres, with elevation) -> screen transform plus a node graph, so components are placed at real coordinates and connected by node. Pipe direction/length then follow from real geometry, connections are shared nodes (so runs meet smoothly), and elevation makes natural-circulation loops read correctly.

tampines::components::Pipe ALREADY exposes everything needed -- diameter: Length, length: Length, inclination: Angle, roughness: Length (crates/tampines/src/components/pipe.rs:37-43), all uom-typed and stable (step() is inert, so they are caller-supplied and trustworthy). No tampines change required for pipes.

OPEN DESIGN QUESTION, deferred by the maintainer (2026-08-04) -- resolve before building: is stroke width proportional to DIAMETER (a true scale drawing; bore area then reads correctly to the eye as width^2) or to AREA (width proportional to d^2, exaggerating large pipes)? Note also that bores (~0.05 m) and runs (~10 m) cannot share one scale or pipes render as invisible hairlines, so diameter needs its own exaggerated scale -- which must be documented honestly as exaggeration, not as proportionality. The V&V write-up has to state which convention is used.

title: htgr_sim_v1: control-rod insertion slider is too sensitive
description:
Maintainer report, 2026-08-14: the control-rod insertion slider in htgr_sim_v1's operator panel (panels.rs, drives PlantCommands::control_rod_insertion_fraction) is too sensitive -- small mouse movements produce large reactivity swings.

Likely candidates to check before picking a fix: (a) the slider's egui::Slider range/step is too coarse relative to the 0.0-1.0 insertion-fraction domain -- consider a finer drag-speed or a logarithmic/non-linear response near the operating point; (b) the rod worth curve (teh-o-prke::control_rod_feedback::obtain_rod_worth_cylinder, the Lamarsh S-curve) is steepest near mid-insertion by construction, so a linear slider naturally feels most sensitive there -- this may be physically correct and the fix may be UI-only (finer drag granularity / a numeric entry box alongside the slider), not a physics change.

Do not silently change the S-curve response to fix a UI-sensitivity complaint -- confirm which one is at fault first.

title: htgr_sim_v1 crash modal: add an in-app 'restart simulation' button
description:
Maintainer request, 2026-08-14. app_scaffold::show_crash_modal_if_crashed (op-4wv, Done) currently only tells the operator to close and relaunch the process -- its doc comment explicitly says it 'deliberately does not try to restart the process' because a panicked physics thread may have poisoned a shared lock mid-write.

ASK: add a button in the crash modal that restarts the simulation fresh, in-app, without the operator closing the window.

HOW THIS STAYS SAFE (do not resume the poisoned state): never touch the Arc the crashed thread wrote into. On click, build a brand-new SharedState<HtgrSnapshot>/SharedState<HtgrPlotData>/ThreadHealth (fresh Arcs, HtgrPlant::new() defaults) and spawn brand-new physics + plot-sampler threads via spawn_physics_thread_monitored, then swap them into HtgrSimApp in place of the crashed ones; drop the old (already-dead) SharedState/ThreadHealth without reading them. This is a genuine restart-from-defaults, not a resume.

Scope: htgr_sim_v1 only for this bead (working on it now). fhr_sim_v2 also calls show_crash_modal_if_crashed and should keep compiling against whatever the modal's return type becomes, but wiring an actual restart button into fhr_sim_v2 is a separate follow-up -- do not silently scope-creep this bead into it.
