title: htgr_sim_v1: default temperature display unit should be degC, not K
description:
Maintainer request, 2026-08-14. op-qpgw (Done) added the operator-toggleable degC/K display unit, but HtgrSimApp::display_unit still opens on LegendUnit::default(), which is kelvin (per app/mod.rs's own doc comment on the display_unit field: "its default is kelvin, which is what this simulator displayed before the toggle existed"). Change the opening default to degrees Celsius.

DESIGN CONSTRAINT carried over from op-qpgw, still binding: this is a display-layer-only default. Do not let the changed default touch HtgrSnapshot, PlantCommands, or any correlation/controller/solver input -- it only changes which LegendUnit variant HtgrSimApp::new() picks for the initial self.display_unit.

SCOPE QUESTION carried over from op-qpgw and still open: htgr_sim_v1 only, or should the shared default in the engine's LegendUnit itself change (which would also affect fhr_sim_v2 and any other simulator built on the same widget)? Given op-qpgw scoped the toggle per-simulator (display_unit lives in HtgrSimApp, not in the engine), default this bead to htgr_sim_v1-only unless told otherwise.

title: Promote PebbleBedPorousMediaNode (implicit 2-node LTNE porous-media balance) into the library, add a molten-salt variant, drive both htgr_sim_v1 and fhr_sim_v2
description:
Once htgr_sim_v1's crates/outram-park-digital-twin-engine/examples/htgr_sim_v1/physics/reactor_model/one_node.rs::PebbleBedPorousMediaNode is tested and human-V&V'd (per the crate CLAUDE.md's example-to-library promotion trigger, op-76hu), it should be promoted from example code into the outram-park-digital-twin-engine library proper (src/), the same standard applied to every example model/widget per that trigger.

PebbleBedPorousMediaNode is a one-node, two-temperature (solid pebble + fluid helium) porous-media LTNE energy balance, discretized backward-Euler and solved each step as a 2x2 linear system via outram_foam_basic_lib::matrix::square_matrix::SquareMatrix. It gives the helium its own thermal capacitance/node (upgrading it from the "0 nodes, external" treatment PebbleBedCore's effectiveness-NTU balance uses), taking fission_power and decay_heat_power as separate arguments summed into one source term.

Follow-up work (deferred, not started):
1. Add a molten-salt variant of the same two-node implicit formulation for FHR (fhr_sim_v2's PebbleBedThermalHydraulics equivalent) -- same 2x2 backward-Euler structure, salt properties (OPCPFluidArray/molten-salt EOS) instead of helium.
2. Once both variants exist in the library, wire them to drive both htgr_sim_v1 (gas-cooled) and fhr_sim_v2 (salt-cooled), replacing each simulator's own example-local core model.
3. Human V&V required before promotion per RESPONSIBLE_USE.md -- AI-assisted output is untrusted draft material until reviewed; the existing tests (two_node_balance_settles_with_all_power_leaving_via_helium_throughflow, fission_power_and_decay_heat_power_sum_into_the_same_source_term) check energy-conservation identities only, not accuracy of the well-mixed-outlet assumption or T_pebble/T_helium against any published reference.

Origin: user request 2026-08-17, "Once this is tested, it should be put inside the outram-park-digital-twin-engine library, with a salt variant too for FHR. Then it should drive both htgr_sim_v1 and fhr_sim_v2."

title: app_scaffold: reusable real-time simulator infrastructure (physics loop, plotting, CSV, OPC-UA)
description:
Umbrella for generalizing the ciet_educational_simulator_v2 'app builder' pattern into
outram-park-digital-twin-engine's app_scaffold/ so every current and future real-time
simulator (htgr_sim_v1, fhr_sim_v2, ipwr_sim_v1, abwr_sim_v1, CIET v3, ...) can build on
shared, tested infrastructure instead of hand-rolling its own. Four pieces surveyed
2026-08-17:

1. Physics loop + real-time pacing: app_scaffold already has SharedState<T>,
   spawn_physics_thread_monitored, and RealTimePacer, consumed by htgr_sim_v1/fhr_sim_v2.
   ciet_educational_simulator_v2 hand-rolls its own version (educational_ciet_loop_version_4
   in full_simulation/mod.rs, mirrored in nat_circ_simulation/mod.rs) with fast_forward /
   slow_motion toggles and a timestep_seconds dt-shrink control app_scaffold doesn't have,
   plus one branch (grow timestep back to max on overrun) that actively contradicts
   RealTimePacer's own documented pacing invariant. See child .3.
2. Plot/graph sampling loop: three near-duplicate bounded-history implementations exist
   (HTGR's own Vec+remove(0), and a shared CIET-v1-derived lineage in both
   ciet_educational_simulator_v2 and fhr_sim_v2 that rebuilds a whole 4000-element Vec
   per sample). See child .1.
3. CSV logging: does not exist as real file I/O anywhere in this crate today -- CIET v2's
   "csv" pages are an on-screen scrollable text label, not a file writer. Needs building
   new. See child .2.
4. OPC-UA server/client: already generalized. src/opcua_core/ (op-szmi.1, Done) provides
   enum-dispatched OpcuaSimulator/OpcuaVariable traits + a generic server/PKI/discovery
   layer; src/ciet_opcua/ is the worked reference implementation. src/htgr_opcua/ has its
   node maps/state but isn't wired to opcua_core yet -- that's the existing op-szmi.4
   bead, not new shared-infra work. See child .4.

Survey done by three parallel read-only agents 2026-08-17, no code changed by the survey.

title: app_scaffold: generic PlotHistory<T,N> ring buffer for plot panels
description:
Replace three near-duplicate bounded time-history implementations with one generic type
in app_scaffold: HtgrPlotData (examples/htgr_sim_v1/app/state.rs, Vec + remove(0), O(n)
shift per sample) and the CIET-v1-derived PagePlotData lineage shared by
ciet_educational_simulator_v2 (ciet_simulator_v2/app/panels_and_pages/ciet_data.rs) and
fhr_sim_v2 (examples/fhr_sim_v2/app/graph_data/mod.rs) -- both insert-at-front then
rebuild a fixed NUM_DATA_PTS_IN_PLOTS=4000-element Vec on every single sample.

Design: PlotHistory<T, const N: usize> on VecDeque<T>, push() O(1) amortized, oldest-first
iterator (egui_plot-friendly, matches HTGR's existing convention). Plain generic, no
trait objects, fits Arc<RwLock<T>> / SharedState<PlotHistory<T,N>> for the existing
sampler-thread pattern.

This is additive -- no existing call site is migrated onto it in this pass (that would
touch htgr_sim_v1/app/state.rs, which is off-limits to this session per a concurrent
fast-forward-control edit, and would touch ciet_educational_simulator_v2/fhr_sim_v2,
which the workspace CLAUDE.md biases against doing as a risky same-pass migration).
Migrating existing call sites onto it is separate follow-up work once this lands.

Surveyed 2026-08-17, read-only, by a fork agent; report retained in op-wqk.22.

notes.content: Implemented: PlotHistory<T, const N: usize> in crates/outram-park-digital-twin-engine/src/app_scaffold/plot_history.rs, VecDeque-backed, O(1) amortized push, oldest-first iteration. 8 unit tests + 1 doctest, all green. title: teddy0@arch-aftershock-rapid-glass-S267454
Migrate ciet_educational_simulator_v2 pacing loops onto app_scaffold (SharedState/RealTimePacer/crash-modal)
description:
ciet_educational_simulator_v2 hand-rolls its own physics-thread + pacing loop in
full_simulation/mod.rs::educational_ciet_loop_version_4 (~2076 lines, pacing tail at
1947-2058) and a near-duplicate in nat_circ_simulation/mod.rs (~937-998), instead of using
app_scaffold's SharedState<T> / spawn_physics_thread_monitored / RealTimePacer that
htgr_sim_v1 and fhr_sim_v2 already use. Consequences: no catch_unwind / ThreadHealth /
crash-modal coverage (a physics panic here kills the thread silently), and one pacing
branch that grows the physics timestep itself back to max on overrun -- which directly
contradicts real_time_pacing.rs's own documented invariant that pacing must never change
the integration. There's already an in-code comment (mod.rs:1982-1985) pointing at
real_time_pacing.rs as "the shared version of this arithmetic," i.e. the maintainer has
already flagged this duplication.

ciet v2 also has two capabilities RealTimePacer doesn't: a fast_forward_settings_turned_on
/ slow_motion_settings_turned_on toggle pair, and a timestep_seconds slider that shrinks
the physics dt itself during slow motion (an application-level dt policy, not wall-clock
pacing -- should NOT be folded into RealTimePacer, belongs in the simulator's own config).

NOT attempted in this pass: this is ~3000 lines across two files, entangled with plotting
and the (fake) CSV display, and op-3g0m (RealTimePacer fast-forward multiplier,
set_simulated_per_tick) is concurrently landing on the exact same pacer this would migrate
onto. Doing this before that lands would mean migrating onto a moving API twice.

Proposed follow-up API (once op-3g0m lands): a small enum
`PacingMode { RealTime, FastForward(f64), SlowMotion(f64) }` wrapping RealTimePacer
reconfiguration, then migrate both ciet v2 page loops onto spawn_physics_thread_monitored
+ that enum in one dedicated pass -- gaining crash-modal coverage as a side effect. Do NOT
port the "grow timestep on overrun" branch; it's the one piece inconsistent with the
pacer's stated philosophy.

Surveyed 2026-08-17, read-only, by a fork agent; report retained in op-wqk.22.

title: Pump widgets: cavitation bubbles at the impeller eye (DEFERRED)
description:
Maintainer: defer until later. Steam-generator bubble work (the 'ngeow' bead) is higher priority and should be done first -- both would share the same deterministic-scatter machinery, so doing SG first makes this cheaper.

IDEA: draw cavitation in the pump widgets (crates/outram-park-digital-twin-engine/src/components/pump.rs).

Cavitation is LOCALISED AND DIAGNOSTIC, not diffuse -- which is what makes it worth drawing. Vapour forms where local static pressure falls below saturation: the SUCTION SIDE OF THE BLADE LEADING EDGES NEAR THE IMPELLER EYE, where velocity is highest and pressure lowest. It should appear as a cloud hugging the leading edges, growing along the blade as NPSH margin falls, and collapsing further out where pressure recovers -- that collapse is what erodes impellers.

Drawn well it reads instantly as 'this pump is in trouble', which is the kind of thing an operator-facing twin should show.

INPUT NEEDED: one scalar -- available NPSH against required, or simply a margin fraction in [0,1].

CONSTRAINT: offline demonstration artwork, not a two-phase model. Same rule as the SG bubbles -- put the bubbles where the physics puts them, but keep it a display heuristic and say so.

Applies to PumpKind::Centrifugal and VerticalCannedRotor. The axial propeller cavitates differently (tip vortex) and is lower value.

title: Real-time multi-fidelity simulator loop: make the low band solid first
description:
Source: docs/real-time-multifidelity-scoping.md (written 2026-08-07; self-labelled "scoping analysis, not an approved plan", AI-assisted draft, not human-reviewed; audited against develop at 8c9ddd05).

VERDICT THE DOC REACHES: exactly one fidelity band runs in real time today and it is the lowest one -- lumped/system TH plus point kinetics, measured on CIET v2 at 94.7 s simulated in 94.7 s wall-clock, 27 ms median compute per 100 ms step (27% duty cycle). The gap to the next rung is ~3 orders of magnitude and does NOT close by optimisation. Design rule: a band that cannot meet its deadline is not allowed in the loop -- it goes offline and its output becomes a table.

TWO LEADING FINDINGS: (1) the crate literally named "real-time process control simulator" is the one component whose per-step cost is UNBOUNDED, and it is still in TUAS's PID path; (2) nothing in the workspace is a surrogate or ROM -- raffles/src/surrogate.rs is 54 lines of doc comment and zero code. There is also NO benchmarking infrastructure anywhere (no criterion, no benches/).

RECOMMENDED ARCHITECTURE: generalise what tampines' fhr_sim_v2 already does -- enum-dispatched fidelity levels on wall-paced threads at separate rates sharing Arc<RwLock<PlantState>>, with conservation-asserting state handoff. KEY SEQUENCING INSIGHT: snapshot/restore must come FIRST, because fidelity switching is a state-serialisation problem in disguise; doing it after the FidelityLevel enum means building it twice.

PHASE 1 is making the band that already runs actually TRUSTWORTHY: remove the unbounded-cost control path, the live todo!() panic paths in the flagship FHR simulator, the ~40 IF97 panic sites that kill the physics thread, and the two pacing defects; and stand up a criterion harness so any of it is measurable.
PHASE 2 is the capability: snapshot/restore/backtrack, then a FidelityLevel enum with conservation-asserted handoff, then a reduced circulating-fuel PRKE demonstrated against moltres.

DONE = a wall-clock-paced simulator sustaining >= 1.0x real-time factor with <= 200 ms control-to-response latency UNDER LOAD (not idle), whose per-step cost is bounded and measured by a committed benchmark baseline per band, that can snapshot and restore plant state, and that can switch fidelity at a timestep boundary with total mass and energy asserted conserved BY TEST.

Everything here remains an OFFLINE DEMONSTRATION ONLY -- never an operational digital twin, never plant monitoring.

DO NOT FILE AS DECIDED PLAN (the doc's own flags):
- The >= 1.0x / 200 ms / 20 Hz figures in section 3.2 are self-labelled ENGINEERING JUDGEMENT, "not values taken from a cited standard". Whether an ANSI/ANS-3.5 anchor is obtainable at all is OPEN, because ANS-3.5 validation needs reference-plant data DATA_POLICY.md forbids. Do not file them as requirements.
- MSRE-first CONTRADICTS docs/reactor-scoping/README.md:120-133, which recommends finishing the FHR widget migration first. That is a maintainer decision; the two docs must be reconciled.
- The bedok seam is gated on an OPEN DECISION (is bedok the neutronics path?), not ready to file as approved work. Until that call is made the nodal-diffusion band cannot even be costed -- it has never executed.
- Do NOT file a raffles::surrogate implementation issue. The doc explicitly says: do not block real-time work on raffles; build surrogates as tabulated offline coefficients and physics-form reduced models in the crates that own the physics. Neural surrogates are recommended AGAINST (auditability posture, no training data).
- Nine explicitly-undetermined items in section 7 must not be cited as facts, notably: the LOADED CIET step cost (unmeasured; the 27 ms is the IDLE state and is "certainly higher" under load); any bedok timing (the 76.5 s figure is Octave running the original MATLAB, not the Rust port); whether CIET v2 physics matches v1 (port-equivalence V&V op-wqk.13.6 has NOT been run -- v2 is "a faithful port of validated physics", not "validated"); Android/Termux real-time behaviour (compile proxy only); all GUI claims (no display available).
- The full tuas_boussinesq_solver suite was NOT run and its pass state is unreliable by construction: 46 #[ignore]d tests plus ~48 more with the #[ignore] commented out by hand.
- All [M] timings are machine-specific to the maintainer's box; re-measure before citing.

title: chem-eng 0.2.0: TUAS full release test suite not run to completion (killed at ~70 min)
description:
LEFT UNFINISHED 2026-08-11 by the op-fm5 O(1) recurrence work. Everything else in op-fm5 verified; this one gate did not finish.

WHAT WAS VERIFIED:
  cargo check --workspace --lib --tests            -> exit 0, no errors
  cargo test --release -p chem-eng...              -> 21 passed, 0 failed
  cargo test --release -p teh-o-prke --lib --tests -> 28 passed, 0 failed
WHAT WAS NOT:
  cargo test --release -p tuas_boussinesq_solver --lib --tests
  Started, ran ~70 minutes wall clock (2.5+ hours CPU, ~920% CPU, actively progressing, NOT hung), then was killed to free the cargo build lock at end of session. NO RESULT WAS OBTAINED -- do not read this as a pass or a fail.

TO RESUME: just run it. Budget well over an hour; consider --no-fail-fast and capturing per-test output rather than piping through tail, so a partial run is still informative.

RISK ASSESSMENT (why this is P2 and not P0): the chem-eng change is a cost change, not a physics change. The summed controller output over six benchmark runs of 40k-80k steps was IDENTICAL before and after to the printed 3 decimal places (e.g. 17175484.304 in both). The only intended numerical difference is that the old code discarded exp(-20) = 2.06e-9 of each step response on retirement and the new code carries it, so any TUAS assertion tighter than about 1e-9 relative on a PID-driven quantity is the only plausible failure mode. TUAS regression tolerances are typically far looser than that. Still needs the actual run.

Blocks closing op-fm5.

notes.content:
GATE SATISFIED 2026-08-11. The TUAS suite completed on a run that was allowed to finish:

  cargo test --release -p tuas_boussinesq_solver --lib
  test result: ok. 323 passed; 0 failed; 46 ignored; 0 measured; finished in 2959.84s

That is 49 minutes wall-clock, and it ran while a second unrelated TUAS test binary was executing concurrently on the same machine. So the two earlier ~70-minute runs that were killed were not hung — they were simply not given enough time, which is exactly why this bead insisted a killed run is neither a pass nor a fail.

This also confirms the CLAUDE.md guidance added today: these tests must run in parallel and need a generous timeout or a background run. A default 120 s command timeout is off by a factor of twenty-five.

Note the 46 ignored are pre-existing and were not investigated here. Recommend closing this bead once the maintainer has eyeballed the number, and separately checking whether any of those 46 should be running.

title: Steel material properties valid to 1200 C (high-temperature envelope for HTGR components)
description:
Maintainer request, 2026-08-13 (filed outside active hours; no code work done).

Need steel property correlations that remain valid up to 1200 C, for high-temperature HTGR/HTR-10 component modelling (hot gas duct, SG tubing, vessel internals, accident-envelope temperatures).

Scope when picked up during active hours (search-before-building rule applies -- do NOT write new correlations before checking):
- Check outram-park-fork-offbeat's material-property library (~70 correlations, incl. cladding/structural steels) for existing steel property sets and their stated validity ranges.
- Check tuas_boussinesq_solver's solid material enum (SolidMaterial / steel variants) -- what upper temperature bound do the existing steel correlations actually claim?
- Check tampines and outram-foam-basic-lib thermophysics/solid-thermo layers for a second implementation before adding a third.
Then: extend or add the needed properties (density, specific heat, thermal conductivity, and thermal expansion / mechanical properties if required) with sourced, cited correlations covering up to 1200 C.

Open questions for the maintainer:
- WHICH steel(s)? (e.g. SS316/316H, SS304, Alloy 800H, 2.25Cr-1Mo / Incoloy) -- 1200 C is above the practical service range of most austenitic stainless, so this is likely an accident-envelope requirement rather than a service one.
- Which properties are needed (thermal only, or mechanical/creep too)?
- Data must come from open/public literature per DATA_POLICY.md, catalogued into kovan with its access tier.

Related: op-szmi.6 (replace invented htgr_sim_v1 geometry with sourced HTR-10 values).

notes.content:
SCOPE WIDENED by maintainer, 2026-08-13: the properties must be usable inside htgr_sim_v1, and the sim is currently CRASHING AT LOW TEMPERATURES (see op-m1jz, P1).

So this is no longer a high-temperature-only ask. The needed validity range spans ambient (~20-25 degC) through 1200 degC in one continuous, non-panicking correlation set. When selecting sources and correlations, check the LOW end explicitly -- that is what is breaking today; 1200 degC is the headroom requirement.
notes.author: teddy0@arch-aftershock-rapid-glass-S267454

notes.content:
CORRECTION, 2026-08-13 07:2x -- disregard the previous note claiming the LOW end (ambient) is what breaks. That was my wrong inference. Real trace is on op-m1jz.

The actual failure is the UPPER bound: the solid steel correlation used by htgr_sim_v1's hot gas duct / circulator tops out around 700 degC and throws ThermophysicalPropertyTemperatureRangeError above it. HTGR hot-leg helium runs ~750-950 degC, so the existing range is unfit for purpose.

So this bead is back to being exactly what it said originally -- HIGH-temperature properties, to 1200 degC -- and it is now on the critical path for a P1 crash rather than being forward-looking headroom. Priority raised accordingly.

The specific consumer to satisfy first: whichever SolidMaterial variant htgr_sim_v1 assigns to the hot gas duct and circulator.
notes.author: teddy0@arch-aftershock-rapid-glass-S267454

notes.content:
DONE 2026-08-13, pushed on develop (f565d31b, wired at 3acc9536).
SolidMaterial::SteelSS304LHighTemp, Kim ANL-75-55 solid-region equations over 300-1700 K -- comfortably past the
1200 degC = 1473 K this bead asked for. Verified against Kim's own published tables, 15 points each: density vs
Table 7 max deviation 0.0061%, cp vs Table 2 0.0341%, k vs Table 10 0.0370%, enthalpy vs Table 2 0.0049 cal/g,
enthalpy<->temperature round trip worst 4.5e-13 K.
Honest about its own limits: 300-1600 K is measured-data-backed, 1600-1700 K is Kim's extrapolation into the melting
range, and that distinction is in the docs. Out-of-range still ERRORS -- nothing clamped, 299 K and 1701 K both
asserted rejected. The old SteelSS304L is byte-unchanged so the CIET regression tests are untouched.
This is VERIFICATION against the source, not validation -- no independent 304L measurements, no human review.

tampines-steam-tables: hs-flash brackets back off 100 MPa by 1e-4 MPa — likely an op-cv1c workaround
description:
Found 2026-08-11 during the op-cv1c range-literal audit.

src/interfaces/functional_programming/hs_flash_eqm/mod.rs uses
  let upper_bound_pressure = Pressure::new::<megapascal>(100.0 - 1.0e-4);
at 8 sites (lines ~504, 532, 578, 605, 630, 673, 750, 800) and one 100.0 - 1.0e-3 (line ~945) as the upper bracket of its (h,s) iterative solve.

Now that region_fwd_eqn_single_phase accepts exactly 100 MPa (op-cv1c), those epsilon backoffs are very likely vestigial workarounds for the router panic: the (h,s) solver could not evaluate h_ps_eqm at exactly 100 MPa without tripping it. Consequence today: the (h,s) envelope is silently 100 Pa narrower than IF97's, so states in the last 100 Pa below the ceiling are rejected with 'enthalpy too high for hs flash'.

NOT changed by op-cv1c's fix — deliberately out of scope, because these are iterative-solver brackets, not region-router range literals, and widening them needs its own verification run against the (h,s) tables.

SUGGESTED WORK: widen to exactly 100.0 MPa, then re-run cargo test --release -p tampines-steam-tables --lib hs_flash and record the result. Related: hs_flash_steam_table::single_phase_table_1000_bar currently panics because the hs flash produces p = 100000837.65614447 Pa (above the ceiling), which is a separate overshoot bug in the same solver.

description:
Maintainer decision 2026-08-14, taken with the consequence stated. This script is the reproducibility artifact for the Annals of Nuclear Energy submission; its own docstring says it is kept BYTE-IDENTICAL with a twin in the paper's src/results_and_discussion/kloc_accounting/ 'so that diff is a sufficient check'.

THE CONSEQUENCE, RECORDED ONCE AND NOT RE-ARGUED: porting raises a journal reader's reproduction bar from 'python3 kloc_accounting.py' to 'build a 40-crate Rust workspace', and breaks the byte-identical diff with the manuscript. The maintainer was shown this and chose the full port anyway. Whoever does the work should make sure the manuscript side is updated in the same window, or the paper will cite a script that no longer exists.

WHAT IT DOES (1,454 lines, inventory taken 2026-08-14):
  Repo resolution + GitHub cloning   repo_url, find_repo, ensure_vendor, clone_missing, resolve  -- NETWORK
  Git archaeology                    git, ref_exists, select_ref, active_days, head_date
  Materialisation                    materialize -- git archive piped into tarfile extraction
  Line counting                      strip_rust_comments, rust_files, count_lines
  Measurement                        measure_repo, measure_baseline, measure_agentic, report_peak
  Console report                     report, fmt
  CSV output                         write_csvs -> baseline_repositories.csv, agentic_crates.csv
  LaTeX tables                       baseline_table_tex, rate_table_tex, agentic_table_tex, write_latex_tables
  Figure                             make_figure -> fig_kloc_productivity.png (matplotlib, Agg, 200 dpi)

PLACEMENT: kovan-metrics. It is repository accounting, which is exactly what that crate already does for 'kovan historian' and 'kovan tokens'. CLI surface as 'kovan kloc'.

FIGURE DECISION: emit hand-rolled SVG, not a raster PNG. No plotting crate is in [workspace.dependencies] and adding one buys a dependency whose font metrics and rasterisation vary by version -- the opposite of deterministic. The figure is two stacked horizontal bar charts with text labels and a light x-grid; that is straightforward SVG. Vector also suits a LaTeX manuscript better than a 200-dpi PNG. NOTE this visibly changes the artifact in the paper.

PARITY IS MANDATORY, per the 'no Python for docs or accounting' hard rule: run the Python FIRST, commit its CSV and .tex outputs, then port, then diff. op-yz7b shipped without a parity gate and that is recorded as a known weakness; do not repeat it. The figure cannot be diffed byte-for-byte across a format change -- compare the underlying numbers instead, and eyeball the rendering.

NETWORK CAVEAT: clone_missing fetches from GitHub. kovan is offline-by-charter, so the cloning path must be explicitly opt-in and desktop-scope, in kovan-cli rather than kovan-metrics -- the same split used for 'kovan setup' and 'kovan api-docs'.

description: root@vm
title: root@vm
Energy-equation BCs were zero-gradient on both sides — audit every fluid array for the same class of defect
description:
MAINTAINER-CAUGHT DEFECT, 2026-08-12. Logged because the failure mode matters more than the instance.

WHAT WAS REPORTED (by agents, all measured and true): TampinesSteamArray::set_inlet_enthalpy has no effect; FvMatrix::solve returns a field with zero-gradient boundaries, and step() re-stamps the BC template for u and p but not for he. Fix briefed as 'restamp the he BC after each solve'.

WHAT WAS ACTUALLY WRONG (maintainer): the energy equation had ZERO-GRADIENT BOUNDARIES ON BOTH SIDES, which is a basic CFD error. Restamping restores the value while leaving the formulation wrong.

- A zero-gradient inlet gives h_face = h_cell0, so advective influx is mdot*h_cell0 -- the domain advects in ITS OWN enthalpy. Self-referential; the interior is structurally indifferent to what flows in.
- Zero-gradient at both ends means no boundary through which energy can enter or leave, so mdot*(h_out - h_in) = Q cannot be posed.
- CORRECT: fixedValue (Dirichlet) at the inlet; inletOutlet at the outlet -- mixed, keyed on face-flux sign, degenerating to zeroGradient on outflow and clamping to inletValue on inflow.

WHY PLAIN ZEROGRADIENT AT THE OUTLET IS NOT ENOUGH HERE: it is only safe while flow never reverses, and this workspace reverses routinely. Edwards blowdown flashes and reverses; natural circulation reverses at start-up and stagnation; a counter-flow exchanger has its two outlets at opposite ends.

SCOPE OF THE AUDIT THIS IMPLIES -- do not assume it is limited to the enthalpy equation or to these two arrays:
1. Every field solved on these arrays (u, p, he, and any scalar added later): name each boundary condition and justify it physically. 'Whatever FvMatrix::solve defaulted to' is not a boundary condition.
2. Both TampinesSteamArray and OPCPFluidArray, since they are sibling ports and both were affected.
3. tuas_boussinesq_solver's FluidArray and SolidColumn, which share the lineage and have not been checked.
4. Any other consumer of FvMatrix::solve -- the zero-gradient default is the shared root, so the defect can recur anywhere the caller forgets.

TESTS THAT WOULD HAVE CAUGHT IT, and which should exist going forward:
- GLOBAL ENERGY BALANCE: mdot*(h_out - h_in) == lateral/source power + d(stored)/dt, asserted at steady state AND through a transient. Catches every boundary defect of this class, including unknown ones. A per-setter test only catches the one already known about.
- REVERSAL TEST: drive a flow reversal and assert enthalpy stays bounded. A forward-flow-only test passes identically with a wrong outlet BC and proves nothing.

PROCESS NOTE, deliberately recorded: the symptom-level diagnosis passed every check an AI would think to run, because the tests were written against the same flawed mental model as the code. This is the concrete instance behind RESPONSIBLE_USE.md's rule that AI output is untrusted draft material until a human reviews it. Human domain expertise caught it; three rounds of AI briefing did not.

title: outram-foam-basic-lib: hybrid wgpu/multi-CPU backend for the numerical-math kernels
description:
Filed after hours (2026-08-11 23:55 +08) as a record only, per the CLAUDE.md
working-hours guardrail. No code was written and none should be until the next
active window.

## Ask

Give `outram-foam-basic-lib`'s numerical-math kernels an optional **hybrid
execution backend**: the same API can run serial, multi-CPU (rayon), or on the
GPU (wgpu), chosen at run time, with the serial CPU path always present as the
reference implementation.

Scope named by the maintainer:

- root finding
- golden-ratio (golden-section) search / 1-D minimisation
- matrix solutions (LDU + Krylov + dense)
- numerical integration
- numerical differentiation

## Why here

These are Layer 1-3 building blocks (`polynomial/`, `math/`, `matrix/`,
`krylov/`, `ldu_matrix/`, `ode/`), so every solver crate above
(`outram-foam-appbuilder-lib`, `outram-foam-turbulence-lib`, `tampines`,
GeN-Foam) inherits the acceleration without its own GPU code. The workspace
already has a wgpu precedent in `njoy-outram-park-fork` (Faddeeva/WMP kernels)
and `outram-mc-libs` (`op-u6s`, `op-9s8`), so the backend-enum + CPU-fallback
shape is established rather than novel.

## Constraints that bind this work

- **Hybrid means dispatch, not two APIs.** One public entry point per kernel;
  the backend is a parameter. The batch size / problem size decides whether GPU
  dispatch is worth the transfer, and that policy is explicit and documented,
  not hidden.
- **Enum dispatch, no trait objects, no `Box`, no lifetime params** (workspace
  Rust design rules). `ComputeBackend { Serial, CpuMulti, Gpu }`.
- **Android/Termux hard rule.** wgpu and any GPU-only test/example must be
  target-gated so `cargo check -p outram-foam-basic-lib --all-targets --target
  aarch64-linux-android` still passes and a native Termux build still works.
  Default features must stay Android-clean. Relates to epic `op-zfr`.
- **`uom` typing is not to be stripped** to get data onto the GPU. Convert at
  the buffer boundary and convert back; the public signature stays typed.
- **CPU is the oracle.** Every GPU kernel needs a parity gate against the
  serial CPU path with a stated tolerance, and the docs must carry both the
  methodology and the measured numbers (workspace V&V documentation rule). f32
  GPU accuracy is a known open question elsewhere in the workspace (`op-0nh`)
  — do not assume f64 on the GPU.
- **No human V&V is claimed** by any of this until the maintainer signs off.

notes.content: Maintainer decision, 2026-08-12: f32 GPU accuracy accepted for now, to be carried as a documented caveat in each kernel's docs and in the crate README rather than solved. See the note on op-yvj.4.7 for what the caveat must state. Also confirmed: the batched/lane-per-cell formulation is the right shape for these kernels -- batch N independent problems, keep single-problem solves serial.

notes.author: root@vm

notes.content:
Closed as GitHub #17. All 8 children done, and — checking scope rather than just the count — the children DID cover the epic's full named scope: root finding (.2), golden-section (.3), matrix solutions (.4), integration (.5), differentiation (.6), plus the dispatch layer (.1), gates (.7) and co-execution (.8).

BUT the epic's stated ambition is only PARTLY realised, and closing it should not be read as claiming otherwise.

The ask was 'the same API can run serial, multi-CPU, or on the GPU'. That is true for the data-parallel kernels — LDU SpMV, axpy, scale, dot, norm_l1, and closed-form linear/quadratic polynomial roots all have real WGSL kernels. It is NOT true, and cannot be through the current API, for four of the five named families: root finding (iterative), golden-section, integration, and differentiation all take their objective as a Rust closure, which cannot be shipped to a WGSL shader. Those kernels run serial and multi-CPU only.

That was not visible when the epic was written. It is a language boundary rather than unfinished work, and it is recorded once as the crate-wide rule in src/math/parallel/gpu.rs's module header. Whether to add a separate WGSL-objective API is now op-yvj.6, deliberately a decision rather than a task.

Second caveat: no GPU kernel is auto-selected. The crossover sweep found the GPU losing to CpuMulti by 5x-100x at every size from 4k to 4M lanes — but on an Intel iGPU via OpenGL against 32 CPU threads, which is close to the worst case. That measurement is re-opened as op-yvj.5 and could plausibly flip several kernels onto auto-select.

Follow-ups filed so nothing is lost: op-yvj.5 (re-measure on a discrete GPU), op-yvj.6 (WGSL-objective API decision), op-yvj.7 (async dispatch, unblocks co-execution forms 1 and 3), op-yvj.8 (characterise the quadratic kernel near a double root), op-x0n8 (six GpuContext implementations — consolidate?).

No human V&V is claimed for any of it.

description:
Batched **golden-section search** (golden-ratio 1-D minimisation) across the
three backends. There is no golden-section implementation in the crate today —
this is new code, in `src/math/` or a new `src/optimise/`.

Why it is wanted: derivative-free bracketed minimisation of a scalar function
on `[a, b]`, for the cases where a root-find is the wrong tool (minimising a
residual, a limiter blend factor, a property-inversion objective that is not
monotone).

What to deliver:

- Serial reference: classic golden-section with the fixed `(3 - sqrt(5)) / 2`
  contraction, a stated bracketing precondition (unimodal on `[a, b]` — say
  loudly in the doc that a non-unimodal input gives *a* local minimum, not
  *the* minimum), and both absolute and relative interval tolerances.
- **Batched** form: N independent brackets contracted in lockstep. Golden
  section is uniformly convergent and branch-free, so this is one of the
  cleanest GPU fits in the whole epic — the interval count after k iterations
  is identical in every lane.
- Optional Brent-style parabolic-interpolation variant as a CPU-only faster
  path; do **not** put it on the GPU, its branching kills the lockstep
  property that makes the batched version worth doing.

V&V: analytic minima of smooth test functions with known answers, plus the
theoretical contraction rate (interval width should shrink by the golden ratio
per iteration — assert it). Record the measured numbers per the workspace V&V
documentation rule.

outram-foam-basic-lib: matrix solutions on the hybrid backend (vecops, LDU SpMV, BiCGStab/GMRES, preconditioners)
description:
**Matrix solutions** on the hybrid backend. This is the highest-value item in
the epic — the linear solve dominates every FV timestep — and the hardest.

Existing serial code:

- `src/krylov/` — `bicgstab.rs`, `gmres.rs`, `preconditioner.rs`, `vecops.rs`
- `src/ldu_matrix/` — the OpenFOAM LDU sparse form
- `src/matrix/square_matrix.rs` — small dense

What to deliver, in rough dependency order:

1. **`vecops` on the backend** — axpy, dot, norm, scale. Cheap to port,
   immediately reusable, and a dot-product reduction is the honest first test
   of the GPU path. Note that a GPU tree reduction changes summation order, so
   results will differ from the serial path in the last bits; the parity gate
   must be a tolerance, and the tolerance must be stated.
2. **LDU sparse matrix-vector product** on the backend — the inner-loop cost of
   every Krylov iteration. Needs the host-side LDU-to-buffer serialisation
   (owner/neighbour addressing) done once per mesh, not per iteration.
3. **BiCGStab and GMRES drivers** that keep their control flow on the host and
   dispatch only the kernels. Do not try to move the whole Arnoldi loop into
   WGSL on the first pass.
4. **Preconditioners** — diagonal/Jacobi is trivially parallel and should come
   first. DIC/DILU are *sequential by construction*; they do not port directly,
   and the honest options are a block-Jacobi-over-subdomains variant (changes
   the preconditioner, so it changes the iteration count and must be
   re-validated) or keeping them CPU-only. Do not quietly substitute one for
   the other.
5. Dense `SquareMatrix` LU/back-substitution — small, so `CpuMulti` at most;
   flag it explicitly as not a GPU target unless batched over many small
   systems.

Known related work: `op-hzs.9` wants `outram-blender` to consume these sparse
solvers, and `op-ulo.5` notes the symmetric-solver (DIC-PCG / GAMG) seam is
still missing — so a CG path and GAMG are adjacent but out of scope here
unless they land first.

V&V: solve a system with a known analytic solution and a fixed-seed random SPD
system; compare CPU vs GPU residual histories, not just the final answer — a
diverging iteration count is the signal that a preconditioner was silently
changed. Record iteration counts and final residuals with the date.

notes.content:
Partial delivery, 2026-08-12 (active hours, +08): the LDU SpMV and its vector operations landed on the hybrid backend; items 3-5 of this bead (BiCGStab/GMRES drivers, preconditioners, dense SquareMatrix) are NOT done and this bead stays open.

Delivered in crates/outram-foam-basic-lib/src/ldu_matrix/parallel.rs (+ parallel/tests.rs), declared from ldu_matrix/mod.rs:
- HybridLdu: spmv/spmv_into, residual/residual_into, normalised_residual, diagonal_reciprocal(_into), auto_backend, with_matrix.
- LduTopology: the cell-gather (CRS) inversion of the face addressing.
- Free vecops: dot, axpy, norm_l1, norm_l2. Dispatch predicates spmv_backend_for / vecop_backend_for.
- One entry point per operation with ComputeBackend as a parameter; rayon behind the off-by-default 'parallel' feature; CpuMulti resolves to Serial when the feature is off. No GPU kernel: a Gpu request degrades to the best CPU path.

Strategy: cell-gather reformulation, parallel over cells, so each output is written by exactly one thread. Per-cell face lists are stored in ascending face order, which makes the product BITWISE IDENTICAL to LduMatrix::multiply on every backend and at any thread count (verified by to_bits comparison, and at 1/2/4/8 threads). Reductions use fixed 1024-element blocks combined in block order, so they are bitwise identical across backends too, though not to the flat sums in krylov::vecops.

- SpMV crossover ~4096 cells (1.04x/1.02x over two runs); loses at 1728 (0.55x/0.65x); 2.5-3.5x from 32768 cells up. SPMV_MIN_CELLS = 4096, which SUPPORTS the crate-wide CPU_MULTI_MIN_WORK_ITEMS placeholder of 4096 for this kernel.

description: teddy0@arch-aftershock-rapid-glass-S267454
title: teddy0@arch-aftershock-rapid-glass-S267454
outram-foam-basic-lib: numerical integration on the hybrid backend (batched quadrature + ODE ensembles)
description:
**Numerical integration** on the hybrid backend — two distinct things, both
named by the maintainer under one heading, kept separate here because they
parallelise differently.

**(a) Quadrature.** No general quadrature module exists in the crate today.
Add one (`src/math/quadrature.rs` or `src/integration/`):

- Fixed-order Gauss-Legendre and Simpson/trapezoid on `[a, b]`, plus an
  adaptive variant on the CPU.
- The GPU-worthy shape is **N independent integrals evaluated at once** (one
  per cell/face/band), not one integral split across threads. Fixed-order rules
  are branch-free and map cleanly; adaptive subdivision does not — keep
  adaptive CPU-only and say why in the doc.
- A summation-order note is required: a parallel reduction is not
  bit-identical to serial accumulation.

**(b) ODE integration ensembles.** Existing serial code in `src/ode/` —
`euler.rs`, `rkf45.rs`, `rosenbrock23.rs`, `integrator.rs`.

- The parallel shape is an **ensemble**: N independent IVPs advanced together
  (per-cell chemistry/thermo relaxation, particle histories). One stiff ODE is
  inherently sequential in time and must stay serial.
- `rkf45` is adaptive-step, so an ensemble on the GPU either runs lockstep at
  the smallest step in the batch (wasteful but simple) or needs per-lane step
  control (correct but divergent). Pick one deliberately, document the choice,
  and measure the cost.
- `rosenbrock23` needs a Jacobian per lane — depends on the numerical
  differentiation work in the sibling bead.

V&V: integrals with closed-form values (polynomials exact to the Gauss order,
a Gaussian, a log singularity for the adaptive path); ODEs with analytic
solutions plus an order-of-convergence check that the observed order matches
the method's theoretical order. Record measured errors and the date.

outram-foam-basic-lib: numerical differentiation on the hybrid backend (finite differences + batched Jacobians)
description:
**Numerical differentiation** on the hybrid backend.

Note the distinction up front, because the crate already has one of these:
`src/fv_operators/` implements *spatial* FV gradient/divergence/laplacian over
a mesh. This bead is about **general-purpose numerical differentiation of a
supplied function** — the derivative and Jacobian machinery that root finders,
Rosenbrock ODE integrators, and sensitivity work need. Do not duplicate the FV
operators; cross-reference them in the docs so a reader knows which is which.

What to deliver:

- Finite differences: forward, backward, central, and a Richardson-extrapolated
  variant, with a documented step-size rule (the `sqrt(eps) * scale` trade-off
  between truncation and round-off error) rather than a hard-coded `h`.
- **Batched derivative evaluation** — N independent points, the GPU-worthy
  shape.
- **Jacobian assembly** for an N-dimensional function: N+1 (forward) or 2N
  (central) evaluations, all independent, which is the genuinely useful
  parallel win here and the direct feeder for `rosenbrock23` and for
  multi-dimensional Newton in the root-finding bead.
- Optional, only if it stays simple: forward-mode dual-number autodiff as an
  exact alternative to finite differences for functions written in-crate. If it
  starts pulling in a dependency or generic machinery that raises the reader's
  context load, drop it — the human-interface-layer rule outranks the
  convenience.
- **`uom` care**: a derivative changes dimension (`d(enthalpy)/d(temperature)`
  is a heat capacity). Do not solve this by dropping to raw `f64` in the public
  signature. If the generic form cannot be typed cleanly, prefer a small number
  of concrete typed wrappers over a generic one nobody can read.

V&V: analytic derivatives of smooth test functions; verify the observed
convergence order versus `h` matches theory (1st order forward, 2nd central)
and that the round-off floor appears where the step-size rule predicts. Record
the measured numbers.

outram-foam-basic-lib: CPU-vs-GPU parity gates + crossover benchmarks for the hybrid math kernels
description:
The gate that makes the rest of `op-yvj.4` trustworthy. Blocked by every
kernel bead; nothing in the epic may be described as working until this passes.

**Parity gate.** For every kernel added under this epic, a test that runs the
same problem through `Serial`, `CpuMulti`, and `Gpu` and compares:

- `Serial` vs `CpuMulti` should agree to near machine precision **unless** a
  reduction reorders summation — in which case say so and use a stated
  tolerance, do not just widen it silently.
- `Serial` vs `Gpu` needs an explicit tolerance justified by the precision the
  kernel actually runs at. **Do not assume f64 on the GPU** — many adapters
  give f32 for compute, and f32 accuracy across a full parameter range is
  already an open human-review question elsewhere in this workspace
  (`op-0nh`, Faddeeva). State the precision and the measured error, per kernel.
- For iterative solvers, compare **residual histories and iteration counts**,
  not just the final answer. A changed preconditioner shows up as a different
  iteration count long before it shows up as a wrong answer.

**Benchmarks.** Measure, do not assert, that the GPU path is actually faster:
report the crossover problem size per kernel, including the host-device
transfer, and record the hardware it was measured on. If a kernel never beats
`CpuMulti` at realistic sizes, that is a legitimate result — write it down and
leave the kernel off the auto-select policy rather than shipping a slower
default.

**Documentation** (workspace V&V rule — methodology *and* results): each gate's
doc comment states what is computed, the reference, the inputs, the pass
criterion, and then the actual measured numbers with the date and the hardware.

**No human V&V is claimed by any of this.** These are automated verification
gates written by an AI-assisted draft process; the crate README's
`## Bookkeeping status` axes stay ❌ until the maintainer personally signs off.

CI note: GPU tests must skip cleanly (not fail) on a host with no adapter, and
must not run at all on Android/Termux.

notes.content: Maintainer decision, 2026-08-12: f32 on the GPU is ACCEPTED for now. Do not block this epic on f64 GPU support or on the op-0nh Faddeeva f32 accuracy review. Requirement is a DOCUMENTED CAVEAT, not a fix: every GPU kernel's doc comment must state (a) the precision it actually runs at, (b) the measured max/RMS deviation from the f64 serial CPU oracle on the stated test problem, and (c) that the GPU path is therefore not the reference result. The parity-gate tolerances are set to pass at f32 deliberately -- that is the maintainer's call, not a loosened tolerance of convenience. Iterative solvers keep the stricter check: a changed ITERATION COUNT or residual history is a real defect even at f32, and must not be waved through as precision noise. Revisit if a validation case is ever gated on GPU output.

notes.content:
MEASURED CROSSOVER for the field-algebra kernels (fields::parallel), 2026-08-12, 4 logical cores, --release --features parallel.

FINDING: compute::CPU_MULTI_MIN_WORK_ITEMS = 4096 is FAR TOO LOW for these kernels. It is a placeholder I wrote without measurement, and measuring it shows it would make callers SLOWER, not faster.

c = a + b, best of 9 after 2 warm-ups, --test-threads=1, least-contended of 10 sweeps:

  n          serial      CpuMulti    speedup
  1024       0.43 us     7.59 us     0.06x
  4096       1.89 us     11.07 us    0.17x   <-- at the current placeholder: ~6x SLOWER
  16384      5.99 us     23.11 us    0.26x
  65536      56.27 us    30.39 us    1.85x
  131072     117.77 us   49.87 us    2.36x
  262144     239.65 us   89.52 us    2.68x
  1048576    2001.64 us  437.34 us   4.58x

Cause: these kernels are memory-bandwidth bound at 1-2 flops/element, so thread overhead dominates far longer than for compute-dense work.

THE CROSSOVER IS A BAND, NOT A POINT. Shared virtualised host: serial repeatable to <5%, parallel varies up to 4x run to run. Win counts over 10 sweeps: <=16384 -> 0/10; 65536 -> 4/10; 131072 -> 6/10; 262144 -> 9/10; 1048576 -> 10/10. Honest statement: crossover lies between 65536 and 262144 on this host and cannot be pinned further.

fields::parallel::field_parallel_crossover() therefore overrides the global constant at 131072 (majority winner), using the override mechanism compute.rs's own docs sanction. Losing at 131072 costs tens of microseconds; setting 262144 would forfeit a measured 1.3x-2.4x.

CAVEAT: one shared virtualised 4-core sandbox. Re-measure on real hardware before trusting 131072.

Kernel speedups at n=1048576 (representative of 4 runs): add 2.75x, axpy 2.49x, pointwise_mul 3.82x, sum 2.95x, l2_norm 2.70x, dot 2.56x, axpy_assign 3.23x. Range across runs 2.5x-4.3x.

REDUCTION DETERMINISM (relevant to this bead's parity-gate criteria): fixed-chunk tree reduction, REDUCTION_CHUNK=4096, chunks summed in index order. Bit-reproducible run to run (32/32 identical) AND identical across thread counts (pools of 1,2,3,4,7,8 all bitwise equal). NOT bit-equal to Serial: measured worst-case relative deviation 7.857e-14 (vol_integral); sum 5.690e-14, dot 7.189e-15, l2_norm 6.785e-15. Asserted tolerance 1e-11. min/max ARE bit-identical to serial. Element-wise kernels are bit-identical to Serial on every backend and size.

GPU: no field kernel exists; ComputeBackend::Gpu routes to the best CPU path, documented rather than silently pretended. The Serial-vs-Gpu half of this bead's parity gate is therefore still entirely open for this module.
notes.author: root@vm

notes.content:
MEASURED CROSSOVERS for the LDU kernels (ldu_matrix::parallel), 2026-08-12, available_parallelism()=4, release --features parallel, idle machine.

HEADLINE: there must NOT be one crate-wide CPU_MULTI_MIN_WORK_ITEMS. The two kernel families measured so far want thresholds 64x apart, and a single number is wrong for at least one of them.

SpMV, time per call, best of 7 samples, two independent runs:

  cells     serial      CpuMulti    speedup   repeat
  1000      20.24 us    20.08 us    1.01x     1.00x
  1728      34.55 us    63.28 us    0.55x     0.65x
  2744      55.67 us    69.32 us    0.80x     1.21x
  4096      83.67 us    80.61 us    1.04x     1.02x   <-- break-even
  8000      165.60 us   114.06 us   1.45x     2.02x
  32768     690.40 us   277.86 us   2.48x     2.03x
  512000    13338 us    4822 us     2.77x     3.48x

For SpMV the placeholder 4096 is CORRECT -- it is precisely where the parallel path stops losing. SPMV_MIN_CELLS = 4096.

For vector ops 4096 is badly wrong: dot only wins from ~65536; axpy is still break-even at 262144 (1.87x one run, 1.00x the other) and reliable only from ~1048576. At 4096 elements axpy on 4 threads is 0.05x -- TWENTY TIMES SLOWER. VECOP_MIN_ELEMENTS = 262144.

Compare the field-algebra measurement already filed on this bead: those memory-bound kernels wanted 131072. So three kernel families, three different answers (4096 / 131072 / 262144). The right resolution for this bead is per-kernel measured constants with compute.rs's global as a floor, not a single tuned number.

THREAD SCALING, 262144 cells: 1 -> 6487 us, 2 -> 3481 us (1.86x), 4 -> 2322 us (2.79x), 8 -> 1830 us (3.54x). Output asserted BITWISE IDENTICAL at every thread count. The >3x on 4 cores is superlinear and reproducible; a cache hypothesis is documented in the code and explicitly labelled UNCONFIRMED.

PARITY (this bead's Serial-vs-CpuMulti criterion): spmv, residual, diagonal_reciprocal and axpy are BIT-FOR-BIT IDENTICAL to the serial path, not merely within tolerance -- the cell-gather stores each cell's incident faces in ascending face index, which is the order the serial scatter reaches them. Verified via to_bits() at 24/512/32768 cells, symmetric and asymmetric, at 1/2/4/8 threads. Reductions are bitwise identical across backends and thread counts but not equal to the flat krylov::vecops sums: dot worst 2.3744e-13 raw at n=4194304 (7.9476e-17 scaled by sum|a_i b_i|; the raw figure inflates because the test vectors cancel to ~150), normalised_residual 7.6520e-15 (~34 ulp), norm_l1 8.9257e-14, norm_l2 2.4996e-15.

Serial-vs-Gpu parity remains ENTIRELY OPEN for this module: there is no GPU LDU kernel, and ComputeBackend::Gpu degrades to the best CPU path (asserted in a test so it cannot silently claim the GPU).

CAVEATS: one machine, 4 cores, idle. Not measured on Android hardware or a many-core server. Under load the SpMV break-even moves right -- an earlier contended run put 4096 cells at 0.72x. norm_l1/norm_l2 were not separately benchmarked; they inherit dot's floor by assumption.

notes.content:
MEASURED CROSSOVER for batched root finding (math::parallel), 2026-08-12, available_parallelism()=4, release --features parallel, idle, best of 7, two independent runs.

This is the FOURTH kernel family measured and it moves in the OPPOSITE direction to the field kernels: 256, i.e. 16x BELOW the CPU_MULTI_MIN_WORK_ITEMS placeholder of 4096, because root finding is compute-dense per lane where field algebra is memory-bound.

Iterative solve, wall clock per whole batch (cheap residual | costly residual):

  problems   serial      multi       speedup      serial      multi       speedup
  64         12.99 us    45.16 us    0.29x        42.85 us    62.99 us    0.68x
  128        25.96 us    57.24 us    0.45x        84.88 us    86.65 us    0.98x
  256        52.94 us    42.79 us    1.24x        175.37 us   126.70 us   1.38x   <-- crossover
  1024       201.83 us   127.52 us   1.58x        695.26 us   284.70 us   2.44x
  65536      13730.89 us 5071.05 us  2.71x        45778.24 us 16260.96 us 2.82x

ROOT_BATCH_MIN_PROBLEMS = 256, the smallest size at which neither closure lost in either run. Closed-form cubics cross at 1024 (POLY_ROOTS_MIN_EQUATIONS); at 256 the two paths are exactly break-even because POLY_BLOCK is 256 and rayon never splits. Per-lane costs are comparable (~153 ns/cubic vs ~209 ns/cheap iterative lane), so the 4x gap between those two constants is a conservative reading of a noisy shallow break-even, NOT a structural claim.

RUNNING TALLY for this bead: 256 (root finding) / 4096 (LDU SpMV) / 131072 (field algebra) / 262144 (LDU vecops). A 1024x spread, with the crate-wide placeholder sitting in the middle and wrong at both ends.

AND A HARDER PROBLEM FOR THIS BEAD: the iterative root-finding crossover depends on the CALLER'S RESIDUAL COST, which the crate cannot know -- the cheap and costly closures above differ by roughly 3.3x in serial time with identical kernel code. So 'measure the crossover per kernel' is not sufficient for this family; the constant is a default, and a caller with an expensive residual should override it. Worth deciding, for this bead, whether the API should let a caller supply a measured threshold rather than inheriting a constant.

PARITY (this bead's Serial-vs-CpuMulti criterion): BITWISE IDENTICAL at 1/2/4/8 rayon workers on a deliberately imbalanced 2048-lane batch, for Brent, bisection, Newton and the cubic kernel -- every observable field (iterate, residual, bracket width, iteration count, status) compared via to_bits(). This is easier here than for ldu_matrix because a root batch has no cross-lane arithmetic and therefore no association to perturb. One documented caveat the module cannot defend against: a caller closure that is not a pure function of (i, x) breaks it.

Thread scaling, 65536 imbalanced lanes: serial 19322.52 us; 1 worker 0.94x, 2 workers 1.91x, 4 workers 2.73x (3.66x on the repeat), 8 workers 2.64x (3.57x). No gain past core count -- the compute-bound signature, in contrast to the superlinear >3x seen on 4 cores for SpMV.

ANALYTIC-ORACLE V&V: cubic roots 1/2/3 recovered EXACTLY (0.000000e0 error) by bisection, Brent and Newton. Worst |x - sqrt(k)| over 64 lanes: 1.776357e-15 (Brent), 8.881784e-16 (Newton). Mean iterations 7.73 Newton vs 13.14 Brent. Cubic batch worst residual 3.979039e-13 over 12288 real roots, worst root displacement 2.079981e-10 (near-coincident random root triples -- ill-conditioning, documented). Quadratic worst residual 7.105427e-15.

Serial-vs-Gpu parity remains ENTIRELY OPEN for this module: no GPU kernel, Gpu degrades to the best CPU path.

CAVEATS: one machine, 4 cores, idle, two runs. Not measured on Android/Termux or a many-core server. POLY_ROOTS_MIN_EQUATIONS was measured with CUBICS ONLY; quadratic and linear are cheaper per lane so they cross over later and inherit the floor as an assumption. POLY_BLOCK=256 is a granularity floor that was not swept, only verified not to change a value.

notes.content:
END-TO-END SOLVER SPEED-UP, MEASURED at last — 2026-08-13. This is the first evidence in epic op-yvj.4 that any of it makes a REAL SOLVE faster; everything before this was micro-benchmarks. Fifth independent run, available_parallelism()=4, /proc/loadavg 1.53 0.85 0.37 rising to 1.67 1.00 0.45, best of 5. Asymmetric 7-point stencil.

  cells     Jacobi ser->par (ms)    speedup    ILU(0) ser->par (ms)    speedup
  4096      12.675 -> 18.785        0.67x LOSS  6.658 -> 11.075        0.60x LOSS
  32768     104.810 -> 61.699       1.70x       54.984 -> 42.558       1.29x
  512000    2024.812 -> 815.677     2.48x       1013.883 -> 676.072    1.50x

*** THE KERNEL'S CROSSOVER IS NOT THE SOLVER'S CROSSOVER. *** At 4096 cells -- EXACTLY SPMV_MIN_CELLS, the constant this bead recorded as SpMV's measured break-even -- the full solve LOSES, in all five runs. The solve only starts winning around 13000 cells. A kernel threshold measured in isolation does not transfer to the consumer that calls it, because the consumer also pays for the vector operations, the preconditioner and the residual bookkeeping, each with its own scaling. This is the most actionable thing on this bead: per-kernel constants are necessary but NOT sufficient, and a caller needs its own crossover.

ILU(0) IS THE BRAKE, quantified rather than asserted. Both phases have loop-carried dependence and are not parallelised. Triangular solves are 29-46% of serial solve time (four runs: 34.1 / 37.4 / 37.3 / 40.7%), which by Amdahl caps attainable speed-up at 1.7-2.1x on 4 cores. Measured 1.50x sits BELOW that cap, so ILU(0) dominates but is not the only limit. Factorisation costs a further 23.8% of one serial solve per coefficient update.

REDUCTION-ORDER SAFETY, now measured instead of argued. The concern recorded earlier on this bead was that ldu_matrix::parallel's blocked dot is not bit-equal to krylov::vecops' flat sum (worst 2.3744e-13) and could flip an iteration count near a convergence tolerance. Swept 216 solve pairs -- 3 sizes x 3 dominances x 3 seeds x 4 tolerances (1e-6 to 1e-12) x 2 solvers: ZERO iteration-count flips. GMRES was included and had never been compared before; it is the more exposed solver, with roughly 4x the reductions per iteration and a stopping test that reads a Givens recurrence rather than a fresh norm. Max relative residual difference 2.220e-4, which sounds alarming but is an ABSOLUTE difference of ~1.9e-16 on a residual of 8.6e-13. The BiCGStab worst case stopped at 0.86x its own tolerance -- about as near the deciding boundary as the grid reaches -- and still did not flip. Zero flips in 216 pairs bounds the rate at roughly 1-in-216 for systems of this kind; it is NOT proof that no system flips.

Serial vs CpuMulti is BIT-EXACT for both solvers including every residual-history entry, not merely the final answer.

TWO SELF-CORRECTIONS the agent made from its own printed output, worth recording because they are the failure mode this epic keeps hitting: a predecessor's claim that 'GMRES gains less than BiCGStab at every size tested' is FALSE at 4096 cells, where GMRES was ahead (0.78x vs 0.67x) -- now restricted to >=32768 cells; and an uncomputed range '23.8-24.7% across four runs' had been written into preconditioner.rs and was replaced with the single figure actually paired.

CAVEATS: one virtualised 4-core host that never idles (bn daemon ~37% of a core); one matrix family; f64 CPU only. There is NO GPU kernel in this path at all, so nothing here speaks to ComputeBackend::Gpu and the Serial-vs-Gpu half of this bead remains entirely open. Absolute milliseconds are not comparable across sessions -- serial times shifted ~2x between container restarts at LOWER load -- so only ratios should be read.

Closed as GitHub #16. Gate exists, runs, and has real numbers.

Parity: tests/hybrid_parity.rs — an integration test, so it sees only the public surface. gate_parity_serial_vs_cpu_multi / _vs_gpu compare bitwise (f64::to_bits) for kernels claiming bitwise identity and by stated tolerance for those that legitimately re-associate, with the class recorded per kernel in ParityClass so the two cannot be confused. METHODOLOGICAL CORRECTION worth keeping: the harness's first version reported deviations of exactly 0.00e0 for four of five kernels. That was not a good result — the test data were dyadic fractions, exactly representable in f32, so the comparison measured nothing. Non-dyadic inputs are now used and are what make the figures real. Caveat on the crossover conclusion: the only usable adapter was an Intel iGPU on the OpenGL backend against 32 CPU threads (the box's RTX A5000 had no kernel driver loaded). Re-running on a working discrete GPU is the obvious next measurement.

title: teddy0@arch-aftershock-rapid-glass-S267454
outram-foam-basic-lib: Hybrid co-execution — run CpuMulti and Gpu concurrently on one batch (split ratio, determinism, mixed precision)
description:
Maintainer question, 2026-08-12: can multi-core CPU run *alongside* the GPU,
rather than being only a fallback? Yes — recorded here for the next active
window. Three distinct forms, worth separating because they have different
costs:

**1. Task-level concurrency (different kernels at once).** The CPU runs the
work the GPU is bad at while the GPU runs the batched kernels. The concrete win
in this crate is the linear solve: DIC/DILU preconditioning is sequential by
construction (`op-yvj.4.4`), so it can overlap the GPU's SpMV/vecops instead of
idling. Needs the wgpu dispatch to be genuinely async (submit, keep working,
map results later) rather than submit-and-block.

**2. Data-level co-execution (split one batch).** For the embarrassingly
parallel kernels — batched root finding, golden section, quadrature, Jacobian
columns — hand a fraction of the lanes to rayon and the rest to the GPU. This
is the direct answer to the question and the easiest real speedup. Two ways to
pick the split:
   - **static ratio**, tuned per kernel from the crossover benchmarks
     (`op-yvj.4.7`) — deterministic, reproducible;
   - **dynamic work-stealing** in chunks — better load balance on an
     unknown/loaded machine, but the split varies run to run.

**3. Transfer/compute overlap.** CPU works on chunk N while chunk N+1 uploads.
Cheapest form, mostly a scheduling detail of (2).

**Two caveats that must be settled before this is implemented, not after:**

- **Mixed precision within one result.** With f32 accepted on the GPU
  (`op-yvj.4.7`) but f64 on the CPU, a split batch means *lanes computed at
  different precision inside a single output array*. Cell 5 and cell 6 could
  differ in accuracy purely by which side of the split they landed on. That is
  not automatically wrong, but it is surprising, and it must be documented per
  kernel — or the CPU half deliberately run at f32 to match.
- **Reproducibility.** A dynamic split changes how many lanes each side handles
  run to run. For elementwise kernels that is harmless; for anything with a
  **reduction** (dot products, norms, quadrature sums) it reorders the
  summation and the answer changes in the last bits between identical runs.
  Recommendation: default to a **static, deterministic split**, and offer
  work-stealing as an opt-in for throughput runs where bitwise reproducibility
  is not wanted.

Suggested scope: do **not** build this first. Land `op-yvj.4.1` (backend enum)
and at least one batched kernel plus its benchmark, so there are real crossover
numbers to pick a split ratio from. Then this becomes a `Hybrid` selection
policy over the existing `CpuMulti` and `Gpu` paths rather than a fourth
implementation of every kernel.

---

## DECIDED 2026-08-13 (maintainer): uniform f32 in Hybrid

The CPU half runs f32, matching the GPU. Hybrid is an explicitly f32-class
throughput mode; Serial (f64) remains the oracle. This resolves the
mixed-precision caveat above: precision is uniform across one output array
instead of varying with the split ratio.

It does NOT resolve the reproducibility caveat -- f32 addition is
non-associative exactly as f64 is, and with a 24-bit mantissa a varying split
perturbs a reduction ~2^29 times more visibly than at f64. The static
deterministic split remains required.

It introduces a third point: CPU f32 and GPU f32 are the same precision class
but are NOT bitwise identical (WGSL specifies only ULP bounds for
transcendentals, GPU compilers contract a*b+c into FMA, many GPUs flush f32
denormals). The hybrid parity gate must therefore be a per-kernel tolerance
gate at f32 epsilon scale, not a bitwise check.

Per-kernel scoping: root finding (4.2), quadrature (4.5) and elementwise/SpMV
(4.4) may take this deal. Numerical differentiation (4.6) and golden-section
minimisation (4.3) must NOT -- both are cancellation-limited, so f32 costs
central differences 5.8 decimal digits (3.67e-11 -> 2.42e-5) and golden section
4.4 digits on top of an objective-dependent floor that is already ~8 orders
worse than its headline on the choked-flow application.

Full write-up, with the computed f32 floors, is in git at
crates/outram-foam-basic-lib/docs/hybrid-precision-policy.md and summarised in
the src/compute.rs module docs. Written to git deliberately: the bead store has
been dropping acknowledged writes this session.

---

## AMENDED 2026-08-13 (maintainer): coarse-to-fine supersedes the split

For the ITERATIVE kernels the f32 pass produces only the initial guess; the CPU
converges to the final answer at f64. This replaces the split, it is not a
variant of it, and the bead's original framing of pipelining as 'cheapest form,
mostly a scheduling detail of (2)' was wrong -- it is the superior architecture.

Consequences: the output is entirely f64, so precision heterogeneity is gone
outright rather than mitigated, and the f32 accuracy floors govern the guess
rather than the answer. Reproducibility is recovered because RootSettings
converges on a tolerance (x_tol_abs/x_tol_rel/f_tol) rather than a fixed
iteration count -- a deterministic coarse pass gives a bitwise result, a
work-stealing one gives a result reproducible to tolerance but NOT bitwise.

It is also the right division of labour for the hardware, which is the argument
that makes it better rather than merely safer: the coarse phase is uniform
(fixed iteration count per lane, no warp divergence, ideal for SIMT) and the
polish phase is irregular (a different count per lane, ideal for CPU threads).
A data-level split gives both devices a mix of both phases.

Revised per kernel:
- Root finding (4.2) PROMOTED, earlier concern withdrawn. Safe by a property
  the API already guarantees -- RootProblem::guess documents that a non-finite
  or out-of-bracket guess is replaced by the bracket midpoint, 'a performance
  problem, not a correctness problem'. Newton's quadratic convergence turns an
  f32-accurate start (~7 digits) into ~16 digits in 2 iterations vs ~5 from a
  crude bracket. RootProblem::with_guess already exists; no new API needed.
- Golden section (4.3) REINSTATED with one mandatory safeguard. Payoff is ~40%
  not an order of magnitude: linear convergence at 0.618/iteration means
  measured 37.5 total iterations from bracket width 1 to the f64 floor, of
  which the first 16.6 reach the f32 floor -- so the GPU pre-computes 44%.
  MANDATORY: the coarse pass must return a WIDENED BRACKET, not a point.
  Golden section converges into whatever bracket it is handed and never
  re-expands, so a tight bracket around a mislocated optimum is unrecoverable
  -- live risk on G(p), which is flat near its maximum and already located only
  to 0.6-3 Pa at f64.
- Differentiation (4.6) STILL EXCLUDED, different reason: a finite difference
  has no fixed point to converge to, so there is no guess to seed and the f32
  floor lands directly on the answer. Only legitimate coarse use is selecting h
  or the Richardson depth, which is small.

Full write-up with the measured iteration arithmetic is in git at
crates/outram-foam-basic-lib/docs/hybrid-precision-policy.md.

notes.content:
BLOCKED, and not for the reason the bead anticipated. Checked 2026-08-13 before briefing any agent on it.

The bead's own scope note says: do not build this first, land op-yvj.4.1 and at least one batched kernel plus its benchmark so there are real crossover numbers to pick a split ratio from. That precondition is now MET and then some -- op-yvj.4.1 is closed, and seven kernel families have measured crossovers (16 ODE / 32 quadrature / 256 root finding / 256 minimisation / 4096 LDU SpMV / 131072 field algebra / 262144 LDU vecops), plus an end-to-end solver measurement from op-yvj.4.4.

THE ACTUAL BLOCKER: there is NO GPU KERNEL ANYWHERE IN outram-foam-basic-lib. Verified by grep -- no  usage outside compute.rs's adapter probe, and no WGSL/@compute/@workgroup_size anywhere; the two apparent hits are doc-comment prose about WGSL lacking f64. Every landed module routes ComputeBackend::Gpu to the best available CPU path, and each says so in its docs. The cross-cutting parity gate (tests/hybrid_parity.rs) asserts exactly this: all seven dispatch-policy functions are queried for Gpu at n = 2^22 and asserted NEVER to return it.

So co-execution -- 'run CpuMulti and Gpu concurrently on one batch' -- has nothing to co-execute with. A Hybrid split policy dividing lanes between CpuMulti and a Gpu path that itself resolves to CpuMulti would be pure theatre: it would add a split ratio, a determinism caveat and a mixed-precision caveat to a computation that runs entirely on the CPU either way. Building it now would produce code that looks like an optimisation and is not one.

BOTH of the bead's own 'settle before implementing' caveats are also unreachable today for the same reason: mixed precision within one result cannot arise when no lane runs at f32, and the reproducibility question about a dynamic split reordering reductions cannot be measured against a GPU half that does not exist.

WHAT UNBLOCKS IT: a real GPU kernel for at least one embarrassingly-parallel family. op-3ep6 is the nearest candidate (GPU fixed-rule quadrature), filed by the op-yvj.4.5 agent, which noted the real difficulty is the caller-supplied Rust closure rather than the arithmetic -- a WGSL kernel cannot call an arbitrary Rust , so the batched-kernel APIs that take closures are structurally hard to move to the GPU. That is worth settling before op-3ep6 too.

SECOND-ORDER BLOCKER even once a kernel exists: this container HAS NO GPU ADAPTER. compute.rs's probe returns false here, so a GPU kernel could be written but not executed or verified. op-b4a.4.8 already tracks 'validate wgpu dispatch on a real GPU host' workspace-wide. Any GPU work landed from this environment would ship unexecuted, which is exactly what op-0nh (f32 Faddeeva accuracy) is already open about elsewhere.

RECOMMENDATION: leave this bead Todo and do not implement it speculatively. It should be picked up after a GPU kernel exists AND on a host with an adapter. Nothing else in op-yvj.4 depends on it.

notes.content:
Closed as GitHub #18. src/compute/hybrid.rs, commit 2c3c1ac641.

Delivered form 2 (data-level co-execution) — the one this bead called the direct answer and easiest real speedup. SplitPlan is a selection policy over the existing CpuMulti and Gpu paths, containing no numerical code, exactly as specified — not a fourth implementation of every kernel.

Both caveats this bead required be settled BEFORE implementation are settled in the API, not in prose:
- Mixed precision: SplitPlan::precision_note() states per call that leading lanes are f64 and trailing lanes f32 and accuracy is not uniform; CoExecution::MatchGpuPrecision offers uniform f32-grade accuracy for callers who would rather lose good bits than have a seam. Default is NativePrecision — silently degrading correct arithmetic is the worse default.
- Reproducibility: the split is static and deterministic, a pure function of lane count and ratio, no timing/sampling/RNG. Dynamic work-stealing is NOT offered at all rather than offered unused, because the moment it exists someone gets a non-reproducible reduction without reading why.

SplitRatio::Measured resolves to ZERO GPU lanes — that is the measurement, not a placeholder (see op-yvj.4.7). A planner that truthfully says 'do not use the GPU here' is doing its job.

Forms 1 (task-level concurrency) and 3 (transfer/compute overlap) deliberately not implemented: both need genuinely async dispatch, and GpuContext::dispatch currently blocks on readback. Recorded in the module's 'Not implemented, deliberately' section.

Ordering honoured: this bead said not to build before real crossover numbers existed. They exist now, which is what makes the default ratio a measurement instead of a guess.
