description: root@vm
title: teddy0@arch-aftershock-rapid-glass-S267454
outram-foam-basic-lib: re-run the GPU crossover report on a working discrete GPU
description:
The op-yvj.4 crossover conclusion — 'the GPU never beats CpuMulti, keep every kernel off auto-select' — was measured on an Intel iGPU via the OpenGL backend against 32 CPU threads. That is close to the worst case for the GPU and the conclusion should not be treated as final.

The measuring box (snrsi-arch-desktop) has an RTX A5000, but nvidia-smi failed (kernel driver not loaded) and there is no Intel Vulkan ICD installed, so wgpu enumerated only the iGPU on GL. compute::gpu::adapter_score now ranks DiscreteGpu + Vulkan/Metal/DX12 first, so this improves by itself once a driver is present.

Do: install/load a working discrete GPU driver, run
  cargo run --release -p outram-foam-basic-lib --features gpu,parallel --example hybrid_gpu_report
and record the adapter line plus the crossover table.

If any kernel now beats CpuMulti: update its doc comment with the new hardware and figures, add it to gate_gpu_kernels_match_the_oracle, and only then relax gate_gpu_degrades_and_does_not_lie for that one module — the tripwire's failure message spells out this exact procedure.

Also worth re-measuring SplitRatio::Measured in compute::hybrid, which currently resolves to zero GPU lanes for the same reason.

title: outram-foam-basic-lib: decide whether to offer a WGSL-objective API for the closure-bound kernels
description:
The structural finding from op-yvj.4: a Rust closure cannot be shipped to a WGSL shader, and four of the five kernel families take their objective as one — solve_bracketed_batch, solve_newton_batch, golden_section_batch, quadrature_batch, the ODE ensembles, derivative_batch, jacobian_batch.

Every one is a GOOD GPU shape arithmetically. Golden section especially: uniformly convergent, branch-free, identical iteration count per lane. The obstacle is the function-passing mechanism, not the algorithm.

The only way onto the GPU is a SEPARATE entry point taking a WGSL source string instead of a closure. That is a materially different API — the caller writes shader code, loses type checking on the objective, and cannot reuse host helpers — so it is a deliberate design decision, not something to smuggle in under a kernel task. This bead is that decision.

Options: (a) do not do it, keep those kernels CPU-only and say so permanently; (b) a narrow WGSL-objective variant for the one or two kernels that would most benefit; (c) a general mechanism. Recommend deciding (a) vs (b) before writing anything, and note that this only becomes worth doing if the discrete-GPU re-measurement shows the GPU winning at all.

title: outram-foam-basic-lib: async GPU dispatch (unblocks co-execution forms 1 and 3)
description:
compute::gpu::GpuContext::dispatch submits and then blocks on readback. That is why two of the three co-execution forms named in op-yvj.4.8 are unimplemented:
- form 1, task-level concurrency: run the sequential DIC/DILU preconditioner on the CPU while the GPU does SpMV/vecops, instead of the CPU idling. Needs submit-keep-working-map-later.
- form 3, transfer/compute overlap: CPU works chunk N while chunk N+1 uploads.

Deliver: a non-blocking dispatch returning a handle that can be polled or awaited, with the existing blocking dispatch kept as the simple path. Note the readback loop already has to re-poll because a single wait_indefinitely does not guarantee the map callback has fired (see the MAX_POLLS loop) — that machinery is the starting point.

Only worth doing if the discrete-GPU re-measurement shows the GPU is competitive at all.

title: outram-foam-basic-lib: characterise the quadratic root GPU kernel near a double root
description:
math::parallel::gpu::quadratic_roots_batch is documented as max rel 2.85e-7 / RMS 5.70e-8 over 262144 equations — but that measurement used WELL-SEPARATED roots only, and the docs say so explicitly rather than implying a general bound.

The gap matters: QuadraticEqn::roots on the CPU uses an FMA-compensated discriminant precisely for the case where b^2/4 and a*c nearly cancel. WGSL's fma is not guaranteed to be a fused single-rounding operation, so the GPU kernel drops that compensation. The near-degenerate range is therefore exactly where the two paths should diverge most, and it is currently unmeasured. The parity gate is set at 1e-4 rather than at the measured value to leave room for it.

Do: sweep discriminant magnitude from well-separated down to ~0 (e.g. roots separated by 1e-1 down to 1e-7), measure max/RMS relative deviation per band, and either tighten the gate with confidence or document a range where the GPU kernel should not be used.

title: OPCPFluidArray pEqn: compressibility carries drho/dp but no drho/dh -- EOS mass unconserved under strong heating
description:
MEASURED 2026-08-12 in crates/outram-park-fork-coolprop. NOT fixed -- it needs a change to the pressure-equation formulation.

SYMPTOM. The array's stored mass Sum(rho*V) falls by more than the boundary mass fluxes account for whenever there is strong volumetric heating, and the transient global energy balance fails by the enthalpy of exactly that missing mass.

MEASUREMENT (Nitrogen, 8 cells, 1 m, 1e-4 m2, 1 bar, prescribed 1.0 g/s inlet, 200 W uniform source, dt 2e-4 s, 4000 steps = 0.8 s, after a 200-step flow warm-up):
  energy: integral(mdot_in*h_in - mdot_out*h_out + Q) dt = 9.5696 J   vs   d(Sum rho*V*h) = 0.1125 J   -> residual 9.4571 J = 5.9 % of the 160 J delivered
  mass:   integral(mdot_in - mdot_out) dt = 2.761e-7 kg               vs   d(Sum rho*V) = -2.556e-5 kg -> residual 2.584e-5 kg
  ratio:  9.4571 J / 2.584e-5 kg = 366.1 kJ/kg, inside the 311.20-511.2 kJ/kg range the field spans.
So the two residuals are ONE event: the energy that fails to balance is the enthalpy carried by the mass that fails to balance.

CAUSE. step() computes a continuity density rho_cont = rho_old - dt*div(phi), then correct_thermo OVERWRITES self.rho with the EOS density rho(p,h). The pressure equation reconciles them only through its compressibility diagonal psi*V/dt with psi = drho/dp|_h. It carries NO drho/dh|_p term, so the density drop caused by HEATING is never fed back as mass the domain must expel.

RULED OUT BY MEASUREMENT (this is why the cause above is the remaining explanation):
- Not the outlet boundary flux (op-nnqi). Residual unchanged at 9.4571 J by the boundary pressure-correction fix that cut the STEADY boundary residual 113-fold (1.3834 W -> 0.0122 W).
- Not spatial truncation. 9.37 J at n=8, 9.43 J at n=16, 8.65 J at n=32 -- flat under refinement.
- Not an unconverged PIMPLE loop. Identical at 1/2/4/8 outer correctors (9.4571 / 9.4796 / 9.4795 / 9.4795 J; converged by 2). This was a stated prediction and the measurement FALSIFIED it -- recorded here so nobody re-derives the same wrong guess.

WHAT A FIX NEEDS. The enthalpy-driven density change must enter the pressure equation, e.g. an explicit (drho/dh|_p)*(h - h_old)/dt mass source alongside the psi*V/dt diagonal, or a genuinely coupled rho update. That is a pEqn formulation change and was deliberately not slipped in alongside a boundary-condition fix. Note the STEADY balance is unaffected and closes to 0.006 % of Q -- this only bites in a transient with significant density change.

REGRESSION TEST (characterises rather than hides it; asserts the two residuals are the same event, so it fails if anything ELSE starts breaking the balance):
  openfoam_algorithms::rhoPimpleFoam::lateral_coupling::tests::transient_energy_imbalance_is_the_enthalpy_of_the_unconserved_mass

COORDINATION. tampines-steam-tables' TampinesSteamArray shares this pEqn verbatim.

title: LMTD cross remedy: the steady state it imposes is not the plant's operating point (-73.8 K on steam outlet)
description:
Flagged 2026-08-13 by maintainer instruction ('LMTD as last resort, but flag this for future correction').

MEASURED: given the plant's OWN boundary conditions and its calibrated STEAM_GENERATOR_UA_W_PER_K, the zoned-LMTD
remedy's steady solve returns
    duty          9.36 MW   vs 10 MWth        (-6.4%)
    steam outlet  366.2 degC vs published 440 (-73.8 K)
    helium return +30.9 K
So engaging this remedy visibly moves the plant by TENS OF KELVIN -- an order of magnitude more than any other
approximation in htgr_sim_v1 (the substep reduction, by comparison, costs +5.24 K).

CAUSE, understood not guessed: STEAM_GENERATOR_UA_W_PER_K was calibrated against a COUPLED TRANSIENT WITH FEEDWATER
FEEDBACK, not against a fixed-boundary steady solve. A steady solve at that UA therefore does not reproduce the
operating point. This is not a defect in the zoning or the LMTD algebra -- both were verified (duty residual exactly
0, conductance residual 1.540e-12, LMTD and eps-NTU agreeing to 1.332e-12 at C_r -> 0).

FIX OPTIONS: calibrate a separate steady UA for this path, or reconcile the two calibrations so one UA serves both.
The second is preferable but may not be achievable -- the transient calibration has feedwater feedback in the loop
and the steady one does not, so they are not obliged to agree.

UNTIL FIXED: LMTD is the last-resort remedy only, behind Bedok, and any state it produces is indicative only. The
variant's doc comment carries this warning.

Related: op-3lay (the remedy programme), and the note that Bedok is the preferred corrector -- it is verified against
a closed-form eps-NTU reference to 0.086% of span and does not have this problem.

notes.content:
Implemented. crates/kovan/src/digitiser/gui/desktop/pdf_reader.rs:
- New "Select text" tool alongside "Select"/"Draw box", using `kopitiam_pdf::mupdf::page_to_stext` (MuPDF's structured-text model, real per-line device-space bboxes -- not OCR, not pixel-region annotation).
- New free function `select_text_in_rect(page, scale, min, max) -> String`: concatenates the text of every StextLine whose bbox (converted from PDF points to this panel's texture-pixel space by `RENDER_DPI/72.0`, the same scale `rasterize_page` itself applies) intersects the drag rect. Line granularity, not character/glyph granularity -- documented as a deliberate scope cut in the module doc.
- `stext_for_page` caches the current page's `StextPage` (re-extracted on page change only, not kept for every page -- a full-res StextPage is a lot more data per page than a thumbnail texture).
- `text_selection_panel`: shows the last selection with Copy-to-clipboard and "Save as annotation" (folds the selection into the same `annotations` markdown section op-96am's hand-typed notes use).
- 4 new unit tests for `select_text_in_rect` against a hand-built `StextPage` fixture (intersection filtering, the DPI-scale conversion specifically, multi-line join, no-intersection case) -- exercises the real kopitiam_pdf types, not a mock.

Known limitation, disclosed rather than silently assumed away: the device-space-to-pixel-space conversion assumes the page has no rotation quirk beyond what `page_to_stext`'s own `page_mediabox` already handles internally -- not independently verified against `rasterize_page`'s own `page_is_quarter_turned` swap for a rotated page, since no rotated-page test fixture was available in this pass. Flagging this explicitly rather than claiming full verification; worth a real-PDF smoke test with a rotated page if that turns out to matter in practice.

Android rule: the 32-bit targets (armv7, i686) appear never to have been built
description:
Surfaced by the wasm audit (op-okqo.5) on 2026-09-04.

outram-park-mpi had 'const COLL_CONTEXT_OFFSET: usize = 1 << 40', a compile-time overflow on ANY 32-bit target. It was caught by wasm32 — but armv7-linux-androideabi and i686-linux-android are also 32-bit and would have failed identically.

The workspace CLAUDE.md Android rule says every crate's non-GUI library must compile for 'aarch64-linux-android and the armv7/x86_64 emulator targets', but the acceptance command it gives names only aarch64:
    cargo check -p <crate> --all-targets --target aarch64-linux-android

So the 32-bit Android targets are claimed as supported but are not in the gate, and at least one crate proves they were not being checked.

Do: run cargo check --all-targets against armv7-linux-androideabi and i686-linux-android across the workspace, record how many crates fail and why, then either (a) fix them and add both to the documented acceptance command, or (b) narrow the CLAUDE.md claim to the targets actually gated. Option (b) is a legitimate answer — what is not acceptable is the current gap between the stated claim and the checked reality.

Expect more width assumptions specifically: grep for '1 <<' on usize, 'as usize' on 64-bit quantities, and size_of::<usize>().

title: cfmesh: boundary layers on curved / polyhedral walls (snappyHexMesh-style layer addition)
description: add_boundary_layers is V&V'd + reliable on FLAT (box) walls but invalidates the mesh on CURVED walls (snapped sphere/cylinder) and on polygonal (dual) wall faces — the averaged inward-normal extrusion self-intersects / inverts on convex curvature. Mesh Studio currently gracefully SKIPS layers there (falls back to the valid polyhedral dual) and reports it. Needed for real curved-geometry CFD near-wall resolution: per-point feature-aware normals, layer-thickness limiting by local cell size, layer collapse/termination where cells would invert (snappyHexMesh addLayers strategy). V&V: sphere/cylinder + N layers -> valid + solvable, prism cells present at the wall, volume conserved. Blocks the full 'polyhedral mesh with layers' story for curved reactors in Mesh Studio (examples/mesh_studio).

notes.content: Curved-wall layers working (commit a52636a): add_boundary_layers_adaptive — smoothed normal field (Laplacian passes over wall-point adjacency) + per-point thickness cap (fraction of local wall spacing) + global validity back-off (scale down until closed). Diagnosis: min-faces dual + THIN layers was already valid on the sphere; failure was thickness-driven self-intersection, not topology — back-off targets that. Mesh Studio now inserts real prism layers on sphere (6583 cells) + cylinder (3978), valid, 0 inverted, volume conserved. BL non-orthogonality ~79-81deg is expected (>checkMesh 70deg warning, handled by non-orthogonal correctors) — GUI explains this. V&V: 3 tests (sphere/cylinder/box). REMAINING (keep open): back-off is GLOBAL (one tight feature thins whole wall); true per-point LOCAL layer termination + height-by-feature-size (snappyHexMesh addLayers / AFLR advancing-layer) still to do for optimal thickness on mixed-curvature geometry.

description: root@vm
title: root@vm
njoy leapr: generate_tape skipped the trans and discre stages entirely (molecular moderators badly wrong)
description:
FOUND AND FIXED 2026-08-14 while wiring light water through to outram-mc.

leapr::generate::generate_tape built S(alpha,beta) by calling ONLY continuous::phonon_expansion (the Fortran 'contin'), then derived dwpix/tempf from the FrequencyModel alone. The Fortran temperature loop (leapr.f90:376-384) runs three stages:

    call contin                       ! continuum
    if (twt.gt.zero) call trans       ! translational term  -> updates tempf (998)
    if (nd.gt.0)     call discre      ! discrete oscillators -> updates dwpix (1388) and tempf (1644)

Both later kernels WERE ported and unit-tested (translation::add_translation, discrete::add_discrete_oscillators, with the correct &mut dwpix / &mut tempf signatures) — generate_tape simply never called them.

Invisible to the graphite validation: crystalline graphite has twt=0 and nd=0, so contin alone IS the whole law. It is severe for any molecular moderator. Measured for H-in-H2O at 293.6 K:

  T_eff          482.49 K  vs published 1194.3 K   (-60%)
  sigma(0.0253)  44.44 b   vs published 52.10 b    (-15%)
  sigma(8 eV)    30.58 b   vs published 20.707 b   (+48%, and NOT decreasing toward the free-atom limit)

After the fix: T_eff 1195.35 K (+0.09%), sigma 52.408 / 21.847 / 21.073 / 20.835 b at 0.0253/1/4/8 eV, all within ~0.6% of the published evaluation.

Also affects every other deck with twt>0 or oscillators: the hydrides, the methanes, ice, D2O, polyethylene. GENERATOR_REVISION bumped 1 -> 2 to invalidate cached artifacts. Regression guard: tests/leapr_h2o_secondary_scatterer.rs::effective_temperature_includes_translation_and_oscillators.

title: root@vm
tampines-steam-tables: (p,s) validity check panics at exactly p = p_sat(273.15 K), unlike (p,h)
description:
Found while doing op-dt3.26. A genuine asymmetry between two sibling validity checks that should behave the same.

REPRODUCTION (release mode, crate v0.2.5, 2026-08-11):
  let p = sat_pressure_4(ThermodynamicTemperature::new::<kelvin>(273.15));
  let s = SpecificHeatCapacity::new::<kilojoule_per_kilogram_kelvin>(4.0);
  t_ps_eqm(p, s)
  -> panics: 'entropy: two-phase (T,p) state (IAPWS-IF97 Region 4) is under-determined
     without steam quality x'

One ULP above that pressure it succeeds. The equivalent (p,h) call at exactly the same
pressure succeeds.

ROOT CAUSE. ps_flash_eqm/validity_range.rs::is_below_isotherm_t_273_15 computes its
lower entropy bound as

    s_tp_eqm_single_phase(ThermodynamicTemperature::new::<kelvin>(273.15), p)

At p == p_sat(273.15 K) bit-for-bit, region_fwd_eqn_single_phase matches its
'pres == p_sat_reg4_pascal' arm and returns Region4, whose (T,p) arm in
s_tp_eqm_single_phase is a deliberate panic (a single-phase (T,p) flash cannot resolve
a two-phase state).

The (p,h) sibling already dodges this. ph_flash_eqm/validity_range.rs:45-58 carries an
explicit NOTE explaining that the whole 273.15 K isotherm lies in Region 1 for every
valid pressure, and evaluates the bound with the Region-1 forward equation h_tp_1
directly instead of routing through h_tp_eqm_single_phase.

SUGGESTED FIX: make the (p,s) check symmetric - use s_tp_1(lower_temp_bound, p) instead
of s_tp_eqm_single_phase, and carry the same explanatory NOTE. s_tp_1 is the correct
saturated-liquid entropy on the saturation line and the correct compressed-liquid
entropy above it, exactly as h_tp_1 is for enthalpy.

CURRENT WORKAROUND, and what to do when this is fixed. interfaces::checked::ps
::check_ps_envelope encodes an EXCLUSIVE pressure floor (p > p_sat(273.15 K)) where
check_ph_envelope's is inclusive, and documents why in its module doc and in the
'(p,s)' bullet of interfaces::checked's own module doc. When this bug is fixed, that
floor should be relaxed to inclusive and three places updated in the same change:
  1. checked/ps.rs - the gate and its 'p == p_sat(273.15 K) trap' section
  2. checked/mod.rs - the '- ps' bullet under 'Other families covered by this facade'
  3. checked/tests.rs::out_of_range_ps_returns_err_not_panic - the assertion that
     p_triple() is rejected, which should become an acceptance
Precedent for exactly this cleanup: op-cv1c, where fixing the router's half-open
100 MPa edge let the facade drop its matching carve-out.

Note this is a low-severity practical issue (the triple-point isobar is an unusual
operating point) but it is a real IF97 state that the library rejects, and the
inconsistency between the two sibling checks is a trap for the next reader.

notes.content: Fixed and pushed 2026-08-11 in commit b37e79a3 on develop. is_below_isotherm_t_273_15 now evaluates its lower entropy bound with the Region-1 forward equation s_tp_1, mirroring the (p,h) sibling's use of h_tp_1; checked/ps.rs pressure floor relaxed from exclusive to inclusive to match. Regression test ps_flash_accepts_exact_triple_point_isobar records methodology and measured results: t_ps_eqm(611.2126774443449 Pa, 4.0 kJ/(kg K)) = 273.15000000000003 K, identical to one ULP above, 2.8e-14 K from T_sat. cargo test --release -p tampines-steam-tables --lib interfaces::checked -> 11 passed, 0 failed. Note two pre-existing assertions in checked_control_volume_constructors and out_of_range_ps_returns_err_not_panic had been written for the exclusive floor and now assert acceptance.

kovan lit import: writes output files AFTER printing its summary, so piping to head silently loses them
description:
Found 2026-08-12 while ingesting the HTR-10 references.

REPRODUCTION: run an import with the output piped, e.g.

    ./target/release/kovan lit import <pdf> --json-out <a> --markdown-out <b> | head -14

OBSERVED: the summary block prints and LOOKS successful — it even lists json_out and markdown_out paths — but kovan writes those files AFTER emitting the summary. head closes the pipe, kovan takes SIGPIPE, and the files are never written. The visible output gives no hint that anything failed.

EXPECTED: either write the artifacts BEFORE printing the summary that names them, or handle SIGPIPE so a closed stdout does not abort the work. Printing the path of a file that was never created is the part that makes this dangerous rather than merely annoying — the caller has every reason to believe it succeeded.

WHY IT MATTERS HERE: the workspace CLAUDE.md mandates kovan for document ingestion, and piping to head is a natural thing to do with a verbose command. An agent or a human could easily believe a document was ingested when nothing was written, and only discover it much later when the archive turns out to be empty.

kovan is a MEMBER CRATE (crates/kovan-cli), so this is a local bug, not a kopitiam upstream issue.

WORKAROUND until fixed: do not pipe kovan lit import; run it bare and check the artifacts exist on disk afterwards.

title: Two vendored openfoam_source ODE trees carried the same NaN-as-success defect (FIXED); de-duplication recommended
description:
FIXED 2026-08-13. RE-FILED after tracker data loss (see docs/kopitiam-issues/).

The op-ad6h defect existed in THREE places: outram-foam-basic-lib, tampines-steam-tables/src/openfoam_algorithms/openfoam_source/ode/, and outram-park-fork-coolprop/src/openfoam_algorithms/openfoam_source/. diff -r showed the two vendored trees differ only in doc wording and use-ordering.

Confirmed by demonstration, not inference. In BOTH trees Rosenbrock23::solve_step imports integrate_interval and normalize_error but NOT adaptive_step, so it duplicates the retry loop; the guard was proven load-bearing by deleting it and watching the tests fail with Err(StepSizeUnderflow) instead of Err(NonFiniteState).

SEVERITY NUANCE: the enum variant surfaced NO consumers in either crate -- OdeError appears only inside openfoam_source/ode/, and adaptive_step is called only by euler.rs and rkf45.rs. So here the defect was LATENT, a trap for the first consumer, unlike basic-lib where it was actively reachable.

Gates: tampines-steam-tables 955 passed / 0 failed / 13 ignored; outram-park-fork-coolprop 282 / 0 / 4; cargo check --workspace --lib --release clean.

RECOMMENDATION for op-xji, not acted on: delete both vendored ODE sub-trees and depend on outram-foam-basic-lib. One defect fixed three times is the concrete case op-xji describes, and the ODE sub-tree is the cheapest pilot because it has ZERO consumers -- removing it changes no behaviour and no public surface. Countervailing constraint documented in coolprop openfoam_algorithms/CLAUDE.md: the vendoring is deliberate so that crate depends only on uom and stays Android-buildable, whereas basic-lib pulls ndarray. Maintainer decision.
